title: Excellent value.
body: I used this travel insurance mainly for the car hire excess. I paid $108 for cover for a family of 5, compared to the car company  excess only insurance of $200. Booking online very easy, with immediate confirmations. I did not claim, but felt assured from other people who had needed to, giving generally positive reviews. Will definitely use this company again for future travels, and would recommend to others.

title: Great service
body:
We took out a cover more policy for a quick 10 day trip as a family of four. We had to make two separate claims for illness and hospitalization. 
Claims were processed and reimbursed on the same day they were lodged. Great service from experienced well informed staff. I would definitely use cover more again.

title: Stay Away from CBA Allianz Travel Insurance
body: My wife developed a medical condition so we had to put off our trip for 6 months. We put in a claim for lost deposits of $2000 supplied Doctors letters saying it was not a pre existing condition, paid another $165 to her GP to satisfy their request for 2 years of her medical history. Allianz chose to ignore the letters and reject our claim on the grounds of an existing condition. I don't care about the $2000 but am very upset that I have being paying platinum credit card fees for over ten years and when I put in a claim on this "tricked up" Insurance Policy. It clearly has so many exit avenues it is absolutely useless and should not be advertised as free insurance. I am in the process now of moving accounts that the CBA earns over $3000 a year from me to another bank. I probably will be travelling for another 10 years so the Commonwealth Bank will be $30,000 worse off.

title: Peace of mind should any problems arise
body:
Prices getting more expensive as we get older even if in good health and still working in our seventies.
Policy easy to set up and did not need customer support

title: made a claim
body: needed to make a claim when I had to cut short my trip when my Father died suddenly.  Got most of what I claimed back so cannot really complain.  process was ok, maybe a little long but happy to receive what I got.

title: Refund do to accident
body: Due to my accident four days prior to our Cruise departure,we unfortunately had to cancel.Our customer support was very good and they kept in touch with us over the phone and by email advising us of the progress to our claim.Our money was also refunded in the specified time frame.We were  contacted to inform us that our claim had been settled and money refunded. I also received a phone call from Budget Direct to see how I was progressing after my accident. I would recommend Budget Direct Travel and will use them again when booking our next trip.

title: Good coverage, good value for money

body:

I wouldnt hesitate to recommend them to anyone travelling overseas

We have used Allianz previously and will continue to do so for all our future travels.

body:

body: When I compared for Travel Insurance against several others, Budget Direct offered everything I was after. I found it easy to take out the insurance online which was great for me.

title: HIGHLY DO NOT RECOMMEND
body:
I went overseas to Hawaii in July 2017, resulted in having an allergic reaction and had to go to Hospital. Had to pay $700US up front to the hospital (assuming we would get it back straight away).  I was still trying to claim from Cover-more in May 2018. Absolutely ridiculous! ALMOST 10-11 MONTHS!

They keep coming back to me saying it will be a further 10 days before i get any response.
Or that they need further documentation to support my claim. I don't understand why they don't just request all the required documents to start off with. As I provided all medical documents and filled out all the paperwork necessary from my family doctor/doctor from the Hospital in Hawaii.

Covermore came back and said it was my fault for not providing the necessary documents, although I had already provided all the documents that was necessary for my claim.
Ended up sending the same documents 2-3 times, felt like it was just going around in circles before any progress was made, even then the claim would backfire and I would have to resend the hospital bill or my medical records through to them again. I felt like they are just finding an excuse to not make the claim as we owed $2000US to the Hospital in Hawaii and we had already paid over $1000US on medication and doctors bills.

I eventually received all expenses paid in relation to my medical incident at the end of July 2018, but took well over a year to get anything back. Would really recommend going with someone else, Covermore representatives were no help whatsoever.

title: Great App, but not really add value to the real service -- disappointing!
body:
This is the first time I get travel insurance when going to overseas and I thought I should choose a good and reliable insurance company.  However, I was wrong.
- I have got delay flights to connect the flight to back to Melbourne. Lucky out of the bad luck, my replacement flight and hotel for the night to stay over in Hong Kong airport was covered by the airline --- but of course that was absolutely not enjoyable as my couldn't follow my plan!
- Lucky my boyfriend can organise to pick me up in the airport, otherwise I have to catch a taxi that will cost me around $200 to home! (this money can fly me from and to Sydney for at least twice!)

Basically, this bad experience didn't incur any out of pocket cost.
However, it did ruin my schedule to work in the next day and lots of inconvenience.

I called TID today and they just say can't help at all as I didn't pay for anything extra...
Fair enough, but it did cost me the lost of paid from work! (as I planned to work as soon as I get home, and I'm a casual admin, there is no way to provide work evidence unless I go to work!...which just bad luck, can't claim!)

The ridiculous thing was, I asked the consultant if my boyfriend can't organise to pick me up, if my taxi cost to home able to claim, and he said "No, you are not able to claim no matter if your friend able to pick you up or you order a taxi, that's not covered".

I understand any out of pocket expenses have to provide receipt, but how about this one?
I'm very doubt of what the policy "Additional public transport expenses to get to a pre-arranged wedding, funeral, conference or back to work in Australia on time. No excess applies" means.

No matter how handy and good looking of the TID App is it, but it's not helpful at all when something really happened.

Well done, you are successfully kick another customer (and maybe more potential customers) away.

title: Your cover is only as good as your claim - excellent!
body:

title: Good Value
body: Compared it to many others. The Gold level great value and plenty of cover. Website was easy to use, the fact Choice had recommended this cover helped seal the deal. we'll see what happens when we travel

title: No cover for international travel
body:
We had flights booked in January to London, and proceeded to book Italy accommodation in February (for our May trip) and had budget direct insurance taken out at the same time when Covid-19 was a problem in China only.

We stayed up to date with travel warnings and what the medical experts were saying so weren?t worried about our trip at this stage.

March is when the situation turned and it was clear it was unlikely any international travel would happen. We then reached out to a girl on the online chat about what we could do and it was clear budget direct were confused and couldn?t give any answers either. 

We then submitted a claim only to wait more than 8 weeks to be told it was denied because it was a ?World known event? in January, therefore a claim couldn?t go ahead.

8 weeks is too long to wait for a response. Budget direct have made up their mind on covid-19?s ?world known event? cut off date AFTER the fact thousands of Australians have booked budget direct for their international travel. It?s misleading to say the least. They shouldn?t have taken our money AFTER their cut off date for any international travellers.

I?ve always gone through budget direct, and I?ve also repeatedly renewed my cars insurances through them. I?m disappointed and have nothing good to say about this company. Look elsewhere or avoid insurances all together!

title: Meets my requirements consistently
body: Good value, easy to set up - a little bit short for older and medically impaired clients in options and cover. Basic cover really quite good. Have used this company for many years all over the world for ourselves and our children.

We joined a Facebook page before leaving on our cruise on our return a lot of fellow passengers were discusseing that they claimed between $50 and $100 per person per port unfortunately suresave does not cover this. And if we had of took insurance with one of these other companies we would have save between $20 to $30 dollars and would have able to claim missed ports. If cruising look around and compare

The online buying process is straightforward and prices are competitive but more importantly, claims are handled quickly, with consideration and courtesy.  Buying insurance is easy; the real test is if or when something goes wrong.  We have had claims while travelling and also prior to travelling (medical cancellation) and both times everyone was helpful and the process was straightforward.  Over the years we have recommended 1Cover to dozens of family and friends and all have been happy.  About to book them again.

title: Easy insurance online.

title: Worst Travel Insurance Company!!!
body: I purchased a policy with Insure and Go and buying a Groupon voucher earlier this year. I took out the top cover prior to my two week holiday to the United States. My bag was delayed and did not arrive in San Fransisco until more than 24 hours after I had landed. As I had no clothing, toiletries etc. with me, I had to purchase several basic supplies. I submitted a claim upon returning to Australia (end of July). After struggling to submit an online claim due to the tedious and ambiguous forms, I filled out the huge document by hand and sent it to the Insure and Go head office in Broadway along with my original receipts of the items I was claiming. The company are now telling me (3 months later) that they never received my receipts (which were in the same envelope as the claim form they DID receive) and cannot process my claim. I have been emailing back and forth ever since, waiting more than 2 weeks for a reply each time. I have just about given up on ever receiving the money I attempted to claim. I have learnt my lesson to never trust unknown, overseas companies when it comes to travel insurance. They?re more than happy to take your insurance premium but don?t want to know when you need to claim. Never again!!

title: Insure & Go are shysters - don't deal with them
body:
We were duped into taking out a travel policy with Insure & Go by an email referral from the SA government's Seniors Card Unit. We took it out for travel to the UK in May.  The policy was competitive at the time.
However with Australia in a 6 month lockdown, and the UK happily accepting flights but keeping their own people indoors, the trip is off.  I have also emailed Insure & Go about a deferral of policy but they have not had the courtesy of responding.  But Paul and Roger have been rejected (see below).  Yes it is something our gutless ACCC should take up.  The airlines, Heathrow Express, Historic Royal Palaces are all offering deferral of purchased tickets/passes.  It's money for nothing for Insure & Go.  If enough people get smart they can be shamed out of operating in Australia.

title: Allianz backed Westpac Visa Credit Card Travel Insurance - A Farce
body:
Waited 3 months for their processing and finally, I get an answer today.

title: DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY EVER- THEY WILL NOT PROTECT YOU only their bottom line!!!
body:
1. July 14th - Parents depart for overseas adventure trip of lifetime- due back in late Sept.
2. July 19th - My husband & carer ( I have MS medically retired age 43) had an unexpected heart attack, released from hospital after one week with a stent and no permanent heart damage. Decided everything would be okay they didn?t need to return to care for me. 
3. August 30th - Due to ongoing chest pain- husband readmitted to bigger city hospital where it was discovered he had terminal cancer with a mass on his lung that had metastasised to the bones & kidneys.
4. September 4th - Parents rush home( cover more aided them to speak to Australian travel agency).
5. My husband died on 1st December- cover more still refusing to make a decision to pay any associated costs incurred due to my parents having to end their trip, rebook flights  & tours they had to cancel that were pre paid for etc. 
They have been provided with medical certificates & hospital discharge reports which clearly state - there was no cancer identified after heart attack. 
6. The distress this company have caused in my families most vulnerable time- I would never want to see another family have to endure. All they want is more information more reports until you finally give up!

The only providers who did not provide a full refund were the airline we booked from Sydney to Munich return and one accommodation provider in Italy.

TID were amazing.  We could have been $1000's of dollars out of pocket but the only cost in the end was the $100.00 excess on each policy. 

Thank you TID.  We will continue to use you for all our travel insurance and to recommend you to family and friends.

title: It took SureSave months to pay my claim
body:
Hey!

I got stuck in NZ for a night because a plane was hit my lightening and my plane was diverted to another airport. 

We contacted SureSave to find out if I was covered and what I was covered for.

They said I was up to AU$2500... AWESOME.

They told me what I needed to make a claim and I made sure I got it all for them.

On submission they would not accept the official documentation from the airline although it was on letterhead and was the same document they gave to everyone one the plane.

They took forever to reply to questions and in the end I had to waste hours contacting the airline and getting a letter from them that said the exact same thing as the document I had in the first place and then they finally paid out... it was not a hard claim... taxi to the hotel, 1 nights accommodation, dinner and breakfast and a taxi back to the airport.

When they would not accept the airline letter I asked why they don't just call the airline and confirm what happened... they refused too.

The impression I got was if they made this too difficult I would just go away.

Murray
Good cover when they pay out
Takes forever to try and make a claim

title: Severe Lack of Empathy
body: My dad died from cancer while I was overseas, so I had to come home earlier than planned which cost me extra due to the need for the changes in my travel arrangements. So I made a claim hoping to recover some of that cost. I provided a death certificate thinking this would be enough, but it wasn?t. Covermore asked that I give permission for doctors to give out more details regarding my dads medical history. The problem with that is legally I can?t give permission because I am not an executor of his estate, which I don?t understand because I am not making any claim regarding my dads estate, I just want to try and recoup some costs from my travel insurance. Losing my dad was difficult enough without covermore playing hardball, now they want me to relive it by making me jump through hoops that I can not jump through. So I am stuck between a rock and a hard place, Covermore won?t payout because I can?t give the required permission. So I will not recommend Covermore as an insurer because apparently an official death certificate is not enough. If it was an option, I would give a zero star rating.

title: Insure'n'go should be renamed InsurengoStuff yaself pal!
body:
Well after doing all the right things ie (Medical, Insurance, Accommodation) before going to India I was in for a rude shock. I had paid for and got Gold Insurance with InsureandGo and had expected if anything went wrong it was covered. To cut a long story short my prepaid accommodation at Celebrity Resort Hotel in India booked and paid for by myself thru Agoda claim they had not received payment.

I went to Internet and I proved I had made payment to Agoda and Agoda confirmed this. Not only that I had my credit card record. But still I was refused a room and asked to leave. I then had to pay 2 other hotels for myself as it was Independence day in India and most hotels were fully booked.

Needless to say when I got back from India I lodged my claim. After almost a month it was refused. Why ? here's why.
Clause 27 on page 17 says this Any claim arising from errors in your booking arrangements by "YOU", your travel agent or any other person acting on your behalf. In regards to your claim, the accommodation was booked and then cancelled due to an administration error with Agoda. Unfortunately this means there is no coverage under the policy as there is an exclusion to booking arrangement errors. This is the exclusion they use not to pay your claim. 

In my claim I explained it was not an error made by Agoda or me but was the Resort Hotel whom had ripped me off. I again explained this to the gent handling my case and he again told me of the exclusion. I reiterated I had paid and made the bookings myself to which I was told my making the bookings was covered under the exclusion under You in the clause 27. 

Being on a  pension and having saved for this trip I could not afford to lose the almost $500 paid plus I had to pay and extra almost $500 for more accommodation. What's more they lied about Agoda and it being administration error when I have repeatedly told them what actually happened.

To me this is deceitful and underhanded by InsureandGo to not pay for something that was not of my doing. I in good faith paid to cover everything before I left by to my dismay it is not so. One thing is for sure I will never again use them and I should have used Travel Insuarance Direct as I always had done.

My suggestions is 1) Avoid InsureandGo like the plague. 2 ) Don't get tempted by InsureandGo low prices ! Refer to point 1. When in doubt refer to point 1 and Please read very carefully any policy before paying for it and if you have to pay more to another company like Travel Insure Direct to guarantee all aspects of your trip is then pay the extra for peace of mind.

title: Treated Unfairly ? not once but twice!!
body:
Treated Unfairly ? not once but twice!!
I purchased an Annual Policy (through Flight Centre) from Cover-More in June 2018. Cover-More was highly recommended to me as being the ?best in the business?. Since that time, I have travelled extensively and did make a small claim for a Doctor visit on a cruise which they paid ($500).
However, during a long tour to the Canadian Rockies I contracted the dreaded travel bug (severe vomiting and diarrhoea) and, I was so ill and, in fact, was not able to leave my hotel room to visit a doctor. I called 911 to the Hotel, and they just said it would take a few days to recover. Local Doctors do not visit hotels in Calgary.  The result of this misfortune was that I missed the next leg of my business class flights for the organised tour of Washington USA. 
I eventually visited a medical clinic next day and arranged for the GP to prepare a Certificate. I was holed up in Calgary for 4 days due to disruption of flights and illness. Eventually I purchased a flight back to Vancouver and travelled back to Australia.
My estimate of my personal loss in dollar terms was about $10,000. That comprised of hotels not used, flights not used, hotels needed to stay in but not previously booked and of course medical expenses. 
I submitted over 100 pages of documents in supporting my claim. During the course of Cover-More processing my claim they certainly made me feel dishonest and depressed. They requested more documents and proof which took me to the limit. 
I submitted my Claim on 19th January and it is only last week that Cover-More finally contacted me to say they were happy to advise that they were paying me approx. $1700 for my loss. I am appalled and disappointed because I was very honest with them. They did explain how they calculated the amount, but I better not go into that on this media. I would just say that the whole method is totally unfair.
The ?TWICE? comment (heading) from me surrounds the overall Policy which was covering the above instance. I paid $4658 for an annual premium (expires 14/6/2019) and apparently at the time of purchase I must have said that my trips would not be longer than 60 days. However, this year I booked a 96-day tour and my existing annual Policy expires a few days before I return. They have refused to cover me unless I pay another $3000 (approx.). I therefore decided to insure through another Company, and I believe that new Insurer is much cheaper and with equivalents or better benefits. 
I therefore asked Cover-More for a refund for the unused months (Mar to June) as they would not cover me.  They refused to refund saying that would be up to Flight Centre. When I contacted Flight Centre, they said it was up to Cover-More.
This is the whole truth and nothing but the truth. For the average traveller I think people should think very carefully about what benefits they may achieve under their Travel Insurance Policy. I was one of those who is sitting here in amazement at how some Insurance Companies treat their Policy Holders who pay money in good faith for supposedly top cover and in the end experience a very bad outcome.

Easy to apply for travel insurance. Cheap domestic travel insurance particularly if you're a member with Medibank (insurance is handled through Mondial).

We contacted them as soon as I was admitted to hospital and they stayed in touch until we made it back to Australia calling us to make sure we were doing ok. We are completely amazed at the customer service we received and would highly recommend this company to anyone.

title: Deceptive travel delay conditions.
body:
I took comprehensive single insurance for $307 with $0 excess for 32 days. When my Air China flight was delayed due to "air traffic control" issue I had to spend night at Beiging airport and then continue to Munich 24 hours later. When on return I submitted my claim, on excessively elaborate internet site, for around $70 for transport and food - it was refused. Reason given: delay was not due to "severe weather conditions". I was also informed that "the policy only provides cover for additional accommodation expences". Luckily for me I did not have any other situations that were "covered" by this insurance and did not have to find out that I was not insured. Good lesson for the future !

Does not cover for what it advertises. Other insurance companies do not put limiting conditions on reasons for travel delay

I did not expect that I would get my money back but I still lodged a police report in Lisbon since I had several bank cards in my wallet as well.  Fast forward, we got home the 8th of May and I reviewed the FREE travel insurance with my CBA Platinum Awards card provided by Cover More.  I submitted all the paperwork they required...easy!

body:
Very bad experience with this company. Will never get insured from them. They seem to find to ways to get around and not to pay claims.

It is a total rip off! We went to a vacation to USA for 2 months and our 14 month old baby had diaper rash on her bottom. She also has milk allergy that was diagnosed a year ago in AU. However there was no relation between milk allergy and diaper rash! When we claimed it via the "travel insurance direct", the answer we get was "because your baby had milk allergy, which is a pre-existing condition, and this MIGHT BE the cause of diaper rash. So we cannot pay your claim!" We were shocked! This is something like "because you have a pre-existing heart problem, and now you are suffering from a wart on your foot, we cannot cover your treatment for your foot!. First of all, we called the sales team and asked them if her allergy would be covered when we bought the policy. They said yes, it will be covered. When you go overseas with babies, you want your baby to be covered and feel safe. This company has no morals.

title: The worst travel insurance experience I have ever had
body:
I travel a lot, and I've used TID many times on many trips in the past. I've made some minor claims with no problems. 

Unfortunately, whilst travelling in Iceland in 2015, I fell on ice and severely injured my hip. I had to have major surgery and have been unable to return to my usual work. 

TID promptly reimbursed me for the changes to my travel plans, but when it came to my claim for loss of income I was repeatedly asked for more information. I provided all the information that was requested, but this would be met with another request for even more detailed information. This frustrating process drew out for one year. Meanwhile, I was in pain, awaiting surgery, and in extreme financial stress because I still wasn't able to work. 

It began to seem like the requests were a deliberate tactic of obfuscation so that this company would not have to pay out my claim for loss of income, as set out in my travel insurance policy. 

Ultimately, I took my claim to the financial ombudsman and the loss of income claim was paid IMMEDIATELY! More than one year after my initial injury. 

This experience was needlessly stressful, time-consuming and frustrating. I discourage my friends and family from using this travel insurer every chance I get.

If you have trouble with your TID claim I recommend taking your case to the financial ombudsman. I wish that I had done so sooner.

title: Make sure you complain to Financial Ombudsman Service
body:
My Cebu Pacific flight in Philippines was cancelled due to bad weather. I wrote to TID; after admitting that the policy covered flight cancellations due to bad weather, its assessor Cerberus Special Risks claimed that it needed more documentation, which I sent to it. Even for low cost airlines, the assessor wants a letter stating that no recompense has occurred although I substituted a 'nil return' from my Cebu Pacific travel fund.

The assessor then settled the claim for a miniscule amount but suggested that the Product Disclosure Statement mandated that only the higher of my cancelled flight cost and my replacement flight with AirAsiaPhilippines would be covered, and of course the standard excess would be deducted.

Given TID's advertising and the ambiguities in its PDS, I have written twice to the Financial Ombudsman Service Limited by mail = the most effective method - at GPO Box 3, Melbourne 3001 asking it to investigate and seek resolution.

Insurers like TID through their assessors hope that insured parties with claims will simply 'give up' and go away because the amount involved is trifling.

However if 20,000 claimants 'give up' and the average value of their claim after deducting the standard A$100 excess is $150, that is as much as $3 million (less assessor costs) in profits for TID and its underwriters such as  
Lloyds.

Don't give up, and don't bother with asking for your partly or fully denied claim to be 'internally reviewed' by Cerberus Special Risks.

While it may have 45 days to respond, far better to go direct to the Financial Ombudsman and put the insurer and its assessor on notice that you are dissatisfied with a claim being fully or partly denied.

When she recovered, the appropriate documentation was posted to Covermore and then they were contacted on:
 1300362644 22/12 at 2.55 pm for 11mins
 1300362644 23/12 at 12.32 pm for 22mins 
The woman she spoke with scrutinised the documentation and also referred to the Head Claims Consultant who further scrutinised all the documentation that had been sent in. My daughter was on the phone with them (not on hold) whilst this was occurring. They both concurred, and she was explicitly told that because of the documentation from both the hospital and doctors there would be no reason why the cost of the fares would not be reimbursed. Further to this she was told the money for the fares would be deposited into her account on January the 8th. 
My daughter still wanted to take this holiday. The new fares to the destination were escalating in price due to purchasing close to the time of departure. The initial fares had been booked since March 2019. Due to previously excellent service on two occasions from Covermore for both myself and my husband, and the understanding that Covermore were true to their word, she booked further fares. 
Yesterday, 4th Feb, 2020, was a shock. She was emailed that the fare reimbursement would not be honoured. Now she is out of pocket for the initial fares of $1019.83. This is a stressful and highly disappointing outcome. The money spent on the second fares was the spending money for the holiday. Back to you Covermore!

title: Complete Joke
body:
My daughters recently travelled to the Uk from Australia on their first overseas adventure and were advised by STA travel to purchase Allianz global assistance travel insurance at an exorbitant cosy of over $600 for 3 months. While staying in a locked room in a backpackers hostel in London, one of their phones was stolen by another traveller in the room. After much frustrating communication with Allianz, when all documents including the police report, proof of purchase, insurance certificate, etc. was provided to them, the claim was rejected not once but 3 times on appeal. Apparently, even though the room was locked, one sister was left in charge of the phone and fell asleep while the other went to breakfast locking the door behind her, and the phone was hidden behind a rubbish bin next to the bed on charge, the insurance doesn't cover it because it is a "public place". When you read the fine print everywhere in their terms is considered a "public place", including everywhere in a hotel. I asked them if there was any scenario that existed where you could actually claim for a stolen or lost phone and they couldn't give me an answer. In my opinion, after my experience and things i have since heard from others, insurance companies like Allianz have no intention of ever paying out on any claims for loss of personal effects. They simply hide behind their cleverly worded terms and conditions and give you the run around until you get sick of it and give up. I would never ever recommend Allianz Global Assitance travel insurance to anyone. Beware!! And also you people who give all the glowing reviews for these companies that have never had to make a claim, give it a rest, you're not helping anyone.

Exorbitant price, will not pay out

title: Claim was accepted, however my medical bills are still outstanding 3 months later!
body:
I was a loyal customer until they messed me around. I was always confident that I will be covered in the event of an emergency, but my mind's changed!

Had a medical emergency in the USA. My claim was accepted without much hassle. The good news ends there.

My claim was accepted early March 2018. It is now nearly JULY 2018 and my medical bills are still UNPAID. 

I was assured 4 or 5 times in the 3 month period after my claim was accepted, that my bills will be settled.
I kept getting bills sent directly to me from the hospital and medical facility (a fortnightly event!), even though TID have assured me that they have fully taken over my outstanding bills, and are apparently "in negotiation" of the fees. 
At one stage, my outstanding bill was sent to the debt collectors in the USA!  It's impossible to get a straight answer from them as to what is actually going on with my outstanding bills, or the actual status of my claim even though it's been "accepted". I don't believe for a second that they are in the process of paying my bills. Why else would the outstanding amount ended up at the debt collectors?

I have escalated the issue to the financial ombudsman. My bills are still outstanding at this point in time.

AVOID this company if you can. Disappointing and very stressful.

title: Would give zero rating if possible.  Will never deal with TID again.
body: I purchased the ?works? comprehensive travel policy months before COVID-19.  Whilst I was overseas I had to book alternative flights to get home due to government travel bans and restrictions imposed by the countries I had to transit via.  When I returned I emailed TID and asked if my policy covered this.  I specifically detailed that the alternate travel arrangements were due to government travel bans and restrictions in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur.  The ?sales consultant? who responded misinformed me that I was covered as my policy was purchased in July 2019 and that I should submit a claim for consideration.  I spent 4 hours preparing all of the necessary paperwork and waited 25 days for an answer.  I was extremely annoyed to be advised that TID then denied my claim as ?government bans and restrictions? are not a defined event.  My online enquiry specifically asked if they would cover this.  They should have advised me no and I would not have bothered submitting a claim.  Now I have to declare a denied insurance claim for the next 5 years.  I emailed TID afterwards and they merely advised that each claim is considered on a case by case basis.  Why bother telling customers to submit a claim when they know it is not covered?  My online enquiry before submitting a claim specifically detailed what had happened (I have proof and TID cannot claim otherwise).  Extremely poor service and their response after was the claim was denied indicated a lack of accountability on their part.  I have purchased 12 policies from them but will never use them again.  By the way, responding to customers in writing as ?hey ....? is unprofessional.  Sums them up.  Update: TID contacted me prior to lodging this review and advised they were willing to investigate this but ultimately all they could offer was the complaint?s department email address!  Why would I bother submitting anymore information to an insurer who isn?t interested in paying claims or taking responsibility when their staff provide the wrong information?  Lesson learnt - travel insurance is a waste of time in most cases.

title: Never again, will do anything to reject your claim
body:
As far as I'm concerned lost or stollen baggage is just that, and should apply to whatever general baggage you have. This company just picks and chooses what they feel like covering, and sneaks in what they don't in the 40 page 'policy wording'. My laptop got stollen and they rejected my claim stating that in the fine print under section 'E1' blah blah this is not covered. Its baggage! It should be covered! Incredibly frustrating and would defiantly not advise anybody to get insurance with them.

Con artists, refused to pay legitimate claim, unreliable

title: Credit card travel insurance
body:
Planned and paid for holiday through Commonwealth Bank Visa whilst Zurich was the insurer. Some months before holiday CommBank changed provider to Allianz who apparently need you to activate insurance whereas Zurich didn't. I was diagnosed with breast cancer and operated on a week before my family holiday so had to cancel. Luckily Jetstar repaid flight fares but Allianz refuses to pay accomodation cancellation because I hadn't activated my insurance. Funny how they will pay medical or dental at holiday destination without activation. Go figure. Very angry

Update 19 January 2016:
Said you would contact me re refusal to pay claim. Still haven't heard. You haven't sent dispute paperwork yet. 
I will be also complaining about you to my credit card provider.

title: InsureandGo - A great product at a reasonable price.
body:

I couldn't find another product which offered so much for the price - and flexible with cover too.  No problems understanding the online system with multiple choices, incl pre-exist medical conditions disclosure.  Easy to try different options to see what any differences were before I selected what I needed.  The 'discount' for seniors is a good incentive.
I referred only one question to 'a human', and this was quickly dealt with and explained fully.
Whilst not at this stage needing to make a claim - and I hope this remains so - if I need to, then if the service/response is as good and as timely as getting the policy was, I would rate InsureandGo as excellent.

title: Quick and Easy
body:
I had my bad stolen in Europe and some flights that been cancelled due to airline has gone to bankrupt. I have submitted my claim upon return (provided my police report and proof of ownership). It was processed in a timely manner just as they said within 10 business days. Overly I was very happy with the outcome apart from that they didn?t cover my additional costs that I have incurred by purchasing new tickets (they been close to $1000). If you are concerned about situations when Airline might go bankrupt I would suggest that you look in to policy more closely. The case manager was polite and understanding and willing to help. I would recommend them to everyone who is traveling overseas.

body:

Whilst traveling in the more remote parts of Java I unfortunately lost my glasses.  I followed Covermore's directions and obtained the necessary information to make a claim ( ie went and reported it to a nearby police station).  On return to Australia, a week or so later, I submitted my claim, online, and almost immediately received funds to replace the lost glasses. I was astounded at the ease of application and the swift response  time.  
Needless to say, I'll be using Covermore in the future.

title: Never get insurance from Allianz - scammers
body:
Hey guys and gals, 

I guess you could say I had two really bad experiences with Allianz. I purchased premium cover for over $300 and made a claim. It took more then 6months of paper work. Not to mention they want every bit of information of you including your full medical history, reports, phone records, bank statements, and they are just as arrogant enough to ask for your social security records. 

Never, never, never purchase travel insurance from Allianz - You have to pay for all your medical expenses, then they "may" reimburse you. And the chances are slim, they work off scope and budgets, they don't give a crap about your wellbeing.

title: TID is ok UNTIL you need to make a claim
body:
Getting cheap insurance is useless if they are are a pain when you need to claim. My father was hospitalised 1 day before I was to leave to go on my honeymoon for 4 week. (he passed away 1 week later) I had to postpone the trip. The trip was supposed to be in March 2011 and was changed to October 2012. I only received a payout for the cancellation cost of the airfare while I was away on October trip (thats 7 months).
I supplied all items requested on the form, but the kept on requesting different paperwork each time I chased it up. Things like 'Proof of what TIME he was admitted to hospital' and "proof his condition was life threatening" (even though he died 1 week later...don't you think that is proof enough). It was not until I complained to the management that they paid. I took out travel insurance through Allianz Travel insurance for the October trip. $20 more but worth every cent. Had to put a claim in for a dropped video camera, received replacement in 7 day!!! Would always recommend Allianz over TID.

title: Disgusted
body:
My partner had a severe Bali belly and ended up waiting over 24h for medical help which never came. She was too unwell to travel to a hospital so we contacted Covermore to help us organise a doctor to the villa we were staying at in Canggu (around 5pm). There was barely any communication and after hours and hours of emails we still had no idea when the doctor was coming or if they were coming at all. After waiting for the doctor for over 5h we were told it was too late and that the doctor was coming to our villa in the morning, but then after numerous attempts to contact Covermore the following morning and still no doctor we got an email saying that we can book an appoitment at a medical clinic. Not once did the Covermore staff ask how my partner was going or if she needed anything. All they were asking and worried about during the whole communication was money, not my partner's well being.
We are both extremely disappointed in Covermore as an insurance provider. I have used numerous different insurance companies before and this one has been by far the worst. I can't believe the lack of care this company showed for my partner and the way they  left us to deal with her sickness. Absolutely disgusted in their service.

body:
The only time I have ever had to make a claim on travel insurance was earlier this year and Covermore came through with the pay-out. I was in Singapore and was carrying a bag with some pottery purchased earlier on the trip in Ireland, the bag broke and the expensive pottery smashed. I made an online claim when I returned home, submitting in detail what had happened, a copy of the receipt and photos of the broken pottery. Two or three weeks later the refund was in my bank account - within the time period they advised when I received an auto-reply from my online claim. It's impossible to know what any insurance policy is truly like until you have to make a claim; for my first travel insurance claim, this was a positive experience and I would gladly use Covermore again.
Online claiming was reasonably simple; my refund was paid without any issue; and it was quite clear what I had to do to make the claim.

title: Very poor communication.  Unsympathetic attitude.
body: I took out a silver plan with Covermore with regard to my trip to Australia which began 28th December until 5th February 2020.  Obtaining the insurance was simple and without fuss. However most insurance companies devote more energy into selling policies than dealing with problems and Covermore are no exception. My problem arose out of the current Coronavirus emergency. I chose to fly to Australia using China Airlines and landed in Melbourne before the seriousness of Coronavirus outbreak had become  public. During my stay it became obvious that to use my return tickets could give rise to a  serious danger of me coming to contact with a victim of the Virus which could then be passed on to me, especially as I would be in contact with many Chinese passengers all breathing into the same on board air conditioning system  So I tried to contact Covermore for advice and to establish what my options were.  In the event, none of the emergency numbers listed in my policy documents worked. I was able to speak to an Australian Covermore agent but he was unable to help as the insurance had been arranged in the UK.  He offered to transfer me to a UK agents but after 20 minutes the line went dead. I went on line and found another number which I tried.  A robot voice asked me to choose an option.  Press 1 to buy insurance, press 2 to make a new claim and press 3 to talk about a notified claim. I pressed two and another robitic voice told me that this option was not available. I tried all three and each time I was told the same thing. So I decided not to press any number and eventually the robot voice said "No calls can be taken at this time"  I tried another number but a recorded voice told me that the office was closed and I should call back during office hours.  No easy from a country with an 11 hour time difference.  After several days of trying various numbers I sent an email to Customers services asking for help and assistance. I received a brief response saying that Covermore are not covering claims arising out of the Coronavirus.??? The whole episode has left me with a feeling of disgust.  I could easily have had a heart attack, with the surgeon awaiting insurance confirmation before operating and judging by my experience,  I would have died before getting it. My advice is to have nothing to do with this company.

title: It's a shame how far TID have fallen
body:

We lost a few items when travelling in Vietnam, we believed they may have been left in a hotel but weren't 100% sure. We contacted the Hotel and asked if they were there and if they can be shipped to out next location (at our cost), but they informed us that they weren't there. Oh well, lucky we got to travel insurance... not. TID completely washed their hands of it and said since we *think* (but aren't sure) we left them, they won't cover it since it isn't classified as a loss by them. I thought not knowing where items were located is the very definition of loss, crazy!

Do your self a favour and pick any other company. It's disappointing that the old TID has started to use tricky tactics and unclear advertising to get out of paying claims.

title: Absolute nightmare
body:
Travelled in May to Europe to visit relatives. Got hospitalised due to illness and stayed for 4 hours at the Emergency room. Tried to call Global Assistance but did not get hold of them. 

Got back to Australia and finally got hold of them. I send in the documents and the bill. From here on the issues just piled up: You need a medical statement beside the bill and an Australian citizen has to sign a medical confirmation - The doctors did not give me a statement and it was a month back so didn't get one. I was traveling to visit relatives and didn't think of taking an Aussie in the backpack in case I need to claim insurance.

The whole circus took a month to settle.
 
Anyhow, Alliance tried to contact the hospital to gather more information on the bank account. I received an email saying there were not able to get the information due to language barrier. You see, the hospital is in Switzerland, the receptionists speak fluently up to 6 languages and English in one right on top of the list. He did not believe me and we had to organise a conference call. After that, the insurance got the idea to send an email requesting the bank details form the hospital (the webpage of the hospital is in German and English). Fine you'd think, now the issue should be solved.

Wrong, I get an email saying they can not proceed with the payment as I was not informed to have to pay 100$ excess fee for the claim to begin with! Calling the insurance and asking for the person dealing with my case I had to verify my identity 3x and still was not connected! Furthermore the person at the phone gave me attitude as if it was my fault to dare to call! 

In the meantime (June - September) my brother gets harassed for payment by the hospital with threats to block his bank account legally until the bill is settled. Should the hospital proceed with the threat, my brother will have 'unable to pay bills' in his records for up to 3 years! For a bill he is not even responsible for.

One star is too much! Absolutely incompetent! I can only imagine through what kind of drama they would have put me if I was to be in a country I can not speak the language and would be hospitalised with a more serious medical issue. I'd be dead by now!

Travel save and don't pick Alliance as your travel insurance.

title: Never Again!
body:
On a recent trip to america, i bought the most comprehensive cover in case of any medical emergency. Luckily there was no medical emergency but with severe blizzards in new york and the rest of the east coast, our flights to new york were cancelled and we could not continue our trip as all airports were closed. We did some research and found out the most cost effective outcome (as requested by travel insurance direct) would be to return home early. 

We did what we could to notify airlines, hotels and activities to cancel things that we had pre booked to make the claim smaller. 

Additional expenses
upon returning home, we made a claim for 2 additional nights accommodation in vegas (very expensive for a friday and saturday night, at the last minute, especially compared to the price i had secured for my earlier vegas accommodation months in advance) and $520 fee to change our flights to come home.

Cancellation costs
i also claimed for the cost of pre booked activities and accommodation in new york and canada. I had cancelled the rest of my internal flights with the same company who cancelled my first flight and received a refund.

The result
after months of waiting, i received less than half of the amount i claimed for. 

Here's why
firstly, tid will not cover cancellation costs and additional expenses. Make sure you are aware of that. I even emailed to clarify before taking any action after my flights were cancelled and was told i could claim under both sections (additional expenses and cancellation costs), not either section as well as being able to claim for having to change my flight to come home. Not the case. Sure, you can claim under both sections but they will not pay for both, which they conveniently left out in the email. This left me almost $300 out of pocket due to 2 extra nights accommodation in vegas!! I find it ridiculous that they don't even cover emergency accommodation when you are stranded!  

Secondly, as i received money back when cancelling internal flights, i was told i won't receive compensation for the $520 fee to change our flights to come home, as i must use the refunded money from the airline to pay for that otherwise i "will be getting a free flight" according to my case manager. 

That was annoying enough but to add to my frustrations, getting an answer to my claim took ages. Every single time i called my case manager, i was told she was "away from her desk" and would have to call me back, which made the process even longer. After opening a dispute when i was not happy with the result, i was told i would have an answer within 3 weeks, it took 5 with no update or anything. I found my case manager rude, unhelpful and condescending. 

All in all, after paying over $800 for travel insurance and then being left a further $800 out of pocket, it is safe to say i will never be using travel insurance direct ever ever again.

Requested this in writing that were were willing to cover me for another $3300 business class flight with another airline that flew direct to my destination, and they told me they would assess my claim and get back to me the day AFTER I was due to leave the country. In the end I just booked an economy flight because they could not be trusted. Surprise surprise, they didn't even contact me on the day they promised they would, but rather the next day asking if they could close the case?

title: Two separate bad experiences - Insurers will weasel out of everything if they can
body:
I have a Bank credit card overseas travel policy which is underwritten by Allianz; hence any claims are made on Allianz. I have made two separate claims:

1. My mother suddenly fell ill after booking a holiday and declined over about 6 months and then died. The illness was related to a pre-existing condition but the Doctor confirmed in writing that my mother was not expected to suddenly decline and die. Allianz rejected the claim on the basis that it was a pre-existing condition; life is a pre-existing condition! This was 2 years ago. The warning is that they will use anything like this to avoid a payout.

2. We booked a (very expensive!) overseas trip and had to cancel because of COVID border closures. The booking was before COVID was declared a pandemic. Allianz declined travel insurance as they only cover defined events and this was not defined. Again, beware of these sort of things before you buy their insurance.

The lesson for me is to be very careful about choosing travel insurance products. Allianz has many 'get out of jail clauses' but others may be just as had as well.

title: Great Except When You Want To Make A Claim
body:
I have used TID many times and like all other reviewers who have given high ratings their sales processes are helpful and easy to deal with however things change when you actually have to make a claim which i have had to recently do. I thought my case would be straightforward, (wife became ill just before the travel date), as we had to delay the trip by 10 days and while i could change some accommodation there were some non refundable costs.
The first thing is every email you send them you get an automated response stating "that we are receiving higher than normal volumes of claims", this has occurred on every message that i have sent them since submitting the claim back in July, (it is now mid Oct and i still have no idea when the claim will be resolved). Then it typically takes 2 - 3 weeks for them to actually get a response to you.
With my claim i submitted EVERY bit of information that had been requested including signed medical forms and original copies of the travel documents and "no refund" confirmations. Despite getting our GP to provide  2 years of medical history and getting the specialist to write a letter they now have asked for a whole lot of different information that was not requested on the claim form. TID confirmed that i had submitted everything that was required but gave some lame reason on why they needed the additional information, (which i still do not understand what it is), so they are now contacting the GP directly. What i thought would be a simple process has been incredibly frustrating and strung out, it appears that they are doing everything possible to delay or avoid paying the claim. I would not be writing this if i had not provided all the relevant and required documentation but i have done this. Once again their sales processes are well honed but absolutely terrible when it comes to make a claim, which is when you need them to be efficient. I will definitely NOT be using TID again.

October 16th 2018 Update: Follow Up To My Oct 13th Review

Just as follow up to my Oct 13th review, it has now been a month since i have had any feedback on the claim that i submitted back in July. I have sent follow ups asking for an update however i just get the same automated response that "Unfortunately we are experiencing higher than normal volumes of claims", which is the same message that i have received with every email since submitting the claim back in July. I cannot understand all these supposed reviewers that give 5 stars but haven't had to make a claim, seems a bit suspect to me especially when they all refer to the need for travel insurance and how cheap TID is.
I suggest that anyone wanting honest feedback read the reviews on the poor people who have had to, or are in the process of making a claim and take note of the 1 or 2 stars that are awarded. Also, where is the customer service person who responds to all the 5 star reviews on Product Review but fails to address those who rate them 1 or 2 stars.

I rang them two weeks after to follow up, that's when they decided to send me an email asking for additional information from my local gp.  I submitted and still waiting for the response.  My point is they could have asked this a week after I submitted the claim and not right after I follow up.  They have been my insurance since 2012, I didn't make any major claims, if you claim for like less than a $100 they will process it straight away and this is the first time that I have claimed for over a thousand dollars (less than $4,000) and the process is painfully slow.  I have to deal with loss of conversion rate (since I used my local card overseas) and now probably late payment fee and an interest because it will be due soon and I'm expecting the money to be reimbursed by them.  Oh and wait, if you try to ring their claims department be ready to wait for an hour before you can talk to someone.  At first I thought, they are just really busy but I have been ringing for the third time now and never even got a short waiting time.  You will really test the integrity of your insurance in situation like this.  It's time for me to switch to a new one I guess next time we travel.  I even refer them to a friend but she have used another insurance and I should have listened to her to try something else.  I will not recommend TID anymore as I'm sick and tired of hearing "sorry to keep you waiting, we will get back to you in a TID!"  I guess they are very quick in signing you up and getting your money but when you need them the most, out there somewhere and you will be more stress! Definitely frustrated customer now!  I have been a loyal customer for 6 years and now that I needed to really claim, they made me feel that my claim is not their priority as they are a very busy company!

title: Extreme slowness in their responses and claim with amount wrong calculated
body:
We acquired with my partner Medibank because he has been a client of the company for more than 10 years. We quote insurance to travel to Chile, Peru and Argentina. Everything went wrong when we wanted to open a case, and it turns out that Medibank does not have the option of local calls to any hub or centralization of calls like other insurance companies do. I had to ask a friend who was in Melbourne to call the company and ask them to call us back. We opened the case, and when we returned to Chile, we had another problem, we opened another case, and in the end, when we arrived in Australia, we needed to make our reimbursement of expenses. 
First, the email to make the claims, it does not work, we had to go to a local in the mall to ask how we could make the claim expeditiously because we had to attach the payment vouchers, once we did everything, then they say no! they must fill out this form and scan and send it, it took more than 2 weeks to respond. Then when they send us the payment, the letter has a refund of 0.60 cents (my case was opened for more than 800 Australian dollars that were equivalent, to the local Chilean and Peruvian currency). Trying to communicate with them is a nightmare, I was more than 45 min on the line and did not respond, I sent an email and that was not that to review a claim already open, which was another, I went through about 5 emails until I found who He had to answer me (curiously a partner of the insurer, not the same Medibank).

I have been waiting for you to respond to me since March 25 so that they recognize your mistake in calculating your payment because they have no idea what the exchange rate or value of the foreign currency is. 

What kind of professionals are behind this company?

 You have autoresponder emails that they will send in 2 more days, then in 10 more days and so on.

 More than 45 days have passed and they are not able to make a calculation correctly to pay what corresponds. I'm still waiting for some answer. 

 Never again contract Medibank, an insult to the high prices that they also manage in their plans. Service with little follow-up, poor call centres, and they do not have access to local calls in the country you are travelling, but if you are roaming, you will not have how to use the insurance. Bad experience.

Unfortunately she was subsequently diagnosed with cancer and within 6 weeks passed away. I followed the processes explained to me when I first inquired about the claims process including providing statements and medical records however these apparently weren't enough as my claims officer said to me "we need to determine if there was any signs of a pre-existing illness before we booked our trip so that we don't have to refund you as much". I found the absolute lack of compassion and understanding of what people are going through at such difficult times in their lives appalling. 

I have since had to provide additional medical records, I have sent various documents proving costs and refunds, only to be contacted weeks later asking for the same information again and again. I fail to understand how I can make the information any clearer to them. title: Insurance   HA!   who are they kidding?  Stay away.
body:
My husband and I were on a long trip in UK then Germany and Italy and paid over $1200 for our insurance with the Commbank.  We were travelling between hotels and decided to stop as it was too early to book into the next hotel.  There were people around and we parked between two other cars.  Long story short...left the car for 25 minutes and when we came back someone had broken in and stolen all of our suitcases which were out of sight in the boot of the car.  EVERYTHING....GONE.
We thought we were okay as we had paid for the insurance.  Reported it to the police in Italy and got all the documentation and pictures required.
Came back home to Brisbane and filled in all the documentation required by insurance.  Six weeks later we have been told that they can pay us 7% of the amount of the claim.   
Never...ever...will I use the Commonwealth Bank Insurance again.  No cover on any electrical items eg: laptop, satnav, i-pod or jewelry.  Any personal items eg: hearing aids, hairdryer, straighteners, toiletries a maximum of $500!!!  Absolutely ridiculous!!
Like a lot of you here I will be changing my bank.  We are going to put in a complaint but I really don't think it will get us anywhere when I read the online comments.
When you read the terms and conditions of the insurance one paragraph conflicts with another so that they can get out of paying you.  I believe its a scam.

title: Misleading product disclosure statement. Wouldn't cover telephone calls that cost me >$200.
body:
Medibank Travel Insurance Claim Number: 1133166
International telephone calls worth $222 to the Airlines prompted by the travel agent were a direct cost I had incurred as a result of my flights being delayed, which Medibank refused to cover as they mean "Additional Transport and Accomodation expenses" even though they specify unlimited cover for "Additional Expenses" in the table of benefits in the PDS. A statement such as unlimited cover for "Additional expenses? implies most expenses arising from these issues are covered. If it only covers ?Additional Transport and accommodation expenses?, then maybe that?s what you need to write in the table of benefits in your PDS document. When I sign up for a travel insurance policy, I expect to be covered for all reasonable expenses that will occur from an issue such as this, i.e. a flight delay. The whole point of getting travel insurance is for the peace of mind that an issue like this won?t affect my finances in a negative manner. Further to this, they said I should have read their PDS in detail before purchasing the policy, A 68 PAGE DOCUMENT! They asked me to escalate the matter to the Customer Relations Team on 1300 36 25 44. When you call the number, you go through the waiting process, and when it finally rings they cut the call. Extremely unhappy with the lengthy claims process involving multiple emails going back and forth. Wouldn't recommend insuring yourself with Medibank prior to travelling as the policy is quite misleading.

body:

I had unfortunate situation with injuring my healthy natural teeth on travel to Europe and I am waiting from September with no response on my claim from processing officer. I tried to contact him more than five times, and every time being on long hold I found same, he is sick or not working. I am wondering is he is part or full time employee? The other corresponding officers won't provide his supervisor name or phone numbers in order to avoid contact. If it happens that they reply, they ask always something new which sets you back on the beginning of the claim. They also expect that you will x-ray your healthy teeth prior your travel and provide the 'x-ray' for them and similar impossible things. When they allege that they contacted your dentist and you check it, you get the information that they didn't. And then they don't know who didn't/sent the queries. 
Any way this is only one minor claim, with one cumulative invoice/statement and proven record payment with Australian Visa card and could have been resolved in at least one month. 
This is reflection of their service
Obviously there is long list of misleading regular clients as shown on this site.

So far, we haven't needed to claim so we can't comment on that.

title: Felt safe in holding this - cheap cheap too!
body: The policy I received was good value! I did not need to lodge a claim but I would definitely be staying with this insurance company next time I travel! Thank you for making my trip secure

title: Pretty Bad
body: You get what you pay for. Injured my knee right before my trip, called up their emergency line to confirm if I was covered because the policy was kind of vague and my flight was going to leave before the daytime line opened, the guy that answered told me he didn't know and to read my policy.. real helpful, ended up getting a small amount paid out (about a third the cost of my flights) after a few months after getting the good old runaround with medical certificate 'not specific enough' etc.

title: Didn't use it but great peace of mind
body: Easy to set up and great to know we have the cover if anything went wrong (which thankfully it didn't!). Didn't use the customer support as didn't make a claim.  The cost of this policy was cheaper than through the travel agent.

title: Will never use them again!
body:
Our family has purchased insurance (gold ) through them many times. And first time we need to make a claim.
They are telling me the wrong insurance was purchased. I specifically purchased cruise insurance for my sons cruise. I made sure of that when getting quote online.  But told them that they were not covered on their cruise, it was wrong insurance.
i know thats not true, because its the first option you tick before entering any other details for a quote and i definitely chose cruise option.
Not happy.
Will not be using them again. 
I only yesterday purchased insurance from them for another upcoming trip and I'm regretting it now.

title: Covermore are an absolute disgrace!
body:
I had to write this review on behalf of my parents as im so disgusted in covermore insurance and i warn others about this experience. My parents recently booked a trip to Las Vegas through Flight Centre and covermore insurance. Unfortunately the trip had to be cancelled due to my father being diagnosed with cancer. You will find this hard to believe but covermore insurance have declined insurance for the trip. They gave my parents the run around for 5 months and then declined the claim due to what they believe may have been a previous condition!
I would stay clear of both flight centre and covermore as i see them both as a fraud!

title: My accident was painful - Covermore were painless!
body:
Whilst watersporting in Malaysia in August 2012, I  tore all three hamstring tendons off my hip bone - at the time i was told it was only a torn hamstring. My friends rang Covermore for me from Malaysia and spoke to someone straight away. All i wanted was some advice at the time ie. if i could fly directly after my accident or not / what was the best thing for me to do in my circumstance / what i would need to do to claim my expenses back when i returned home - the basic things you worry about when in a foreign country and are hurt severley. The man on the phone was great - told my friends some medical advice on how I should fly and explained what paperwork i needed to submit a claim when the time came. After surgery in Australia I was stuck at home, i put my travel insurance claim in via the internet and submitted photo's (taken from my iPhone) of the documentation Covermore required which was merely the receipts i had from the doctors / pharmacy in Malaysia. IT WAS THAT SIMPLE - within minutes i had filled out the online forms and submitted all the documentation. My claim was approved within 5 days and money deposited straight into my bank account. I would recommend Covermore to anyone travelling.
Inexpensive, Assistance Telephone Line, Online Easy to Claim Process

title: It?s a con. Don?t waste your money. Terrible service and no coverage.
body:
Unfortunately this company has been terrible. It?s taken them almost 3 months to process a small claim for a flat tyre on a car hire in Italy and decline the claim. All of the promotional material seems misleading when it comes to the crunch. I deliberately didn?t take excess insurance with the car hire, given I was lead Into believing I was covered by my travel insurances  
Slow, misleading, inaccurate. I?ll never take out cover with this brand again.

title: Don't expect Covermore to Refund Your Airlines Tickets in a Hurry
body:
We bought a holiday which we couldn't go on due to a medical emergency.  Upon submitting the Covermore Claim and all the documents including the breakdowns and the fare details, after 10 weeks the claim has still not been paid for the airline portion (almost $2500.00).  Apparently we must wait to see if the airline will refund the taxes before they will pay anything. They dont return calls and when you ring to speak with the complaint department you don't get there.

Nobody wants to be responsible to get a claim paid - ring someone else, ring an airline, ring a travel agent

title: Excellent to deal with online and on the phone.
body: Excellent value compared to all others we have used over the past 35 years. Extremely easy to set up online. A few minutes at most is all you need. Have spoken to Customer Service and I was highly satisfied with their help. All up I would recommend insure and go to everyone.

title: Didn't need to claim
body: It seemed OK, fairly easy to complete on line. We had medical conditions to be covered and this makers it all but impossible to compare-an area the industry needs to address. Didn't have to claim so impossible to rate on that basis and no need to use customer support.

title: Awesome price, deal and app
body: I highly recommend this travel insurance co for their service, friendliness, value for money on great deals and the fact that a request for a donation is made with each policy. It's humanitarian presence and policies are perfect fit!

title: Good cover until you actually make a claim
body:
I have travelled to a number of countries over 30 years and this was my first claim ever for travel insurance as I lost my phone at a club. This was the worst experience of trying to claim and took up alot of time in terms of emails back and forth and getting information from the Phillipines after I got back to Australia only for the claim to be rejected. 
If I was told certain things at the start of the claims process I wouldn't have bothered with all the exclusions on the account even for the extra coverage.
Just be aware that if you have alcohol in your system they will try to say that you were negligent or careless and this is a reason to not pay out. 
I wasn't able to get a police report as I was waiting to ensure my phone was in lost property and after being told that I could get a letter from management confirming this which took weeks after I was back from the Phillipines, the claim was rejected as this was one of the factors. 
Also not being able to tell them where I lost the phone was also negligent(If I knew where I lost the phone I wouldn't have lost it)
All in all poor outcome and service from the claims team as the phone was lost early in the night with details provided and claim was rejected. I have used this company a number of times but will look elsewhere from now on. Please read the PDS careful as there are a number of exclusions in the policy terms.

title: Great stuff great peace of mind
body:
Very easy to use. Targeted for our needs. very supportive and clear instructions before we departed  the informatoon provided was clear and essu to usr  we mew what to fo it we needed to claim  Great back up service after we arrived home  Great price. We are using TID again for our trip to Asia
Easy ans haste free
Nothing

title: On Line Process
body: Didn't need to make a claim but it was all very easy to choose and select on line.  I googled reviews first then compared different policies. I was still however drawn to a company name I recognised.

title: Good value and easy to purchase
body: While I didn't have to make a claim, the insurance was good value for money. When choosing travel insurance, i compare quotes. Allianz was competitive and, because it was easy to purchase and Allianz is a reputable, well-known brand, I went with Allianz.

title: Perfect Experience
body: I decided on 1 Travel as it was very comprehensive. What was covered was easy to understand what was included meet my needs. I am very happy with the customer service and the price was also very good.

title: Technical Problems on Mobile Site
body: Issues selecting my date of birth on the mobile site. Emailed Allianz to let them know that the site had a glitch and to update my policy. Allianze takes over a week to reply, asking for $26 to update my DOB despite explaining it was a technical glitch. Then had to wait another week, 3 emails and a threat to report their actions to ACCC before they updated my details. Added stress to my holiday for no reason

title: frustrating but satisified in the end
body: The policy seemed the best price wise around. Was easy to find details and get quote but site kept dropping out, 6 or 7 times while I was trying to finalize.

title: Travel Insurance you can count on!!
body: Never imagined that I would actually need to use travel insurance, but I knew I couldn't leave Australia without one. I had a toe injury over in America recently and called up the international number to get advice on what to do. I was told by a lovely woman by the name of Carol to go to the ER or see a GP and that I would have to pay the fee (obviously) and that a claim would be processed once all the doctors report and receipts were given. $500USD later, I put a claim through and the following day I receieved a phone call from Carol genuinely asking how I was. I told her what had happened and she told me she was taking care of my claim and that the amount in AU would be in my account in 5-7 days. She was fantastic, I highly recommend 1Cover and I will definitely be using them when I travel again.

title: Great cover and value
body: Policy was easy to setup, good value and offered great coverage for existing conditions. No other insurer would cover my existing medical conditions but it was no problem with Suresave.

title: Great reliable cover and service
body: I have been using 1 Cover for travel insurance for many years. It is easy to setup via the website or over the phone, providing friendly and customer service. 1 Cover is also the cheapest when compared to other insurance companies providing value for money. I would highly recommend them.

title: Making a Claim
body:
I have been using TID for some years now I have recommended them to several people and to a lot of family. We usually travel 3 times a year I never get a quote from any body else go straight to TID.
But for the first time I had to make a claim we travelled to Bali and I lost my Opitacal Sunglasses which cost me near on$1,000. I put the claim in it took some time to get back that sorry you claim is unsuccessful and we can't make a claim for them. The reason being I was at my hotel swimming and they were not on me and that is classed as a public place!! Tell me when u go on holidays and u catch taxis go shopping and stay around your hotel swimming apparently your not covered.
I think this is outrageous what do we pay insurance for!!  
I work at the Perth International Airport and have been there for 25 years I have dealt with so many customers in the departure lounge asking me that they have forgotten to do travel insurance and I have said it's not to late get on your phone and take out insurance with TID it's always the best price but never again will I recommend or use this company again.

Donna
Perth.

title: Worst Insurance Company I've ever dealt with
body: One month before my 12 month waiting period was over, doctors found an abnormal growth that had to be removed. Doctors advised that I had to get it done as soon as possible so that the growth would not turn cancerous. We paid for the procedure up front in hopes that Allianz would cover us. 5 months later and numerous calls (all with a hold time of 30 minutes or more) and constant emails asking for more documentation and we still have no resolution. To top it off every time we call the notes on our file are never accurate. I'm a medical student with a child and money is tight and I'd like my claim to be paid. This has been by far the worst experience I've ever had with any company. I'm flabbergasted at the amount of stress and incompetence I have encountered. I would NEVER recommend this company to anyone I know.

title: Professional. Responsive. Easy
body: Good value cover, responsive to questions and reasonable on claim process calculations. I have used this company a few times now and highly recommend them for any travel insurance needs.

title: First time user
body: First time user. Found site user friendly, quick and easy to obtain quote and make purchase.  Information set out well so easy to understand what we were purchasing and to compare for value.  Wish I'd known could have used Seniors card for discount though.  Haven't been on trip yet so can't comment on claims process and hope to need to either.

title: Well done!
body: Our policy was very good as it covers everything I needed. I felt secure knowing that what ever happens, I know that Allianz will cover my needs. It gave a relax feelings knowing that I am covered. The policy was very easy to set up.

title: Great safety net

body: This travel insurance company has been dreadful. They never resolve anything. I dealt with probably 5 different people whilst trying to lodge my claim. They have a call centre and they never return your calls or emails - just promises! I submitted my claim on the 26/3/2020 and I'm still waiting to hear from them (2 months so far).

I have never had an issue with the services provided and staff are always eager to assist.

Would recommend everybody to use 1cover. 
Since the day I lodged my claim it only took a few days to resolve and money was back in my account.
