body: Hard to review insurance when I didn't have to make a claim, but Online was easy to understand and to purchase, so I guess they are okay. The crunch always comes if you have to claim, and luckily I didn't.

title: Disgusting way to treat Customers
body:
I have taken out travel insurance policies on a number of occassion with Insure and Go and have found them quite good to deal with UP UNTIL NOW. I purchased a GOLD policy which included cruising and with the current situatuion of COVID-19 and the Government imposed travel ban my husband and I are in the same position as others not being able to travel. It's not like we wanted to cancel but it was forced upon us due to the current world situation as everybody knows. I called Insure and Go for a change of dates for our policy but like everyone else they used the 14 day cooling off period in not being able to change the dates or offer a credit to be used at a later date, let alone a refund.  This company has no heart look at all the airlines, hotels, cruise compainies, Flight Centre and YES other travel insurance companies offering refunds or change of dates on policies not used. I have not lodged a claim and have now paid for a policy that is of no use, as a customer I have paid for a service that is not being supplied!!!
INSURE and GO WAKE UP you are going down a good path of loosing an enormous amount of customers. Just read all the BAD reviews on social media, all the complaints in writing to you, all the complaints on this website PRODUCT REVIEW, as well as on your own website. 
I have lodged a complaint on the Insure and Go website but after reading the reviews I won't be holding my breath for a reply.
HAVE A HEART INSURE and GO look after your customers

June 27th 2018 Update: Great experience no worries

body: We had a claim on our car rental for a vehicle we rented for 17 days.  Unfortunately, as we found out after our claim was rejected, the insurance only applies for car rentals of 15 days or less.  So, our claim was not paid.  Very disappointing.

body: The amount was almost irrelevant to this case, but the outcome of this complaint was ridiculous. Excess term was not well explained to me during the purchase of travel insurance. customer support were very helpful when i asked for clarity of the cover - One Trip Cruise Asia vs One Trip Asia and option tours coverage ie: Vesper, tuk tuk

title: Very happy with the level of service
body: The policy is very easy to set up and good value. I was pleasantly surprised to get a reminder toward the end of my holiday to extend my cover if I was going to be away for longer than originally planned.

title: Good valve for money, easy online form to use

We haven't needed to make a claim but I know that if something did go wrong and needed help I trust that TID would be there for us. The policy was so easy to set up using the online form, with confirmation taking only a few minutes to come through. All questions/concerns were answered very quickly and in easy to understand policy language.

title: Repairs paid for
body:
Hi All. I was recommended Cover-More by a friend who travels frequently (lucky bugger) and took his advice and used Cover-More. I had to make a claim when my 2 surfboards were damaged on the the way back from my trip and after I submitted all the relevant info they required, my claim was dealt with swiftly. They responded to all of my emails and I can highly recommend Cover-More to all who travel. I'm heading to Hawaii soon and will most definitely grabbing another policy from Cover-More.
Happy customer,  
KENNY

title: Great service!
body:
I have just had our claim processed after being delayed in New York due to Hurricane Sandy and I have been delighted by the service that I have received. The communication throughout the process was excellent and the result was positive and fair. I would definitely use TID again and will recommend it to my friends.
Efficient and inexpensive

title: Read the 92 pages of the PDS prior to taking out the insurance.
body: First and last time. We had gold card insurance and could have used it, but were informed by our travel agent that we should insure with this company as they were reliable. She never bothered to tell us that flight cancellation cover was very limited to six situations. If the airline decides to cancel a flight you may well be left with no compensation from Sure Save. Our early morning flight from Palma to Barcelona was cancelled without any prior notice so we missed connecting flights to Singapore and Brisbane.  We were forced to fly to Barcelona late in the day at our expense and spend two nights at a hotel and pay for new flights to Australia. Veuling airline refused to provide a reason for the flight cancellation and the insurer refuses to process our claim until such time as they do. As stated above they will only pay if one of the following six situations is triggered :  1 Severe weather  2 Accidents  3 Riot Civil Strike or Commotion 4 Airport Closure 5 Emergency Landing   6 Flight Cancelled because of Insufficient Numbers. I have precised some of tha above.  You will see there are a thousand reasons why the company WONT pay so be very careful.

title: Excellent Service
body: The process was hassle free and very clear. Customer service personnel were very helpful and supportive in the complete process.We were very happy and satisfied with the service provided to us.

title: Great to know we were covered for any emergency
body: Policy was good value and very easy to setup. Have bought many policies and have had no trouble with setup or claims. Didn't need customer support but good to know it was there.

title: helpful staff, easy claim process
body:
1cover staff were very helpful over the phone, researched nearest hospital for me, than their doctor called to give some advices as well, and they followed up on my son's condition every couple of days. 
Felt supported whilst being on an isolated island in Thailand

title: Great service
body:
After many trips having used TiD, I finally had to make a claim.  I was somewhat worried, given that insurance claims can often be painful, drawn out processes, but TiD were responsive, provided easy to understand information, and the claim was resolved very quickly.  They were professional, courteous and quick.  I'd recommend them to all.
Easy, efficient, quick

title: Great value
body: Havent made a claim but great value cover. We have used for many years. We have also recommended to lots of friends.

title: Competitive rates
body: I felt the policy was good value. When choosing travel insurance, I normally scout for the best value and yes, the policy was easy to setup. I did everything online. Didn't have to engage Customer Support so can't rate them.

title: Wouldn't it be nice...if everyone looked after their customers like this
body:
The cruise was fantastic until my son was literally struck down with with Influenza A on day 12, quarrantined to cabin and sicker than when he had Swine flu. Three doctor visits, 4 lots of meds, 2 episodes of projectile vomiting and 1 complete cabin decontimation later I struggled to transport an exhausted and unwell boy home. Once he was recovered I completed the online claim form, scanned and sent my receipts and the rest was easy. All expenses refunded in record time no problems at all. Brilliant!
Very reasonable cost of coverage, fast and easy claim process, no stress and no delays or arguements.

title: highly recommended
body: it was very good value and very easy to step customer service was excellent . Thank God I didn't have to use it on my trip. but i'm sure i would've had a problem

title: Peace of mind
body: Very easy to purchase online. Have used Allianz travel insurance for the last 4 trips. Haven?t needed to claim so can?t comment on that. Was able to save my quote and go back to it which was great.

title: Excellent Coverage and Help
body: I have used this company 3 times. I have not made any claims.  They are easy to communicate with and go out of their way to help in any circumstance. The staff are friendly and easily understood. When they promise to ring back at a certain time, they do. The documentation is clear and concise. Pre and post communication is appreciated.

title: Didn't have me covered when I needed it.
body: We have used 1 Cover in the past and never needed to make a claim until now. We were broken into while staying with family in Zambia. All of our cash was stolen during the night, from our room, while my husband, our two young kids and myself slept. When we woke the next morning and made the call,  the lady told us "not to worry as we were covered for theft of cash". We spent days chasing up the police report so that we could make the claim when we got home. We even had to pay for the police report. Turns out we weren't covered as the money wasn't physically on us at the time of the theft. Say what?!? And please check if your policy covers you for airline insolvency. Lots do, but not 1 Cover. We were sweating thinking SAA was going to collapse and leave us out of pocket with our airline tickets.

title: Ridiculous claim details
body:
Not happy as was asked to provide proof that luggage belongs to me. 
If i borrow luggage from a friend, i would not be able to claim. Ridiculous request.  
None of the customer service staff bothers to call and my claim request is ?resolved? or rejected.

title: Piece of mind in Bali
body: Policy was good value and was very easy to set up to have that piece of mind while travelling in Bali. Have used Allianz previously and will probably use again.

title: Was good to have peace of mind
body: Was good to know we had it as there was a possibility of flights being cancelled. Was also good when we did our adventure activities incase something happened

title: It seems good value for money.
body: Relatively easy to set up online, and clarified on the phone. Contact was prompt. Being seniors, we are happy to have a policy. This is our second time using 'Insure and Go' therefore received a discount which is much appreciated. It is reassuring to know that we are covered.

title: We go nowhere without TID travel insurance
body:
Policy great value very easy to set up very lucky in the sense we haven't had to use customer support confident that support is there if needed
We recommend this company

title: Easy to apply and value for money
body: Although a claim was not needed I felt the coverage was comprehensive and it was comparatively great value for money. I have utilised TID for my past 3 overseas trips and will be using them again for all my future travels.

title: 4 months later, still waiting
body:
A group of friends had planned on going overseas but due to the Ash Cloud in June, it didn't happen. Flights were cancelled, trip was over so we began the arduous task of trying to get our money back from Covermore. 
Everything has been covered, the issue is mysterious lost emails, the repetition of wanting our details and a general slack, unprofessional attitude of the staff dealing with our claims. They have not only lost our business, but the business of all friends and relatives we have discussed our story to. Disgusting excuse for an insurance company, they should be deregistered.
Full coverage for our trip
4 months later and still waiting for money, mysteriously continue to lose our claims.

title: Absolutely excellent service and great cover in an emergency overseas
body:
Allianz is our travel insurer through a HSBC Platinum credit card. In May whilst travelling in Thailand with my husband I was taken by ambulance and hospitalised for 4 days for a bad bacterial infection.  
Allianz handled the claim quickly  (4 days and this included a weekend) and arranged payment for the hospital in full (after $200 excess) They provided medical telephone assistance by a registered health professional . They kept in contact through what could have been a very much more stressful experience. I could not fault them.
They covered the medication and everything.
I could not have hoped for better coverage or service.

title: covermore is the best travel insurance
body:
i wouldnt be without covermore travel insurance,they are an excellent insurer, i had a fall last year in Bali and when i contacted covermore in relation to my accident they organised every thing i didnt have the worry all my medical bills were taken care of and the staff are very caring and professional, excellent  sevice from a company you can totally trust.
totally reliable, inexpensive

title: Good marketing bad when it comes to claiming
body: I've registered twice with TID. Reading through all the T&C's. This time round it came to lodging a claim and they proved to be very difficult. They came back and forth to me several times requesting more and more documents that didn't have any relevance to the claim. They requested I obtain a writing letter from my cousin to confirm the stay and my uncle had cancer so I didn't think it would be best. Still this was not taken into consideration and they wanted me to get the letter. There is no empathy. Not happy with service, will be using a different company for my next trip.

title: Easy to use online purchase
body: I have used Insure and go a number of times, maybe a half dozen times. I have precasting medical conditions which the online sales site processed quickly and efficiently.

title: Highly Recommended
body: Easy to obtain a quote, easy and fast payment, user friendly site, easy to claim when needed to in the past.

title: Very happy with CoverMore
body: You MUST read the PDS and try to understand it. It is difficult to imagine every scenario but the two times over past years that I've had to make a claim I've been very happy with the outcome. I had no issue regarding reimbursement after lodging the claims - both were for medical issues - nothing pre-existing. I was a bit anxious at times when having to deal with different CoverMore staff to bring them up to speed during discussions while I was overseas, but I think half of this was because of different time zones and different staff rostered on. I will continue to use them for further overseas trips.

title: My personal experience with Cover More Insurance.
body:
My husband and myself, both aged pensioners, love to cruise and enjoy our special time together. As we have cruised several times,both in the south pacific and asia. We would never leave home without Travel Insurance. We have tried others but when it came to the crunch, Cover More far exceeded our expecations. To endure the pain of any medical problem was nothing to be pleased about.  However, returning home, and after contacting our travel agent and finding out how to go about making a claim, this made everything so simple for me.  I completed the form lodged the claim, a short time later I was contacted by Cover More to advise me that the claim has been accepted.  This was very pleasing news for me and my husband.  I believe that Cover More go the extra mile for their customers, in my case they did for me. We will always consider Cover More for our future travel insurance
The efficient manner in which my claim was dealt with, accepted by them, and refunded to me in full.

title: Fantastic Service
body: Thank you so much, I use 1Cover all the time - great rates! -  and have never claimed until my last trip to NZ.  Unfortunately I had a urgent call to get home sooner from WA as a family member wasn't expected to last.  In all my distress and sobbing I changed my flights and forgot to call 1Cover. Its not recommended but they still understood!  Thank you so much the extra expense was refunded into my bank account, no problems!

title: didn't need it but knew I had it
body: This time haven't had to use customer support, thank goodness! Otherwise it means that something went wrong!  But always good to have.  We usually buy an annual policy but unfortunately the premiums have gone up a fair bit (I assume due to the ongoing issues in Bali).  Still a good policy (from someone who works in the industry) - we are scuba divers so are able to get coverage for diving - which is very useful.

title: Prices are good, cover is comprehensive
body:

The reason that I took out cover is that it is underwritten by Lloyds. However, all this counts for nothing. 1Cover has my $568, they are happy, but I am not! Surely, 1Cover has an obligation to those who took out insurance before the event. I was to leave this coming Saturday, but I can't travel without insurance cover and I now can't buy cover. title: Misleading Policy booklet!!!  So called PDS policies,even the Cover More team cannot agree!
body:
Took out an insurance policy with Cover- More with extra ?Cruise Cover?. Will never purchase travel insurance with Cover-More again, and extra for Cruise Cover is a joke. 
We went on a cruise to Fiji and due to a cyclone missed the Prebooked Port of Lautoka and Suva.

In the policy booklet it says (v) Missed Port
If during the period of insurance you are on a journey from or to Australia and due to an unforseeable circumstance outside of your control you miss

a) your Prebooked Port; or

b) Your prebooked connection, where you have allowed the minimum connection time between transport as stipulated by your transport provider.
You can claim. 
Now if you refer to section a) your Prebooked Port; or 

What does the word OR mean??  It mean either this happens OR that happens!!

First person I spoke to at Cover More said yes I can make a claim, to get in touch with the cruise line and retrieve a letter telling Cover More of missed ports. 
I did this and rang back Cover More to be told aggressively  ?no you cannot claim for this only if you have section a) AND b) as above.? Now apparently the? word? is AND not OR
I said ? well the person I spoke to last week said the opposite,? and I asked to speak to the manager. I then spoke to the team leader who assured me that I had been given the wrong information from the first advisor, and he would look into it and ring me back.
I have received no phone call or further information about my claim. I have tried to ring today and got put on hold for so long I gave up.
Customer service is BAD. They need to reword their PDS because it is MISLEADING. 
I wasted my time getting in touch with the cruise line for a letter for missed ports, and not to mention that the cruise line went out of their way to do this on the request of Cover More. 
Poorly organised customer service, and even the Cover More team cannot agree on their so called PDS policies.

title: Nil contact whatsoever!
body:
We purchased our travel insurance for our USA/Canada trip of our dreams in November last year before setting off on March 1st. We were of course hit by the Covid-19 train and upon the Australian Government urging all travellers to return home and all destinations listed as DO NOT TRAVEL we made immediate arrangements to return to Sydney from Montr‚al. I immediately contacted I&G who sent through the relevant form and told me I had to claim after we returned. I also specifically sought clarification by follow up email that we would be covered in the circumstances. I received a prompt reply from a senior claims officer that all locations gazetted DO NOT TRAVEL would be covered. We were currently in Canada and our return flight was from Boston, USA. The border was closed and both the country we were in and the country we had to get to were DO NOT TRAVEL destinations.

I submitted the claim after we returned and after it was lost in the black hole, I got the lovely news that it was declined. Reasons cited were the circumstances were not covered in the PDS (but it was an unprecedented event and not specifically excluded), and also they declined it as we went to a DO NOT TRAVEL location which was declared almost a week after we arrived there! WE ALSO had to get back into the USA to return home which also wasn't possible.

I submitted the complaint of the outcome on May 7th and to date still haven't heard anything whatsoever from them. I have called each week and sent follow up emails, on several occasions promised a call back from the Internal Dispute Resolution Team the same day! This was all despite their complaint auto reply saying I will hear from them within 14 business days. 

So on 22nd June, I lodged a complaint with the AFCA who gave the insurer until 24th July to contact either them or me. Again I still haven't heard a thing.

This company is a complete joke and there is only so long you can continually cite inundation by the pandemic as reasoning to completely ignore a customer for months. It also doesn't fill me with confidence that the underwriting Japanese company has no contact details.

title: Travelling Partner
body:
Travelled to Thailand with my boyfriend in Jan 2013. Boyfriend was covered by a different insurance policy through his work. He got extremely sick and I incurred extra costs in order to fulfill my role as his carer (including changing flights, paying extra accommodation, making phone calls etc). I read the PDS and believed that these extra costs that I had to incur were covered under s3 (1)(a)- additional expenses that resulted from "You being unable to continue the trip because of the sudden illness of... your travelling partner". Travelling party was defined in the glossary as being "...any travelling companion who has made arrangements to accompany you for at least 50% of the trip."

TID said that I would not be successful in my claim because my boyfriend (who i spend 100% of the trip with) was not listed on my insurance policy. I argued that nowhere in the PDS (certainly not in the definition of 'travelling partner') does it say that the travelling partner has to be listed on the same policy.

TID told me that it was a matter to be resolved by my boyfriend's insurance company, but his insurance company said that it should 100% be covered under my policy with TID.

1st Major issue: I did not appreciate being told information that is completely non-existent in the TID PDS. If a travelling partner is strictly defined as being someone listed on my policy, then why is this not specified under the definition? 

2nd Major issue: If i was wrong, why not explain clearly and specifically why i cannot claim? Just plainly and unsympathetically dismissing my claim and hand-balling it to someone else is not great customer service.

title: Not happy
body: My hubby and I took out your Gold Policy in August 2019 for our upcoming UK/European trip in May. As a result of CV19, I contacted Insure & Go on Friday 13th March 2020, went through all the automated prompts only to get a recorded voice telling me that "due to the high volume of calls...blah, blah,blah, one of our operators will return your call ASAP", no return call....roll forward to Monday 16th, same thing, still no return call...today, March 19th I finally hit pay dirt & got through and spoke to one of their customer service people to see whether we could move our policy to a later date as our airline is offering a 12 month full credit on our fares. Seems I was a day late & a dollar short because as of 8.00 am 18th March, Insure & Go will not move the dates of our coverage, nor will they give a refund. Am now hundreds of dollars out of pocket, this needs to be addressed by the ACCC or someone in authority, the travel insurance companies must be rubbing their hands together in delight at the easy money they have made off the policy holders. We have always used Insure & Go for our trips, but no more, we're done.

title: Nastiest Customer Service experience ever
body:
It wasn't cheap but it sure was nasty. I had been warned off Allianz previously but you don't expect the worst to happen so that was, admittedly, my mistake. When it does, however, you don't want to have to fight to make a claim. Beginning with their useless claim portal that cannot save more than a few pages of plain type. How anyone could be expected to get multiple page, densely printed medical reports uploaded is beyond me. I certainly couldn't and I work in IT. After much backwards and forwards and far too many emails, while fully expected for a complex claim, when Allianz continuously 'lose' your documents and you are submitting the same documents, over and over, you start to suspect they don't really want to remedy the situation as per their legally binding agreement. My presumption is Allianz deliberately make proceeding claims too painful for most people to complete the process. Either that or their staff hate them so much they can't be bothered following procedures and/or Allianz management do not have appropriate training in place. Either way my experience with Allianz insurance was a very disappointing experience all round, from the claim process to the resultant payout.
I will never insure anything with Alianz again and I warn off anyone else who will listen, too.

My only complaint (It could be the way they all do it anyway) is that I had to pay for a complete new policy to cover the amended trip even though it was deferred from the first trip and not a cancellation. title: Highlights of the Allianz Travel Insurance Experience
body:
Apalling service and support while sick overseas.
 I got ill on first day of a 5 week holiday in Europe. I flew out a week ahead of my wife to do a trek, so i was alone.
At first suspected food poisoning but after GP consults and trip to hospital, had emergency surgery in France to remove gangrenous gall bladder. 
"Highlights" of my Allianz experience were:
The 24/7 emergency telno on my insurance certificate was a disconnected number. My wife in Australia found new number for me. I advised I was unwell and told to go to GP/hospital - no suggestions offered. In great pain it took me a day of trains, buses and cars to eventually find a hospital that could help.
I contacted Allianz to advise hospitalisation -Told I may not be covered. Rang Allianz when about to go to op theatre. Told they may not cover me for surgery
My wife rang Allianz when she found out I was in surgery. Allianz would not talk to her even though she was emergency contact on the policy.
Allianz took 8 days before they advised I would be covered. In the meantime they had me chasing faxes and emails that had never been received by the intended recipients - And I"M now certain were never sent by ALLIANZ - all from my hospital bed in rural France. It was a 24hr job and just as stressful as the surgery.
I phoned Allianz 30 times from my hospital bed in France over 8 days trying to meet their requirements and expedite their stalled communications with my GP in Sydney and the hospital admin. Each time you must go though 3 Auto promps followed by music on hold for up to 10 mins - on the "Emergency line".
If you try to pin them down by sending emails, all you receive is a no-reply response saying they will respond in 72 hours - not that they ever did.
Allianz systems were down on and off for 3 days days so often Allianz couldn't trace my case notes.
Allianz said they would not fly me home after discharge from hospital. - that I could catch my scheduled flight in 4 weeks. It was only the intervention of my French surgeon, the night before I was due to be discharged that got them to fly me back the following day.
Even after Allianz eventually agreed to cover me, they couldn't organise the guarantee of payment to the hospital prior to my discharge. Hospital will send me the bill.
No one from allianz ever rang to ask how I was. When a nurse did ring me in post-op, she just wanted to go through pre-existing illnesses. They only ever wanted me to do something to meet their requirements.
My assessment: My experience with Allianz was of wilful disregard for my condition; unrelenting demands for me to chase up their communications problems and unreliable internal systems. The consistency of my difficulty dealing with the company suggests a deep cultural deficiency in the organistion. 
I plan to report my experience to Insurance Ombudsman. Yet to claim.

title: Travel Insurance Claims Warning - Dont usr Cover-more.
body:
Travel Insurance Claims Warning.
Don't ever take out travel insurance with either Cover-more.
Cover-more's modis operandi is to delay claims for as long as possible. They only communicate by email with all responses taking 14 days or longer. My wife badly broke her leg in Japan & we needed assistance to fly back to Australia (wheel chair & flight upgrade). Despite numerous phone calls/emails (20+) to the emergency call centre (MAFRE - in the Phillipines) we were unable to get much or any assistance at all. They could not even organise a wheel chair & everytime we sort assistance from them they always had to refer the matter back to their "management team" - this was very time consuming & it just seemed to be a delaying tactic. We only got any help at all once we got angry. In the end, I had to tell the call centre to stop ringing me unless they were going to give us support - they were only making the situation worse. Luckily we had sufficient resources ourselves to pay for the extra expenses upfront ($7,000) & we were able to organise the trip back to Australia. It actually got much easier once Insure & Go stopped helping us. We eventually got re-imbursed from them 12 working days after our claim was lodged although we had to ring them up a couple of times & eventually asked to speak to a supervisor (in Australia) before our claim got any traction. If you are going to insure with this company, make sure you have the financial resources yourself to get home in an emergency because you are in for a long wait if you are relying on them to get you home.

title: GOOD TO HAVE
body: Have done the Cruise in The South Pacific and the latest was the Trip to Cambodia.I hope to use the Insurance Company again in the future.

title: Flight Cancellation - expenses not covered
body:
Our family holiday recently got off to a bad start thanks to a mechanical failure of a Virgin Airlines plane that was to fly us between Brisbane and Queenstown NZ. We sat on the tarmac for 90 minutes before being informed that the flight was cancelled (due to a mechanical issue) and that the earliest we would be travelling was the following day. I mistakenly thought that this type of event would be covered by any reasonable travel insurance provider - how wrong can you be. It seems reasonable that our pre-arranged acommodation and hire car costs (for the day that we were to travel) plus additional taxi fares to return us home and back to the airport again the following day would be covered - not with Cover-More. It seems the only situation that cancellation costs associated with a cancelled flight will be covered is when there is a strike. Airlines don't and won't cover this event, silly me thought our travel insurance would. So we are $500+ out of pocket for expenses and Cover-More are happy to accept their premium and have no concern about NOT covering this totally unavoidable event. Will I use Cover-More travel insurance ever again - I think you know the answer already - NO!
Affordable
Cover is not worth having. Learnt the hard way!

body:

title: They don't honour their quotes.
body:

Once I asked the question I had to wait for an answer before proceeding further.

After 36 hours and no reply to my question I logged on again and found that the price had gone up to $500. 

Calling TID on the phone I was advised that they had changed underwriters overnight and my quote was no longer valid. I was offered a $50 discount however that was still $100 dearer than the quote I had received 36 hours earlier. While the lady on the phone was understanding of the situation  she could not do anything.

She provided a email address for me to send my complaint. 3 days later I have still heard nothing.

I have moved on and booked with 1Cover direct Insurance, much more seamless, honest and easier to deal with.

They do not honour their quotes, and do not respond to email questions , certainly not in a timely mannerer

title: Why Bother with Medibank Travel Insurance?
body:
Our Travel Agent asked about insurance and as a long term Medibank Medical Insurance customer, I chose them for our travel insurance. That was Mistake Number 1! We took insurance initially to cover our travel, as we had a daughter with stage 4 Bowel Cancer. We thought a short cruise would be a good break from supporting her and her young family during her illness for nearly 5 years. It became obvious that she was in her last stage of life so we had to make the decision to cancel the Cruise. She passed away shortly after. I phoned about making a claim about the lost deposit and was told that her illness was pre existing and therefore nothing was covered. We were able to rebook the cruise (thanks to our very helpful travel agent). At this point we decided to have a few extra days in Sydney, pre and post the cruise. We live in Brisbane. So we booked airfares, accommodation in Sydney. I called medibank and paid to extend our travel insurance beyond the cruise. Sadly we received an email from Royal Carribean CL yesterday that the Radiance of the Seas (Cruise Liner) needed immediate repair and the cruise was cancelled! Let me say (at this stage!) that Royal Carribean have been very good. However on contacting Medibank Travel Insurance Customer Relations, we are not covered for the pre or post components of our travel as breakdowns to ships are not covered. The Customer Relations person who told me that the flights and accommodation were not covered, did however say that we could put in a claim!! 
Why bother? 
Guess I'll ask more questions next time, never insure with Medibank Travel Insurance again, and question why I actually have my health insurance with Medibank. Maybe this company is just another "couldn't care less bank!"

title: More like cover less
body:
Firstly I was not informed about an excess fee by the travel agent and when making a claim for  glasses I lost and subsequently purchased overseas covermore did not pay the full amount that I paid overseas despite having a proper receipt. 

Further I was required to submit a receipt from my optometrist here which I was lucky to be re-issued with, Covermore paid the difference only after taking out the excess fee. I also saw a g.p and purchased antibiotics -again validated with legitimate receipts-and I had to put in a separate claim. This claim was rejected as it was less than the excess fee and that would mean I would have to pay them the difference.

Excess fee not disclosed at the beginning that you do have to read all the fine print, communication was by email only (they never rang me) and the red tape involved despite having legitimate receipts; albeit from overseas but still legitimate

title: We eventually got something, but...!
body:
We purchased insurance with Cover-More via FlightCentre.  Trip was in 2nd Quarter of 2013, supposed to be for three months.  Just before leaving the US for South America (the last month - and a long-term dream) - wife got sick, followed shortly by me catching the same appalling bug.  We were declared unfit for travel by doctors in Los Angeles.  Weakened and unable to continue, we travelled home as soon as we were able.  It was not sensible to go to a remote location, as planned, in a country where we didn't speak the language, and perhaps infecting other travellers (etc, etc).  On our return, we put a claim in for our costs.  
First - they lost the claim.  Then - they lost the paperwork - again.  On the third try - and thanks entirely to the lovely lass at FlightCentre Tuggeranong, who was embarrassed she'd sold us this insurance - we began to get some results.  
As others have reported - they treated each item (almost) as a separate claim.  Then they kept asking for 'more information' - 'info already supplied! Twice!! - certified copies!!!'  
We did get the bulk of what was owed to us.  But it took a long time - and I reiterate - without the assistance and determination of one staff member (and her boss) at FlightCentre Tuggeranong - we'd have been out of pocket about $10K+.  
We did not - as far as I can determine, through the forest-of-white - get everything we should have done.  That we got anything at all - almost entirely due to FlightCentre Tuggeranong.  

NOT recommended.

PS - apparently Cover-More is part of a giant US insurance mob - one can buy insurance elsewhere and still be dealing with pretty much the same organisation or organisational culture.

title: An interesting scenario which Covermore approved
body: I have been with Covermore for years now. Most recently my team was held up on the Kokoda Trail in PNG and demanded 700 Kina by landowners as blackmail. title: Added stress when dealing with cancer + 2 errors on their part.
body:
We were happy to pay a bit extra for Covermore insurance as we felt it had good cover and if we needed to make a claim we would be dealing with a known and professional company. 

Unfortunately we did need to make a claim due to me being diagnosed with breast cancer and needing to cancel our much awaited Thailand holiday. Cancelling is hard enough, but the claims process was ridiculously lengthy and I felt like they are trying to find anyway out of the liability possible. If a doctor gives a report with attached pathology report saying cancer and has filled out the claim form that should be enough. But no - we had to get the same information from other doctors involved and make the process extra long. 

Then after another phone call from me - (there were many on my part) It was revealed that the other report we were waiting for had been received but then my claim had been misfiled! "Oh, because this is our error we will fast track this secondary review for you. It should be looked at today or tomorrow". I called two weeks later to be told the payment was being processed - I had not received any notification of this. When I queried when I would see it or notification they sent through an email about the payment. I was still on the line so opened the file to find it was the wrong amount. "It's because of your excess" and yes, I hadn't factored that in but it still didn't seem right. On insisting that the consultant stay on the line whilst I checked I discovered they had not refunded one of our flights - on checking the form it was definitely listed - it had just been left off completely. So we had to wait again for the final payment.

No one likes to cancel a holiday - especially due to cancer. Covermore made a very stressful situation so much worse - we should have felt like that was one less thing to deal with/worry about but they only added to the burden.

title: Worse Travel Insurance - Keeps delaying claims, rude, and won't pay for honest claims
body:
With my daughter traveling around UK and Europe on her own it took me a long time to select a travel insurance that would ensure she was cover, being covered by alliance I was sure this company would be respectable.  How wrong could I be.

My daughter was staying at a Hostel in Wales, she left her personal belongings out of sight under her bed.  The next day she found that her camera had been stolen overnight.  She did all the right things by contacting the reception, calling the police and obtaining a police report.  I had to console my daughter over the phone as this camera is the reason why she is traveling.  She had saved for years for this trip and camera.  I reassured her over the phone that it would be ok and that is why we purchased Travel Insurance.  

How wrong can a mother be, this company refuses to pay based on "she left her camera in a public place".  After asking the same questions 3 times - yes having to wait 10 working days each time, this is the answer they came back with.  I then disputed the claim in which I had to wait another 5 working days (which actually took them 6) to say that her bed is a public place.  Well I don't know about you, but calling my 18 year olds bed a public place is beyond a joke.  How dare they call my daughters bed a public place.  

They have been beyond rude on the phone, have only had one nice lady talk to me and said she also found it quite unusual to call a bed a public place.  

I would be very careful if you think you will be covered by this insurance company if you lose or have an item stolen as they class everything as a public place and that is how they get out of paying.  I would agree with them if she had been careless and left her belongings in the common area, but this is where she slept.  She has not only been violated by someone taking something where she slept but also by 1Cover Travel Insurance, which seriously is not worth anything. 

For those that have written good reviews on this company, thank god you have not had to claim.  I had called them before taking this claim and they had assured me this camera would be covered, it's the only reason why we purchased this insurance.  

for anyone that is in the same boat as me, I will be taking this to the FOS, the more people that complain the better, we need to put a stop to companies such as these that take advantage over people.  It's no wonder why people do not trust Insurance Companies.

title: Left High and Dry.
body:
My 87 year old mum had an unfortunate fall in Amsterdam resulting in a broken right shoulder and severe knock to her head. Medical advice was that she needed to return to Australia but due to her pain must be in a laying position and required me being with her as carer. 

Trying to arrange return to Australia through Budget was impossible. Firstly the local consultant we were promised never eventuated meaning that we were forced to working through the night when Australia was open to try and arrange things. 

My mothers condition did not allow her to sit up for m ore than 1 hour as supported by a medical certificate, however, two days of negotiations went back and forth where Budget Direct kept saying that they were just processing the payments on a number of flights and they would get back to us. The time would come and go and no flights were ever booked. I would try and call Budget Direct as they never returned my calls only to then have them notice my number and not answer, my wife, in Australia, then started calling but soon they recognised her number and ignored it. The only way through in the end was calling the general number and selecting the emergency option as they couldn't recognise our numbers. 

After 3 days of trying to get something from Budget Direct and my mother now sitting in the Foyer of a hotel for 6 hours Budget Direct finally called to say that they could get my mother on a flights that would take over 30 hours with a 10 hour stop over in Bangkok but their was no seat for me. This was despite the fact that my mother could not feed or dress herself and certainly could not sit up for 30 hours in Bangkok to get a connecting flight. I instructed Budget Direct that we had to travel together and that if we were to be in Bangkok for that long they would need to arrange a bed at the airport. I was instructed that if I insisted I flew with my mother they could not get a flight with 2 seats together for another 7 days. Although my 87 year old mum got on the phone and pleaded they showed no compassion nor were they prepared to change their decision.

By this stage my mother was in incredible pain and I instructed them that I would make my own arrangements. I called my wife in Australia and told her I was heading to the airport and would head to the airport if she could get us on flights or a nearby motel if she couldn't. Within 30 minutes a wonderful txt cam through. "Flight Booked.Come on home!!!!". 

Budget Direct showed no compassion or understanding of our situation. For some reason they couldn't arrange a flight yet my wife could make arrangements within 30 minutes on a flight that took only 21 hours.

After returning to Australia my mum spent 6 weeks in rehabilitation hospital.

Budget Direct is underwritten by Auto and General Insurance as are a number of other companies. I've now cancelled all my insurance that is underwritten by Auto & General Insurance.

Luckily, I had Australia Post Insurance and made a claim that day on-line and although it took a month to finalise due to completing the holiday, and Apple inspecting the phone and denying any fault on their side, Australia post came to the rescue by paying $700 of the $800 replacement program through Apple ($100 excess).

I replaced the phone while on holiday with a Huawei Y7 and was delighted with it's performance - see my review of it.

All in all the experience was a small negative in a wonderful trip, but the icing on the cake was that Australia Post (who I have paid premiums to for some years, but have never needed to test the claims procedure) came through with flying colours. I have now sold the i Phone X, as I was too disgusted to keep it and I have replaced it with a Huawei P20Pro - a worthy contender.

title: Good following up after international calls but customers need to take a notice on choice of oversea
body: My husband had a problem with swollen feet while travelling in Thailand and it was not his pre-existing medical condition. We rang 1Cover international emergency numbers and asked which hospitals we could attend for seeing a doctor. The staff who answered the phone told us that we should go to an emergency department of the public hospital in order for them to keep the cost low. It will be very inconvenient to queue up for long hours among local patients. In Thailand (and other Asian countries), there are number of private clinics/hospitals serve during business and none business hours for both emergency and none emergency patients in major cities. In the end, we observed his condition over 48 hours without going to a hospital. 1Cover left following up messages on our cousins' phone we borrowed during our stay there. However, we had left Thailand to another country on our way back to Australia. The policy is inexpensive when comparing to other insurance companies but I would recommend customers to ring and confirm about choice of hospitals before buying a policy.

title: Do not trust Allianz with your travel insurance
body:
I purchased a comprehensive travel insurance policy well before it was apparent there was going to be a pandemic (one being declared) for a trip overseas in April this year.
Like other reviews here, I experienced:
- long delays in processing claims and returning calls. Well outside the industry mandated 10 days
- offering every excuse under the sun as to why the claim couldn?t be paid out
- inability to explain how, even though I purchased the highest possible cover, it did not cover events
- and when you do get staff on the phone, they just cheerfully parrot talking points and do not make a good faith effort to engage with you 

In my view this is misselling, plain and simple. Allianz sold me a policy knowing full well I couldn?t claim on it. This kind of thing featured at the recent Royal Commission.

I will keep escalating this through Allianz internally. I have also complained to Westpac, who I bought the insurance through, and also to the Insurance Ombudsman.

Shoddy sales practices and shoddy products are unacceptable. Steer clear of this company and this product if you actually want travel insurance that does it?s job.

body:
I call it Claytons Insurance, Insurance that doesn't actually Insure anything.

Was a long term, claim free customer and all was rosy.  Made a claim, a really simple claim, and it couldn't have been harder, even to the point that the agent handling the claim had an email account that bounced messages.  Went to a lot of trouble to recoup as much cost as possible and save TID any unnecessary cost, even though entitled to claim everything, and it was still to hard.

Some advise, Avoid TID.  Remember reviews are skewed by non claimers telling how great the value is.  Insurance that doesn't give you anything when you suddenly need it actually has no value. Tick the box to show reviews from those who have made claims and the rating will drop considerably.
Secondly, if you persist anyway and find you do need to claim, claim every cent, don't waste your own time trying to recoup costs solely for TID's benefit, the outcome won't change as a result of your efforts.

A company you can trust?  Not even a little bit.

If that were the case, half the population of Australia would have cancer. This company does everything in its power to not pay and the amount is a measly 1,000. I intend to fight this one as Alliance insurance takes ones money and then refuses to pay.  Another friend of mine has had a similar experience for dental work required OS. Apparently the condition was also "pre existing". Never buy insurance of any kind from this company, they just seek not to pay. A worthless company that you must stay clear of. Nothing

title: Do not waste your money or time with Covermore
body:
From what the company states you can claim for to what it will actually pay is a very big grey area. 

They have worded the policy In such a way that they will despuite the claim regardless off all the information they requested to you to comply with your claim. 

When I hear that 75% of claims are settled that is misleading and false and needs to be addressed by the ACCC and Insurance Omburdsman. I was paid $34 of a claim that I actually had no receipt for.  But Covermore  were willing to pay the $34 for a Doctor but would not cover the rest of the claim that was $2300 due to not being well enough to continue onward travel. This $34 apparently is considered a settlement. 

After spending hours assembling the most rediculous amount of information to process the claim. The claim process is arduous and supposed to be online but conveniently keeps crashing and not saving the information. It?s all set up to make it too hard for people to claim and most likely just give up or miss the deadline to claim.  
I was called to say it was approved and would be processed in a few days for the full amount. Then called 30 minutes later by the same gentlemen to tell me he was sorry but made a mistake and it would not be approved . What sort of business are they running. 

It became clear to me that the paper the policy is written on is worth more than the policy itself. I have been a loyal customer with Cover more since 1997 and never had a claim. I get about 3-4 policies a year as I travel frequently. 

No longer a customer and now question any insurance policy. I actually think it?s better to just wear the brunt on unexpected holiday cancellations and save my money. Your more than likely not likely to get anything back from Covermore and the hops they make you jump through for something that should be so simple is another level of insanity.  It?s a total Leah all sham as the company regardless of what it states in its policy can do whatever it wants as the wording is o ambiguous and you are under the sole discretion of the company. It?s set up so you can?t claim basically or they make it near impossible. 

I will be certainly taking this further to small claims court though where I feel there maybe a less biased opinion and might make them look at their claims policy. I think mot people would just give up by now and that is what they are relying on.

title: Its not about the premium price, its about when you go to claim.
body:
I have had a policy with Cover More for some years now. I have always had no problem with making a claim. (and for some reason I seem to have been getting ripped off or hurting myself more than normal whilst trying to forge a new way of life and business overseas? however that?s a different story.) 

This year I went to make a claim and things were different. I put things into the system, and heard nothing back, I sent emails and still heard nothing back, we made a few phone calls and things started to occur. This for us was very unlike Cover More. Systems we not functioning well from an outsider?s point. Then for the first time I had to do phone interview style thing and this is where I met Phil. 

After getting off the phone with Phil one of my mates said ?Why did you tell them (the insurance company) all of that? That?s way to complicated, just tell them what you need to get the outcome you want, you have nothing to hide, what happened, happened, but don?t tell them this? don?t tell them that, just say ?I came home and this stuff was missing? and then they wont look for a loop hole to get out of it. I?ll be very surprised if you get anything after telling them all of that.?

Of course? this started a doubt in my mind, should I have told them (Phil) everything? Anyway, Phil asked me to get some more evidence for him? I did that, and a few weeks later to cut a story short, Phil communicated with me that the claim was going ahead, and I would be hearing from JB HiFi shortly, they would be sending me a new laptop. Telling Phil the truth had paid off, and I got to subtly tell my mate that I was getting my new laptop sorted out, to which he replied? ?don?t tell me your insurance company paid out on that long story you told them? I just smiled. Enough had been said.

Job done? what was expected on my insurance company, and quite frankly it?s ?THE? reason I stay with Cover-More. 

The laptop was delivered, and we put off setting up the computer because I had set up an older laptop and was happy with NOT setting up a laptop for a while (setting up a laptop from scratch is just above ?Moving House? on the scale of things I don?t like doing. Moving house being on the bottom of the list). I then decided I wasn?t going to do set up the laptop, so we got a guy in to do it all. I just didn?t want the hassle.

The laptop was all set up and after the computer was all set up I noticed it wasn?t the same, it felt ?slower? but not slow slow. I know that won?t make much sense but, in the end I checked the ram and the SSD. The SSD was half the size of what I had. I had a 512 gig SSD, this was a 256 gig SD, and with windows installed, I had something like 40 gig left, let along pictures and stuff I was about to load up.

I was going to let it go, until I realised the way I was treating my new computer? ?Oh yeah? that thing? like it wasn?t as good as what I had, but it will do. It was really because I couldn?t load anything on it, so that was a problem for me, it wasn?t the computers fault. 

Without knowing what to do expect getting an external SSD, I contacted Cover-More again. I sent an email, nothing. I sent another email. Nothing. I called, and I got onto Phil again.

First of all, Phil apologised that it had taken so long to get back to me; my emails had gotten lost in the system. At this point I was able to listen. Phil offered me solutions. He said ?we don?t have to do this, however, I want you to have a good feeling about Cover-More.? Phil asked me to get some quotes. We got a few quotes and twisted the arm of one computer guy to give us a good price on fitting a new SSD, and we sent that through. I let Phil know my preference for having an External SSD or an internal SSD and yesterday? Phil came through with the goods. 

My point is this:

In a time when insurance companies are doing everything they can to find every little loop hole to get out of covering people, where people would they feel they would be covered, Cover-More?s ?Phil Heo? is gaining and retaining customers doing the exact opposite. When Phil knew the Cover-More system wasn?t working properly with the emails his first thing to do was put his hand up and say ?Sorry about that? He didn't try and say it was my fault, as people tend to do. 

In our minds, Phil?s name should have a ?r? in it. ?Phil Hero?.

We would like Cover-More to assure us that they would do what it takes to retain Phil in the claims section. That Phil can always be assigned to us should we need to make another claim. And? whom ever trained Phil? they trained him right. Even down to the person that hired him? they hired the right man for the job.

Last thing? we own a tour company in Bali. We are looking for Public Liability Insurance. If Cover-More covers this type of insurance, could you pass on our details to this section and have them call us? If this is the way your claims department will help us should we have a claim there, this is a company we want a quote from. We didn?t even think that an Australian company could help us with a business in Indonesia. Insurance is insurance right; it doesn?t matter where the insurance company is.

Please ensure Phil is adequately communicated to that the way he has conducted himself has retained us, and had us looking for more business we can do with Cover-More. What more could you ask for in an employee. Doing sales whilst ding his job. The perfect employee.

title: Zero zero zero star...Don't use commbank's travel insurance "Covermore by Zurich Australia
body:
I recently went OS on a family holiday and used CommBanks Travel Insurance provider Covermore.  

Covermore is a Zurich Australia underwritten company.

We, unfortunately, had items stolen from our checked in Qantas luggage on our return trip.  Upon lodging a claim, Covermore handed me a list of hoops to jump through in order to review/deny my claim.  I obliged and jumped through the time-consuming hoops.

After a lengthy Covermore delay, I called to find out what was happening with my claim.   The following day, it was declined. Covermore claimed the airline is responsible for items/luggage that has been checked in.

The airline, states items such as electronics are not covered by the airline's luggage insurance and Covermore should be supporting the claim.

As a consumer of both the airline and the insurance company (Covermore/ aka "Coverless") you are left with both companies (QANTAS and COVERMORE) pointing the finger at each other.  This obviously leaves the consumer stuck in the middle with no resolution.

Would I use Commbanks Travel insurance again (CoverMore)?  Not a chance.

If I had have researched other travellers experiences, prior to using Covermore, I would have used someone else.

Other reviewers have had the same experience.  Loophole after loophole in order to deny ones claim.

If I was Commbank, I would disassociate myself from this company ASAP.  It only leads to bad press.
#covermore
#coverless

title: Bad Customer Service, Did not pay, and Cancelled half a year of comprehensive insurance without refu
body:
Do not choose this company. The customer service is terrible, and they will do anything to not pay what is owed.

I paid for a year of comprehensive insurance ? which was not cheap. In June my passport was stolen in Vietnam by a bag snatcher. My drivers licence had expired while I was travelling, so I was required to return to Australia in order to get a new passport.

I am incredibly disappointed in 1 Cover. Not only did they refuse to pay for my flights back to Australia (a necessary expense in order to even get a new passport), they also cancelled my insurance when I returned home ? despite the fact I had paid for a full year, and despite the fact I had no choice but to return home, and despite the fact I always had every intention on continuing my travels when my new passport was issued.

Dealing with the company has been a constant headache. A claims consultant called me to inform me that most of my claim had been denied. I asked for more details and was promised that I would receive a call the next day. After waiting for almost a week, I received an email with the details, and a number to call. The number was disconnected. I had booked my flights to continue my trip, and had to leave the country uninsured due to 1Cover?s incompetence. I emailed them a complaint 2 weeks ago and still haven?t heard back from them.

1Cover has failed to reimburse me the money I was owed, they have cancelled my insurance half way through the year (with no refund), and they have been unresponsive and difficult to contact. They have made a horrible situation so much worse, and I am now overseas and uninsured because of their terrible customer service.

My travel companion made a claim with Travel Insurance Direct and found the claims process easy and got reimbursed more than she had expected. Next time I will be going with them.

title: Misleading advertising. unfair assessment
body:
So covermore is "pre-selected" insurance when you book through Flight Centre. Fight cancellation is in bold and at the top of the list of inclusions. You might be forgiven for thinking that if you needed to cancel your ticket then you'd be covered - not so.

I work Fly-in, Fly-out, and booked a ticket to travel in. I later got a letter from my employer advising that my position is now redundant. I therefore needed to cancel the ticket. Cover-more's position on this is:

1. the redundancy was not unforseen as the letter refers to previous correspondence.
2. there is nothing physically stopping me from using the ticket
Therefore the claim will not be paid

My position is:
1. Although redundancy was possible there was no guarantee that it would actually occur, nor of the timing if it did. The noted previous correspondence occurred more than three months prior with no specifics and no subsequent discussion. If I had known before hand that things would work out the way they did I would surely not have purchased the ticket

2. obviously there is nothing physically stopping me from using the ticket. by that reasoning there would be very nearly zero circumstances under which a claim would be paid. With no further reason to travel, and no accommodation at the destination, why would I go? I suppose I could just go for the fun of the flight and great air-line coffee and then come straight back but it seems wasteful to me.

very dissatisfied and feel mislead

body:
I have often used Cover More for OS travel since 1994 and have never made a claim. They have always covered my existing condition although the extra cost has become very high. Last year it was more than $500 extra on a $300 policy for a 6 week trip. Today I bought a policy for a shorter trip to the same destination. I went with (non-existing) medical-only cover as existing condition cover was declined, although there was no offer or requirement (as there used to be) to accept input from my GP or specialist). 

Cover More eventually offered me a ?manual assessment? ie by a human, but only after I had bought the policy, written this review (at their request) and redone the online assessment over the phone - they had called me ?to discuss why you weren't offered the chance to share relevant health information?.  I was told you have to phone (or write a negative review!) to be offered this. This is not mentioned anywhere on the website, so that would explain it! 

The consultant I dealt with, Richa, was very helpful, and after a manual assessment I was offered cover for my existing condition. Even with a 15% discount ($723 for four weeks, down from $850) it was still a loading of nearly 200% on the base policy and more than 4x the price of their medical-only policy. This time it was I who declined.

title: Cover.More taking over 4 months to assess travel/medical claim

As he has medical conditions including a heart bypass and emphysema, we took out very expensive travel cover for him costing over $1,700.00 and cover for me costing over $500.00 (multipolicy).  He fell ill on 2 March while still in Melbourne and went to his respiratory physician who advised him not to travel for 3 months.  We realised he was just not well enough to embark on a cruise. Note, this was before the Covid-19 became widespread and before it was declared a pandemic.  We immediately put in a claim for cancellation and have been completing everything Cover.More has asked us to do.  We have been assisted by his doctors who are fully supportive and been submitting their medical records.  We are continually thanked for our patience but I have now run out of patience.  Where is the customer respect and service?  Where is the value for money? We took out expensive cover, consulted with my husband's physicians and yet, are still waiting 4 months down the track for something more than a standard letter asking us to wait 10 business days or, what appears to be, stalling tactics after every form or medical letter is submitted.  I have made several phone calls and keep being asked to wait. This is not good enough.  We recognise the difficulties being experienced by the insurer but I request immediate action and the refund of our travel expenses which are significant - approx $35,000.00 - and which we trusted Cover.More to insure us for.  If this insurer wants to have a business in the next few years, how they treat their customers now, will be the measure of the success of their business in the future.  Trust is everything.

title: Refused my legitimate claim
body: My trip to India was cut short when I became severely ill last January with what I believed at the time to be pneumonia ( I have a medical background BTW). I rescheduled my flight to come home the next day which cost me over $2000. I saw my GP the day I came home who certified I was unfit to travel and made the right decision to come home when I did. I believe in retrospect I would have died if I had stayed in India. They rejected my claim on the basis I had not obtained a doctor's certificate before leaving India and had not sought their "permission" to fly home. Section 3 /1 of the policy document states I needed to have my treating doctor certify I was unfit to travel with my original itinerary which I did on my return. It does not clearly state that I should have done this prior to having left India. They have avoided paying me based on clause B1-2 ".... and if Insureandgo approve this! What a a convenient loophole. So basically if Insureandgo don't approve your claim they won't pay up. I suggest you read their policy schedule fully before signing up and realize they are based in the Philippines and have no company representatives in Australia you can deal with face to face.  Two lessons I have learned here: 1) always read the policy fully before agreeing to sign up and 2) you get what you pay for. I believe I have stated enough here already to deter anyone with half a brain from going with these shysters.

title: Did what they say on the box.
body:
My claim was for a travel delay, which inexplicably, is not eligible for online submission, so I had to spend quite an additional time putting together a stack of papers and then scanning them and emailing them in. The form and the instructions were easy to follow and understand. Resolution was reasonably fast - about 10 days/1 working week. The only communication I had with them was form letters - first acknowledging lodgment and then providing the resolution - so no real interaction. In many ways I don't mind that it all just happened smoothly with no fuss or counter-claims. they are a good value insurance product - so their efficiency is to be expected.

My only other recommendation is to read the PDS thoroughly and understand how they will pay e.g. for Travel Delay they state they will pay up to $2000, on provision of proof and receipts.  Deep in the PDS it says they only pay $200/12 hours delay to cover all your costs - and I assume up to a limit of $2000 (or 6 days). so read your PDS to understand exactly how they pay out.
Fast, easy, fair price,
Perfunctionary, travel delay claim had to be lodged manually, not a simple reimbursement.

title: Repatriated after car crash in Cambodia
body:
I was involved in a fatal head on car crash, travelling in the back seat of a taxi, within an hour of arriving in Phnom Penh. I suffered a broken neck and my wife was severely battered, the other driver died. In dealing with Travel with Jane in the aftermath, whilst I cynically expected that they'd be looking for ways to get out of, or minimise the cost of the claim, I found that it didn't seem to be their first priority at all, in fact all the people that we spoke to either by phone or email dealt with us professionally, promptly and with empathy. The repatriation on 2 flights was excellently organised with attending doctors and nurses, and we were delivered to Royal Perth hospital without further incident. Together with the 10 day stay in the Cambodian hospital, I would speculate that the total bill would have been around $100k if not more - my contribution was the $200 excess! 
Travel insurance is one of those costs that we all hate to add onto our cheapy bogan holiday to Bali or wherever, but I would say to anyone reading, things sometimes happen that are outside your control, that are not your fault and you cannot plan for them. Do not rely on "Go fund me" to get you out of the poo, and know that a bad decision made abroad to mitigate your uninsured costs ( the Cambodian doctor wanted to fuse my broken disc with another with rods, Royal Perth has me in a brace for 3 months) can lead to a lifetime of pain and regret.

title: Warning - Insure at own Peril
body:
After conducting research which also took a reasonable review by Choice into consideration, I purchased I&G Gold travel insurance early December 19 for overseas travel in June 20. 

As Government stopped overseas travel and Operator cancelled flights, I initiated claim online in April (including requested documentation) with I&G . I was issued an automated claim number. 

After waiting 3 weeks for I&G to respond, I ended up contacting them in May and was informed that there was a delay and that they had all relevant documentation for processing.  Fair enough, but then the fun started! 

I waited another few weeks weeks and still no further response. I then made numerous followup calls over the next several months to their generic contact number (on hold for long periods and then eventually switched to an overseas call center, who mostly answered with an air of indifference) to inquire about the progress of my claim (or the lack of it). These calls were accompanied with requests for my actual claims officer to contact me (to no avail, even though called backs were promised by their operators).

In June I eventually received an email from a claims officer requesting more documentation. I submitted the requested documents and have recently been informed that the claim is not approved. I wont bother going into the reason for the rejection as it has been covered in depth in several entries below and after the time wasted and frustration I have faced with this mob, I won't be trying to pursue to recover my actual costs of taking out their Gold policy coverage, as a partial credit refund would not probably cover any further waste of my time and angst incurred. 

I booked my travel with 2 other couples. We were all booked on exactly the same flights, dates and destinations. Each couple took out respective travel insurance policies with other companies in early December 19.  I wish had I listened to them as their polices were around the same price but I thought paying a bit more for Gold with I&G would give more coverage in the event of an incident. Both the couples placed a claim around the same time earlier this year due to the flight cancellation and have received refunds for travel costs from each of the travel insurance companies they insured with. Their claims were processed and accepted in a matter of weeks!

Lesson learnt and after reading the copious adverse reviews on this site by the poor people who have also fallen into the trap of insuring with I&G, I strongly advise to look to other travel insurance company's who have a reputable track record and good customer service.

I have also been informed that due to numerous complaints, Choice are in the process of reviewing their rating of I&G Travel Insurance. Has anyone been in contact Canstar?

title: Be aware if your claim is not made along with ORIGINAL receipts of goods purchased prior to your tri
body:
Took out an Insure&Go Silver policy to cover a world trip including cruises (as also did my wife's sister and husband for same trip).
Our premium for 2 was approx $1,800
We had a suitcase stolen in Genoa. It contained a number of items including ones that had been left to my wife by her recently deceased niece. Also had a fitbit watch and a Kindle e-reader plus all my medication for the trip.
This insurance company is now refusing to make payment for our claim (which was not huge) because we do not have original receipts for the stolen items. We had replaced some of the items (shoes, clothing) naturally but they will not pay for these because we do not have ORIGINAL receipts - only the receipts for the replacements (this was at the very start of our 8 week trip around Europe).
The Fitbit watch and Kindle e-Reader we have not replaced as yet. We do not have original receipts as we destroy these after any warranty has run out (ie after 1 year).
The items left to my wife by her deceased niece were jewellery and fortunately my wife left the very expensive items at home. However (for future buyers of insurance especially from Insure&Go be aware that for items like these you need original receipts - not sure how we can get these from a deceased niece so this is ridiculous.
Out trip was in June/July/August and although we had a police report (unfortunately in Italian organized by our multi-lingual hotel manager) we are still battling with Insure&Go over this one claim. I even volunteered to sign a Statutory Declaration in relation to our claim but that made no difference. We are pensioners in Australia and, unless paid out, are unable to replace our stolen items. We would never go back to or recommend Insure&Go to any honest people.
This statement is probably a waste of time here but it will in general be going to a lot of places to warn other travellers to watch out for travel insurance policy details.

He just could not have sat upright in economy for all those hours from Istanbul to Sydney. On arriving home in Sydney, I spent much time accumulating all the details of the extra costs we incurred & expenses forfeited. Covermore accepted everything except for our claims for subsequent medical visits back in Australia. As they pointed out, we have Medicare/Medibank for that here....Covermore is not a health fund. And we thought that was fair enough. Thank you Covermore. We have told many people how well you treated us. We are two fit & healthy travellers - but this was an unexpected emergency....who would be silly enough to travel without insurance?
Easy, efficient, professional, understanding....not resistant or combative

title: Still waiting for review . should I be happy with what I got?
body:
I was on holidays in South America and got altitude sickness. It got bad enough that I had to be hospitalized when I arrived by bus in Cuzco, Peru. I tried to manage the condition once released from hospital but after a few days and following a review by my treating doctor, I was advised to stop traveling in high altitude (which means cancelling the last 3 weeks of the tour I had purchased since all future locations were in high altitude except for the last two days in Santiago). I was also advised by the doctor to fly out to sea level (i.e. Lima ) ASAP after the review (i.e. on same day). 
So I followed the doctor's orders and purchase a flight to Lima and was reviewed again by another doctor in Lima who confirmed I could not continue at high altitude. I sought advice from TID as to what to do since I was in Lima and my return flight to Australia departed from Santiago and in three weeks? time. 
The contact number on the policy turned out to be to Specialty Assist in London,. This seems to be the branch which deals with emergencies for TID customers.  I was advised that my medical costs in in Cuzco will be paid directly (which was good) but that I would have to make a claim for other costs when I got back to Australia (fair enough) . 
As to what to do next, the advice was vague namely to stay safe ( i.e.  don't go in high altitude) and opt for the cheapest option for the rest of my holidays . Not having planned to be on my own in South America (and particularly Lima) and being unable to finance another tour at short notice nor three week freelancing in Peru (in low altitude), and somewhat shaken by the whole hospital experience,   I contacted my travel agent to organize an earlier flight home to Australia from Lima.  
 I had arrived to South America from Europe via the US on a World ticket and had to purchase an additional flight from San Francisco to Quito (where the tour started from) , returning from Santiago (where the tour ended) to SF. So I had to have a new ticket issued for the Lima to SF flight and my World ticket had to be amended to an earlier date, 
Having submitted my claims upon my return to Australia  I was dismayed to find out that TID would refund the portion of the tour I had to cancel due to altitude sickness but not any cost related to airfares including the flight from Cuzco to Lima on medical orders and the costs of amending my return flights to another date and departure location . 
I have asked for a review of my case and now more than 3 weeks later, I have heard nothing in spite of being told I would be advised within 15 days. 
When I queried the delay  I was advised the case was not submitted to the review team until the end of the week following my request for review; that 15 days were in fact working days;  that the review team has a backlog. And lately the customer service staff inferred I should be happy with what I got (i.e. the refund for the trip portion I could not do). 
Beware travelers as to what you are purchasing when you get travel insurance from TID....be prepared to be happy for what you get , even if you incur additional airfare costs due to medical reason,  and never mind if your return flight home departs thousands of km away and you cannot get  yourself there .

title: Absolutely not aligned with global events.
body:
This is the last time I will consider Allianz. Bought our travel insurance in late Feb. As the situation with Covid-19 developed, I have been wondering what the insurer will do. 

On 13 Mar, it release its FAQ reiterating its exclusion condition when it comes to pandemics (Covid-19 was declared a pandemic on 11 Mar by WHO). On 16 Mar, Allianz US-Coverage provided an update to its terms allowing for some situations to be claimable even if events are related to Covid-19. For example it is stated that in the website "https://www.allianztravelinsurance.com/coverage-alerts/2019-novel-coronavirus.htm"

However, until further notice, although not covered under most plans, we are currently accommodating claims for:
    Under Emergency Medical Care Benefit: Emergency medical care for a customer who becomes ill with COVID-19 while on their trip.
    Under Trip Cancellation or Trip Interruption Benefits: Trip cancellation and trip interruption if a customer becomes ill with COVID-19 either before or during their trip.

It is challenging to reach out to the Allianz number to check if the same stipulations apply to similar insurance bough in Aus. But if the website FAQ is any indication, the answer is 'no'. 

In summary, very disappointing experience with a company who is not prepared to recognise global events.
