title: Near death experience due to Allianz
body:
My family went to Bali in June, my young son fell ill with gastro type symptoms. We called Allianz and they suggested we go to BIMC (private international hospital). The conditions at the hospital were poor. The hospital was dirty and the nursing staff lacked basic medical training. We raised this multiple times with Allianz.

After two days, and waiting 24 hours for an ultrasound whilst my son was in excrutiating pain with his stomach swollen to look like he was 7 months pregnant, my son finally had emergency surgery. A near 30cm cut down the middle of his stomach.  

He was admitted to intensive care and his condition continued to worsen. Call after call to Allianz begging for repatriation to a hospital that were equipped to deal with my son. Even the BIMC recommended to the insurer that he be evacuated, recognising they were not equipped to deal with pediatrics.

Allianz blatantly lied about his ability to fly - told us that air ambulances don't fly at night, that after stomach surgery you cannot fly for 5 days, 7 days and 10 days (the timeframes changed with each phone call). At one stage they also lied about the availability of the air ambulance when we had been in touch with their providers and they had confirmed that they were available.

My son was near to death - septacemia, severe pneumonia, pressure point sores on his little body, had been left heavily sedated for days, was hallucinating, severe weight loss and muscle wastage and still they refused.  

Eventually after threats of legal action and the media, and many thousands of dollars of phone calls (we called the Australian number direct not global assist because we were always left on hold with global assist) we were evacuated to Australia and he spent five weeks in a pediatric hospital.  

The lies and rudeness could take pages to recount, but you should get the message very clearly.

Allianz did everything they possibly could to minimise their costs with complete disregard for my son's life and for the distress that they caused my family.  

I would never, ever recommend Allianz to anyone EVER.

title: Still waiting for TID to pay 4 months later
body:
I booked my family to go to Hong Kong.  I took out TID travel insurance.  My 87 year old mother died days before our planned depature and we cancelled our trip so that we could organise her funeral.  
Our airline charged us $600 dollars to cancel our flights and I claimed this $600 from TID in October 2017.  
TID have asked me for things like "details of all medication" taken by my mother "over the past 24 months"; what my mother's "state of health was"; and "what was the likelihood of" my mother's "hospitalisation or death (being) due to any pre-existing medical condition".  I'm not sure what the suggestion here is, but this is clearly a ploy to explore the insurer's options not to pay.  $600.  By way of comparison, although I had made a non-refundable booking with the hotel, when I told them we weren't coming they refunded the full $2312 cost without me asking them.  They clearly know what it feels like when a member of your family dies.  I can't say I think the same of TID. 
Every time I email the case manager I get an email that says "unfortunately we are experiencing higher than normal volumes of claims due to the peak holiday season".  It is March.  March.
I also see on the Cerberus Special Risks Pty Ltd website - yes you'll be dealing with them if you need to make a claim, not the insurer - that "Cerberus ... does not act on your behalf".  I wish I'd read that first.  They certainly don't !  They are all shiny, friendly and nice up front - with a glossy brochure, cheap price, chatty packing list email - but don't pay at the back end.
In my case I feel personally offended as it colours the whole memory of my mother's death and funeral, but that's just how it feels for me.  I feel done over and will never use TID again.

Cover-more did not advise me that further information was required from them until I pursued it recently.
Everytime further information is received a further 10 days is added to resolve the matter
The policy was easy enough to set up but the claims procedure is not customer focussed and in view of all of the above it seems Cover-more is stretching the payment to me as long as they can.
To confuse things even more Today at approx 2.45pm I received an email saying that I hadn't given my correct doctors name on the original claim.
While this is correct, as my doctor had directed me to my specialist, however on 24th September I emailed the doctors information and was acknowledged. I have checked further with my doctor today, and he has not received any letter from covermore requesting further information than that he has already supplied.
I ask why it has even taken 16 working days to request further information from my doctor?

title: Forget this insurance if you need to make a claim!
body:
After being a loyal customer for 4 years, countless trips and not a single claim - I finally needed to make a claim. I had always purchased the Gold plan, so felt comfortable with my claim because it includes lost items. 

On a flight back from the US, and in my tired state, I left my laptop in the seatback pocket. Of course, the airline couldn't find it, so I had no choice but to make a claim as I need the laptop to run my own business.

I completed the online claim form to start the process but the claim process isn't simple. Firstly, I had to submit a 'Repair report' before I submitted my claim, which was a challenge because I couldn't send my lost laptop to be repaired.... because it was lost!

After my claim was submitted I had to wait 10 business days. During that time, I received no update. After I emailed to ask for an update I was told the claim would be processed within 5 days (that's 13 business days not 10). I thought great! 

5 days later I received an emailing saying my claim had been.... rejected. The response went into great detail about why it wasn't approved. So, the claims team had spent 13 business days scouring through the conditions of the policy to see where I couldn't be covered. All for a claim that was under $2,000.

The lesson? It would have been better to save the money I had spent on travel insurance to pay for a replacement laptop. I shudder to think of what would happen if I had an emergency or a high dollar-value claim. Good luck with that!

I could have lodged an appeal but the reality is they wouldn't have changed their decision and it would only have been a further waste of my time. 

If I do get a response from InsureAndGo, they will likely send a standard response about how they go to great lengths to explain the conditions of the insurance (Note: Not sure about the 'great lengths' part as they simply sent me a link to their PDS). The reality is the things they say you're covered for... probably aren't covered, or they will go to great lengths to find reasons for why your claim won't be paid. 

I'll be looking for a different travel insurance provider as InsureAndGo has made me 'InsureAndStop'. I'd encourage you to do the same!

It's been disappointing that the only advice they offer on their website is that they don't cover anything related to the disease - leaving us to financially manage all medical, hospital and other costs while we are travelling. Well guess what, we had damage to the vehicle which was entirely NOT our fault and after claiming with 1Cover we had NO out of pocket expenses except for the policy. Had we purchased the reduction of the car rental excess it would have cost us $200 plus the policy of $125.

Be aware however that if you take out your own insurance to cover the excess that if you have damage, the rental car company will immediately deduct the full excess from your credit card which in our case was $3500 plus a premium location surcharge (plus the rental). This can be a problem depending on the limit on the credit card. Another word of advice, always check the vehicle before you start the hire, we found damage to the roof of the vehicle before the hire which hadn't been previously reported.

title: Doesn't do what it says on the tin - avoid if you can
body:
Lovely when taking your money and absolutely terrible if you ever need help - buyer beware, I will never use Insure and Go again!! 

I have used insure and go a couple of times, both the Australian and UK companies. I have been impressed with customer service when taking out the policy and have always found the documents sent to me clear HOWEVER do beware if you ever need to make a claim, my first experience of having to do so marks the last time I'll ever use this company. 

I recently went abroad and had a problem with my tooth. I called MAPFRE to ask for advice on where to go to get my tooth fixed that would be safe, hygienic and approved by regulators whilst in Bali. This is precisely the type of service Insure and Go advertise that they offer but despite this I was repeatedly told that they would not help me until after I had lodged a claim and it had been determined whether I was successful under that claim: this is illogical because to lodge a claim I would need to incur the cost of a dentist so I would have chosen one by that point, what I needed was advice on where to go and MAPFRE is advertised as a service available on a no cost no approval needed basis for customers. When I asked to speak to a supervisor I was told none was available as the Australian office had closed (I was calling at a time when they should still have been open, pre 5pm Australia time), when I made clear I was not happy and would be complaining I was put on hold for 20 minutes before someone told me they had googled a dentist and gave me the address. I am able to google dentists myself, this fell far below the standard of service I expected and I had had to threaten a complaint to get even that help.

I was also not happy at all that I was being told they would only assess my claim once I had actually incurred the cost and lodged all of the documents, nowhere in the policy documents I had received was this process made clear and with other insurance companies I have used you are usually given a medical decision over the phone or within a short time after having notified the company. 

A word of caution also to any ex-pats thinking of taking out this policy - in the end I didn't have to spend enough at the dentist to make it worth claiming (I spent less than the excess), but despite having asked 2 separate individuals with the company on 2 separate occasions whether I would be covered as an ex-pat and having been told on both occasions I was definitely covered provided I had some form of medicare card (I am not a permanent resident but I do have a medicare card which is all the policy documentation asks for - though I still sought clarification from the company directly, twice, to be sure) when it came to claiming Insure and Go demanded proof of residency from me. Who knows whether had I actually tried to claim they would have honoured the representations made by two staff members over the phone, but it was just another red flag in an already chaotic and unimpressive claims process. 

Go elsewhere if you can!

title: Corrupt
body:
They use every trick in the book to cop out of paying up when everything has been done correctly.
They also took so much time to review our claim obviously hoping that we would forget or not follow up.
We were in Hawaii heading to SF via LA when an engine malfunctioned as we were about to take off and had to return to the terminal. We changed planes and as we were about to take off a second time the pilot was called back to the terminal due to being over his hours. 
Unfortunately, we couldn't take off again as there was no availability and therefore lost our accommodation in SF, lost our Frequent Flyer points, had to pay for a new airfare to SF and all we wanted was to be reimbursed what we'd lost.
It took SureSave almost 8 months to assess our claim and then we received a minimal amount as there must have a cop out clause for them to use.
The service by their claims department is nothing short of atrocious.
The number of calls we made (and our travel agent made) were numerous and each time they said they would get back to us, but they never would.
This is obviously how they make their money, by taking travellers monies but not paying up or avoiding to pay when the traveller has a need.
An immensely CORRUPT company.

title: Do not trust this company ....will never use again!
body:
We took out a 12 month policy end of January and we travelled to Bali in Feb for 2 weeks (no claim made on the policy). We requested a cancellation of the policy in early March due to Covid and we were advised by our travel agent that the balance of the policy ie. 10 months would be refunded. WE also accepted that we were not covered for any claims due to Covid. It is common practice that, if any insurance policy is cancelled, the holder is entitled to a pro-rata premium refund.  Today,  4 months after the refund was requested, we were told that only 25% of our premium is being refunded ($595 from a $2299 premium). The refund should actually be around $1900 - this is absolutely unacceptable and not in line with any other insurance company I have dealt with in the last 50 years! How is this fair Covermore?
Because of this, we are highly unlikely to use Flightcentre or their subsidiary Covermore again!

title: Strangest Ever Exceptions - Be very careful before using this company
body:
Even though they are clear in stating countries they wont cover you visit, it becomes an anomaly when on a cruise (one of their great claims to be the best cover for cruises). Before purchasing the policy I noticed they don't cover Haiti (one of the stops on a planned cruise), so I called to confirm what is and isn't covered. Turns out it's not (as I wrongly thought) just if you go ashore in Haiti or do an excursion or just fall over and break your leg that isn't covered. It's even if you stay on the ship.

I asked this specific example: Me "you cover cabin confinement if you're sick?"
Them: "yes"
Me: "So if I'm sick and confined, for example, Mon, Tue, Wed and we dock in Haiti on the Tue and I'm too sick to leave cabin and told to stay inside am I covered?"
Them: "No"
Me" So you'd only pay the insurance for the Mon and Wed?"
Them: "Yes that's correct - you're not covered for anything in that country's sovereign water"
Me: "What if we get diverted from Haiti and don't dock due to bad weather, is that covered?"
Them: "no"
Me: "Why not?"
Them: " Because we don't insure anything in Haiti"
Me: " But I wouldn't be in Haiti, we were diverted and your policy pays out if we miss a port due to weather etc"
Them: " Yes but we don't cover Haiti"
Me: Very confused....

I can understand not being covered in the country for any activities or even just being there but on the ship? What happens if you get sick and are being treated as sailing into Haiti waters - do they stop treating you???

Crazy policy, obviously decided to go elsewhere...

December 10th 2018 Update: Terrible st settling claims

Delay after delay tactics when I had to claim. And the excess applies for each ?event?. So if you have medical bill some damage and a loss that 3x the excess. Will never use or recommend them. How can a PDF document sent as evidence be ?unreadable? just a delay tactic.

title: Enough to ruin our trip of a lifetime.
body:
Always used 1 cover. Never had any issues. Was always quick and easy with a high level of coverage for a low price. A 3 month trip to the US had a few unplanned incidents. 1 involving my partner needing a trip to the hospital. Not long after that our credit card was skimmed and the bank cancelled it. We didn't realise until we got to the airport and went to collect our hire car. We had to stay in the same place for 3 weeks and wait for our new one. We were left stranded forking out last minute hotel costs when we were supposed to drive 5 hours south to stay with friends. Then the fun began.
1. When I originally contacted Allianz from overseas and informed the credit card was skimmed, I was told to include it with our medical claim. I was not advised this wasn't covered. Not an issue as it could have been
picked up somewhere along the line within the next 9 months, but it wasn't.
2. I was asked to provide all sorts of documentation confirming the card was skimmed. I had great difficulty obtaining 1 document from commonwealth. This held up the process most. I rang Allianz for help on numerous occasions and asked if this was needed or I could provide an alternative. Still over this couple of months there was no mention of this not even being covered from the start. I feel that this was all an attempt to prolong the medical claim as much as possible.
3. Commonwealth finally provided documentation. Passed onto Allianz straight away. Things started to go very slow on Allianz end. Due to my work hours I would ring nearly every day during lunch and have to hang up because I couldn't get through. My emails hadn't been responded to. I was told a maximum of 15 days but this went on for months. When I was finally contacted to be told only the medical claim could be paid, I was very frustrated as you can imagine. Had I have been told from the start this wasn't going to be covered there would be no issues - and my medical claim could have been finalised much sooner.

Now when I look back on our trip all I remember is the nightmare of this claim.

1 Cover was fine, but their insurer is Allianz so be mindful of this. Unfortunately for Allianz we had them for 2 cars and 2 home and contents polices. These have since been cancelled and I will never use this travel insurance company again.

body:

Took out a comprehensive international cover for a trip to Hawaii. Luggage for two of our party went missing for 4 days, with medications included. We were told that because we were traveling as 1 adult and 2 children, we were not classed as a family, OUCH! (We didn't know to check the 'family' box, apparently) 
We were told we had $200 each cover to replace essentials. Not until we got home did we find out that, that was $200AUD, not USD, which is what we spent it in and then we're told it was $200AUD TOTAL, not each! with a $100 excess, which we thought we had eliminated with an extra payment. We didn't bother to make a claim as we would have been further out of pocket for a $100AUD return. I assume this is what they prey on. 
It seems we did for medical, which I got nothing back for, after spending $250USD for a doctor to get scripts for missing medications and the medications themselves. 
We are traveling next year, I will NOT buy insurance from 1Cover, they've lost a long time customer. 
Your insurance is only as good, until you have to make a claim, not how much the premium costs.

title: Fair to Good.
body:
About the sixth time we have used 1Cover.  Not in a great position to judge 1Cover as we've never needed to make a claim so who knows if they are + or - minus when actually paying out.   However the other feedback seems good to me.  I give credit to the way what really counts for busy travelers like most of us who go to 1Cover is the way they are upfront and concise/detailed  (a balancing act between adequate info vs. too much or too little).

Part of me wants something on my trip to go wrong so that I could give honest feedback about the actual/real  efficiency in terms of paying up when needed.  Of course insurance is like that - wonder why you got it when you get home and have made no claim.  However I think rationally about this issue - what you are buying from 1Cover is peace of mind.  U don't really want to have to claim anything from them, u just want to be assured that if something big did happen you are definitely covered.  For my partner and I we DID get caught in middle of Bangkok political protests and worried something bad could happen.  But the reassurance of knowing we're covered by 1Cover meant that we didn't stress about being in middle of potential trouble (possible big hospital bill if we got shot or something).  However for us having not read the fine print of 1Cover - out of interest still need to retrospectively see what would have happened if some type of bad (= need to claim) would have occurred so still don't know if they might have had exclusion clause for political riot.  In any case, the irony is that Thailand (LOS) being LOS meant that a possible insurance claim in TRUE fact became another great day in Thailand.  Despite (or maybe becuase of the peace of mind provided by 1Cover TI, we actually had a memorable/authentic The protesters actually GAVE my partner and I FREE (rare in Thailand) food, Thai flags and water for taking part in the "fun" of a riot.  Just got home from Thailand and jet-lagged big time.  SUMMARY - I suspect most of us will never make a claim FROM 1Cover but they give you peace of mind (like all insurance does).  Fully do not mind paying $100 for no benefit needed in retrospect (getting home safely and not out of pocket requiring claiming from 1Cover) but in the knowledge that the bucks spent fairly contribute to what I saw often in Thailand - people badly hurt (physically financially etc).

When in Thailand, a German friend of mine DIED from a motorbike accident in the town of PAI.  Obviously devastating.  The German friend stayed at one of my best friend's guesthouse (so you know this is not made up the incident happened at HAPPY HOUSE in PAI - head on collision with two Thai military men on motorbikes,  owner of Happy House was Frits).  The dead guy had travel insurance (not sure what company - probably not 1Cover as he was German national).  Anyway my mate owner of the guesthouse the deceased was staying at considerately took it upon himself to make all the necessary arrangements that one never thinks of when a death happens os  - get hospital/morgue/death certificate, fly body home, spend big money on phone calls to everyone in the deceased's diary.  Frits mentioned that hospital and all THAI authorities needed big money up-front for all the xpenses and that the German man's travel insurance would not pay UP FRONT without full documentation of circumstances (understandable - big money, need paperwork before handing money over).  So Frits pays out of own funds until German travel insurance paid him back two months later.  My point is that i wonder with 1Cover what happens when big trouble occurs - do they trust you or have mechanism so that you can get an advance before paperwork happens when obviously you are traumatized by whatever the reason for your claim is.

Anyway all these years of no problem with 1Cover so will keep using them.  Don't want to sound stingy/scroogey but it would be nice if after many years of three weeks travel per year they gave some kind of no claim bonus or acknowledgement of continuous loyal custom.

Philip - Melbourne Australia
Website functioned as should.
Should acknowledge prior custom as have now spent about $2000 over many years with them and never needed to claim.

title: We Were Refunded Full Amount - Medical & Auxiliary Expenses
body:
It is such a pity that I am now encountering so many complaints about "Insure & Go Australia". I can imagine that because of the sudden downturn in international travel due to Covid 19, all operators in the tourism and travel sector are experiencing difficulty in catering to their clients.

My husband and I are in our 70s - an age that requires an addition to the normal premium. Based on Choice Magazine's recommendation last year, we purchased  I & G's comprehensive Gold travel insurance. A few months after purchase, my husband suffered heart problems for the first time and had to have a cardiac pacemaker inserted. So I phoned I & Go Sydney to inform them about this, and they requested a top up for this additional medical condition.

While overseas, a full month PRIOR to the announcement of the Covid 19 pandemic, my husband contracted pneumonia. This was followed by a heart attack. Although he recovered, the doctors refused to sign him off as "fit to travel" and advised an angiography plus angioplasty. In the end, in lieu of angioplasty, my husband underwent bypass surgery. Our initially planned 3-week Christmas holiday stretched to three months. In all that time, Insure & Go Australia, through its auxiliaries in Asia, patiently took my phone calls and liaise with our  Aussie Family GP and the Australian Hospital where the pacemaker was inserted. This was despite poor, frustrating internet/phone connections with the Third World Country where we were stranded. To make a long story short, Insure & Go Australia honored EVERY single aspect in its "comprehensive" cover - hospital theater fees, surgeons' fees, all hospital-related fees, hospital accommodation, and my booked accommodation outside the hospital. Not only did the insurer reimburse us for our return airfare on Singapore Airlines; it also upgraded us from Economy to Business Class as per doctors' recommendation. We were safely back in Australia by the end of February, two weeks before the borders were closed.

I and my husband are very happy to testify that INSURE & GO AUSTRALIA did not fail us in our hour of dire need.  Our gratitude and KUDOS to them! 

Signed: Emilie Mae Wickett, Perth, WA

title: Complicated process for getting pre- approval  for minor but emergency medical treatment
body:
Hi
I recently needed emergency medical treatment in a middle -eastern  country. It involved some minor surgery on my shoulder due to a sudden skin infection.  I was at the point where I could not carry my backpack because of the pain. I spoke with a local doctor over the phone who had been contacted by my hotel. We made an appointment for him to see me and he had explained that based on my description I would probably need a  minor  procedure quite urgently.  We made an appointment for later the same day as I was flying on to my next destination in a couple of days time and I wanted a few days for healing before travel. I rang 1cover to report and discuss what was to happen. Although the rep was very friendly and courteous,  she said she could not guarantee that any medical claim for this procedure would be paid.  For them to guarantee that, I would need a report from the doctor  outlining the problem with proposed treatment before he did anything. This Report would then go to the "medical panel " for judgment about whether the proposed emergency procedure was "appropriate". The Rep.  could not say how long that would take as "they are very busy" but it certainly  could not be done  in the next couple of hours. 

In the end I  had the required procedure on the day and made not yet made a  claim as once the excess was taken into account I was not out of pocket by more than approximately $50. I am not sure its worth the hassle, although I do have paperwork.

However, the requirement to get pre-approval to guarantee a medical claim would be paid , seemed silly. If I had not had had the procedure when I did and waited perhaps days for approval, I would not have been able to continue my travels which would have resulted in a quite a significant claim cost wise.(extra hotel costs and claim for flights)  Surely 1cover can develop a fast track process for such minor emergency situations which although minor are emergencies nevertheless and which could if not dealth with promptly , lead to more substantial out of pocket costs for the travelor. ?

title: Smooth sailing in Cuzco
body:
My boyfriend and I used Travel Insurance Direct for our South American holiday last May - we were away for 5 weeks. I have insured with them quite a few times in the past, as they have good prices and from what I can tell their "comprehensive" seems quite thorough, however I've never had to make a claim before. This was the first trip that we had to use the insurance - once we landed in Cuzco about 3 weeks into the trip, my boyfriend got horribly sick with severe gastro symptoms. I wasn't sure if it was altitude sickness or gastro! But after a few house of extreme gastro - he was getting worse and worse, severe shakes and chills etc, I've never seen someone get so ill like that from food poisoning ... so I asked the hotel manager to call us a doctor. A doctor arrived within 20 minutes, he recommended we go to hospital to go on a drip - so we jumped into the mini ambulance waiting outside - and got checked into a private hospital on the outskirts of Cuzco. The hospital checked us in, got our travel insurance details, treated my partner, and I stayed in a little bed in his private room overnight. We stayed in for about 36 hours - we had a private ensuite room (albeit a blocked toilet.. but I'm not complaining), meals for both of us (not that he really ate!). They dosed him up on antibiotics and a drip and he was like a new man. Travel insurance direct called us at the hospital to check on us, and asked if they should contact anyone back home for us. All in all it was a dream experience considering a foreign hospital in Cuzco was pretty much the worst case experience that I had imagined. We didn't have to outlay a cent (we had $0 excess on our policy), the entire thing was covered. We never even had to give our credit card details to the hospital which seemed too good to be true, but was very reassuring. Thanks for a good trip we'll definitely use this company again.
inexpensive, comprehensive, good service, covered private hospital

In April we lodged 2 section claims so $800 will be deducted if our claims are successful.  1st claim: as we were not allowed to board the ship in Norway if we travelled via Hong Kong thus we rescheduled our flights via Tokyo.  As airtickets were purchased in June 2019 we incurred additional rescheduling airfares expenses.  2nd claim: cruise was terminated on day 2 of the 13 nights cruise. We were transported to Heathrow airport for quick departure home as the government authorities won't allow cruising passengers to remain in the UK, thus ending all our original UK travel plans.
Received disappointed email on 2 June rejecting one of our claims insisting that "you decided to cut the trip short in your own volition".  We thought we were doing the right thing, obeying government and cruising authorities directives, etc?

Overall a shocking claim experience!

title: Disappointed.
body:
I realise I?m bucking the trend by giving 1Cover a low rating, but see what you think.

This review is written at the end of January 2020 and the situation is:

CNN say:
"At least 132 people are dead and more than 6,000 cases (of a new virus) have been confirmed in mainland China, as the Wuhan coronavirus spreads across Asia and the rest of the world. China on lockdown: Nearly 60 million people are under partial or full lockdowns in Chinese cities."

The Australian government says:
"At level 3, there are serious and potentially life-threatening risks. This can make the destination unsafe for tourism and unsuitable for most travellers. ...
Check your travel insurance policy carefully. It may not cover travel to 'reconsider your need to travel' destinations."

Around 16 airlines have stopped flying to China and others have reduced their services. Yangtze cruises enter the 'locked down' Hubei province. 

So I emailed 1Cover and asked if I can claim for cancellation on my Comprehensive travel policy. Their answer was ?No.? In fact they wrote: ?With the advice 'Reconsider your need to travel', you do not have provisions to claim to change your mind for your trip to China.?

In my opinion, cancellation should be covered under these circumstances, but as far as they are concerned I?m just changing my mind. Who?s right?

At least it seems that they would cover me to go to this dangerous place and pay if something went wrong, but I don?t want to be quarantined in China for an indefinite period of time even if I could get there, which is unlikely.

title: Paid bills but terrible treatment regarding flights home
body:
Whilst overseas my partner fractured his spine in a speed boat accident, it was no ones fault really just a freak of nature accident but it was terrifying. My partner and I were in a Thailand hospital for 6 days, so we were lucky we got insurance. Allianz were great in that we did not see a bill, they paid my partners medical a bills straight away and told us what we were eligible for regarding the claim. I was covered too - we appreciate and are grateful for that. However, we didn't appreciate the way he was treated in regards to the flight home. The doctor who treated my partner whilst in hospital stated in his medical report that he was ONLY fit to fly business class home. My partner was in a brace, a lot of pain and extremely uncomfortable most of the time, without being stuck on an plane, imagine our disappoint and confusion when we receive an email 48 hours before our flight telling us that the Allianz doctor thinks he's fine to fly economy and therefore won't be upgrading his ticket. Without much time, we rush to dispute this decision, several emails, calls and even a trip back to the hospital to see the doctor (Allianz told us the only way they will change the decision is if the doctor does a follow up exam and report) who refused to change his decision on the medical report. Whilst at the airport, 6 hours before our flight, Allianz call to tell us the decision has been revoked and they'll upgrade his ticket. However, it was too late. After several more calls, Allianz tell us they can't upgrade the ticket from their end and there's no more they can do, we have it figure it out ourselves. At this point we didn't know what to do, we had to check in and my partner was in a lot of pain. 3 hours before the flight, my partner who has a fracture spine and is in a brace is running around Bangkok airport trying to upgrade his ticket. At this point, it was up to Thai Airways to upgrade the ticket but they refused. In the end, my partner had to endure a 9 hour flight in economy with a fractured spine and in a back brace. These flights are uncomfortable in general, so you can imagine how upset I was to watch my partner suffer again just so Allianz could save a few $$. Won't be using them again.
Paid all medical bills
Refused to upgrade ticket for injured person

They took hospital specialist reports on board, they asked for a bunch of paperwork from me and checked my medical history with my GP (that this medical issue was not a pre existing problem)...they gave the go ahead for surgery within 24-48 hours. title: Medibank/Allianz medical travel insurance excellent
body:
I am a male 52 years that was hospitalised in St. Mary's Medical Centre San Francisco for 24 hours for a suspected stroke. I underwent a series of tests including CT, MRI, MRA, and ultrasound. It was expensive - they assigned an accountant case manager! It was ultimately diagnosed as a non-serious "painless migraine." If you get sick in San Francisco go to this hospital. Once over the initial anxiety of my illness I became worried that the insurance company would not support the claim. These fears were unfounded. The insurance staff were helpful and maintained frequent contact via my partner. They quite correctly could not make a definite decision until they had received and assessed the hospital reports, and it was a nervous wait for two months until resolved. Establish direct contact between hospital and insurer, and let them deal with the accounts. Carry policy number and contact phone numbers on your person in wallet or iPhone. Be scrupulously honest pre-existing conditions otherwise they will have a reason not to pay the claim.
Inexpensive. Frequent telephone and email contact. Polite, knowledgable, and helpful staff.
Slow processing, but almost all of that was waiting for the formal issuing of hospital discharge certificates. It might be a nervous wait until they receive and assess hospital reports.

It contained all of our documents, passports, tickets, photos, computer, iPad etc. It took me several hours to recover it (which I did, thanks to the honesty of a London taxi driver). By the time I had recovered it the airline had offloaded us from our flight (Heathrow to Singapore) and told us we would not be able to get another for 13 days! I had to cancel a prepaid three day booking in Singapore and stay in London for three extra days. Eventually we were able to find a flight direct to Sydney, missing out on our Singapore stopover altogether. The rebooking of the flight and the extra accommodation and travel expenses cost me more than $1500. Covermore compensated us for this. After excess I received about $1100, for which I was very grateful.
The cover and the treatment of our claim was practical, no nonsense and easily the best experience I have had with insurance.

title: Broken Leg - No Worries with TID!
body:
During a trip to Santorini last year, I slipped off a wet marble step and fractured my leg in two places. Nightmare! But as soon as I got to the clinic on the island, TID were in touch with the doctors straight away.
I've never claimed anything on insurance before and was a bit worried about how it might go, but TID organised everything quickly and efficiently - Eight hours later I was on a light plane (fun!) accompanied by a cute Italian doctor to Athens' main public hospital where I received further care and constant contact from [name removed] (Legend!) from TID. They kept me for four days to ensure there wasn't any internal bleeding in my leg, but then I was moved to a great little hotel for two days while they organised my business class flight home! TID even arranged for the taxi driver that picked me up to head to a chemist and get me some crutches - It's the little things!
The claim I submitted when I got back to Australia required a lot of paperwork and supporting documents but, having worked in the insurance industry, I can say this is pretty par for the course. They covered my missed tours and flights, and refunded me for the private clinic bill I paid.
Heading off on another trip tomorrow and selected TID as my insurer again - During a time when I was physically and emotionally distressed, they helped me out with everything both financially and with a cheery, supportive voice on the line. Thanks [names removed]! Thoroughly recommended!
Great attention to detail, always able to get someone on the phone, friendly staff!

Cover More Insurance,easy and simply to arrange on line and if required customer service is excellent.Recently we travelled to Fiji and needed to make a claim on our return. The process was very quick and stress free, unlike the loss of the wedding band which is now floating in the coral sea, back where we spent our honeymoon 13 years earlier. High recommended for product and service.
Flexibilty of product,excesses and inexpensive.

body:
Signed up for a weeks cover, they took the money. As I didn't need to make a claim would they honor their "promise to pay" as that is all an insurer does?

I don't know and not sure I would use them again as plenty of options out there.

body:
!00% value quick operation simple to make a decision
Good value policy-easy to organise.Response to all emails made communications a pleasure to respond with details required.Customer Support was the best I have been involved with for the past 3 years,

title: Great product
body: have always used Insure and go and have no dramas. Very prompt with their emails and communications.  Making a claim is very straight forward. highly recommended

title: Very speedy claim!
body: We recently had to go to a hospital in Italy and we were with 1 Cover. When we returned home, I lodged the claim and it was approved within 5 days .It was very quick, and there were no problems  which we appreciated.We would definitely use 1 Cover again

title: Would not travel without it.
body:
Policy was good value and easy to set up.  Would not travel overseas without it.
We will definately consider this insurance for our nexy trip.
We have used Allianz on several previous trips and found claiming to be easy to do.

title: Convenient and affordable.
body: The policy provided was best I found for the best price, it covered exactly what I needed. It was convenient & easy to set up and I felt comfortable in knowing that I was provided covered for my holiday overseas.

title: A necessity if travelling overseas
body: The premium was competitive under the circumstances. I needed to contact customer service due to an existing health condition. The person was very helpful and set everything up while on the phone. Luckily, we did not need to claim. Our previous claim for a holiday cancelled due to ill health was paid within a reasonable time.

title: Dont leave home without it
body:
Yes, good value for your money.
The policy was easily set up just like counting to 1,2 and 3.
Support was very helpful when setting up our travel insurance.
Thankyou

title: Had to have it
body: I needed the security of cover for pre existing illnesses and Allianz provided that. Other companies took exception to my age and would not insure me so I was very pleased that Allianz accepted the risk.

title: The Best Insurance company that I've ever delt with.
body:
We have unfortunately had to claim twice in recent times due to illnesses abroad and at home.
1Cover were exceptional in both case and helped us with our claims in a friendly and professional manner.
Our recent claim was a total cancellation as my wife broke her ankle, after all the documentation was presented and refunds claimed from the booking agents, 1Cover processed and paid our claim in full long before the refunds came back from the cruise line, airline and travel agent. Thank you 1Cover for your prompt payment which helped smooth out a painfully and stressful time for my wife. I will only recommend 1Cover to my friends and friends.

title: Efficient insurance.
body: The policy was indeed good value for money and easy to arrange.   And in our case where we had to make a claim, this was handled efficiently with good follow up.

title: So far so good
body: The policy seems like very good value and easy to purchase through their website.  This is the first time I have used this insurance company and haven?t yet departed on this trip.

title: Very easy to use online and covered everything
body: The online application was very easy to follow and was happy that a pre existing ailment did not increase the policy price significantly  - I felt it was good value - I did not have to use customer support at all

title: Would never use 1 cover again
body:
Have used 1 Cover before but never again! 4 of our family insured with 1 Cover. Rang 1 Cover yesterday to make a claim as my 23 year old son was unable to travel as my mother who was also travelling hurt her knee and .needed someone to care for her as she lives with us. As it was our 30th wedding anniversary trip our son kindly stayed at home.
The 1 Cover told my son couldnt  claim anything.
Disgraceful.

title: Excellent service
body: This is the second time I've booked travel insurance through Covermore, after my first experience with them was so positive. They made it so simple to make a claim (providing I followed the instructions in the PDS, which I did). I found setting up a policy very straightforward and the PDS is very clear and easy to read. The service I was provided through the 'Live Chat' function was also faultless - I was pointed in the right direction clearly and valued the quality and efficiency of the advice. Thanks CoverMore :)

title: Holiday Insurance
body: Haven't used this policy yet, Paid for in 03/19 won't use till 09/19 you've got my money 6 months early ! I wonder if I get a bigger discount next time ?

title: Paid for a policy which was not honoured - had to raise through AFCA to resolve
body: Disappointing to say the least. I took out a travel insurance policy on 7/2/20 and was unable to travel due to Covid 19. Not only did InsureandGo refuse to payout on anything issued after 31/1/20 they would not refund or defer the policy to another date making it completely redundant. I had paid for a product as a safeguard which became completely worthless yet they decided to keep the premium. After lodging a complaint this was completely ignored, after which a complaint was lodged with AFCA, after some time a deferral was offered and a subsequent refund however I would not recommend using this company. If you're willing to take receipt for a product you should honour that.

title: Very happy
body: Great value covers us for our pre existing conditions  covers you for natural disasters have been using insure and go for years have only had to claim once when I broke my foot in Bali they paid everything so very happy

title: Did not use, felt safe having it
body: Used over past two travels. Why do I have to use twenty words. Why do I have to use 20

title: Worth knowing when travelling
body:
I had commenced my journey and forgotten to take travel insurance.  So I emailed 1Cover Travel Insurance, the company I usually use to cover me when travelling.  I got an immediate response and quote on the same day and was able to get cover with the following provisos which are fair:
This plan has comprehensive benefits, however it is subject to the following conditions:
[i] There is no cover under any section of the policy for the first 72 hours from commencing your journey
[ii] Non-removable excess of $200
[iii] Does not cover for pre-existing medical conditions [unless noted on the PDS]
[iv] Your journey must END in Australia.
[v] The maximum duration we provide under this cover is up to 12 months.

title: Great price sold me
body: I had been talked into purchasing travel Insurance through our travel agent which was hideously expensive. When Insure and Go advertising popped up in my emails, as we have used them before, I thought I would just check the price for comparison.  The $350 difference in price for comparative cover had me contacting my travel agent and cancelling my original insurance and taking out a policy with Insure and Go. I have never made a claim with them, but they seem to offer comprehensive cover for my trip.

title: A solid choice.
body: I used 1Cover on my recent holiday to North America, which included a week or so of skiing. Having read the PDS carefully, 1Cover are one of very few insurers who will cover off piste skiing (even though most skiiers will constantly go 'off piste' at a regular ski resort without even realising it). They were helpful on the phone, and gave me a small discount for being a return customer. I didn't have to claim this time (phew!) but have claimed before and found it very straightforward.

title: Satisfied Traveller
body: I thought my premium to be quite substantial but I was aware that my age and pre-existing medical conditions did contribute towards that and I was happy that Insureandgo was prepared to give me full cover. Due to an illness travel  plans changed en route with additional costs. I lodged a claim on my return home and without any hassle from the company, my claim was fully refunded. There was good contact along the way from Customer Support.

title: No hassle Insurance Cover
body:
I got the policy cover I requested and it was set up within minutes.  No complaints but, thankfully, nothing happened
that I needed to make a claim, but I felt comfortable being overseas knowing I was covered if sick or injured.

title: A very disappointing experience to say the least
body: My wife and I booked a cruise in January 2018 to the pacific islands in July.  Unfortunately approximately two weeks before departure I was admitted to hospital and undertook open heart surgery and was unable to travel as planned.  Fortunately we invested $346 in travel insurance in case of unforeseen circumstances and assumed that we would have no problems claiming the pre-paid cruise cost of around $4000.  How wrong could I be!  CoverMore have been very unhelpful and non communicative for the past three months in handling the claim and deliberately using stalling tactics to hold any payment at all.  Eventually a payment was made which seems to be less than we expected and now four days later we have still not been notified of the payment or the break up of how the figure has been arrived at.  We will not recommend CoverMore to anyone and will never use them again for future insurance.

title: Just Great
body:
I was fortunate enough not to have to make a claim, but knowing that i was covered on my trip made me feel so much at ease. Knowing that there could have been a possibilty of maleria and dengue fever made me uneasy and the fact that i was travelling in cyclone season was a bit scary but 1Cover truly put me at ease and especially when it came highly recommended by a friend.
Cheap, quick, reliable
Only thing i would change would be the print your own policy; i would have prefered one to be posted to me as i dont own a printer.

title: This is the opposite of perfect. Trying to work through & settle a claim is a horrible experience.
body: Unfortunately I won't ever use this insurance again. Responsiveness of the claims rep was borderline non-existent. Most queries went without a response back. I could not contact my rep via phone - in all attempts made to do so, I was told not only could I not get through to him, I could not speak to a supervisor of any kind. My claim was for 2 lost phones. I was notified what my settlement was via a JBHiFi rep telling me I now had a voucher of X amount to them. I was never contacted by my rep to advise of this. The JBHiFi rep was just as shocked as me to hear this. After a few emails to my rep, he responded without a reason for not advising me of this. Next, I requested a cash settlement (it's in the Ts&Cs that Insure&Go chooses the method of settlement) as opposed to a JBHiFi voucher, which he was able to process. I was advised this was processed and would transfer to my account, however the settlement amount decreased $600. When asked why, the rep had no reason for this. I told him I do not accept this settlement and never heard back from him again. I gave up at this point as the ending the headache was more valuable to me then $600. In the end, I'm glad I made a claim because I'll know I wont spend the rest of my life wasting money on their terribly unprofessional travel insurance.

title: Perfect Insurance
body:
Cover is the first port of call for all of my travel insurance needs.They compare favourably to any other company.
The website is easy to navigate and payment procedure is very easy.

title: Will always use 1Cover they are fabulous
body: I purchased mine online which was great, however unless I called I wasn't offered the returning 10% discount, similarly people who I referred to you were not able say I referred them.

title: Excellent service when you NEED it actually!
body:
Hi,  i always purchase insurance from 1 cover whenever i fly overseas.

From day 1 the customer service team were very helpful and most importantly,  the communication was very quick and promt.

I recommend this company for it's service.
Actually you don't know how good or bad one company is unless it comes to claim. 
I will recommend them to everyone. 
I will purchase the insurance for my next trip within a couple of weeks time.
Regards Avijit Bose

title: So very affordable
body: I have now used this company 3 times, and each time it was so very easy to purchase online.. Very simple outlay and also very quick to do

title: Great cover for a reasonable price
body: Insure and go were able to cover pre existing conditions (excludes North and South America) at a reasonable cost. Multi Trip cover well worth considering for regular travelers. Telesales staff were helpful and able to answer all my questions.

title: value for money
body: Good value, easy to set up. Never had to claim but feel it is worthwhile. Good options for cover. Mainly use for peace of mind while travelling. Would use again

title: Simple and economical
body: The policy was economical for a mature person and you had many levels to chose from. The computer interface was easy to use.

title: It's only travel insurance once you are 50klms from home
body: Well I learnt something new today.  My policy kicks in tomorrow but I needed to hire a car to get to the airport over 100klms away fir a 6.30am flight.  So I ring customer service explain what I am doing and am asked if I am hiring the car 50klms from home.  I explained that the Avis depot is only 3 Km from home but I had to drive to the airport over 100klms from home I was then told that I could pay for the extra day but it was pointless because I wouldn't be covered because I am less than 50 kms from home and it would be considered a domestic trip.  Not happy.

title: Holiday without it - is no holiday
body: Policy was really easy to obtain. CoC was issued seamlessly. As usual an easy process. Charges from nominated paying account was instant. PDS clear and concise. Website easy to navigate.

title: Travel insurance claim
body:
Yes good value.
Just hard to be 100% sure about the policy until you lodge a claim and you go through that process but all good from taking out the policy and cost and what is offers

title: never leave home without it
body: I didn't need to claim this time, but have had to on two other occasions. The ease of obtaining cover and the excellent service when making a claim in the past has me coming back time and time again. I recommend it to all of my friends who all agree with me.

title: 1Cover Loyalty
body: Very easy to set up either online or directly with customer support. Excellent value and amazingly quick claims service on return if required. I have bought many travel policies over the years with 1Cover and recommended them to many friends. Everyone has been very satisfied with their purchase of travel insurance with 1Cover.

title: Bali holiday
body: Family was sick while in Bali. Travelcard was exceptional. Very easy to use and great communication. Only downside was the $50 phone bill I got when we got back home.

title: Great customer service, prompt response, very efficient.
body: This is my first time buying with Insure & Go, I was hesitant at first as there are so many insurance companies out there esp on the internet, but you guys at I&G have exceeded my expectations. Claiming was all online, done in a very prompt and hassle free manner. Response was quick and outcome in very reasonable time.

title: Good VChoice
body: It was ok to cover all the basic needs in case something goes wrong. It is great to know that you are covered. Must have one when travelling overseas, for peace of mind and sense of security as you dont know what can happen in a foreign land.

title: Terrible
body:
My luggage bags were stolen outside of the airport,they were sitting next to me and my son.I was told that my claim is accepted, even they told me how much money approximately they have to pay me after my claim goes to another department ("It is usual process" - they said). After that no one contact me. When I rang them they couldn't find my claim,but the same day in the afternoon when I rang them again I was told that "My claim is declined. My bags were left unsupervised in a public place"!!!! Well done!! I have lodged a complaint again, if they decline again I will be more than happy to contact The Financial Ombudsman Service and ask them for their opinion!
Nothing. It is a very disappointing company. They are very friendly when they need to take money of you unless you make a claim.
Unfortunately, whatever you tell them or write in details regarding your complaint, they will on the end make it that "it has happened different"! You have no chance to prove the truth!

title: Great Service - Very helpful
body: Had some questions before taking out the policy and the staff member was very helpful etc. I took out the policy over the phone and the staff member was knowledgable and efficient.

title: Insure & Go with satisfaction
body: My policy was good value for my age & it was simple to complete forms on line. The customer service I received was  prompt and to the point  Excellent  service  Thank you  Liz Garrett

title: Very disappointed with their communication and processing
body:
Made a claim with cover- more, extensive paperwork. Claim accepted and notified that in 10 working days will have the amount to pay out. Exactly 1 month latter receive the same email again. Have emailed for a response. Nothing. I may add I have given now 8 days for a response. Try phoning and go through your keypad responses only to always end up with your operator and then put on hold with no response after 30 minutes. Have phoned over 6 times and always same process.

March 28th 2019 Update: Cannot answer the telephone

Spent months getting a positive result. Informed of the amount we would receive and told would be in account 3 days later. 6 days later tried to ring to get an answer and redirected 5 times back to switch. Told only ring between 8 and 9 am or after 5.30 pm because all the staff are talking to travel agents. Understaffed, want your money but no claims service after that. Had to complain on this website just to get a decision which happened in 24 hours.
COVER MORE focus on your clients.

title: had to have peace of mind to know we were covered
body: The policy was easy to set up staff was very pleasant and helpful was rather expensive for such a short policy and that we had not had any reaccurance of illness satisfied with service

title: all went well

body: I never travel overseas without travel insurance. Always expect the unexpected but happily I have never had to make a claim. Will continue to have insurance in the future.I also trust Allianz.

Was easy to do online great pricing good value it was easy to understand what cover i needed to get Would definitely use again Am a very happy customer 
thank you

title: Satisfied customer!
body: Yes good value, competitive and I spoke to a very pleasant gentleman who set me off with relative ease. Fortunately did not need to make a claim. Nice To know though that I was covered.

title: Convenient
body: I have used TID for a few years now.  It is easy to set up, the policy is clear and it is better value than others I have checked. I have also called a few times for advice (usually relating to available discounts) and had good service.  Being a recent retiree, I tend to look for longer trips overseas (around 9 weeks) and a number of shorter trips.  But I can not seem to find a once off annual policy to cover my circumstances.  Last time I checked the annual policy was limited to max of 4 weeks per trip.

title: Covers Motorcycle riding for over 65's
body: Used once so far.  Great that I can get coverage for international motorcycles riding over 650cc.  Have to check the ski policy next.

title: Burglary in USA
body: I was burgled in the USA and lost a number of items including a one year old Macbook Pro and a one year old Iphone 4, two cameras, a thousand dollars of newly purchased clothes bought on sale,external hard drive etc. My email had gone astray and initially i thought the  cheque i received was for full payment. i have now spoken to them and they have deducted a very fair amount for depreciation and my final settlement will be  extremely reasonable. In addition i found the service to be very personable and helpful.

title: Great service easy to set up and very reasonable
body: Great value I felt secure in the knowledge that I had good cover and simple to contact in the event of a claim. The policy was easy to set up and the value was excellent

title: Terrible!  They take your money but look for any reason not to pay
body: I got sick on a carnival cruise 2 days prior to the end of the cruise.  I was diagnosed with norovirus and restricted from flying and ordered to be under quarantine.  We were booked to fly to our 2nd home in Canada (on a 457 visa in Australia) and had told medibank this when purchasing the insurance.  They refused to pay for our flight change fees until I was well and not contagious to fly, they would not pay for a rental car for my husband, even though the policy says they will pay transportation costs for a relative that is staying with you.  The only thing they paid for was the hotel because I could not leave Sydney and the doctor on ship.  The doctor on ship could not do anything further for me he said, so I vomited violently for more than 24 hours, then once ship docked, went immediately to the hospital.  Even though I was sick for a couple days, technically I was back in Australia so no coverage for medical treatment even though I was covered on the last day we docked and went straight to the hospital.  I guess I was supposed to swim to a hospital prior to docking in Sydney.  This company is criminal, approved me, then changed their minds and said no, then when we fought for the policy we bought they approved us but only for hotel and doc on ship.  They looked and looked for any reason as at all possible to deny my claim,kept going back and forth. I bought insurance in case of a medical emergency, which this clearly was, and they could care less, all about saving them money. We have the top 85 Medibank private insurance for living in Australia, pay $540 a month and never have made a claim, not one dollar.  We are cancelling with Medibank altogether because of what happened with the travel side.  I would not want my worst enemy to fall ill like I did, I literally thought I was going to die, never been sick like that in my life.  Shame on you Medibank Travel!!  You take peoples money but don't want to help them when they have an emergency.  Rude staff all around, I think they enjoyed telling me most of the expenses incurred due to the emergency would not be covered. Don't know how these a holes sleep at night.  Do not get your insurance with them!  unless you want to fight for what you deserve and pay for expenses yourself.

title: Great product and easy to use
body: Probably one of the easiest applications for travel insurance, and hopefully the claim process would be the same, although we fortunately didn't have to use it. Competitive rate, so would use this travel insurance again.

title: Super
body: This was the second time that we used this insurer and unfortunately had to submit a small claim which was handled quickly and efficiently. Will use Insure and Go for my future travel.

title: great
body: Very easy to set up. Third time I have used online travel insurance and never had a drama. Thank you very much

title: Satisfied
body: The policy is easy to set up ,and satisfied with the customer support that I received.  Did not made any claim, but looking forward to use Budget for the next trip.

title: Easy and simple!
body: My policy was easy to purchase, everything was explained in black and white and I knew exactly what I was covered for, especially as I have a few medical needs. Fortunately I did not have to make a claim! Thanks TID.

title: Should not send reminder texts whilst away as you have not considered the time difference
body:
I did not enjoy receiving a text at 2am asking if I want to extend my coverage whilst away.
You knew where we were and should be able to arrange a text if needed at an appropriate time.
I have used 1cover many times but this may be my last time.
I have never made a claim so cannot comment on that part of the service..

title: Used Cover-More for many Personal Trips again and again!
body: At my age (pre-computer upbringing) Cover-More make it very easy. Peace of mind knowing my needs are covered. Cover-More has been the Travel Insurance company for a number of my family members. Thank-you.

title: Not enough support with medical assistance
body:
I have been using 1 cover for approx 5 years including two lots of 12 month travel insurance.  We have claimed once in 2016 for a stolen bag which was eventually honoured after first having to appeal twice.  
We have just returned from a trip to China where my husband hurt his back after a very rough landing in a plane.  It was neatly at the end of the trip and we just wanted to get back home so that he could be treated in Australia by his own doctors.  We requested assistance with an upgrade on the flight home so that he can layback as sitting was very painful.  1 cover decided that he needed to go into a Chinese hospital to be assessed.  Even though I can understand why they wanted that course of action it meant that we would be left behind from our family and friends plus the tour group which had at least a guide who could interpret for us.  That left us both in a very stressful situation in a country that the language barrier was insurmountable, where it was lucky to even get wifi in some places and to be separated from each other (him in hospital myself possibly in a hotel).  I found there response unreasonable and unsympathetic to our situation and to that note will not use them again.

title: Try making a claim
body:
Yes very easy to obtain travel insurance but I hope you don't have to make a claim like we did, my wife is going through cancer treatment and I thought I would send her back to Brazil to say hi to her family and whilst in Brazil she was robbed.
When she returned we claimed for the stolen camera and 7 weeks later the investigations team has now finished and it will be a further 10 days to see if our claim is accepted. They have spent 3 times the value of our camera investigating, what a waste of resources, we are very disappointed with allianze travel insurance and don't recommend them stay clear.
I have just cancelled house insurance contents and car insurance with allianze and gone with a VERY REPUTABLE INSURER RAC YES RAC AND THEY ARE CHEAPER

title: I just new I had the backup and that means security
body: I am a return customer because this travel insurance is so easy to set up. I have used this company on a number of occasions and remain absolutely satisfied by the way applications are managed. I have fortunately not needed to make a claim on travel insurance. However I have made a claim after hail damage to my car three years ago and the response to the claim was impeccable.

title: I always use Allianz
body: I travel overseas with my husband and two children always once but sometimes twice a year.  I always have travel insurance, however, Allianz is definitely my insurer of choice.  This is based on the actual cover and my past experience.  My 7 year old cut his hand and needed stitches whilst in Hong Kong.  This was my only ever claim, but the experience was great, my claim was approved and paid up almost immediately.  Every part of my claim experience was seamless as well as helpful friendly people on the phone

title: Insurance Claim
body:
I had a minor skiing accident and submitted my claim as soon as I returned.  The claim was settled within two weeks without query.  Everything was handled on-line and very efficiently. I was expecting the ninth degree, or usual insurance company procrastination, and was pleasantly surprised by the whole experience.
Easy to purchase policy and great to be able to download claim documents on-line rather than have to snail mail.

title: This company should change its title to 'COVERNOTHING'
body:
The worst travel insurance company I have ever come across. 

The company should be called 'Covernothing Travel Insurance'. I paid for a PREMIUM travel insurance product (assuming id be well covered), only to be told that 'pandemic' related claims are an exclusion in the contract (which i wasn't advised of when i bought the product). I suggest reading the fine print with these guys because it pretty much excludes everything you could ever want to claim. 

Covermore provides generic email responses that don't answer questions (or they don't reply at all). 
Any company hiding behind an excuse of 'delayed responses due to covid' - 2 months later is completely unacceptable. And, instead of the generic we're so busy emails -  get on with the task of giving me my money back like you said you'd do months ago. .... A bank transfer takes 30 seconds to complete - its really not hard!

title: They take trouble to amend a problem
body:
Review amended from 1 to 5 stars after they rectified a problem I had not receiving a promotional voucher. I now have confidence they will step up to the mark in the event of a claim. 
UPDATE: I did in fact need to see a doctor during my trip (cost was $400US!). 1Cover paid without any problems. 
Note: print out your 1Cover policy/details and include it with your travel paperwork as if you need to see a doctor overseas, they will request to see it. I had to ask 1Cover to email me my copy, which they did.

title: Satisfied with policy.
body: Very good value policy.No claim made,and will use Budget on my next trip if the value is still there.Really nothing more to add as I did not make a claim.

title: Best value
body: Easy to purchase online, including assessment of preexisting conditions. Good value--cheaper than others without compromising on benefits. Only had to call customer service to ask whether they offered an add-on for rental car insurance, but they were polite, friendly, and happy to help.

title: Always making excuse why they can't pay Choose another Travel Insurer
body: Trying to make a claim through Cover More was terrible they lose documents, so they say, 15 emails to get a response back. They depreciate items and deduct them from your claim without explanation. Treat you with the utmost disrespect. Will never insure with them again and will tell everybody I know about our experience.

title: Excellent service
body:
Did not require a claim this trip but still thoroughly impressed with the ease of purchasing online with followup pre & post holiday. On previous occasions have had to claim & have done so with no problems, so I would thoroughly recommend TID to my friends & family & will continue to insure with TID on future holidays.
My only concern being is that we are now in our 60's but in good health but having to paying higher premium, but guess that comes with maturing.

title: I shudder to think what would happen if a person had a real life-threatening emergency with these ca
body:
First off, there's A LOT of fake reviews of this company, Yo' Allianz, get some better fake profile writers to make y'all seem genuine and value for money...PATHETIC!

Purchased the Allinaz travel insurance before heading off on a world trip last year. Long story short, sustained a minor yet persistent leg injury in Thailand that sidelined my trip for 2 months.  Made it to Europe but soon realised that my leg wasn't properly healed and In the end I had to cut my trip short due to my leg not being able to sustain the weight of my back-pack...cuz' let's face it, 'back-packing' usually involves some burden of weight right. This trip cost me alot of money and I didn't even get to complete it.

Gave these clowns every damn document/medical certificate and doctors report and still they wanted more. These Capitalist pigs who gorge themselves at the trough of human misfortune, just want you to jump through endless hoops and needless diversions so as to wage a back-handed war of attrition against decent people who do the right thing and take out insurance so as not to burden another country's medical system should something go wrong.

AVOID THESE CRETINS AT ALL COSTS, THEY ONLY WANT TO PREY ON YOUR FEAR OF THE UNKNOWN FOR MONEY!

title: Generally positive experience
body: I had to cancel a solo trip at the last minute due to my husband's illness. It was an unusual situation and I was out of pocket over $3K so I expected a fight about it, but claim was accepted. body:

I rang TID straight away with the details and they told me to lodge a claim when I returned. I spent weeks compiling all my receipts (with over $2000 worth of stuff stolen). However when I lodged my claim, it was rejected due to a hidden "sunset clause". Ie they will not cover any theft after dark, which is the peak time it occurs! They googled the sunset time for that day to be 6.45pm and my stuff was stolen around 7pm. I appealed it but they continued to reject my claim, saying it was after sunset and not covered (it was actually still light until about 8pm). I am totally disgusted with this company and the way my case was handled. I will never travel with them again and recommend eppeople read their sneaky policies very carefully!

$10,000 out of pocket later not to mention the thousands already spent on flights and accommodation that I had previously paid. I come home and apply to be paid out to be told that they will not be paying my airfares, the bulk of my accommodation, transfers. They sent me a statement telling me that out of the $10,000 they would refund me $3200!!!! 

I then called up the company and spoke with the man dealing with my claim asking him why my flights and accommodation werent being paid he told me that I had traveled to Bangkok and it wasnt their fault that I didnt have a good time whilst I was there! So they wouldnt be paying for any flights.

title: Denied my legitimate claim

Yet when I put the claim in, they denied it under an added clause, saying the property was in my care and therefore not covered. The rooms were rented, not the whole house. what on earth is personal liability then needed when it wont cover for property damaged not owned by you. They have those clauses set up to minimise any claim that could happen. WONT EVER USE THEM AGAIN!!. NOT FOR ANY REASON OR COVER.

January 25th 2018 Update: Dont pay claims

I purchased comprehensive travel insurance and some property, not mine nor family nor friends, was damaged through an accident. I got told when I rang it would be covered under personal liability. However when the claim was made, they denied it due to an added clause in the PDS that the property was in my care, therefore outside of the policy. Its a load of rubbish and they seem to apply what they deem to wriggle out of paying. Took forever to get back to me too. Never use them again.

title: Very unimpressed - after 3 policies - finally had to claim on 3rd and been denied payment! AVOID!
body:
I have had 3 TID policies in recent years, and on this 3rd policy after a trip to USA finally had to claim and was very unimpressed with the response.
I had a camera lens - fairly cheap one too $200 worth - which received some damage during our trip and wasn't functioning properly. A local camera store in USA confirmed the physical problem and I purchased a new lens. I made a claim with TID and didn't hear back from them for a month. I emailed them again and they finally got to my claim - then surprisingly came back with - "you didn't provide enough information - assumption its a mechanical fault - which is not covered by warranty." I waited a month with no contact, and then after bringing it to their attention, they couldn't even ask for more information about it if they so required it.
I asked if I could provide more information and why it wasn't requested in the first place, she agreed to re-examine my case if I provided a insurance report from a camera repairer. I did this and paid for a full insurance assessment of the lens from a very respectable camera store. The report said this type of damage is due to some type of external force to the outer ring. I then forwarded it to TID. I received a very abrupt phone call basically saying we won't overturn the decision - they suggested I pay for the report but didn't even properly look into.
This issue was then escalate to their claims review process - and again the same story - and I quote "your camera has stopped working as a result of a mechanical breakdown or malfunction of unknown origin". Seems quite funny that they are so certain of this - since they never saw the camera and had a insurance report saying its probably due to some force on the lens. What is insurance for if you cannot get paid out when you claim. 
On another claim I was successful and they said I will receive the money within 5 business days . After 2 weeks no money was received and I emailed them. Received a lame excuse "oh sorry - the money bounced back - I had resubmitted payment". Bank details were correct, and if it bounced back why not get in contact with me? How unprofessional!
Avoid like the plague!

Unprofessional, sloppy, doesn't payout, doesn't investigate claims properly.

title: Fast and professional
body: I often use TID for my travels. Earlier this year I made a claim and am definitely impressed with their service and the outcome. My daughter accidentally broke my spectacles while we were traveling and I had to purchase another pair while overseas, in order to complete my travel safely. I submitted a claim online once I returned back to Australia. Soon after I received an email and a phone call from TID; requesting more info and to clarify a couple of things. I received the money a few days later. The whole process was quite quick without unnecessary delays. The only thing that was of concern initially was on how to prove the ownership and value of my broken spectacles as I did not have the original receipt as proof of purchase. Luckily I had the overseas photos of myself with the spectacles - before and after the event. I also had the quote/receipt from the optometrist for the purchase of new spectacles, as the broken ones could not be repaired. TID initially said they will have to depreciate them, as I did not insure them separately. I did not agree with that, as in my case the spectacles are a customized necessary item, related to travel safety (just like a walking stick, a prosthetic leg, a denture etc. for other people). In the end I was fully reimbursed for the purchase of prescription glasses overseas. I was very satisfied with the outcome and do not hesitate in recommending TID to other travelers.
