title: Total cover without any stress in an extreme situation.
body:
I could not believe that for the second year in a row my holiday would be interrupted and that I would have to call upon my insurance company to bail me out. Last year I was in Kathmandu when the earthquake struck, absolute disaster for Nepal and its citizens. Tourists were in the way and needed to be moved along. Cover-More covered all expenses associated with my having to leave a tour early. I wrote a report last year for Product Review, giving them five stars. I had no idea I would need far more from them less than 12 months later.
This year I had an accident while travelling in Laos. I fell whilst photographing the beautiful Kuang Si Waterfalls near Luang Prabang and could neither stand nor walk after the fall. The driver who took me to the falls managed to get me back to the car with the help of a few of his friends, then he took me to Luang Prabang Provincial Hospital emergency. X-rays revealed serious tendon damage, and the hospital contacted Cover-More to discuss my situation. The company needed more information to make certain they had an accurate description of my condition and determined that I be flown to Bangkok for an MRI. The insurance agent was apologetic about not getting me on a flight the very next day, but I was pleased they were able to organise a flight for the 17th, given that I had to be flown on a stretcher and accompanied by both doctor and nurse. It must have been difficult to arrange that flight.
In the meantime, I was unaware that many hospitals in that part of the world do not serve meals or even water to patients. Relatives or friends are expected to provide such things. There was no one to help me and I was worried. [Luckily, l one of the nurses (Ann) gave me some food at her own expense! (It still touches me deeply to think of how kind she was.)] As soon as I told the Cover-More agent of this, she contacted people from the touring company and enlisted their help. That was a great relief! 
I was admitted into Bangkok Hospital on the evening of the 17th and received the best medical attention I could imagine from that day until I was discharged on the 31st. The MRI revealed that my right quadriceps tendon had ruptured and that I required an operation. All medical advice said it would have been extremely unwise to try to fly back to Australia for the operation, and I do not think I could have been given permission to fly, so I had the operation there on the 21st, six days after the injury. They would have operated sooner but it was necessary to take me off some of my regular medication and wait 3-4 days before it was deemed safe to proceed. I later learned that with this type of injury, surgery should be done as soon as possible. All along, Cover-More liaised with the hospital and monitored my situation. They also kept in touch with me personally. I never felt isolated at all because of the reassurance given me by both the insurance company and by the medical team at Bangkok. I was in excellent hands because the orthopaedic surgeon who treated me, Dr Pornthep, handled surgeries for the Thai national sports teams. He and his team told me what was happening every step of the way and took every precaution in order to ensure success before, during and after surgery.
Cover-More flew me back to Melbourne ten days after the operation, once again on a stretcher and accompanied by a nurse, and they organised to have an ambulance waiting at the airport to take me to my home city of Geelong. They also organised for me to be admitted to a rehabilitation facility in Geelong. In other words, they looked after me conscientiously from the time I entered Luang Prabang Hospital until I was admitted to Grace McKellar in Geelong. They were thorough. I am incredibly grateful to Cover-More for the care they gave to me. I did not have to worry about anything. 
Finally, Cover-More refunded in full the portion of the trip I was unable to do, and they refunded the cost of a short flight that I had not claimed. To anyone who has read this far, you may think I am working for the company, such is my gratitude. That is not the case at all. I was in a very, very difficult situation, and Cover-More knew exactly what to do each step of the way. I could not have been in better hands.

I used to grumble about having to buy travel insurance. Never again will I complain about that!

title: What a dysfunctional Team leader and Team. Took nearly 3 months to actually settle an account.
body:
We took out a policy for 12 months this time after using Covermore for most of our trips either abroad or within Australia over a 15-20 year period!
Policy setup by our Travel Agent of many said years as above. 
Customer Support absolutely atrocious!
My wife had her suitcase stolen on a trip from Frankfurt to Milan, the suitcase was stolen from the coach to the Hotel Foyer a matter of 200 meters, all my wife had on her back was the clothes she wore. We still had another 8 days in Tuscany and another 6 night in Singapore on the way home to Australia.
We rang the hotline and told the said person what had happened and was advised to purchase what was needed but keep the receipts as was expected for repayment!
Arriving back home our Travel Agent helped fill out the paper work, she did do it online, made hard-copies, sent photos, had receipts, had Milan Police Report, had lists of stolen items in suitcase including presents and Christmas gifts, all sent in via express post!
Weeks later, got a phone call needed more info "What info" list of the items stolen, sent list, needing clarification, not good enough, this procedure went 4 times. I think they must have half of the ration of paper the Sydney Morning Herald gets weekly in what we sent them.
Another 2 weeks, the "dysfunctional system" sets in. 
Where is the paper work, again told what was sent. Was informed we should sue the "Travel Agent for costs" er hello aren't YOU an Insurance Travel Company! 
Will get back to you, another 2 weeks, how do we know these items are what you say? LOOK at the receipts we furnished in our BANK Statements, yes people this went on and on hence we were told at one point "My Team Leader" will not pay this!
Also was told the "Police Report is not like other Police Reports, er it was in Milan Italy and it has" Milan Police Report of Crime!" 
We were even accuse that the phone call I made to Sydney "only talked about medication and that's all and yes we have the phone recording!"
My wife response was "please hear the recording and WHAT could one talk about for 19 minutes about medications and NOT about a stolen suitcase, er hello and WHERE do you think the medications were in the suitcase hence the phone call!" This is what I mean about dysfunctional!!!
This so called "Team of assessors" were trying to wear us down I feel but my wife was determined to fight this after the distressing time she had of this holiday and the amount the Insurance wanted to pay was 1100 dollars, the jewellery we bought for Christmas for each other and presents for our family in Czech Republic was more than that and the replacement clothes, underwear and suitcase, what about those items?
We were made to think we were criminals in the way this "team" addressed our problem after 10 weeks of "nothingness and judgement" I decided to fight this to the Travel Ombudsmen, my...my...my, what a change in attitude!!!
Eventually my wife's claim was paid, not the replace costs of the items but what was in the suitcase and suitcase that was stolen!!
Do you know Covermore, we have traveled for more than 20 years and most of that time been insured with Covermore. THIS is the first time in all of that time we have made a claim!!!
We now have "Trakkdot" stashed in our suitcases if this ever happens again so at least we can track our suitcases and after this yearly insurance policy finishes we shall look else where for our insurance!
SHAME! SHAME! SHAME on you COVERMORE!!
Look elsewhere people, we shall!

I received a quote for a replacement phone and provided it to cover-more as required.

-They would NOT cover any medical bills in Australia as a result of the attack. $800 worth gone.
-They would only cover the phone for what they deemed it was worth . Half of what it was quoted by Apple to be replaced. 

I would hate to think what would of happened had I suffered a serious head injury and needed to be flown back to Australia for surgery, further treatment or care etc.. None of which would of been covered by Cover-more.  

A truly horrendous insurance company that will NOT be there for you when you need it. Go somewhere else and check their fine print.

title: Disgrace- When you buy 1cover policy you are not buying anything
body:
I recently had my iphone stolen on a recent trip to Thailand. Over the course of 4 hours while out at a bar, the bag my girl friend and i were sharing was entered into and my phone taken most likely when i was in close proximity. The facts are, i left the bag on a few occasions to see the surrounding areas (bag supervised by my gf) for no more than 15-20 mins at a time and this was deemed to be unsupervised and i quote "where they can be taken without your knowledge; or at such a distance from you that you are unable to prevent them being taken"

This is the definition of leaving your things with a travel companion. Allianz seem to know this as they say you can leave it with a travel companion, but then undo its practical use by saying you left it unsupervised.

You cannot have your eyes on your things at all time, anyone who has traveled with a companion will know this! 1cover has created a unfair, deceitful and disgusting policy whereby you are a) leaving your things unsupervised by being too far away, or b) you were too close and therefore weren't providing appropriate supervision. In short, they have created a false insurance that covers no body in the event of a theft.   

I hope you don't scam one more person out of their money and dont sell another policy. They are not difficult to deal with over the phone but will interpret your facts given however they choose to best fit their "we will not pay" scenario. Looking at are these complaints (14 in the last 2 months on this website alone) i wouldn't be surprised to see this business model under real scrutiny.

title: Stuck overseas waiting to fly home for 2 weeks
body:
While overseas I was diagnosed with DVT and advised that after a 5 day hospital stay I would need to be flown home.

The hospital contacted TID for me, and as soon as I was discharged I rang the emergency number to discuss being flown home.  

After providing all my paperwork, I was finally told 5 days later that TID agreed that my insurance would cover my flights home.  After being asked to provide a "fit to fly" from my doctor, I was deemed "unfit" due to blood test results.  After 4 days my blood test was within parameters but it took a further 3 days for TID to agree after receiving the report. 

4 days later I am still waiting for flights home as they are having trouble obtaining medical clearance from the airline which are apparently always a difficult airline to obtain clearance from.  It has been over 2 weeks that I have been stranded here on my own waiting to fly home.

After calling today in tears I was told that maybe they could fly me via a different route on a different airline and will look into it.  Why was this not done earlier if the original airline are always problematic??

This whole time I have had to continually chase for updates, and have been handled by 4 different case workers so far.

To me, this company doesn't seem to care how long it takes to get me home, never mind my fragile emotional state at having to abandon a 6 week trip 2 weeks in, then spend a further 2 weeks on my own in a foreign country waiting yo go home.  I should have just paid for my own flights home 2 weeks ago!!!

Extremely slow at confirming cover during emergency situation and take excessive time to arrange flights home.

title: Difficult beyond belief
body:
I just got off the phone to Covermore for about the fifteenth time. I am trying to finalise payments for a claim launched in APRIL for a trip scheduled for May, which I had to cancel due to job loss. It is November and I am still getting nowhere trying to arrange reimbursement for my flights. 

Everything was *in principle* fine for my claim. I had all the paperwork I needed for accommodation and flights, plus some invoices for smaller items and a hotel stay on the way to our destination. Unlike most people, I actually did read the PDS, from start to finish. This was going to be my first, VERY hard earned, holiday and I wanted to enjoy it worry-free.

From the very beginning, it's been a case of me having to chase and chase and chase this company at every step of the process. At NO POINT has anyone from Covermore called me, it's always me chasing them. 

Heard absolutely nothing after submitting my paperwork online through the (extremely crap) "Claim Tool", so rang them to see what was happening as it was well after the 10 business days they require to assess something. Their on-hold message reminds you to use the online claim tool to "check the progress of your claim" ? which gives you some absolutely useless and ambiguous directive such as "your claim is being assessed". Wow, thanks for that. The offshore call centre staff are rude and under informed, and if they?d shut up for 10 seconds to let you speak instead of arguing over the top of you, you might be able to get somewhere. I must say though, the Australian call centre staff I?ve dealt with were in fact very good, even if the system they work within sucks. In fact, I have had a very strong feeling at times that this process is deliberately difficult as a means of discouraging you from pursuing the claim to the stage of reimbursement, and I have made this observation a number of times to my partner. 

I submitted paperwork, it got "lost". I resubmitted more paperwork, no one could find my emails. When they finally did get their act together and either find or properly look at my paperwork (which I had to call them several times to action), sorry ? it?s not legitimate. A bloody email invoice from Booking.com CLEARLY stating the date, a booking number and the cancellation policy for the booking ? the only form of paperwork provided now that everyone does everything online ? is apparently not acceptable. I got so fed up with the stonewalling I threatened to talk to the ombudsman and my lawyer, and it must have put the fear of God into them because things started to actually happen after that!

But then came the absolute saga involved in ACTUALLY getting payment. Twice I called, and got the ?not sure why those payments haven?t been made? excuse. The third time I called after no payment had hit my account two weeks later (despite being told it ?will be 2-3 days) I was advised the payments had been ?returned?. I checked they had the right bank details ? yep. Apparently ?this just happens sometimes?. That?s actually what the lady I spoke to on that occasion told me. No that doesn?t just happen. There is no reason for my banking institution to return an inward payment from my account. So then they said they could write some cheques. Ok fine, now we?re getting somewhere. 

But I am STILL trying to get reimbursement for my flights, and just now when I called the system they use for looking at claims was down. Ok, IT problems happen, but no offer to call me back later. ?We don?t make outcalls from here, try calling again later.? 

After a ridiculous six month process, after which I?m only halfway there, Covermore should be bending over backwards to get in touch with me, the very least they could do for the unreasonably long delays.

About six weeks ago I spoke to another rude call centre member who informed me that they had to ascertain whether the taxes on the flights were non-refundable. They needed something from Flight Centre in writing to state this, presumably so they could reimburse me for the whole lot. So, Flight Centre say they?ve passed on these details a couple of times now. Covermore say they haven?t received what they need. And so on this ridiculous circus goes, and I?m expected to be making phone calls to Flight Centre to chase this up. Apparently Covermore can?t even make phone calls to Flight Centre directly to just resolve this issue on their customer?s behalf. And I?m not getting anywhere, because apparently everyone?s done their job. 

I have taken COUNTLESS hours out of my time to essentially do Covermore?s work. It has been so difficult that at times I?ve got off the phone in tears of frustration because I really need this money refunded and I cannot for the life of me understand how something straightforward can become so drawn out and painful. HOW can it possibly take SIX MONTHS when all correct and proper paperwork was provided?! 

I would absolutely NOT recommend Covermore and I will never use them again for any travel plans, and they have been so appallingly unwilling to resolve this that I would actively discourage anyone I knew from using them as well.

body: The policy was easy to set up but when trying to make a claim different story. Ringing from a ship is not easy as you have to go through operator on board the ship before you get transferred, and then when i do get transferred saying no they can't find me in the system that I am not insured with them. So now I start to panic and think maybe I went with someone else. While Still on the ship I try another insurance mob and they so no I am not with them. For some reason i couldn't find any emails from the insurer who I had gone with. So then I go and check my bank account and see who I've paid for travel insurance and sure enough it's the group 1cover who I first rang where my cover is. We were only on the cruise for 3 days in Sydney so I waited till we were back in Sydney to let them know that I am insured with them only to be told that I am not covered. body: We were a little hesitant in relying on the TID excess insurance when hiring a rental car in NZ because it had the potential of leaving us seriously out of pocket if things went wrong. body:
Tried to extend my policy the day before it expired. The 1cover system responded with errors after multiple submissions to extend. Credit card has no issues. Emailed them, was provided a different quote that was $62 _more_ than I was quoted online. Long story short, after over 15 emails back and forth over the day trying to pay them (they all went home once their work day was over so I had no response for hours), the clocked ticked over and I was left without cover.
Fully aware of what had happened, 1cover then offered me a 'Residents Already Overseas' policy for $200 more than the original online extension quote, with a 7 day waiting period, and told me now there was nothing they could! Yes, really. I bought a new policy with World Nomads instead.

title: Complete waste of money
body:
I had my skis stolen/mistakenly taken while I was eating lunch. The skis were stored in the only place you're allowed to store them on the mountain, though this isn't covered as it's deemed to be leaving them "unsupervised in a public place". Despite the fact their definitions saying "unsupervised" specifically applies to "luggage and personal effects" which are then defined as your suitcases and articles you're wearing. I would also have thought this was more intended for leaving them outside the front of the supermarket, rather than the designated storage racks.

Looking further into it, there's almost no circumstances you will be covered should you skis be stolen or damaged. If you somehow are covered, the maximum coverage is $200, which you would struggle to buy a pair from Cash Converters with.

The claims process is also pretty average. I got an email telling my claim had being decided, though it didn't tell me what the outcome was. If I wanted to know, I had to ring them or email them, the online claim status also wouldn't work for me. I rung them, waited on hold for over 20 mins before hanging up. I tried sending a few emails over the next few weeks and got no reply so rung them again. To their credit, they did answer pretty quickly this time, though only to tell me bad luck.

I'm not too sure if any other insurance companies would have been any better as trying their best to not pay out seems pretty common.

I do not understand how every travel provider (flights/accommodation/hire cars/day tours/events) has allowed me to cancel with a refund or kept deposits and rescheduled bookings yet InsureandGo would not allow me to do likewise. You have taken payment for a risk that no longer applied as we were unable to travel anyway due to Government restrictions and flight cancellations. 

I will never use InsureandGo again and would not recommend this company to any traveller.
Shame on you!

Bad and inflexible service

title: Extremely difficult to deal with.
body:
Booked the trip of a lifetime to U/K and Ireland back in May / June 2017 for travel in Aug 2018, got travel insurance Sept 2017.
Diagnosed with cancer June 2018 cancelled trip due to commencement of treatment,  no prior signs or symptoms. Submitted a travel insurance claim mid June. staff continually stalling by asking for more information, ( already supplied ) and then told we will get an answer in 7 to 10 days 6 times so far. 
The stress and worry they are putting us through is almost unbearable considerinmg my current circumstance.
I honestly believe they are waiting for my cancer to do it's job or hoping we will drop it.
Having to resort to legal action.
My advise is stay well clear of Allianz Insurance, we will gladly take you money but how dare you make a claim.

title: Middling - read the fine print!
body: I rated this 5 stars (once) cos it was easy to get insured, despite a pre-existing hard condition. However I later discovered that that condition was Excluded so cover may have been useless for main purpose. Be very wary if in the same position.

body: It was very easy to set up on line. We have made no claims from either trip. This was my second time using Allianz comprehensive travel insurance. I feel it was good value for money.

title: Big Let Down In Time Of Need
body:
Currently stuck in UK with my wife sick in hospital.
I phoned the UK helpline to check if I was covered, it related to a pre-existing condition so we were not covered as expected. This is fair enough.
However I then asked if I could extend my insurance cover as we might be here for some time and want to be covered against theft, accidents, etc. The UK helpline said they could renew it for me and asked how long I needed it, I said I didn't know how long my wife was going to be sick so they suggested that I wait until the day my policy expired and then call back and renew it with them as I may have more information by then.
So I called them back on the last day of the policy only to be told that they could not renew it in the UK and I would have to call the New Zealand office which being 12 hours ahead was already closed.
I called them the next day (having to make an international call from a hotel room) and was told that the policy had now expired and the only way to get cover was to buy a new more expensive policy. I tried to reason with the call centre that I had been given the wrong information from their UK representative but they couldn't care less, they just kept telling me that I had spoken to the wrong people and the policy could not be extended. Asked to speak to a manager but was told that no one was there and it would be a waste of time anyway.
So don't expect any support from this company if you are in an emergency situation, all they are interested in is making more money out of your crisis. Shame on you 1cover for using a customers bad fortune and trying to exploit it and make their stressful and tough time even worse by leaving them without cover.

body:

I have yet to make a claim on previous travels so I have no experience on dealing with an "InsureandGo" insurance claim.

title: They could have been better - room for improvement
body: Hospitalised in Malaysia with pneumonia and pleurisy for 6 days. Arrived ER at midnight and all set for admission by 3 am only to be told Allianz Global assist 24/7 doctor in Australia had to approve and he was in bed and not in the office for 5 hours. Rather than wait 5 hours on a gurney in the ER corridor I stumped up $5000 surety on my credit card for instant admission. Lesson is to not count on 24/7 global assistance sales pitch and have plenty of credit on one's credit card.  Subsequent communications with Allianz about getting me home were poor and characterised by unreturned calls and being left in the dark so I organised my own flights back. Then it was three months before my claim was fully settled. As a retired engineer I was well able to argue my case with the claims dept and had plenty of time to make sure I was not ripped off.  Many others would have given up and had their claim rejected as mine initially was. I doubt that I would use them again.

title: Thank you
body:
1Cover kept us up to date with our claim and successfully paid most of our claim.
We were claiming the difference we had to pay for new flights when British Airways cancelled a connecting flight from Madrid to Casablannca.
We appreciate their assistance.

title: Instant decision
body:
We have used 1Cover several times before, but I still shopped around, however I found 1Cover to still be number one, so in future now that we will be travelling more often, no need to shop around, just go straight to 1 Cover. Good value and straightforward to set up.

November 22nd 2017 Update: Save time by going back to 1Cover

As usual before travelling, we compared insurance companies, but again found 1Cover to be best value. We had to address age and health queries and found this process effective and straightforward. We received assistance promptly when asked for. Next time we travel, it'll be a quick and easy decision to return to 1Cover.

title: Very poor service indeed
body: We had some problems with our most recent overseas holiday to Europe and decided to lodge my first travel insurance claim.  I collected all the data and emailed it to covermore and the first issue is the gateway into covermore is tiny and the claim was rejected and I was not aware so after I found out had to break the claim into 6 tiny bits and re email and then they don't process the claim in a timely and efficient manner which is standard procedure for bad insurance companies.  It is best for them to delay and string out the whole process.  It would be nice if they answered the phone in a timely manner as well. It is easy to pay the insurance premium but what is really important is how they process a claim.

title: Don't bother! Read the fine print and forget it if you have a Mental Health Condition!
body:
Purchased through Flight centre as their preferred Insurance company. 
Had to make a claim after cancelling my trip due to Mental health Issues. 
Customer service through my claim was non existent. The process is incredibly invasive, timely and unprofessional with hidden loop holes that Cover More happily use. Claim was rejected based on a "pre-existing" condition, however no actual medical records stated this they simply relied on a GP statement that they chose not to follow up or research. They discriminate against Mental Health and are completely ignorant in the matter.
Their sales representatives are incompetent, under trained and plain rude.

If you are discriminated against with a mental health condition by Cover More get in contact with Beyond Blue or [name removed]. Take your matter further.
[link removed]
https://www.beyondblue.org.au/about-us/about-our-work/discrimination-in-insurance/stop-insurance-discrimination 

They have lost me as a future client and will never recommend them to a fellow traveller again.

title: Great value, however not great on claims!
body: The policy was great value and easy to set up, hence why I selected it. However i missed a transit flight due to being unwell in the bathrooms, and while trying to organise a contingency flight I was left on hold for over an hour, at which point I had to hang up and take care of the issue alone otherwise miss the replacement flight. It did make a stressful situation, being a female traveling on her own in the Middle East. I followed the situation up twice via email to see whether I was eligible for a reimbursement, but no response was ever received!

title: Covered pre existing conditions at an additional cost
body: I have just purchased the Travel Insurance and was accepted for declared pre-existing conditions. It was an expensive exercise but I was prepared to pay what I needed to pay to be covered. I have used InsureandGo for a previous trip and was happy with the policy. On both occasions, I applied online and had no problems-it was a very straightforward process. Hopefully I will not have to make any claims and am unable to comment on that process as my travel is for 2020.

title: Excellent value, coverage and service
body: I have had an Annual  Multi Trip policy for over 5 years now and I think it is excellent value. I have had a couple of minor claims and all OK. Recently I had a more serious accident - blew my knee- in Japan and the TID Emergency team were just excellent. Their first concern was my welfare and ability to manage. They kept in contact and then arranged and paid for our early flight home.  It all worked seamlessly. title: Read fine prints before you buy!
body:
We recently came back from a frustrated trip. The trip has got cancelled, we did not know until the last minute, airlines could not give us any written evidence until we got home. The flight cancelled due to flight maintenance according to the airlines. And my travel plan has been rejected because of that. I would highly recommended to go through all the fine prints before you even purchase travel insurance from them! Pretty sure insurance company got themselves covered pretty well!

title: very bureaucratic + no help in an emergency
body:
Ive used covermore for years as they seem high quality however i agree with the "bureaucratic" label. ive now had 2 bad experiences with covermore -  (1) my father died while i was away last year and i had to clarify whether it was a pre-existing illness before theyd agree to pay for an earlier flight back. he was in his late 80s and with cancer however medical opinion before i left was that he was fine, however he went downhill rapidly after i left. anyway they refused to give me a ruling on whether theyd refund me or even guidelines on their decision making - i was just supposed to spend $$ paying for a new last minute airfare home and theyd decide after that whether to refund me. 
(2) recently went on an alaskan cruise that was cancelled a couple of days before i was to fly out (mechanical failure) and meet friends in vancouver for the cruise. Our agent managed to find a cruise leaving a day later from seattle nearby - different line. No worries i paid for $4000 cancellation cover, that will cover new hotels, a new internal flight, transport from vancouver to seattle plus new hotel costs right!!?? NO - my expensive cancellation cover didnt cover the cruise being cancelled at the last minute - they deem a cruise to be "transportation" and transportation is excluded  from my cover (although that wasnt mentioned when i got cover for my cruise holiday of course).
In short they're not a firm i would trust to do the right thing in an emergency theyre more a bureaucracy that will trawl through the fine print looking for an excuse not to pay. Not what you need in an emergency or tragedy.
easy to  buy
bureaucratic, lacking in initegrity and compassion, dishonest

body:
This is a quote from Cover-More:
 "It is impossible for travel insurance to cover everything, as this would make premiums extremely high"

We Paid for I months Platinum with no excess $633 plus Stamp Duty, that equates to $7,667.52 for 12 months. how much higher can they go? To read the PDS you have to be a bit of a bush lawyer and to "really" understand that Cover-More don't really cover anything.
Our flight was delayed 7 hours due to lightning strike which caused us to miss our connecting flight and also the first nights accommodation at that destination. Our claim was for a mere $300. The claim was denied. They called it "Operational"  British Airways sent a letter to say: "Damage during flight ops"  The claim was still denied. 

If you want to get technical, they do pay if there is a strike, but I doesn't say what sort of strike. We had lightning strike, is that the same? Will you pay now? I doubt it...
We still have lots of traveling to do but we wont be going to Cover-More with our hard earned cash. BIG MISTAKE

title: Flight delay cover is very restrictive
body:
I tried to claim for costs relating to a flight being delayed, but my claim was rejected, since CoverMore only pay out for flight delays in the following scenarios:
Disruption of your scheduled transport because of riot, strike or civil commotion; or
Your scheduled transport being delayed for at least 12 hours due to severe weather conditions (and in this case they only pay $250).
Neither of these applied in my case. There are many other reasons why a flight might be delayed, and this policy gives no peace of mind that other scenarios will be covered. Unfortunately I had to pay extra costs to avoid being stranded at Bangkok airport at midnight, when I had already been travelling for 24 hours and just wanted to get home.
CoverMore wasn't even particularly cheap. I have used them before but now don't want to use them again, and I will not recommend them to other travellers.

title: Paid the wrong person
body:
My brother was estranged from his ex-wife, had an accident in Bali and needed family to be with him (on life support) didn't know who would be next of kin to make decisions. I paid for his ex-wife and myself to travel to Perth, only to find on arrival he had been flown to Singapore.She had an intervention order on him at the time. We then flew to Singapore I paid for flights to Perth, accomodation, taxis, food and then my airfare to Singapore and the accomodation in Singapore and everything else for the both of us. She had no money. He passed away a few days later.I paid $6500.00 all up in expenses. I put in a claim to Cover More but she didn't for months (not that she had much to claim for) as I had paid for everything except her flight to Singapore (her mother paid for that). I found out that when a person passes away any claim approved would be paid to the Estate. As a will could not be found she found one from many years ago and she was the Executor. Cover More used my original receipts to pay the Estate and now she wont give me a dollar after all i did for her!

The Estate was paid and not the person who paid for everything

title: Terrible, Look Elsewhere
body:
My Sony DSC HX50V got accidentally dropped in a flowing river whilst taking photos of some some stunning falls. I'm glad I didn't. 
Upon return i filed an insurance claim with 1Cover online.
This is their reply:

"Thank you for submitting your travel insurance claim with us. 
I can confirm that we have completed your claim and it has been approved for $90.40.
Your policy had an $100.00 excess applicable that has been deducted from your settlement."

That was a close to $500rrp camera.
All I got at the end of the day was $90 regardless of their claim to be $100 for the excess. 
The lady on the phone kept on insisting on the disclosure of the product policy which I don't have an issue with. I didn't take this cover, the wife did. 
The issue I'm having with and at which she became rude is why would I take insurance cover if I don't get covered? 
Regardless of how much an object has depreciated (or has it? what if some items go up in value or maintain it like SLR lens) An insurance company has no value to a client if at the end of the day I cannot have that item back or a replacement in equal or better value. 

When I proceeded to tell the lady I was going to take my feedback online she had the rudest voice tone and hang up on me. I also stated that it is pointless to insure old items, only brand new ones within a few days of purchase. She agreed. It has all been audio recorded.
Even if a brand new item is insured, a few days old item will likely be depreciated as 1 month old and depreciation and excess will again make it less likely to take their cover. 

Rule number 1: The customer has the money, he makes the rules or else you as a company are out. The more people will wake up and think this way the less we get taken for a ride and we as Aussies are taken for a ride here down under from all points of view. 

No company in the past has ever done this, i went twice in 17 years thru similar incidents and the replacement was better than the original. 

As such I will ensure all my clients that I come in contact with on a daily basis will be told what 1Cover has to offer when it comes to insuring their valuables.

title: Scammers - take your money but don't pay out claims
body:
In August I had a trip to Scandinavia, and on the return flights to Australia, the Etihad flight to Sydney was delayed in Abu Dhabi for 13 hours; so I missed the Sydney to Armidale flight. In fact, I had to wait in Sydney 12 hours for the next available flight to Armidale as the Abu Dhabi flight, which was supposed to land in Sydney at 6:25 am, 31st August, landed just before 7 pm, 31st August. So I had to purchase another ticket for the Sydney to Armidale flight. This made me angry enough with the fact that I would have to have another day off work - never mind the fact that CUA Health, managed by Allianz 'Global Assist' (assist who, I ask), refused to pay out my claim on the purchasing of another ticket to Armidale. 
It started with the phone call to make the claim. "Oh, we won't cover that. Don't bother claiming." After pointing out that, according to their own brochure, if I have to pay another ticket due to the delay of one flight from reasons outside of my control, they will cover the cost of up to $2000 (I am only asking for $390). I could not afford the flight as I had car rego and service to pay out. (My holiday was due to stress leave, not because I could really afford it) She said I could put in a claim for consideration due to the circumstances, but not to expect anything. I purchased this travel insurance because I had health insurance with CUA (which I have cancelled). According to Allianz, they would contact me in 10 business days. I only heard back from them 12 business days later because I think CUA Health had contacted them, as I told them why I was cancelling my health insurance with them. ALLIANZ wanted me to prove the flight delay of 13 hours in Abu Dhabi was not my fault. The airline only lists the delay as 'operational reasons'. We sat on the tarmac 2 hours, due to some problem with the fuel pipes. Not long after, we were ordered off the plane, told we would be changing aircraft. At first they said 4 hours, then 4 more...nightmare. How could that possibly be my fault?
Yesterday (26/9/14) I responded to a phone message to Allianz asking me to call them back - they didn't say why. This operator was, politely put; an absolute halfwit and very rude. She seemed to think I was claiming for 'additional costs' which to them, only means hotel accommodation and meals, and not additional flights at all. She refused to acknowledge that according to their brochure, I am covered for the additional flight, and argued with me about the details of the claim. She then actually seemed surprised when I said I was lodging a formal complaint. 
I know they won't pay out my claim even with the complaint, however I have already been told by FOS that it is a necessary procedure. 
As far as I am concerned, Allianz Global Assistance is a scam. 
Stay away form them

November 20th 2014 Udpate:
I'm updating an earlier post; this has been ongoing since the 1st of September 2014. 
I had to purchase a second flight ticket due to a 13 hour delay in Abu Dhabi, the cost of $390.00. I was under the understanding that I was covered for up to $2000 if I had to purchase a second ticket due to a flight delay of 6 or more hours. 
They claim I am not, even though it clearly states in one of their letters to me that:
"Section 3.1 - Additional Expenses 3.1.1 We will pay f) In addition, we will reimburse your reasonable additional travel and accommodation expenses if a disruption to your journey arises from any of the following reasons: an incident involving your mode of transport. You must have written confirmation of the incident from an official body in the country where the incident happened." 
I have two letters confirming the details of what happened in Abu Dhabi, one from the airport, one from the airline. 
Allianz refused to pay out the claim; their phone operators are very rude and (politely put) stupid. Three times I was told that my claim had gone to the complaints department for independent viewing. Three times the claim was simply resubmitted to the same consultant who, of course, gave the same answer. She never answered any of my questions at all. In the end it only went to their Internal Disputes Resolution Officer because the Financial Ombudsman gave me the address to email and I sent a formal complaint about the handling of my case. 
They apologized for the treatment I had received, but still refused to pay my claim.
They keep on using documents I never received as reference to their reasons for not paying out the claim, refusing the existence of the documents I have that support my claim. They refuse to acknowledge I do not have these documents they mention. I looked some of them up on their website and these files don't exist. 
November the 2nd the case went to the Financial Ombudsman, and within the first 24 hours of FOS taking on the claim, Allianz offered me $300 of the $390 they owe me, because they don't want the Financial Ombudsman to investigate them. 
I said fine, I'm sick of this (I suppose the $90 is a fee for 'processing' the claim) 
So I accepted the offer of $300 to settle the dispute. 
They of course, have not paid me this amount. Nor have they contacted me to inform me of any problems processing the payment. 
If they have not paid me by Monday the 24th November I am relaunching a dispute with the Financial Ombudsman and will naturally, ignore any offer to have the dispute resolved without investigation. 
They are a disgrace - stay away from them. If they are refusing to pay out a claim they do owe you, tough it out - report them to FOS - the more people report them, the sooner someone is going to have to do something about these liars.
I forgot to update this - they didn't pay me by the 24th of November 2014, so I contacted the Financial Ombudsman that day. The Financial Ombudsman said that maybe Allianz didn't have the correct details; yet without contacting me again at all, I was suddenly paid the next day. 
Like I said, just stay away from them - there are other travel insurance agencies. And if you do have the misfortune to find out what they are like when making a claim, report them, and don't give up no matter how long they try to drag it out.

My claim was only around $100 above the excess, and compared to some other people who have complained this is trivial, but I'm glad I found out how badly they handle claims and I can avoid them in future. body:
Booked insurance on the 26th of Feb and assured countless times on recorded calls up until the worldwide travel ban that I would be covered in the event of a ban. This information was also displayed on their website during the early stages of March explaining you may claim under the cancellation clause if you had not yet departed if a level 4 travel ban was put in place. Apparently the message isn?t being heard well enough by budget direct that you can?t just mislead people and assure them multiple times via phone calls and website updates that they can make a claim before a certain date and then back pedal when it suits them. Jan 30th we should have known?! You could still travel to China at that point! 30+ days to receive a response and I am appalled that I have to wait another 15+ days for a response to my complaint. 

Myself and 8 other consumers in the same boat have now created a group where we will be escalating this further to the Ombudsman and to the media if our circumstances are not resolved promptly. Feel free to get in touch with me if you have similarly been mislead by Budget Direct!

title: Not recommended for corporate or personal travel.
body:
I don't usually make comments or reviews- but my experience with covermore has warranted a response.  I am happy to be contacted by other potential corporate clients regarding my experience.

I recently travelled to Cambodia (as a corporate client) and had the unfornate experience of losing my IPhone 4 in a hammock.  This is an essential tool of my profession so I needed a prompt response.  I took time out of my holiday to make sure I had the required police report in the 24 hour time frame required.  

Thankfully, I was glad to be covered by covermore... or so I thought.  After two rounds of lodging the required paperwork, my claim was successful - albeit the amount refunded to me was surprisingly low.  Well below the ability for me to replace my phone with the same or similar model.  This was thanks to a 'depreciation model' that removed more than two-thirds of the _replacement cost_ of the phone.  (addit:  there is nothing in the PDS regarding the depreciation model and how this is calculated).  

I know there are other reviews here that describe the disappointment with the amount refunded, even after a successful claim.

I lodged an appeal, however am still waiting to hear back from covermore (I actually had to pursue them to acknowledge receipt of appeal).  While this is still a work in progress, I have been extremely frustrated by the process.

Ultimately I have been disappointed with the turnaround time and communication surrounding my claim, especially as a corporate client.  There are a number of other companies that colleague and friends have travelled with who have made successful claims for similar experiences (for example QBE, TID).

Travel insurance is only as good as the claim process and after sales support, based on my experience I would be using covermore again for either corporate or personal travel.  This is a shame as I have used them several times in the past and recommended them to friends (however have not had to make a claim with them until now).

title: 2 experiences, one good, one poor - check your policy.
body:
Oh holiday in Koh Tao in Thailand I came down with Dengue Fever. I was evacuated by ferry and ambulance to Koh Samui and spent 5 days on a drip in a rather upmarket hospital room. 
As far as the medical costs were concerned I never saw a bill or paid a cent. To this day I have no idea what it cost. As I was only semi conscious when I entered the emergency room the nurses got a guarantee of payment within 2 hours (I think, I had a temperature of 40 and was seeing unicorns riding tandem bicycles). An Australian nurse called twice to check my condition and the treatment I was being provided and if there were any pre-existing conditions for which cover could be denied.
I didn't bother claiming for my hostel room, as I only had a day left on it anyway ($15), nor did I bother claiming on my divemaster course as I got half my money back from the vendor anyway as I had done half the course.

4 Months later I was in Nepal, and got really bad diarrhea (firing both ends simultaneously and cursing the lord). I was unable to contact Allianz as I was placed on hold until all my phone credit ran out (20 minutes). I tried to make a claim upon returning to Australia, but the excess amount was not reached (medical bills cost about $150 and the excess was $250). I had some complications (an anal fissure and thrush infection for which I was prescribed vagina medication) upon returning and was informed that once you return to Australia you are on your own. All up those would not have reached the excess anyway and they were right to say no.

CONCLUSION - Came through for me when I really needed it, but were firm in saying no when i was not covered. if you want to make petty claims lower your excess.

title: simply the best

two years ago when I made a claim one cover paid all my lost and broken items excellent customer service I received  
I would recommend you to any one

title: Very happy customer and will definitely purchase again
body: I have used insure and go 6 times when travelling and have been very happy with the service each time

title: Delaying payment technique
body: I'm writing a review on behalf of my parents. My parents booked a holiday to New Zealand and 3 months prior to departing my mother was diagnosed with breast cancer. She had the cancer removed and her doctors advised that she needed to have 20 weeks of chemotherapy, and then 3 weeks of radiation. Her doctors said she was not fit to travel as she will still be having active treatment. We called to find out what we need to do to cancel the trip and claim back any losses. The staff were very nice and told us that we needed letters from specific professionals (oncologist, GP and travel agent) and the exact wording of these letters. Unfortunately they didn't mention that we actually needed the professionals to fill out medibank specific forms. After this, they then needed to access my mothers full health record and obtaining permission with each email response taking multiple days. Once they had gained access and it proved my mother genuinely had cancer and didn't know about it prior to booking the holiday, they then weren't happy with travel agents invoices saying how much money was refunded to us. They now required letters specifically from the individual companies that they had to cancel travel arrangements with. As you can see we are now 6 months in and we have received one part refund. Very frustrating process.

title: Value for money. Easy to obtain!
body: Have used this travel insurance 3 times. It is very easy to set up. Fortunately haven't had to make a claim.. Very good value compared to other companies offering travel insurance.

title: Easy to purchase with a pre-existing medical condition

title: Travel insurance the easy way

title: Gone sadly downhill
body:
Lost count but probably have had more than a dozen policies (family and single) at least

Cerberus  ?deals?( and I use the term loosely) with the claims for TID, and obstructive

title: What a con!
body:
Went to Hawaii May 2013. Paid for comprehensive travel insurance with1cover. Flights were cancelled by an an airlines. Out of our control. They do not pay up unless there's a terrorist attack or civil riots, so they told us. Their comprehensive policies are not so comprehensive. Pay a little more for an insurance company you can trust. Put in a standard claim and refused to reimburse us.

title: Worse experience
body:

Doctor recommended not to travel unless in a lie down position. Asked insurance they said it need to upgrade ticket to business class, i mentioned i did not have funds to do so, they said they could not do anything on my behalf. 6 hours before flight insurance said business class was approved, but i had to pay for and then claim a refund, then got a new email that i need to see doctor again few hours before my departure  and insurance will need few days to check my case, could not afford wait... had the worse experience travelling 24 hours with my medical conditions... once i got home i saw an email from insurance saying that they approved the business update. The catch, they knew the time i had to departure, they approved after i left, they did not bother call me, it was all done by email... like if you are on holidays how easy is to access email...

I paid about 100 dollars for that so i recommend spend a little bit more and use a descent company, because once you are in a bad shape you regret the few dollars your saved by using a cheap insurance company.

title: Insureandgo or take your money and go
body:
What an absolutely shocking company to deal with. My wife took out a yearly silver policy with this company in November 2019. In December 2020 she suffered a fall resulting in a back injury that prevented us from taking our cruise in January. We supplied, repeatedly, medical documents upon request plus all the travel details, what we had been able to received back from airlines, accommodation etc and claimed the balance. Of the approx $7,000 we spent we were able to receive back, by our own means much of that, leaving a claim to Insureandgo of $2,700. After months of back and forth with this company they knocked the claim back due to a previous injury some 21years prior! We then sent a letter from her doctor, he, explaining that her previous injury had no bearing on her claim, at which point internal disputes re-evaluated the claim and agreed to process the claim. Disputes said they would send a confirmation letter within the week. That was March 31st! We have received nothing from them and have emailed and phoned many many times in the last 6 months with them promising correspondence and still nothing. Insureandgo may have won industry awards but they obviously do not want to fulfill their legal obligations when the claims begin to mount up due to Covid-19. Our claim was well before the virus hit.

title: Travel Insurance that doesn't cover you for injuries sustained on your vacation
body:
I recently returned from vacation in North America and UK.  Sadly the last leg of my journey from Dubai to Sydney was not a pleasant experience, my seat had a massage function that could not be turned off - after 14 hours of vibration I suffered a slipped disc.  This is the first time in my life I have experienced any back issues.  6 hours into the flight I started to experience the back pain, the flight was full so I could not move to another seat.  By the end of the flight I was curled over with pain, I couldn't walk properly.  Sleep was impossible for 2 weeks after the incident.

I was informed I needed to make two claims; one from the airline for the cost of the flight and the other with Allianz Travel Insurance for my medical bills.  I submitted my medical costs immediately, I visited my local GP twice and Health Centre twice which included X-Rays, chiro and osteo treatment.  I was also prescribed anti-inflammatory tablets and pain killers to help with sleep.

Today I received notice from Allianz Travel Insurance they would not cover my medical expenses, despite the injury occurring during my vacation.  I had taken the most comprehensive travel insurance policy with Allianz.  They said Medicare would cover the costs - which they do not.  Medicare does not cover Health Centre costs and only a proportion of the GP costs. 

This injury is well documented, I have a report from the airline, the cabin steward, even the pilot was aware of the issue - during the flight he contacted the maintenance team in Dubai to check what they could do to fix the chair.

I travel 3-5 months of the year, mostly for business and I have never heard of a travel policy that doesn't cover you for an injury sustained overseas.  For example; in 1997 I fractured my knee in Thailand and the insurance company covered my hospital costs when I returned to Australia.  I will never use Allianz Travel Insurance ever again and will ensure this story is discussed and shared on as many social media sites as possible. 

By the way, the cost of my medical expenses was less than the cost of the insurance policy.  This company is deplorable.  Yes their policy is easy to use online - I agree with the comments made on this site, but equally the fine print needs to be read.  Allianz Travel does NOT cover you from start to finish - only in the middle.

She was awarded a small amount for her glasses but it was never put into her savings account. She contacted the office where she purchased the insurance and they were very helpful but she still has not received the claim amount. I will not use Cover-More again.

title: Worst insurance ever! Avoid the hassle and ignore the 'recommendation' from Flight Centre
body:
Recently had an overseas trip to Italy where unfortunately I was involved in a rental car crash. Although I was out of pocket 1000EUR from the hefty rental car insurance excess, I was comforted in knowing that I had taken out a comprehensive insurance policy withCover More which would reimburse me for most of the rental car insurance excess. How wrong was I...

I submitted the claim the day after the accident and heard nothing for 3 weeks. After spending 15min waiting on the phone to speak to someone, I was eventually told I needed to gather more paperwork (specifically, they wanted an 'invoice of the rental car repair invoice on the repairer's letterhead'). Seriously? How in God's name am I meant to get this paperwork? By this time, I was back in Australia so you can imagine the issues I had trying to get this paperwork over the internet from an Italian rental car company. Through no fault of my own, the rental car company never provided the paperwork and because of this my claim has been left in a perpetual state of limbo for 5 months. It will probably remain this way indefinitely.

This is my issue. The PDS for the insurance product clearly states that the policy covers 'rental car insurance excess'. There is no question that I was involved in an accident involving a rental car, and I demonstrated that I had been charged the 1000EUR rental car insurance excess (I supplied credit card transaction history, rental car company invoices & damage reports). Common sense would dictate that my claim should be successful, but because Cover-More have requested irrelevant paperwork which (they likely know) is completely unobtainable, they have stonewalled me.

Cover-more's reason behind asking for the 'repairer's invoice on the repairer's letterhead' was to verify that the rental car insurance excess charged to me was less than the cost of the repairs. Why does this matter? I have legitimately paid a rental car insurance excess, and as per the PDS I should have been covered.

To people who are reading this, please do yourself a favour and do some online searching on the different travel insurance providers as I'm sure there are better options out there.

Cover-More, you're lucky that you're in bed with the Flight Centre Limited group of companies, as I'm sure you'd be out of business otherwise.

title: Avoid and use Allianz instead
body:
Insured for Bali for 2 weeks.  Had to cancel trip due to illness deterioration of two family members (mother & brother) which resulted in both members passing away whilst we would have been overseas, so easiest decision in the world to make.
Unlike my choice of travel insurers.
All contact with InsureandGo made over the phone.  Advice given and duly noted.  InsureandGo will not pay out for loss of flights paid ($1400), loss of one night's accommodation at Ubud ($80), and especially loss of 10.5 days/nights at Holiday Inn Bali Baruna ($2,250).   Reasons for initial decision was basically, as both had pre-existing illness (cancer which became terminal after trip booked and paid for).  I could go ahead and submit claim but claim would not succeed based upon (ill at time) family members known cancer illness.
Absolutely heartless and clinical.
Had to cancel trip in early May 2015, family members passed away (with us at their side as should be, rather than swanning off to Bali).  Contact with InsureandGo over May and into June 2015, before giving up on them.  
Have better words for Garuda, dealt with them directly with lots of assistance from Melbourne office, received refund minus $100.  
Ubud accommodation would not return money, so gave that away (it's a family run business, only paid one night so lost $100, we could live with that.
18 months on and have now gone back to Bali Baruna to appeal for refund or at least something, citing circumstances of cancellation/non-show.  Still in process of this as at 07/12/2016.
Fellow travellers will have some understanding of the uncertainty and stress involved in these procedures when dealing with refund from accommodation places.  Add time line of 18 months.
All in all, based upon above, will leave it to the reader to make their own decisions about travel insurance, we certainly have.

title: After all, it's about protecting their business not about the clients
body:
My passport got lost days before my scheduled flight. After the approval of my tourist visa, I was waiting for my passport to arrive when I got a call from both the embassy and the courier service company confirming that it was lost in transit. This unfortunate event prompted me to cancel all my travel arrangement in Europe and to notify Allianz which I entrusted of my travel insurance should adverse situations happened -- so I'd thought. 

After gathering all documents and submitting it to Allianz for my claims, I got a call from their insurance agent, confirming that I would be able to claim only less than $100. That covers all my travel arrangement and accommodation. What upsets me the most is that I couldn't get any claims for my lost passport because as the agents said "it got lost before the trip and not during the trip". 

Allianz failed to understand that a passport is not just a mere document. As for myself, it holds all my valid visas. Now that I needed to apply for a new passport, I am also obliged to apply for new visas which would amount to more than $500. What's even worse is this event has caused me mental stress which just shrugged off by Allianz. The agent who I spoke to on the phone briefly laughed at me when I uttered this while saying "I understand where you are coming from". It is frustrating.

I thought travel insurance company will protect you and will be there for you should something bad happen but I failed to realise at the onset that it is a business after all. I also have my medical insurance with Allianz but I seriously thinking of moving to another company. I may not get anything from them if something happened to me because "it is what the policy is about".

title: Terrible service and process
body:
I am in the middle of the claims process and find the treatment by Covermore to be disgraceful.
I've had no response to emails (2) and have had to hang up twice while on hold, both in excess of 20 minutes.
I experienced theft while overseas and having incurred significant additional expenditure, have received no positive communication from Covermore whatsoever - it is now 2 months since the incident and I am no closer to compensation or rectification.  I cannot even replace the stolen equipment as they won't tell me if I will be reimbursed or get a voucher.
Just terrible.

September 19th 2017 Update: What a terrible company - avoid at all costs

In June I had my luggage stolen while in Europe, including our passports and camera equipment.  Including additional expenses incurred through getting emergency passports and cancelled accommodation bookings, the total of the claim was just over $20,000.  After three months of being put through the ringer and made to feel like I was the thief, Covermore have now offered to compensate me to the tune of $1,140 - that's right, about 5% of the value of my claim.  As an example, a lense I bought for $1,100 less than 2 years ago was valued at less than half, and because I couldn't find the receipt for an ipad I bought a couple for years ago I was awarded nothing at all - that happened to half a dozen items.  Why would I have a receipt for a pair of sunglasses or a pen I was given as a gift.
Covermore actually cover less - as a company you should be ashamed of yourselves and consumers beware - if you buy this policy, having your luggage stolen will be the least of your problems.  I am so glad nothing happened to any of us requiring medical attention - never again Covermore.

title: Good for some things NOT good for cancellations or delays
body:
Recently went to the USA and took out an annual policy. Flight was cancelled from sydney to LAX for 22 hours. I had booked a flight straight out of LAX to San Fran so lost flight, lost a night accomodation there and lost pre booked tours and had to book another last minute flight to SFO, which was very expensive. Although beyond my control, cancellations are not covered unless caused by such things as..strike or natural disaster. Qantas won't cough up a cent either!!! Don't be so deceitful and hide it away in the fine print. It clearly states in your policy that "WE WILL PAY , We will pay your cancellation fees and lost deposits for travel and accommodation arrangements that you have paid in advance and cannot recover in any other way if your journey is cancelled or shortened at ANY time through circumstances neither expected nor intended by you or outside your control". OK sounds good, But when contacted regarding this you say we need to also read the 'what we will not pay' which goes on to cover mechanical breakdown of any means or delays or rescheduling by bus, airline etc...... So in other words you pay nothing and the policy is worth nothing and I should not have wasted my money even buying a policy.

Explain it the large print don't hide it in the fine print!!!

body:
I found reading reviews helpful in making choices for recent big overseas trip, so will add my comments to this one.
1Cover were one of the cheapest companies offering travel insurance and they have a very user friendly website. Very straightforward process to obtain quote and complete purchase.
The saying goes, if you can't afford travel insurance, you can't afford to travel, as it turns out we returned after 6 weeks with 2 claims. One for passport theft (cost of emergency travel documents, replacement UK passport and cash), and a second for the fatal damage to my beloved new camera which bit the dust at St Peter's Sq.
The claim was submitted upon our return and the amount in full (less excess) paid in full and all in very good time.  We just had to provide a quote to fix the (un-repairable) camera. (And also had a police report for the pick-pocketing which I imagine would be mandatory. One tip would be to insist on making police report as the French Police at Gare du Nord gave us the brush off, but our B&B host advised us to go back and demand it, which we then did. I think they want to keep their statistics looking better than they are). 
No hesitation in fully recommending 1Cover. Our experience with them was excellent. I have since bought another policy for a trip to Australia which resulted in no claim.
Inexpensive, user friendly, efficient, easy to buy, quick to settle claim

title: I probably would have been better off cover-less ;)
body:
Use a different company. Personally, I would have been better off not purchasing the insurance at all and putting the money towards buying the emergency essentials I needed when my luggage was delayed.

I travelled from Australia to Europe earlier this year. My baggage went missing when I flew from Berlin to Copenhagen, and I received it approximately 75 hours later.

The PDS I accessed via Cover-more?s website (because, strangely enough it wasn't attached to the email with my certificate of insurance as it should have been) stated that for baggage delayed over 24 hours, up to $375 will be covered for emergency essentials on the ?Premium Plan?. According to the PDS, this amount doubles after 72 hours. The PDS also states that if you are on the ?Inbound Plan?, only up to $200 will be covered. 

When I got home, I lodged my claim and received a letter pretty soon after, which seemed promising. That is, until I opened it and discovered they were offering me $200- much less than I claimed, and less than I paid for my insurance in the first place. Further, it came with no explanation of why the full amount I was claiming wasn't being paid. I called Cover-more and they assured me this was the amount I was entitled to with my policy. I almost believed them and thought I?d made a mistake... Maybe I was on the Inbound Plan and not the Premium Plan. So I googled Cover-more's Inbound plan. Turns out that the policy is for "non-Australians travelling to and within Australia?. Seeing as I am an Australian who was traveling in Europe, that doesn?t seem right to me.

I am obviously not on the Inbound Plan, and I am claiming less than the $750 maximum benefit limit outlined in the PDS for the Premium Plan with receipts for every purchase. So why am I not being given this full amount? Why am I not even being paid the $375 that at least corresponds with the relevant policy plan? I don?t know either because Cover-more hasn?t responded to my emails. Cheers guys. Maybe they will now?!?!

title: Ripped off
body:
My recent experience with InsureandGo is the worst experience I have ever had with a travel insurance company..and I have traveled a lot and taken out many travel insurance policies. I had to delay a trip to Europe in January 2016 due to a severe virus. I thought the right thing to do was inform InsureandGo of the changed departure date (knowing how insurance co's are with not being notified of changes). So I called and advised them I had changed my departure from Melbourne to one week later. Before I knew it my original policy was cancelled and a new policy was set, starting from the revised departure date. When I questioned this approach I was informed that's the way they "must" deal with this situation. I thought they would simply note the revised departure date - I wasn't looking for a refund of any sought. 

So now I have a new policy - But, the reason for my delay, the virus, has been noted as a "pre-existing condition" and unless I pay a premium of $2000, yes $2000 I cannot claim against the virus, not for anything. Of course, the original policy is now "inactive" and I cannot claim against it either..and, of course it cannot be re-activated. A week after first contacting them I had to cancel the trip due to the severity of the virus. I have been left unable to claim for a single cent due to this "Switch of policies". This is clearly InsureandGo's way of shutting off all possibility of paying out on a claim made prior to departure. I am in the hole for about $2000 now. I am sure this is legal but it is far from moral and possibly not ethical, in terms of business practice. 

They did refund the cost of both policies, after a fight and after I was told by one call center staff member, I could not get a refund on the second policy, despite being told there was a 14 day cooling off period, because it was linked to the original policy. Strangely though, this supposed "link" did not allow me to make a claim. The two policies were linked when it favoured them and not linked when it favoured them. This change of "interpretation" of their own terms and conditions has just proven to me their staff are most likely trained to go to all lengths to prevent refunds and payout of claims. What a stressful experience, especially considering I had to cancel a trip to Europe that I had saved for two years for due to a severe illness. What a disgraceful approach to my situation. Of course I will never go near this company, or any of its affiliates ever again. I would advise you to steer clear.. at least be very careful.

After having a camera, camera lenses, money and sunglasses stolen on a bus we put a claim in with a net worth of over $2000 the camera alone was worth $1400 to then find out we were on policy L and they only pay out $250 per item! What a joke by far the lowest payout of any company ( I started looking for a new policy and no one else is this low) also more expensive than a lot of other good companies, we received back less than $1000 which in no way covers the cost of the camera. I also was unable to access my online credit card statements as my credit card was stolen and even though I explained this to them they refused to take a copy of my transactions to prove that I'd actually had got Thai bhat out of an ATM, so couldn't complete my claim for months after it was lodged as I was still traveling and ended up having to get a paper statement sent to my house which then was scanned and emailed to me, which I then had to send on to them. Even though policy says they will refund money stolen if it's in a police report, make sure you keep your ATM slips or money exchange receipts!

Read the fine print very low payout on personal effects

title: Inflexible and unreasonable
body:
Booking online was easy and the premium was reasonable. However, when I needed to extend my policy they were not helpful. My original policy was valid thru 27 May, which was the date I was leaving LA. I had to change my trip at the last minute on 26 May to leave on 01 June instead. However,the phone line for TID was only open for 4 hours on Sunday and they were already closed after making the booking. I called on 27 May from the US to extend my coverage, but they would not because it was 28 May in Australia and my policy had expired according to their date. I was given the excuse of "the computer won't let me renew it". I was told I would have to buy a new policy and was only offered 10% off. When I asked for a larger discount since it was still 27 May by my local time, I was told "10% is the only discount available on their computer." 

They should have been more reasonable considering the time zone and date difference, and considering that I couldn't even call when I first changed my flight since they were only open 4 hours on Sunday.
Decent price, easy to book online.
Poor customer service availability on weekends, inflexible and unwilling to consider my circumstances

title: Never Again!
body:
Never buy insurance from this company! I repeat, never buy insurance from this company! Especially if you are buying it because you want coverage for a medical emergency or the like? I have travelled frequently and extensively and have used TID many times previously, however I have never had to make a claim until now! I am genuinely surprised at any of the positive reviews on this site (you can discount all the people who say how great they are but have never made a claim as they essentially just bought a piece of paper on the web).  I fall into the same category as many of the other negative reviews left on this site, having experienced exactly the same lack of competency, clarity, communication and overall misrepresentation. When I book my trips I always seek out "user reviews" on websites as that is the best way to gauge a service realistically and more importantly honestly, as to its validity and thus I feel I have a responsibility to give you the same insight about this company.

I had a dental emergency within 24 hours of leaving Australia in Dec 2012 and without going into specifics I could not get an exact diagnosis from a Thai dentist but after presenting to a local hospital in Bangkok for treatment of a swollen face and flaring infection, I was encouraged to seek medical care in my home country (medical certificate in hand stating this) by the attending medical physician. I flew home on the next available flight and after seeking medical treatment from an Australia dentist, I had to have the tooth extracted because of a severe infection that incidentally lead to further complications I rang TID to ask if my insurance would cover this and they said it would ?depend upon whether I had a medical certificate stating that I needed treatment back in my country?.  

I submitted every relevant document to TID including multiple certificates/ dental reports/tax invoices/receipts and a report citing no existing ailments were present as attested to by a dental examination 2 weeks prior to departure. The first assessor of my case haphazardly contacted me numerous times about getting receipts for cancelled accommodation and flights and events that included showing evidence that I had not received any refunds for the services cancelled. This took about 2-3 weeks. On the website they say you should receive a response in 10 days. After I made a complaint to TID about their lack of customer service and sporadic communication a different officer took over the case and decided she was going to go back to establishing the nature of my medical complaint (did the first officer not know what she was doing?)?.I was confused as to how this was not established at the onset when my claim was submitted weeks ago. Her final assessment claimed that because I refused medical treatment, my condition was not deemed an emergency, but the concerning issue here, was that this never occurred and I confronted the company about such a fallacy. Essentially their assessor had made this up and of course she had no documentation to substantiate it. Did I forget to mention that TID actually did pay out a small cost of $29 for visiting the hospital in that same period of time? Apparently, that part of the situation was an emergency but not the rest which involved more substantial sums of money such as the return flight? Also just a note, apparently if you have had dental work in the past it is considered pre existing and thus not covered?..so that would probably rule out 80% population? I took the case to the dispute resolution centre clearly concerned about the professionalism and fraudulent activity. In the meantime I started reading reviews on here and noticed one staff member who responded to posts and essentially was doing what I call ?damage control? to uphold the company?s image so I also sent a communication to her. She assured me she would look into the case and get back to me and that the dispute resolution would take 15 days, this communication happened 15.4.13. After not hearing anything after this time had passed, I emailed her once again and phoned her but received no reply or follow-up. I finally received a notice of re assessment on 6.5.13 (clearly much longer than the 15 days) resulting in the over turning of the first decision but with no explanation as to why or how this whole debacle transpired? Ultimately I got back most of what I claimed for but it was difficult, the process frustrating and overall unnecessarily drawn out. (Maybe they thought I would just give up?)

 When you buy travel insurance, you do so knowing you have peace of mind that when you are travelling, if something goes wrong, you will be OK and covered. This company has not intention of offering such a service, evidenced by others on this site. I am not sure why that only when a negative complaint is written on this actual site, the customer service officer can ?look? into it and sort something out?..what sort of business is this? There is either an existing policy or there is not?  For a few dollars more I prefer peace of mind and a valid document, this policy is not worth the paper it is written on.
I repeat NEVER, EVER go with this company or do so, but it will be at your own risk....... 
Trust me, I know first hand.
Nothing.
They don't honour their contract and they lack professionalism
