body: I called up and received  good value policy and great customer service, very friendly and easy to understand and easy to arrange. As for the online version would not recommend if you are not a computer savvy.

title: Great peace of mind
body: It was good to know that if anything went wrong we were covered and that all would be looked after.

title: Will never use them again
body: Had to cancel a holiday to Bali when diagnosed with secondary breast cancer after being clear for 6 years. This company took 3 months to process my claim to get approx $1500 in refunds. They insisted on 6 years of confidential & private correspondence between doctors & specialists, x-ray reports, oncology reports, etc etc. I was having enough stress without theirs on top of everything else. When I phoned the claims officer to ask why they needed so much documentation, the reply was that it was the "medical team" wanting more and more detail. Disgraceful conduct. All they needed to do was state clearly the exact information they needed - which was one line in a letter from my oncologist stating dates from end of treatment to beginning of the new diagnosis. I felt like they were enjoying reading my personal medical history for their own amusement. Keep away from this company.

title: Read the fine print!
body: If you need to make a theft claim, they are hopeless.  Maybe my mistake however to me theft is theft.  Whilst holidaying I had a beach bag stolen from a public place when making claim was advised this is not covered as the bag was unsupervised.... will look into other insurances next time and would be worth the couple of extra $$$ to have things like this covered!!!

title: Amazing... Repeat customer never disappointed
body: Love 1cover they are the best value and always take care of any claims promptly and without delay. Love them and use them every time I travel!!! Last time I travelled I was in hospital and they covered everything no questions asked! Couldn't ask for a better insurer

title: a very highs expectation of customer understanding of legal requirements and responsbilities
body:
I took out a high level of insurance to account for what i thought would be a worst case scenario on my trip. A very unfortunate incident happened and I had my possessions stolen from me, only to be told by the insurer that I was required to provide receipts and other significant proof of ownership which would be fine for a person that did not travel a lot (or even then, perhaps not), going back a number of years( a minimum of 2-3 years), including for items that were provided as gifts. 
My complete claim was rejected, even items for which i provided proof.

title: Unimpressive service
body:
Claim took over 13 months to be processed. Unprofessional customer service. Will never use covermore again and have told friends and family travelling overseas to steer clear of this company, who go out of there way to make the claim process as difficult as possible, through non communication, loss of documents on several occasions and having to do most of the running around yourself.
Nothing.
Everything.

title: Lack of disclosure
body:
Very disappointed to be told 3 weeks after purchasing insurance that there is no cover for covid-19 
At time of purchase their banner on the website stated no cover for travel to China. There was no mention of covid-19 
Also due to some medical issues had a long conversation with a staff member over the phone  prior to purchasing insurance and also not once was I informed that covid-19 issues would not be covered. 
There is also no mention of covid-19 not being covered in any of the information they sent me after purchase. 
They have offered me a full refund however

title: Excellent service
body: Having taken out travel insurance many times over the years without having to use it, I was unsure what to expect when having to make a claim. On a recent trip overseas, our bags were delayed by 24 hours. I called up TID and spoke to a wonderful staff member. It was comforting to hear an Australian accent on the line and she couldn't be more helpful. We were advised of how much we could spend to get us through the next day and off we went in the morning to do some shopping. It was a nice feeling to restock the wardrobe without having to worry about eating into the holiday budget. Upon returning home I got into the claim process. Yes, this was a little clunky I must admit, with a whole lot of supporting documentation required as well as the receipts of course. If you stay organised and keep everything, it's not so bad really. The money was paid in full very quickly. Happy with my first claim experience and have just taken out insurance with TID for my next trip. Fingers crossed I won't need to use their excellent service this time round!

title: Travel Cover - with extras & pre-existing conditions
body:
I did not need to make a claim, but Allianz were excellent in setting up the policy. My partner has a pre-existing medical condition and we also wanted to participate in activities such as Quad Biking and White Water Rafting, but maintain full cover. Not only were they able to provide us the cover, with not too much difficulty (re the pre-existing condition), but the price was good too.

I have previously had a Travel cover through Aussie Travel Cover, underwritten by Allianz, when I was travelling to the US. In that instance I needed both an ambulance and hospital claim - which were completely covered by Allianz and the claim process was smooth with no issues - all I had to do was email the form and paperwork from the Hospital and Allianz dealt with the accounts directly.

title: Cheap cover & expensive service
body:
I recently travelled to Bali & realised I had bought insufficient vital medication with me. On advice from a fellow traveller, I tried to obtain medication (after gaining a prescription) from several chemists within Legian area. When unsuccessful, I phoned T I D, hoping they could suggest a chemist that stocked my medication . The lady I spoke to, took some time in understanding my predicament, & could only supply the 'stock' answer of re-visiting Dr/hospital and getting them to suggest a supplier & if unsuccessful to re-contact T I D for further advice . As I had already explained that Dr couldn't suggest chemist, I visited a medical centre & was finally put in contact with chemist that stocked my medication. I wrongfully assumed that T I D could pinpoint chemist who stocked  my medication.  I was disappointed that ph number supplied by T I D was not a toll free one. Especially when it took some time to explain my predicament to lady who answered my call. If I hadn't been travelling with friends who knew of a medical centre close by, I would have been more concerned. I would use T I D for future travel, however, I feel they are more for emergency situations. It was my failing that  I didn't carry sufficient medication on this trip.
Someone to talk to in Aus, when there is a problem.
Expensive. No Toll free number & would help if medical ( maybe nursing experience staff) answering calls

title: Avoid this company like a pandemic
body:
This company should be called NO COVER!

Hang on to your money and avoid this company like a pandemic. Paid extra cover for my son with an existing medical condition to be covered for a Europe trip for June 2020.  Our policy was taken out in December 2019. Spent $780 for 6 weeks to not be covered anything relating to Coronavirus as excluded from their policy

I'm now looking at cancelling our trip or rescheduling for next year. The airlines are changing their policies by waiving fees for date changes and  travel vouchers for those wanting to cancel. 1Cover are not interested in assisting their customers even if wanting to make changes to travel dates, except if you pay for a new policy.

They are not answering  phones nor responding to call backs. I can just imagine if needed to make a claim how terrible their service would be.

Leave a negative feedback if you to have experienced similar experience wanting to cancel or change dates. 1Cover needs to be more accommodating to their customers in this unprecedented event. 

My printed policy is to be used as a substitute for toilet paper.

title: good service and helpful
body:
on a recent trip to overseas we were in New York and we left our computer in a taxi an after reporting it to the police we then had to wait for a report number ; as we were leaving there the next morning this was an issue for us? After some delay we were able to get a report no. In order to obtain the report we needed to send 20 American dollars; as they would not accept Australian dollars or a money order? Once we received the report our claim was settled very quickly and effeciently.

title: Easy website to use
body: I can't remember how many times I've used TID, but this trip was the first time I've had to extend a stay. And the TID website made it so easy to extend my cover as well. Two thumbs up.

title: Covered pre-existing
body: A good premium covering two people in their 60's. Also was able to get coverage online for my back after spinal surgery without having to submit details and proofs to an underwriter.

title: Weird gender default
body: We didn't have to use this policy, but I did have very good experience talking to the help desk when I had to sort some admin out. But... I am female, and booked to cover my male travelling partner and myself. I am the primary user noted. The email address is mine. I paid. I'm also older. Yet every email I got was addressed to my male partner. We have different surnames and my title is 'Ms'. I don't know why in this day and age such a default exists, but it's a touch belittling and a little off-putting for next time.

title: Didn't need it, but felt better having it.
body: Another fortunate trip with no need to make a travel insurance claim.  But I felt better knowing I have another avenue to get assistance if I needed it.

title: Travel Insurance Claim - SKI TRIP JAPAN
body: I would like to commend TID on the excellent support and service they provided to me. After injuring myself on the ski slopes in Japan I was unable to continue my trip. TID flew my father to Japan to collect me and flew us both home business class (due to my injuries requiring me to have my leg in an upright position). Upon return I submitted my claim and in a timely manner my claim was dealt with. There was only one discrepancy and I contacted TID they investigated further and agreed to pay my claim in full. 5 STAR SERVICE - my only disappointment is that I can not use them again due to the fact that they will not cover my left knee again under any circumstances.

title: Excellent
body:
I had never dealt with an insurance company before in terms of making a claim, and was nervous about it after hearing all 'the stories'. Though I'm glad it's nearly over after four months and I can put it behind me, I know how complicated it all was, for your staff as well, and so I am also very happy with the assistance I received from everyone. If I ever do tempt fate and book another overseas trip (this was meant to have been my first!) I will definitely use TID again.
I never even made it on my 6 week overseas holiday after falling ill, and have had quite a complicated, four month process of putting through my claim. It has just been approved and I'm awaiting payment, so I am extremely happy and relieved. The staff have been good with keeping me up to date on my claim, it had a lot of elements to it, it was a complicated itinerary, and not once have I felt as though I'd been forgotten amidst all the other work they had on. Also, their instructions on what sort of extra information I needed to send in has been detailed and easy to understand on every occasion, even if at times it has required my travel agent and I to do a bit of work. Every request has been communicated in a friendly and professional way.I have really been impressed by your staff's attitude towards this process and their appreciation of what it has been like for me; of the effort I've put into getting the information, my health, effects of delays etc. This approach really has been welcomed during what has been quite a hard time for me personally. I have been really happy with the level of service I've gotten over the phone and via email - very helpful, kind and precise.
Making a claim took time, but then it was a complicated claim ...

title: Easy travel insurance
body: I found the policy very easy to take out being a senior I found it quiet simple to understand although I did not have to make a claim I had full confidence in the company.

title: Covermore for the win!
body:

body:
The cost of Travel Insurance Direct was the first thing that I noticed being quite cheap and offering good coverage.  I had used them twice before having any issues.

On my most recent coverage with TID, I had the unfortunately experience of having my notebook computer stolen.  Checkout is in the morning as usual so I had my luggage and bags stored in my hostel's secured and locked holding area.  My laptop was unfortunately stolen out of my bag so I made a claim with TID and their insurance company (Cerebus Claims).  

After providing all the information they opted not to award the claim in favour.  The reasoning was that because the hostel is a public area and hostel patrons have access to the secured and locked room as well.  This is unfortunate because a hostel is a communal residence with shared bathrooms, bedrooms, etc.  Therefore using their PDS and wording, they are covered for anything that is stolen if you are staying in a hostel. 

Summary: Do not use TID if you plan to stay in a hostel.

When filling out the pre-existing forms and sending them through, I had to prompt 1Cover consultants to progress the documents to the Medical assessment Team as they had not forwarded them through and must have been sitting in their IN Box without action. This has happened before the last two trips I applied for that cover, it makes you feel a bit uncomfortable especially when it's getting close to your trip. They also don't give reasons why they decline to cover a pre-existing issue - I had a kidneys stone removed over 12 months ago and they refused to cover Kidney Stones if it occurred on the trip, I don't understand why as it was a procedure I went through and the stone was removed and I have had no problems since and its hardly a pre-existing ongoing "Condition", maybe if I had the Flu 6 months ago they may consider it a pre-existing condition??. We all have general maintenance of our bodies over the years but it would seem 1Cover see all of these as Pre-Existing conditions so you may not be covered for anything you've seen the doctor for in the past!! 
However, if you have had anything stolen during your trip, which I have, they have honored my claim without too much problem, just a lot of paperwork and questions about the articles stolen.

title: Covermore really hasn't been to helpful so far!
body:
I am currently in europe, and when i was in rome i was robbed of my iphone, camera and jewellery i had purchased while being overseas, the worst experience ever! And covermore hasn't been any help at all. I submitted a claim online, i had to wait more than 10 days for an initial reply (and mind you i am overseas with no contact with anyone back home because i've had my phone stolen and the only photos i can take is by borrowing fellow travelers cameras and phones!) this is extremely stressful and upsetting knowing i'm missing out on so many valuable photos on my once in a lifetime trip! I replied to the email straight away with the details covermore requested and still haven't had a reply! If i could call them i would but obviously my phones been stolen! And at a charge of 5euro per minute from my hotel phone, email is my best means of communication. They also mentioned replacing my phone for me, that's all fine, but i am overseas still and will be for another month! So will they be delivering my phone to me while over here? I very much doubt it! Clearly where it states in the cover policy "you will be covered for immediate reimbursement for loss of luggage" it isnt true! I hope they can get back to me as soon as possible and reimburse me so i can go purchase replacement items while i am still over here! But at the moment it isn't looking very promising! So unfortunately i cant say i'm extremely satisfied with my covermore experience so far. Fingers crossed it gets better.
The up side is I should be covered for what I've experienced! Better than not being covered at all but let's just hope my claim is processed in due time.
I feel like my emails arn't being read or acknowledged and there's no sense of urgency or understanding by the company, considering the price I payed for my insurance opposed to fellow travelers, you'd expect a really good service, but so far I can't say it's going to well.

title: Happy Ending in Vietnam
body:
Travelling through Vietnam was our ultimate holiday: full of adventure, shopping, delicious food and most of all constantly coming across warm, friendly locals. Unfortunatly, on one of our first domestic flights in Vietnam the airline check in person tore off my return home ticket.... Being unfamiliar with paper tickets, I did not realise at the time. My boyfriend noticed this as we were about to fly home to Australia. Panic struck. Calls to my travel consultant were tedious, but the story unravelled and Vietnam Airlines found my ticket in Ho Chi Minh. I was advised to buy a new return ticket and they would refund me back in Melbourne. On my return I called, and visited the office of Vietnam Airlines many many times. Each conversation was the same. Yes, they said they would refund my ticket as it was their employee who made the mistake, but nothing happened. It was at this point I called Covermore. I spoke to someone who understood the situation and took the matter up with V. Airlines on my behalf. After he had several futile and frustrating conversations aswell, he understood that they were never really going to repay me. So after a long and disappointing experience with the Airline, Covermore's friendly, swift action (and reimbursement) I could finally look back and remember the best holiday of our lives, rather than the tangled mess of my return home. 

Since then,  I have used Covermore for all my holidays. Last year I flew to Switzerland with my father to visit family. My father has been back to his home country almost every year for the past 6 years. It amazed me that he never took out travel insurance. I convinced him it was a good idea, and amazingly enough he did need to claim when he was struck down with some medical issues. 

Covermore provides peace of mind that if something was to go wrong, there was a friendly and understanding fellow Australian to listen and help.

title: Will do anything to wriggle out of a claim
body:
I purchased a policy with this company with the assumption that I was covered for 'unforeseen consequences' while travelling. The long and the short of it is, I had to return after a few days due to family illness, forfeit my original ticket in the process, and buy a new ticket. They rejected me outright, and sent me a long daunting letter detailing the reasons (i.e. there is so much 'fine print' - i.e. 14 pages of literally tiny print - that virtually allow them to slither out of every situation they initially say they will cover). Coincidentally, my mother had to cancel a trip for the same reason and was with the same insurer who also rejected her. After several months of fighting through the Financial Ombudsman Service (a fun thing to do when one's partner is very sick), Cover 'More' gave in and paid her out. I continued my dispute through FOS, which took seven (7) months to reach the conclusion that their fine print did, indeed, allow them to avoid covering my situation.

In each letter of 'denial', the subsequent claims officer brought up spurious and incorrect information as though they were trying to obfuscate the situation, lest their 'pre-existing condition' exclusion be insufficient. Overall, I found this company exists for one reason only: to ensure that, once they have received payment from their customers, they can avoid paying out any claim and thus absorb maximum profit. The company's name is a complete misnomer: it should be called 'CoverLess'.

Dishonesty; lack of compassion; determination to avoid payment at all cost

title: Was easy to get cover we needed to give us travel free worries

title: More on Covermore Insurance.
body:
Well, after appealing Covermore's refusal to honour my claim, I received a very short and curt letter today advising they had accepted my appeal and all monies owed have been paid in to my account, I should be happy right? Well no, given the references I relied upon in preparing my appeal were obtained from Covermore and were the same references Covermore used to dismiss my claim one wonders whether it was incompetence or dishonesty which prevailed.   
A lesson can be learnt here: never give up in your dealings with insurance claims, if you can provide documentary evidence to prove your claim - stick it to them. Would I insure with Covermore again? No more than I would with any other insurance provider, I have learnt my lesson well, never should I have had to waste so much of my time putting forward evidence Covermore already had in their possession to prove my claim. Whether it be incompetence or dishonesty, Covermore failed to provide the service they purport to. Once again I say: No company is dishonest, it is the individuals employed by that company who, for whatever reason, choose to follow that path.
I cannot in all honesty state Covermore's policy was good value, neither can I state I was happy with their support. On the positive side, the policy was easy to set up - I simply gave them my hard earned cash and gave them my trust!

title: We made our first medical claim ever, and it was paid
body: My husband got quite sick in Morocco, with flu and diarrhea, and consequent dehydration and weakness (he's 73) so we couldn't meet up with our adventure camping tour in Sierra Leone. We contacted TID, asking for help.  We went to a doctor, then to the local hospital, but didn't get the officially recognised certificates ( we were lucky to be even seen at the hospital, and certainly didn't want to stay there). We made the decision to return to Australia. A nurse rang us with medical advice about the flight home, and rang us again while we waited for our connection in Abu Dhabi. We made a claim for the tour we missed, and the fee to change our flights (just over $6000 in total). After filling in MANY forms, and a few weeks waiting for various local doctor reports, our claim was paid.

title: TID?s Intransigence
body: I have used TID twice in the past 2 years. This time I needed to change the dates and wasn?t able/allowed to as I had a pre-existing medical condition. This is stated in the PDS. The thing that really annoyed me was the intransigence and lack of flexibility shown given the changes in dates actually REDUCED the number of days of cover, thus reducing TID?s potential liability. To make it worse, by the time I wanted to make the changes, TID had issued a new PDS. In that PDS, if your pre-existing medical condition was not listed you CANNOT get cover with TID. Of course, you can apply for cover with a sister company at an exorbitant rate which I didn?t- I went with another company. I am very unhappy with TID?s rigidity- it was totally unnecessary. I?ll not be using TID or a related company for my future travel insurance needs.

title: Inconsistent customer service. Poor policy documentation. Misleading sales.
body:
Inconsistent customer service leading me to doubt the validity of the policy I purchased. Dubious management of customer service enquiries and handling of complaints.

I get the impression that its poorly managed and lacks credibility as some larger companies.

Although it advertises having insurance underwritten by Lloyds, for me that does not support the product sufficiently and the way customer service representatives bungle enquiries, give wrong information and generally present themselves and the company leaves me to doubt that if I needed assistance, whether anyone would actually be there and manage a claim sufficiently.

It might be a good company, a good product but until there is a consistent approach to managing customer enquiries and resolving issues early on it is going to be a company that will always suffer and continually struggle to gain the credibility thats needed when customers seek a travel insurance product that they can rely and have peace of mind from.

I've used a variety of companies in the past and I will be returning to one of those once the refund of my policy is finally made. Sadly, another fault of this company is that it fails to live up to the promises/decisions it makes. I am still to wait for a refund and have, in the interim referred the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

title: Injured in Botswana
body:
In May 2014 I fell 2 metres from the deck of a remote safari camp and fractured my pelvis in 3 places and broke 2 ribs (and yes I was sober - the deck was dark at night).   Allianz prevaricated for nearly two days before they finally approved my medical evacuation to a Johannesburg hospital.   I was in agony, with no medical assistance or pain relief and not knowing what damage I had done.  They kept asking stupid questions like "can you call a local doctor (witchdoctor?) or get to a local clinic for x-rays"!!  We told them that we were over an hour from a town by 4WD and then small aircraft.  It occurred to me that their payout was lower for death than the cost of a medivac!!

Our problems with Allianz continued when we tried to return to Australia after I was treated in the Johannesburg hospital - the Allianz doctor in Queensland  did not agree with the Johannesburg Trauma Specialist and told me I was fit to continue the holiday!!  Claiming the cancellation costs was also difficult and we ended up out of pocket when Allianz would not pay for the accommodation for my husband while I was in hospital, nor the hotel costs for us both when we were waiting for Allianz's approval for us to return home.

But the question is - are any of the other travel insurance companies any better?

title: Unable to board flight - claim not paid
body:
I was recently travelling to the USA on 2 passports. One passport had my permanent residency visa and the other one allowed me to enter the USA under the visa waiver program with an ESTA. I arrived at the check-in counter 2.5hrs before boarding time. Queue was long and moving slowly and it took a while to get to check-in counter. 

The Border Force system flagged the check-in as requiring clearance due to me travelling on 2 passports. They were unable to authorise the airline before the gates closed and I missed our flight. The airline rebooked me and said this is regular occurrence and no one can know when Border Force will require this clearance. It has recently been implemented. Apparently you also cannot have your passports cleared prior to arriving at check in to avoid this. This was the first time I had heard or been told of this. The airline also never informed me of this. One would think it should be in the electronic itinerary at least.

I put in a claim with Travel Insurance Direct for taxi fair, and miscellaneous expenses incurred in getting to the airport and spending entire morning there. I completed the offline claim form as required and provided supporting documentation. 2 weeks later, they email me back stating that they require a letter from the airline and Border Force. The airline is unable to comment on Border Force but is able to confirm that I had to be rebooked. Border Force does not explain themselves to the public understandably. I explain the situation in great detail in the email. 

I then get a email back saying claim is rejected as I should have known that the USA requires me to have a visa to enter the country. What a load of nonsense. They couldn't have read the email

I email them back telling them to read the email and facts again because the basis of their decision is flawed based on their interpretation of the facts provided.

2 weeks later I get an email stating that I will will receive a call from the agent. The agent had gotten her facts straight by now, had called the airline who had informed her of the clearance issue they regularly get. She then went on to say I should have known this and taken relevant steps to ensure that I did not have this issue at check-in. 

The claim was still rejected despite the new facts. When I asked what would've happened if I had booked a hotel, and had other prepaid arrangements I was told I that my claim would've been rejected for the same reason.

Long story short - the amount of effort and time I had to put in to prove claim vs the claim amount, the delayed correspondence and stalling tactics forced me to make a decision and not appeal. I would really NOT recommend Travel Insurance Direct and will try another travel insurance policy next time.

title: Help Needed
body:
We bought IAG 'Silver Couple' cover for our trip to Bali. Their quote was really competitive and at the time it seemed like great value. Unfortunately, on the last day of trip, my phone was stolen (pick pocketed). International roaming wasn?t activated on my phone & so I was only using it at places with Wi-Fi, therefore didn?t realise that my phone was gone until I was at the airport luggage scanning gate. At the scanning gate, I looked to get the phone out of my pocket but realized it wasn't there. I thought I may have kept it in my bag pack (which was already on the baggage scanning machine). When I crossed the gate, I checked my bag pack and could not find my phone. 

We spoke to airport staff, explained them the situation and told them we need to lodge a police complaint for insurance purposes. We were told there is no police beyond the scanning gate, only airport security.  We requested them to let us go out to lodge the report but they didn?t. We then went to airport security and narrated the incident. They wrote it down in dairy but gave us no reference number. The day we landed in Sydney, I called Insurance & Go and spoke to a lady (think [Name Removed]) ? I told her what has happened and that we were unable to lodge a police complaint. I was offered no advice that for my claim to get accepted I must report it to airline/local police (within 72 hours). Today I got a call from IAG rep [Name Removed] who initially told me that he has rejected my claim as there is no police report supporting my claim. When I reasoned with him that given the circumstance I couldn?t have lodged a police complaint, he told me it?s the policy and I should have reported the matter to police or airline, therefore he cannot approve my claim. I told him I can complete a statutory declaration, which is a legal document and accepted in Australia. He said they don?t accept stat dec however can offer to cover 50% cost and if I don?t accept this offer, he would reject my claim and then I?ll have to go through IAG dispute resolution team. 

I expected the rep to tell me what the requirements were on the initial call. I wish everything was black & white but this isn?t how the universe functions.  It is a lot of money and if IAG can?t cover it then what?s the point of getting travel insurance. Hoping for a positive outcome.

title: Used to be great,,,,   not so much anymore
body: we were in bali for a 50th birthday last october.  My father who was 79.5 years young fell over a mat as he only has one leg and his crutches caught the mat.  He hit his head, he was knocked out and also swallowed his tongue and wasnt breathing. We rushed to him and pulled out his tongue and he was out cold for 3 to 4 minutes, ambulance to BMIC which were great. As he fell he also smashed and broke his reading glasses. He spent three days in hospital with 16 stitches, a small hairline fracture in his pelvis and SEVERE concussion. contacted cover more from the hospital and they were great at the time. Told my mother 78 years was fine to stay with him as they were due to fly home. i cut my holiday short (daughter) to travel home with them as the carer as mentioned above father is an amputee above the knee, which cover more paid for.  Upon getting flights home they then said that they wouldn't cover my mother who was the policy holder to fly home with her husband Absolute joke, do you think she is going to leave him in hospital on his own.  The hospital report said that he was to fly home business class to allow lying down due the severe concussion and pelvic back pain.  when we arrived at the airport it was bloody economy.  My father did not have a comfortable flight home.  Upon putting our claim in, it has been a nightmare,,,,,  3 times i have had to upload paperwork which they say they haven't received, which we know they have as they have part paid from our credit card statement.  His reading glasses which were smashed and replaced when we got back for $1200 they have not paid for, they say they need his receipt for his old glasses,,,   who keeps that!!!.  I also sent in pictures of the broken bloodied glasses but still no as they to do a depreciation on the old ones.   This claim is still ongoing but very frustrating.  We have used cover more many many times and had two claims and there was no problem,  something is going on with this company at the moment,  but they are definatley not the same from our claim back in 2008 where my mother broke her leg in vietnam, our whole family is considering moving travel insurance, and thats a big loss for them.

Impressed by just my basic cover
body:
I was on a holiday with family in Germany and went to on a sailing trip in Croatia. Sailing trip over, I ran after a bus on my way to the airport in Split and tore a muscle in my right calf, went lame, had to go to hospital and missed my flight. Reorganised a new flight after treatment in hospital and got home the same day with a taxi. I was on basic cover and informed InsureandGo of my accident and treatment the day after the incident.
I am very very impressed with their constant care by email, walking me through everything, down to a medical assessment specialist who called me to inquire about the treatment. 
I had a 100$ excess and that s what I paid. I got refunded for everything else, and literally everything: the hospital treatment in Croatia, crutches in Croatia, taxi to the airport in Croatia, the entire new flight, taxi home in Germany, new cast and all hospital treatment and medication (blood thinner) in Germany, down to the cost for the doctor s certification that I can fly and taxi back to the airport when it was time for me to come back to Australia, all in all close to 2000$. I did not have to have any of the letters from the hospital in Croatia translated, nor the doctor s report in Germany, not sure how they re doing that, but that was a relief.
I must say it does help if you re organised. Do keep all the receipts and follow the instructions of the insurance and keep them in the loop.
Back in Australia I sat down and drew up a nice timeline with all the happenings and all the original receipts and got refunded everything.
I ll go with them again, that s a no-brainer, but will probably upgrade to even silver next time.

Medibank Insurance would only pay for the two nights accommodation missed on the island ( this was non-refundable) and well as taxi fares to and from the airport. When I challenged the assessor he said the policy didn't cover two accommodation claims. The amount we claimed for the hotel and meals was $261.18 which was not excessive and yet Medibank will not pay this out of pocket expense even though we were financially disadvantaged. I will never use Medibank Travel again as I believe that we were unfairly denied payment for a circumstance which was beyond our control and should have been covered by our insurance. We are considering taking our claim to the small claims tribunal.

title: Slow repatriotization process when in urgent need
body:
Having acutely hurt my lower back last Sunday (30th of August), seeking medical help and being advised by a doctor to return to Australia immediately for further treatment, I am still left waiting in a small town in rural Brazil while TID have been ever so slow doing whatever needs to be done in the process. 

I submitted all requested documents Tuesday morning AEST (including a medical report from a hospital and medical release forms for my past doctors back home) and was told that the TID claims team would take 1-2 days. On Thursday I had a phone interview with TID's medical staff and was told that their recommendation: (I) agreed with the Brazillian doctor's medical opinion that I should return home immediately; (II) and that the condition was not related to any past medical pre existing conditions. It is now Saturday morning AEST and I have rung the TID contact number twice a day and only been told that they weren't sure where the process was at and were waiting for the insurer to come to a decision.

A huge complaint of mine is that the 24 hour contact number is only for a TID subcontractor - 'We Assist'. They are very friendly and helpful staff, however, there has been so much back and fourth between them, TID and other external bodies. Despite being the main contact number, We Assist have not been able to provide firm answers about where the claim approval process for repatriotization is at. This has been most frustrating when in great pain and a dire time of need.

Considering they received a medical professional's report stating that repatriating me as soon as possible was important on Tuesday, followed by their own medical team supporting this opinion, it seems like very poor and uncaring service on behalf of TID that I am not yet on a plane back to Australia, let alone have any idea regarding what 'the plan' is, if any exists at all.

On a positive note, I re-iterate that the 'We Assist' 24 hour team were very friendly and helpful where they could, and the medical team was also great. Finally, the TID mobile app is a great little addition. TID are doing good stuff on that front.

title: Disgraceful.
body:
Unfortunately, I am forced to write the below complaint due to the extreme misconduct, insincere and inhuman treatment of myself and my family during the coronavirus pandemic. We are at the mercy of both Air New Zealand and their insurance provider Cover-More. 

I have reached out to Air New Zealand both by phone and email, my request for compensation was denied. I filed an insurance claim with Cover-More which too was declined. I am now releasing my complaint across the social channels of both parties, the insurance ombudsman along with the aviation governing bodies. We are unquestionably out of pocket unfairly and I want to share our story to try and help others avoid the same mistakes. 

We were amongst some of the unfortunate Australians left to fend for themselves when our flight was cancelled due to Covid-19.

It should be noted we both booked our trip with Air New Zealand and purchased Cover-More insurance in December 2019 BEFORE the coronavirus pandemic.

We had a planned trip booked for the end of March; however, we had to move it forward so we could say goodbye to my terminally ill father-in-law (during our trip he, unfortunately, passed away). We had to take this trip as my husband had already lost his mother in the past 12 months and did not want to miss saying his goodbyes to his last surviving parent.

It was as we were trying to get home that the drama all unfolded. Our original flights from New Plymouth to Brisbane on Sunday 22 March were cancelled, and we were told we could not get a flight home until Monday 23 March. After spending our savings on getting to NZ so my husband could say goodbye to his father, we were forced to pay additional our of pocket expenses as the airline would not cover the costs due to the 'pandemic.' I begged, pleaded, explained our situation over and over again. Not one person from either Air New Zealand or Cover-More Insurance showed any form of compassion or understanding. 

I explained we didn't have the money to cover the costs of accommodation, food, and transport for the additional day. I begged for assistance with covering the costs as this was not our fault, nor could we have prevented the situation. We were OFFERED NO COMPENSATION BY EITHER PARTY. We were told due to the pandemic, all additional costs for the extra day were on us. Can you believe it? On us. Disgraceful.  

This trip was not for leisure. We did not extended it because we were having a wonderful holiday. Our flights were cancelled, plain and simple. Covid-19 or not when an airline chooses to cancel flights the have a duty of care to their passengers. 

While I acknowledge the position the airline has taken, they have chosen to fall back on their 'policy' so they can deflect costs and not show any due diligence to their passengers' health and safety, this is not right. As a young family with two children under five, on a single income taking an unfortunate trip to say our final goodbyes to a parent and then having to pay additional expenses due to an event entirely outside of our control, I plead with you to look at our case. Show some compassion, humility, and assistance in covering our extra expenses. We are out of pocket for accommodation, car hire, parking, and meals equalling $577.40. I have all receipts and have written explanations for each and every expense.

I raised all of this with Air New Zealand, sent receipts and explanations as soon as we arrive home. I received an email (after waiting three weeks for a response) saying Air New Zealand would not cover the costs and that we should endeavor to recover our expenses from our insurance provider as they do not cover costs due to the pandemic. 

I then filed a claim with our insurance provider, Cover-More, to which they told me that 'due to our flights being cancelled because of the pandemic,' they too would not cover our costs. 

I then paint this picture for you. With neither the airline nor our insurance willing to cover these costs, and should we not have been able to scrape together the last remaining money we had to pay for transport, food and accommodation was the expectation from both the airline and Cover-More insurance that myself, my husband (who just lost his father, his last surviving parent), my three-year-old daughter and one-year-old son spend 36 hours at New Plymouth airport in the freezing cold with no food, no place to sleep or transport? As no-one is willing to cover these costs, this is the reality we face. How is this fair? How is this the level of assistance we received? Why three months down the road are we still fighting to have our costs reimbursed? 

Again, disgraceful. This is the only word I have to describe the treatment we have been subject to. Both Air New Zealand and Cover-More should be ashamed of how they have pushed my family aside in a hope that we would just accept their denial and ?go away?. Seems a little bit rich that they are claiming to be doing all they can to 'assist people' during this crisis, doesn't it.

I eagerly wait a response.

title: Appalling service - a waste of money
body:
Two weeks ago my family and I travelled to Japan for a skiing holiday. I took out comprehensive insurance with 1 Cover. My son had an accident skiing and broke his shoulder. He was taken to a medical clinic where it was x-rayed and strapped. The doctor there advised he should return to Australia for medical treatment. 

We rang 1 Cover that day. My partner made several calls to provide the relevant information and seek advice and assistance, including sending through the x-rays, doctor's letter and ski patrol report. In one of the telephone calls my partner asked how long the process might take. The person she spoke to said, this is a very busy time of the year and they weren't sure when they could get back to us! This would have to be the absolutely last thing a parent with an injured child in a lot of pain would want to hear! In another call we were told that the insurance company doctor would look at the x-rays within 24 hours and then they would get back to us!! We didn't"t get a call back within 24 hours - it was 2 days later!!! And,when speaking with customer support to seek advice or clarification my partner said she felt quite demeaned by the responses from the staff. We were also told that there was no advice or assistance that 1 Cover could offer until our claim was processed which apparently would be up to 24 hours.

In our view this was appealing service and so we decided to make our own arrangements for our son. While doing this we realised we also had insurance cover through our bank (CBA). We rang them and within about 3 hours the customer support had; referred the x-rays to a doctor who confirmed it was a bad break and our son should return asap, arranged for our son to go to a big local hospital to be seen by a paediatric specialist and arranged the taxi there and back. This insurance company then arranged for my partner and son to fly back to Australia business class ( as they were very empathetic to the fact that travelling back economy class would be very painful - whereas 1 Cover had earlier suggested to us that even if they did accept the claim my son most likely would have to fly back economy)

The service through our bank insurance was brilliant - they were very sympathetic constantly contacted us and keep us updated. The difference in service and support between 1 Cover and our bank travel insurance was the complete opposite experience.

1 Cover might be OK if you have a lost baggage claim etc but our experience with a medical emergency was disappointing and depressing and a complete waste of money. When we realised that we had travel insurance cover with our bank we withdrew our claim with 1 Cover - my partner says she wouldn't be surprised if 1 Cover now sent us a bill for having their doctor look at the x-rays.

I cannot Reccomended this travel insurance. I"m only writing this review because 1 Cover asked for feedback!

title: Poorest Service Ever - Don't use Covermore Insurance
body:

Covermore has still not settled the claim and the hospital is continuously chasing us personally via international debt collectors for the outstanding balance on the account. That is annoying you never get a response.

My latest phone call told me they had settled with the overseas hospital and payment had been made but it ends up that according to the overseas provider they have received less than covermore said they paid and have no record of any agreed discounts. The covermore consultant  was also going to send me the settlement confirmation so i could provide it to the debt collectors. I have not received it yet a week later.

I cannot understand how a company that provides such poor customer service can still be in business. I would recommend that anyone looking at covermore as a potentially provider save themselves the headache and find a more reliable alternative. I had a family member who had a medical evacuation for a life threatening illness from a cruise ship in the pacific and their claim was settled immediately by virgin travel insurance yet my claim for stitches is still going 2 years later.

Covermore also ignore the debt collector from overseas and do not reply to their emails or calls, making it my responsibility to try and mediate  which is not my role!! That's why i paid the insurance............

Do not use covermore they are not worth the money!!!!

title: Cover-More are Thieves
body:
In April, 2014 we booked airline tickets to travel to Chile to visit our very close friends in December 2014. In conjunction with our airline tickets purchased through Flight Centre we purchased the Flight Centre recommended Cover-More travel insurance for each person on this trip including my wife, Samantha O?Doherty, who was pregnant at this time with our second child.

The next month in May, due to unexpected excessive and severe blood loss Samantha O'Doherty had an emergency caesarian resulting in the premature birth of our son Oliver at 26 weeks gestational age. I very nearly lost both my wife Samantha and our son Oliver, which would have left our 2yo daughter and I alone. Fortunately after multiple blood transfusions the specialists were able to save both their lives.

Oliver spent the first 14 weeks of his life in intensive care, during which time he required multiple surgical operations including bowel surgery and bowel removal, eye surgery, throat surgery and a stoma surgery and closure operation. During this time we regrettably decided to cancel our upcoming trip as we correctly predicted that Oliver?s medical needs would prevent us from traveling. Statements provided to Cover-More by our G.P., Obstetrician and Neonatologist from the Royal Children?s Hospital in Melbourne provide evidence to support the reasoning for the cancellation of our trip.

In October 2014, we filed a claim to seek reimbursement of our flight costs through our Cover-More policy. We sought reimbursement based on this statement on page three of the certificate of currency of our policy and page 18 of the product disclosure statement:

 "Cover is only provided for unexpected serious pregnancy complications which occur before or during the 26th week of pregnancy.?

My wife had a normal straightforward pregnancy and birth with our first child and no
 prior medical history that would explain such a complication. The birth of our son Oliver was certainly severe in nature, the pregnancy complication was unexpected, as our medical evidence has attested. 

In December 2014, approximately 12 weeks after our claim was submitted Andrew O?Reilly from Cover-More denied the claim.

It was interesting to note during the 12 weeks they spent assessing the claim they asked for our credit card details to try to claim reimbursement from our credit card's travel insurance policy, so they didn't have to pay out!

Our claim has been rejected twice and is currently undergoing a third review process by Cover More. Regardless of the outcome of this review I will never again seek insurance from these heartless, hypocritical, thieving creeps and advise you not to either.

title: Travel Insurance Claim

He also said my claim documents were only received on the system on the 16th Jan (registered post on 2nd Jan). I gave another follow-up phone call last Thursday, 11th Feb and was told claims could take a while to process and my claims officer will call me within 24 hours. To-date, no one has called back from this company. I kept getting automatic acknowledgments for my emails including one from a Claims Officer (had a name), on 5th Feb saying they "are experiencing delays from substantial influx of claims for January." To date, no one has attempted to call me to discuss my claim or progress of my claim payment despite my several phone calls and emails querying progress of my claim payment. I have sent another email today (14 Feb) so will post another review the outcome if I do receive a respond eventually. I would suggest before buying any travel insurance from this company, think carefully if you are likely to get assistance when needed whilst overseas or receive any payment if you have a claim on your return.

title: Allianz Travel Insurance Review - Allianz: Lacking in integrity
body:
Similar to others here, Allianz denied my flight cancellation claim due to 'government interference' even though there was none on me, the route I was traveling, or the airline (most government restrictions were on the passenger, almost never the airlines who choose to cancel flights for commercial reasons). Allianz claims 'government interference' but can't, and don't, actually say exactly what that was. Allianz will seemingly go to any lengths finding other reasons to avoid meeting their obligations of the contract, 
 making broad generalisations like COVID-19 related, when it is not. It seems they bank on most people just walking away and not pursuing the claim further. 

I appreciate they would be busy at this time, however, Allianz falsely claimed on all correspondence to comply with time limits and other aspects of the insurance industry code, when a simple check of dates shows this is not true. (Having done this for months, Allianz can't claim its a template or ignorance). Allianz don't even provide updates or meet the other requirements of time-related factors within their industry code, which is a lack of common courtesy, in addition to the lack of ethics.

I strongly encourage others to write their reviews here so consumers can make informed purchase decisions; complain to the industry body (insurancecode.org.au) about their lack of integrity and knowingly breaching of the code; and most important lodge an appeal about your case, and complaint about code of practice breaches to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority, and inform your bank (if your policy was from a bank scheme). 

The more people do this, the more Allianz will be held accountable for their actions, because, sadly, their business strategy counts on people not doing anything.

title: Beware Broken Teeth with Fillings
body:
Enjoying a bit of Duck when I bit into a bone and my tooth broke with an audible crack. Followed by bucket loads of real pain.

(Note first called the helpline and was told yes the situation was covered but thought I'd better check via email)

Me - Questions via Email 
I have broken a tooth or filling. I need to get a temp filling and pain relief. Please advise.
I am at the Sheraton Ho Chi Minh City. 88 Dong Khoi Street. Room XXXX.

TID - Answers via Email
Thanks for getting in touch and sorry to hear you have broken a tooth.
The medical section of the policy allows for medical, hospital and road ambulance costs and when agreed by us, medical evacuation home or to the nearest appropriate medical facility. The policy also includes overseas emergency dental treatment up to a maximum amount of $500 per person per trip for dental costs incurred which the overseas treating dentist certifies in writing is for the relief of sudden and acute pain to sound and natural teeth. There is no cover for filling of teeth.
To complete your medical claim we will need the following supporting documentation
?	Proof of travel dates eg, etickets, booked itinerary
?	Original medical/dental receipts
?	Treating doctors report
?	Hospital admission & discharge reports where relevant
?	Letter from dentist with details of emergency treatment provided and confirming that the treatment was to sound and natural teeth for the relief of sudden and acute pain.
?	A medical certificate from your local GP
Please try and have any reports and letters translated into English where possible.
Within the claim form you will also need to provide a medical certificate from your local GP. We require this when assessing your medical history as many existing medical conditions are not covered unless we have previously agreed and provided cover. Pre-existing conditions apply to you, your family, travelling party and relatives

ME

So if I have broken a filling and need a temp.filling to get home without pain there is no cover?

TID

That is correct, our policy only covers dental costs incurred which the overseas treating dentist certifies in writing is for the relief of sudden and acute pain to sound and natural teeth.

Me

I am not sure as I can't see inside my mouth but I suspect I have a broken tooth and filling which means no cover.
Not much point in having a policy if pain relief is excluded is there?
So my TID experience to date. First since I answered the questions honestly when taking out the cover I'm excluded for all pre-existing conditions due to having one operation over a year ago. Now I find I am excluded from pain relief, again for being honest, for a busted tooth. I could ask the dentist to lie but I won't.
Note this is not what I was told when calling the help line. Who did little in the way of helping really, just said I was ok to claim for pain and suffering, left me to find a dentist and said they would send out a claims form.
I look forward to letting other travelers know about my experience with TID on all the review pages online I can find. I will have time on my hands now to start blogging whilst still here in Vietnam!
First I will see about getting some pain relief at my own expense.

TID

You mis-understand. Dental treatment is only covered for pain relief. As per our policy wording under Section 1 Medical expenses incurred overseas. point no.2 We will pay the cost of overseas emergency dental treatment up to a maximum amount of $500 per person per trip for dental costs incurred which the overseas treating dentist certifies in writing is the the relief of sudden and acute pain to sound and natural teeth.
Please read the attached Product Disclosure Statement for more information.

Me

No mis-understanding. I just want pain relief and the best way to get it is with a temporary filling. But I broke a filled tooth and your policy excludes filled teeth.
Bad luck for me, I should have found another provider.
But if you think it makes the pain go away or will make me happier then keep on pointing out the fine print.

TID
No Further response via email. Someone called my house whilst I was travelling home to explain the misunderstanding (no misunderstanding filled teeth are not covered)

Me
You know what else sucks, I took out extra cover for my video camera and peripherals and I was in a hurry and forgot to bring them. So TID have been paid for cover I didn't actually need.
I could have used the extra to pay the dentist, it almost would be funny except for the pain.
I am off to find the dentist now. Lets hope I don't get hit by a car, I don't want you straining yourself to find the policy section to exclude that!

End result: No Help from TID but I found West Coast International Dental Clinic at 71-79 Dong Khoi Street ,& Dr [name removed] in my case, great to deal with. I need a fair bit of work on the tooth but had to fly out so Dr [name removed] did just what was needed to get home. Fantastic service. I am thinking of returning to get the work done as it's half the price in Australia! - www.westcoastinternational.com

Further hospitalisation from complications for another 14-15 days in intensive care + medical evacuation back to Oz = much more than $150,000....  

BASIC RULE WHEN TRAVELLING
DON'T go anywhere overseas without travel insurance...

Medibank Private Travel Insurance is backed by good underwriter. 
Benefits are comparable, or better, than most other travel insurance polocies. 
Overseas medical support is provided by another company selected by Medibank Private and is very good. They will arrange to pay hospital costs direct to the hospital, so you don't need to pay the hospital upfront and seek re-imbursement when you get back to Oz.

BE WARNED (all travel insurance)... 
If you are injured overseas and get evacuated back to Oz and need further medical treatment, you ARE NOT covered once you arrive in Oz. This is standard with Travel Insurance polocies.
    If it's a 3rd world country, come back to Oz to get the good medical treatment...!
    If it's a country where you get good hospital treatment, have it done overseas.

title: Even before the journey began I got a taste of what to expect
body:
Dear Cover More,

I read people talking about cancellation and how your fine prints make buying the policy useless but I chose to ignore. Why oh why did I maketh the mistake. 

I pay for a policy and chose $5000 cover for cancellations
I get an email from the airline saying that due to circumstances outside my their control the flight has been cancelled. My options? A credit to use towards a future flight. 

Consequences- no option to chose an alternate connecting flight, All onwards booking to hotels and flights will be lost as we wont actually now make it to the locations

Call to Covermore for help and oh it was far from the help expected. I was very insensitively directed to the section which goes something like this:

If due to circumstances outside Your control and unforeseen at the
Relevant Time:
1. You have to rearrange Your Journey prior to leaving Home, We
will pay the reasonable cost of doing so (We will not pay more for
rearranging Your Journey than the cancellation costs which would
have been incurred had the Journey been cancelled).
2. You have to cancel the Journey (where You cannot rearrange it prior
to leaving Home) We will pay You:
a) the non-refundable unused portion of all travel costs prepaid
in advance including the travel agent?s commission (the travel
agent?s commission is limited to the lesser of $4,000 or the
amount of commission the agent had earned on the pre-paid
refundable amount of the cancelled travel arrangements).
b) for frequent flyer or similar flight reward points lost following
cancellation of Your airline ticket. The amount We will pay is
calculated as follows:
(i) the cost of the equivalent class airline ticket, based on the
best available advance purchase airfare at the time the claim is
processed, less Your financial contribution towards the airline
ticket multiplied by
(ii) the total amount of points lost divided by
(iii) the total amount of points used to obtain the airline ticket.

Oh great! So as I haven't yet left home, and looks like i will have to cancel the journey and book another flight or if nothing available I will need to cancel the trip, Covermore will come to my rescue! 

BUT WAIT!!!

The fine print then tells me that : 

We Will Not Pay For
Claims caused by:
1. Transport Provider caused cancellations, delays or rescheduling
other than when caused by strikes.

So basically my cancellation cover is USELESS unless the airline workers go on strike. 
Any other cause for cancellation and we are at the mercy of the Airline

Good job guys. Now I know which insurance policy to never go for and to warn everyone I can to stay away from it. It's COVERMORE or rather Cover-No-More

Everything. Even before the trip commenced the ridiculous CoverMore fine print resulted in immense disappointment

title: Any communication and claims process is a nightmare
body:
I agree with most of the reviews here... SETUP is not a problem. Of course because it means they receive payment. The problems begins there after... Any communication and claims process is a nightmare:

- Allianz is unable to meet any of their "guarantees". They guarantee being able to find you high quality health care around the world where ever you are within 24 hours. I was in Turkey, in Trabzon, not "in the wild" by any means but they were unable to find me a suitable place for an MRI scan. Further, I gave them 24 hours notice BEFORE arriving in Trabzon, it took them 4 days to reply which meant I was paying for accommodation in a place I visited solely for treatment. It should have been a quick 24 hour treatment and then continuation of my planned travel schedule. (I am still negotiating with Allianz to receive payment for these unplanned accommodation days in Trabzon - it has now been over 1 month since submitting my claim and Allianz last communication with me was over 15 days ago. Allianz guarantee a 10 day turn around for claims whether in the form of payment or further communication).

- When I found a hospital MYSELF that was suitable, and this hospital contacted Allianz on my behalf, Allianz refused to offer funding or even communicate with this hospital before speaking to me first. The problem here was that Allianz had already given me written permission to get an MRI so it should have been a simple "yes, all systems go". An even larger problem exists here... imagine if it had been a life threatening case and Allianz had stamped their foot and demanded to speak to me before giving the "yes, go ahead" permission. Absolutely disgraceful. 

- Allianz always provide the most basic health care they can "escape with". Allianz take the cheapest and least action possible. Do not think for a second that you have to right to just take yourself to the dentist or the local hospital for an MRI or X-ray as you would in your own country. Every decision you make regarding your health must be first reported and cleared as "ok" by their medical department before proceeding. You have zero autonomy. You must report like a child to a distrusting adult. In my situation, I severely injured/tore ligaments in my ankle. Allianz defined my injury as a standard day to day "rolled ankle" type injury. I have skateboarded all my life where one regularly rolls one's ankle but you do not need crutches. In this particular case (snowboarding injury) I was on crutches. I was on a long term overseas trip, planning to travel for 1-2 years. Allianz first treatment advice was that of RICE (rest, ice, compression, elevation) for the first week and then a further review. RICE is a standard "First Aid" treatment and is designed solely for initial treatment immediately post injury to assist with further comprehensive treatment and assessment. Allianz continued to advise this same treatment for over a month, resulting in me being stuck in Japan, unable to travel, paying for accommodation (which Allianz refused to cover). I have medical training and can safely assess when I require more then just a physical assessment to rule out further complications. It was 3 months before Allianz agreed to an MRI. When they received the MRI they were unable to translate it from Turkish into English. Their own Turkish agents were also unable to translate it into English meaning I still had no idea of the outstanding reason for pain and swelling after 3 months - I re-iterate here - NOT a standard rolled ankle. Disgraceful guarantee of being able to offer suitable care ALL AROUND the world. Imagine if I had been in the Amazon or somewhere more remote... 

- Further, if you ask for permission to have more in depth medical treatment or assessments (other then First Aid treatments such as RICE), their customer service agents casually start mentioning "repatriation" - threats of being sent home. If Allianz sends you home, it means they don't have to pay out any medical costs. All medical costs back in your own country are paid for by your private or public insurance in your own country. It means Allianz can wipe their hands clean of your case... all they need to do is pay for your flight home. Hopefully you STILL HAVE your day to day health insurance in your own country. Woe to you if you don't. The injury is now your problem - sucker. 

- Due to the constant reporting and communication needed to clear up problems, ask permission or simply provide directions, you are required to constantly call or write to Allianz. This means spending money on overseas phone calls. Allianz provide an overseas "free call" number but to use this number you must first call the "connector" in the current country in which you are residing. In Australia or America or a westernised country this poses no problem but try giving this phone number to a hospital or to a hotel / hostel and then explaining that they must first call the "connector" and try explaining all of this in your non native tongue... try this in India for example - it is absolutely impossible and extremely frustrating. For those of you who don't know, to use this "free call" number, there is another number that you must call first (which is different in every country) which connects you to a particular person / department which you must then provide the "free call" number to this person to then be connected to Allianz. Allianz provide no list of these numbers for every country around the world. This meant I had to wear the cost of all the constant calls. Further, for those of you who travel a lot, you know how sparse WiFi can be and that stopping every moment to write another email while you are on road is impossible and results in missed buses, extra accommodation costs, lost time for museums or archeological sites or trekking or whatever the case may be. Allianz, you need to take more responsibility in this area by first providing a list of the connector phone numbers around the world plus being more comprehensive and minimalistic (more clear information / questions in less emails and phone calls) with your communication requirements.

- Allianz guarantee that "We will process your claim within 10 working days of receiving a completed claim form and all necessary documentation. If we need additional information, a written notification will be sent to you within 10 working days". I have sent in my claim on the 19th July. I received their first response on 6th August. I replied and provided the extra information they required. I have received no response since my reply. There is no evidence online of my claim or possible progress that they have made. 

- To make matters worse I took out my cover policy through an agent. I thought that this agent was covering me and that I would be communicating with them. I found out later I was covered by Allianz and the agent was unable to provide any assistance after the sale process. Very disappointing on the agent's behalf. 

- Allianz is a disgraceful, dishonest, and unprofessional company to deal with. The above written information does not capture the heart ache, lost time (hour and hours of emails and phone calls - which in my business should be billed to Allianz), lost funds, and frustration that I have experienced. There were many other continuing problems and other claims. Dealing with Allianz is like dealing with large telecommunications companies such as Telstra or Vodafone or something similar in your country. It is like talking to a computer. I highly recommend you find a different option. Maybe a smaller company. Don't expect to be heard or be treated like a human. Allianz cannot and will not be fit for long term travelling HOWEVER If your choice of travel is 2 weeks here, 3 weeks there, hit a few capital cities and stay in hotels and hostels and on well walked / travelled roads then I am sure Allianz can provide what you need BUT stay away from jungles, camping, trekking, cycling, rock climbing, in depth cultural experiences, photography adventures for the special rare shot of animal species or geographical phenomenons or anything outlandish or adventurous.

Just wanted to share my experience on what should be a very simple claim with covermore, especially after reading the "glowing" reviews below.
I made a claim as our flight to LA was delayed, resulting in us missing our connecting flight. I have claimed for reimbursement of the second flight we had to book. Two weeks after I submitted all the required documents, I received an email saying they required further information, a receipt for the second flight purchased. This had already been submitted, however I forwarded it again. Today, two weeks after I submitted the receipt for the second time, I received an email asking how much I was claiming for as I was the only person on the policy. You have to be kidding me, the policy clearly has mine and my husbands name on it, as did all the supporting documents, air fare tickets etc. Very poor service.

title: Great Service and Understanding
body:
We have used InsureandGo previously and always very easy to organise etc(never made a claim yet)
We were traveling to USA end April 2020 and i booked insurance to cover it on 3rd February via phone with consultant .As i did not book this time online, the consultant who i discussed the policy with unfortunately did not tell me as it was after 29th January (InsurenadGo policy decision)that Coronavirus would not be covered by InsureandGo .I would not have booked the policy had i known this. 
In subsequent discussions with InsureandGo this week they have accepted that i should have been informed of no cover for this issue and have now agreed to refund my insurance premium which they have now done . I am thoroughly impressed with this/acceptable fair  business decision and when i re book holiday for a later time i will certainly use InsureandGo for the policy.Thank you for understanding and great service from David (team member)and other staff  when i phoned to discuss the issue   
Spare a thought for all personnel in insurance/travel /hoilday industry as to what they must be going through with this nasty virus as it must be extremely frustrating and energy sapping in trying to deal with it ongoing  .   Lets all hope the virus is bought under control quickly 
Phil

title: Good value, minimal fuss when claiming insurance

I was a little worried at first that these guys were a little dodgy as they were so much cheaper than everyone else. But as it turned out I had nothing to worry about. I stepped on a sea urchin whilst swimming in Thailand. I contacted them within 24 hours of the injury. It ended up costing me $265 AUD in medical costs. I filled out the forms within 30 days of coming back to Australia. I sent travel insurance claim forms on a Friday. It got approved on a Tuesday. Money was in my bank account by Thursday. I think as long as you make sure you abide by all there T & C's you will have no problems with these guys. I was very happy with them and will purchase with them in the future.
Cheap, no fuss when claiming.

title: Don't try and claim
body:
I have used Insure & Go in the past and never have put in a claim. After reading many good reviews thought we would use them again for our next trip....Big mistake. After accidently leaving my mobile phone in a chemist and racing back as soon as I realised only to find that it had been taken.
 I rang Insure & Go to tell them what happened, the woman on the phone said that I could claim for the loss of my phone, she told me I would need various forms of paperwork to go with my claim, I went about organising all of this including getting a police report whilst in Bali . 
I submitted my claim with all the relevant paperwork, only to be informed 2weeks later that my claim for my phone had been rejected due to the fact that it had been left unattended in a public place !  Why offer cover for loss if there is no intention of covering lost items. No one intentionally leaves something of value in a public place ,hence  it is lost !
 I think Insure & Go might need to reconsider their policies in regards to lost items or maybe don't give people the false hope that their items will be covered if lost whilst travelling . Maybe Insure & Go needs to be more transparent with their policies .

I have lodged a complaint but I am sure it will go no where.
Thanks for wasting my time & money Insure & Go.

title: WARNING TO TRAVELLERS - DON'T USE COVERMORE!!
body:
I had to give a rating so I gave 1 star, but I actually wouldn't like to give any. 
Insensitive, inhumane people.  Would far from recommend to anyone and will not use them again.  Worst experience during a very tough and testing time.  There is no point in paying $10 for insurance on AirNZ flights because these people do not pay out.  
Would not pay out for flight changes we had to make for my father and mother to get to a specialist appointment as he was diagnosed with terminal cancer 3 days before they were due to fly out, and was given 3-6 months to live.  They say it was because he was put on a waiting list for a gastroscopy two days before we booked the flights.  GP had said this would take place 2 or 3 months after we would fly to my brother?s engagement.  So we booked flights.  Opportunity came for him to have the gastroscopy 4 months earlier. This was investigating anemia.  While they were investigating this they got suspicious of the liver so he was sent for more tests.  We had no idea what was going on, the doctors only told us 3 days before they flew that he had terminal cancer.  Even though we got doctors certificates to say he was still fit to fly, and a note from his GP to say he is suffering from a terminal illness and may need to return home quickly, these inhumane people would not accept anything and closed the case.  As this is a very tough time for us all it was passed on to a family advisor but they refused to talk to him. 
Warning, whatever your situation, they will have a ?policy wording? for it so they don?t have to pay out.
Worst people ever.

title: Terrible level of cover- especially for solo travellers. Cannot recommend to anybody!
body:
I took out insurance with TID back in June this year before going on a 4 1/2 month trip through Asia on my own. The cover is affordable and appears to be highly rated and recommended- even when reading other reviews.

My trip went very smooth up until 4 days before returning home where my luggage was stolen from the luggage holding point at the Gili Air Harbour in Indonesia. Everything which I had taken and lived with as well as collected over 4 1/2 months had been stolen. As a solo traveller this was a very stressful situation to be in, thank goodness I had my passport on me! The remainder of my trip was spent emailing hotels and boat companies in case there was any sighting of my bag, and collecting appropriate documentation for my insurance claim. TID denied my insurance claim deeming the incident to be my fault as I left it unsupervised despite leaving it with the boat company I was travelling with. 

The cost of the insurance and the time spent collecting information for my claim was all a waste and the piece of mind that I believed I was purchasing prior to travelling was false. Thank goodness I was not making a claim for a health issue or hospital visit!

They will either point you to a list in their PDS of what is covered, and if a pandemic isn't listed there, then it won't be covered, no different to breaking your fourth vertebrate and twisting your arm:-  Since this specific injury isn't listed there, they will argue that it isn't listed under "What is covered" 

Allianz Credit Card Complimentary Insurance is a SCAM and not to be ever used or trusted. You've been Warned! 

If anyone else has experienced the same response from Allianz, please let me know, so we can start a class action law suit.

title: Does not Pay out legit Claims. Stay away from this travel insurance.
