title: Was told hospital was covered - debt collector contacted me 1 year later with $1000 bill
body:
I used the annual coverage for years. I tore a ligament in my knee and required xrays in the USA. At the hospital the receptionist spoke directly to covermore. I was told I had 2 options - pay upfront and then submit a claim on return to Australia or pay the excess and covermore deals directly with the hospital. I chose to pay the excess, and trusted everything else was dealt with. 12 months later I received a letter from an international debt collector for $1000. I was never told I would need to pay for the xrays, never received a bill - so you can imagine my surprise! I also imagine this is affecting my credit rating. When I asked covermore I was told that I was never guaranteed cover and that I will need to submit a claim. Because the hospital dealt directly with covermore and I did not ever receive a bill - I am finding it very hard to make a claim and receiving no assistance. 

I am extremely disappointed with this product, and feel very nervous about going to hospitals overseas under this coverage. 

Covermore if you are reading this - some help would be much appreciated, as your staff are not replying to my emails

title: Read the PDS and make sure you don?t miss a thing
body:
Make sure you read the PDS. If you loose something or have an accident or anything, get the PDS out and read it straight away. There are many reasons in the PDS that they can find to reject a claim. Don?t bother claiming unless you have an original receipt for the product that was lost. The policies seem to be great, well priced and easy to purchase. Not so easy to make a claim. You may find that your credit card has insurance attached to it if you buy the travel tickets with the card. Use the card? insurance instead. If you have ticked every box and are successful in making a claim this is when it gets even better. They pay you a pro rated amount for the product. Not the full amount. Really, shop around for travel insurance. TID looks great, but I can only give them 1 Star here. We won?t be using them again, ever. 
P.S. we contacted customer support after submitting our claim to reduce the amount of the claim and quess what TID did, nothing.

On my next trip, I would definitely not go with Cover-More again. I cannot believe I was naive enough to believe that paying such a high price for insurance would actually mean that my items would be insured. Definitely not recommended to anyone - I would have been better off not paying the $196.00 insurance premium, and going through the hassels of submitting a claim only to receive such a disappointing result.
Very prompt, got back to me in 5 days, but I would prefer them to take more time and consider the claim more carefully

We broke our trip to attend the funeral (from South Africa), and after all the obsequies were finished, rejoined the trip. Covered? NO....she should have died in Australia, and we would have been covered! Apparently in the fine print on page 23 of one of the documents! Why on earth would it make any difference as to where your mother died? The company initially did not reply to three emails over a two month period, and so reluctantly I went the ring-in route and was transferred three times after the usual interminable delays, only to be told that my mother-in-law had not done the right thing by dying in the right place......incredible! I notice most of the reviews are about the ease of obtaining the policy, not about claims.....hmmmm?.

The only email responses you get is to say they will contact you in 10 days which they dont do and today I have been in the phone Que  now for  one hour and twenty five minutes so far.  While waiting for a response today I will lodge my complaint with the Australian Financial Complaints Authority and would encourage others to do the same. It seems clear they are delaying hoping you will just drop your claim because it is too hard. Here is the link  https://www.afca.org.au/make-a-complaint

title: C.B.A. ALLIANZ TRAVEL INSURANCE...... STAY AWAY FROM THIS COMPANY
body:
After paying extra annual fees for a GOLD AMEX and Gold MasterCard credit cards, because a Commonwealth Bank Branch advised us that we could get "FREE TRAVEL INSURANCE" if we had the "Gold Cards", these Gold Cards of course have an increase of around $80.00 annual fee verses credit cards that do not have the Travel Insurance and extra Qantas Points as an incentive. However after reading the Allianz travel insurance policy contract, it basically states in writing "Allianz will NOT PAY FOR most items which are most commonly claimed on travel insurance claims" and if they do then the excess is incredibly expensive! My advise to anyone depending on this Travel Policy is READ THE CONTRACT CLEARLY, BEFORE YOU TRAVEL I have read it and fortunately before travel started I got a different policy from another Insurance provider / company. I will soon cancel the two Com Bank Gold Credit Cards. As the increased annual credit card fee for the extra Qantas points does not equate to a good deal either as 4 Com Bank credit card points = 1 QFF point, it's a joke! My advise is save the credit card fee money and pay for your fare outright as it will be cheaper in the long run!
Commowealth Bank and Allianz should be ashamed of themselves for theiving from there long term Bank Customers for trying to CON CUSTOMERS.... absolutely terrible!

title: Cant leave without it
body: Good value policy and easy to apply. I didn't have to claim but I had complete peace of mind. See a bye.

title: Horrible/unorganised/useless/dont care about the customer at all
body: Absolutely disgraceful insurance. Had about $13000 worth of stuff stolen in January on holiday and the claim is still processing and we have been told about 5 times the payment should be in our bank in 3-5 business days to then call up when its not in and be told we need to wait another 3-5 days. Then get told the 4th time that its been audited and they had reduced the payment again by another $1000. Ill fight this poor service till we get treated like a paying customer. They are more than happy to accept your payment for insurance but as soon as you need something paid out they wait as long as they can hoping you will give up!!! Dont ever use this service!!!!

title: No goodwill shown in these extraordinary times.
body: I understand we purchased a contract for specific dates. InsureandGo is running a business-I get that. I unsuccessfully asked for a future credit for when we can reschedule not a refund. The goodwill generated and our future loyalty to the brand in these extraordinary circumstances would have been guaranteed. We are personally seeing generous rescheduling provisions from other ?non-refundable? travel arrangers.  IAG interestingly have just announced they will refund all their travel insurance policies no longer applicable.

title: Insureandgo is perfect
body: This is the first and will not be the last time.I will recommend this company to all my friends.I have no more words.

title: WORST travel insurance company - stay away
body: DO NOT purchase this travel insurance, they have no idea about customer service. It has been almost 2 months since I made my claim and have never been able to speak to a real person. They have a 15-day response time on reply email only (seriously 15 days.. but you end up waiting longer!!) when you call them - they take a message but nobody ever calls you back. This company is a joke.

title: Never Again Will I Choose Allianz
body: Rude and arrogant staff. Very slow with my claim, always ringing for information already given to them. It was easier for them to ring me then to read through our claim information. Put me of travelling again in case I ever needed to make a claim in the future. Will never recommend to friends or family.

title: Only one to use

title: Easy to use online

title: Quick to take my money, not so quick to pay back
body:
I have to say I am disappointed (that is not strong enough) I am furious with you guys as it never occurred to me I would not get what I felt was a legitimate claim, but when I read the fine print and your very generous interpretations of what a "public place" and  "due care" were, I realised yet again the insurance companies win and it was never even a vague contest. title: Do not buy expecting rental car excess insurance
body: Our rental car received a small dent in a theme park from some unknown low life who left no details. The invoice for repair provided by the rental company totalled just over $1600 so wasn't covered by the car rental company insurance (we had to pay the first 2200). We opted not to take the rental car company optional excess insurance as we already held the Allianz policy... So we submitted our claim with all details required, thinking this will be straight forward. Unfortunately that couldn't be further from the truth. First up I received a text message a few days after submitting the claim. The message said please call "home front" regarding your claim. No contact details were provided and the phone number the text was received from could not be used. I called Allianz and quoted the number on the text. They confirmed the text related to my claim number but they had no idea who Homefront was?? They advised the text I received was an error. A week or so later I received a phone call from a claims manager advising me they were about to decline my claim. In short, the reason, the rental company calls the amount a "single accident fee" rather than an excess. At this point I am still fighting the details with them, but be warned... It is not worth taking this insurance if you are hoping to be covered for your rental car excess. They WILL try and weasel out of it!

title: Poor company
body: We booked a trip to France in may for my 50th birthday in October, as we've never travelled together before we bought the insurance on the advice of the travel agent. In September after having no health issues in the passed I was  diagnosed with a kidney disease and advised not to travel for between 4-6months as one of the complications was high risk of blood clots. We cancelled our flights and rebooked for February. We had to incur further expense to change the flights which we understood we could claim due to health reasons. Apparently easier said than done. So far we have experienced delay after delay for the claim. We submit the forms they ask for the 10 days later they ask for something else another delay for 10 days. The last 2 times we submitted what they asked we asked if they had everything they need and we were told yes. Now they are asking for my clinical notes, for which I'll need to go threw freedom of information act to get access to. More delay tactics. This is a terrible company who pray on people when they are most vulnerable they seem to delay until people become frustrated and give up. Give this company a wide berth, I'd give no stars if I could, still waiting for my money.

title: Just don't waste your time getting insurance from Covermore, they will avoid paying at any cost
body:
On a recent trip overseas my camera stopped working and my phone stopped charging about 1/2 way through the trip. Both of these were clearly not caused by me (obviously I wanted to use both the camera and the phone on the trip, otherwise I would not have taken them). They were just merely accidental damage while on a trip overseas. I was annoyed at the time but I thought, no this is why you pay for travel insurance.

Covermore will "probably" cover you if you lose your luggage or a 100kg gorilla stands on your bag ("probably" because after this experience I think they will find a clause to get out of those as well) but if for some unexplainable reason your electrical or mechanical devices cease to perform the function they are supposed to perform, they will refuse to cover it.

Their PDS very clearly advertises that they cover damage to phones and cameras, but once you read the fine print they have a clause that says they don't cover damage due to "electrical or mechanical breakdown". Long story short it is a convoluted get out of jail free card for pretty much everything else but dropping and smashing your phone into smithereens. 

Why does this annoy me? Because I have used Covermore about 4 times a year for 7+ years. I am a long standing, very loyal customer that never claimed a cent in the past. I have what I thought was a legitimate claim when two items of my luggage cease to function while on a holiday and Covermore have so far spent the best part of 6 weeks giving me a run around.

They don't cover you for damage.

They made a lot of requests for paperwork in multiple forms in English and did not readily accept alternatives or understand I was not travelling with a printer for their forms.....After I took the process in to my own hands - organised flights, transfers, liaison with airport and airline re mobility assistance etc, the insurance was quite willing to pay my preferred supplier. title: Will do anything to avoid paying a medical claim
body:
TL;DR - Sick in USA mid-June, put in claim immediately. Jerked around for two months, still no outcome on insurance claim, it's now late August.

I purchased travel insurance for my trip to the North & Central America for June/July 2013. I did so thinking that the areas I was going to had a reputation for travellers being robbed, and I should be prepared, should my camera/credit cards/other valuables be stolen. I had purchased travel insurance with TID before, and had never had to claim - the reviews were good, what could go wrong?

Well, it turns out I would be robbed, but not by an individual. By TID. While in a cafe in San Francisco on the 17th of June, I fainted in line, hit my head, and while I was unconscious, the cafe called an ambulance. Fun thing about America, they are terrified of lawsuits. So I wake up to a barista who is an RN in her home country, letting me know an ambulance is coming. I?m not exactly in a position to complain. 

The paramedics come, assess me and decide that I should be looked at at the nearest hospital - I email TID from my phone *in the ambulance*, ask what I should do. Doctor isn?t sure if I have pneumonia, does an X-Ray decides to rule it as bronchitis. They release me, tell me my bill will probably be around $4,500. Thank god I got travel insurance, right?

So, I go back to my hotel, and now that I?m in a place where I?m able to use Skype to make phone calls, look at the website to see what I?m supposed to do. Right, call Specialty Assist. 
(gentle reader, I hear you ask: ?what of the email you sent?? - no response until over 12 hours later. This would be my fastest response from TID, ever.) 
Specialty Assist send me a bunch of documents to fill out. I print them out and scan them, returning by email within 24 hours. Over the next weeks during my holiday, I will go on to waste hours emailing and filling out & scanning forms. 

It?s a waste because I?ll go on to hear nothing from them about the outcome of my case. Eventually, when I realise ?okay, these guys have had enough time? on the 30th of july (that?s right - a month and a half later!) they'll reply with ?The insurance company have told us that as this is no longer an emergency assistance case that we should to close our file and advise that you should submit a claim to Cerberus.?
Are. You. Joking. Not until I emailed them did anyone tell me.

I contacted TID. Asked what?s going on. Was told to submit a claim through TID. On paper. They will mail it to me. That?s right. All those hours I should have been enjoying myself on holiday that were lost to paperwork were for nothing. The paper form eventually arrives. It?s asking the same questions I already filled out for Specialty Assist. Including the one about your regular GP. I don?t have one of those. I don?t get sick beyond a regular flu - If I think I need to, I?ll go to whichever clinic is closest and open. I've already given TID permission to see my medicare record.

I emailed and resubmitted, following all instructions I was given ?For the attention of [name removed]? on August 5th. I hear nothing back until August 8th ?Thank you for sending through your documents, please be advised that they have been passed on to the case manager for review.?

Hear nothing back. We?re now close to two months after the event. I call them on the 16th of August, ask what?s happening. Again, I'm the one initiating contact. The girl I speak to tells me I need to submit a claim online.

What. No. Are you kidding me. I am not filling out a third claim.

I tell her, no fracking way am I doing that. I *just* emailed in my claim on August 5th, as I was told to by [name removed].
Oh. Um, do I mind waiting on hold?
She comes back. When did you email the stuff in?
I tell her. 
Okay, um, I?m going to put you on hold again.
She comes back, tells me that it takes ten business days for someone to assess the claim, so I shouldn?t have expected to hear back until Friday (9th of August) or Monday (12th of August)
Fine. I can wait four extra days.
No surprise, those days come and go. 

August 20th, I email info@tid.com.au again. ?What is happening with this case? I keep trying to follow it up, and am getting no response.?
[name removed] calls back that night (8ish at night), makes a lot of ?I understand you?ve had a lot of bad experiences with us and I sincerely hope going forward we can work together to improve your outcomes, I can hear in your tone that you?re unhappy with me??
No, this is my usual speaking voice.
?Yeah you?re frustrated, that?s been your tone from the start?
If anything, I?m now annoyed by the fact you?re passing judgement on my voice. Dude, it?s been two months with no action and I?m not swearing and yelling. I?m keeping my tone even. "Sorry, this is just how I talk".
He asks when a good time to call and let me know what?s happening. I have a late shift the next day, so I say before 11:00am the next day. 
[name removed] calls at 10:30, so kudos to him.

Says that it was a "technical error" and [name removed] never submitted my paperwork. So all the conversations I?ve had in August were a lie.
A second call comes at 11:23am, but I?m already at work. I have a message from [name removed] from claims, asking to call her back. I do that afternoon and find out I was missing the itemised bill from my claim, email it through that afternoon with all of the other info I had, but was never asked to submit (basically one other disclaimer from the hospital).

title: WARNING: Comprehensive is not actually comprehensive
body:
Hi All,

On a trip in Europe I had my 'business' bag stolen in Krakow Poland. It had over $3,785.67 of electronics (not hard when an iphone is $1,800). I received a police statement and lodged the claim.

After months of back and forth, the most this company is willing to offer is $1,200 to replace the items stolen when I bought comprehensive insurance. The reasons stated is 1) depreciation (which they will not provide me the depreciation schedule and none of the equipment was old enough where the resellable value would have been that low on the second hand market) and 2) there was an ambiguous $750 cap on all electronic items. The reason why I say ambiguous is because the product disclosure statement 'Luggage and Personal Effects^ $7,500, Including sub-limits for laptops, tablets, cameras and video cameras, mobile phones only $3,000'. At this point I stopped reading, but underneath that is 'Including single article limit/pair or set of items limit $750.'

I don't believe anyone in Australia would agree that $750 is enough to cover a high quality phone, camera, laptop or any high quality electronic device.

Anyway, STAY AWAY. I am submitting a further review to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority and recommend anyone in a similar position to do the same.

title: Dont rely on the included car excess !

This was our first need to claim on travel insurance - although we have always taken it with Covermore.
The insurance cover states that they will cover the cost of  out-of-pocket excess on car rental damage.  They won`t - without a fight!   We had a small ding with our car, getting it back into the Europcar depot in Lyon, France. Europcar charged us just over 1000 euros for repairs and when we returned home we put in a claim accompanied by all the paperwork.  Covermore refused to pay the bill unless we supplied the original workshop repair invoice - something the customer is not given.   We had 6 months trying to contact the repair garage in Lyon in our limited French before we could get the requested repair sheet. The garage said it was an `unusual` request but eventually sent it (all in french and largely illegible).  Only after 9 months and a threat to go to comsumer affairs did we get a cheque from Covermore. Imagine if we had had to go back to a garage in Mongolia or Zimbabwe or somewhere remoter than France!
Its easy to pick up with your tickets at the travel agency

This means I can't claim for my original flight that got diverted to Christchurch! After no emails or phone calls from TID I finally contacted them and they told me that they would only pay me for the re-booked flight from Christchurch to Queenstown for $6.23! (after $100 excess). Come on TID, do the right thing and cover my original ticket, because there were no more flights with that airline until the next day I could of got a hotel in Christchurch, transfers and meals over night and claimed for "delayed" flight for more than 12 hours [section 6: Travel Delay] and not had to pay any excess and it would of cost you 3 times the amount, but instead I booked with another airline and saved you money! Let the buyer beware, you actually have to deal with "Cerberus Special Risks" when you make a claim... not so friendly! Imagine if you had to make a big expenses claim!

body: First time to use this insurance company for holiday insurance. The price is right and it seems to cover all my needs.

title: We will likely use Allianz for our next overseas travel
body: We compared nine policies to cover two people over 65 for five weeks in Europe. Allianz cost less than most and offered all the cover we needed. It was easy to set up. Documentation was readable and clearly explained the cover.

title: Peace of mind
body: Applied online had cover immediately, TID followed up to ensure all was well. I didn't need to make a claim but l am confident that all would be well if l needed too.

title: Easy and fast claim process
body: We had to cancel our holiday and the claim process was fairly simple and the processed within a week. All the paperwork was emailed they and we just needed to fill it out and send it back via email.

title: So simple
body: I have only just purchased and am yet to travel. The process could not have.been easier. Great price too. I would have thought I would have received email confirmation with policy details.

title: Best cover I found!
body: The policy process was so easy. No need for all the medical questions if you chose that option, and the value I found was as good as any other travel insurance provider. I am very happy, please keep up the good work!

body:
- Average value, $2 less than policy offered by airline (short duration). Noticable that all email promotional discounts I receive as regular user, do not apply to basic policy, I suppose not enough margin.
- yes

title: Disgusting
body: I bought insurance in February for my upcoming trip in July however due to COVID-19 I had to defer my trip to 2021, I rang Insure and go in April 15th to have a refund or credit I was told no I since then sent 3 emails to their complaints department with no response.  I have been on a lot of overseas trips and always insured with Insure  and go but in times like this you really do find out how good your travel insurance company is, I will never again insure with Insure and go.

title: Very easy to buy.
body: Very easy to buy which was good. I didn't have to use it but that's also good. I wouldn't travel without it. I have other Allianz policies so it made sense to pick this policy.

title: Absolutely disgusting to do business with during a global pandemic
body: I have no good words to say about Cover-More Travel Insurance. Yes, I understand we are in a global pandemic and yes, I completely understand that there are many people who are wanting their insurance refunded/credited. In saying that hire more people to deal with the high volume. Cover-More should have had a backup plan for when something like this happened. I emailed in March for my refund. No reply. I phoned in April and after being left on hold for 2 hours I gave up. Emailed again, nothing. Tried the live chat many times, nothing. Disgusting!!! Absolutely disgusting. If a global pandemic can happen once it can happen again. Maybe be better prepared next time Cover-More.

title: Took 3 months for outcome
body:
Absolutely pathetic customer service and took them three months to come with an outcome. Would not recommend Allianz insurance to anyone. Waste of money.
No support at all. Avoid any Allianz insurance.

title: Easy to do

title: Family Travel Insurance
body: We have used Insure and Go on a number of occasions. We have also used Insure and Go for our son when he has travelled to Thailand on numerous occasions. We will be using Insure and Go for our next travel.

title: applied for cover online
body: Applied for cover online. While completing the online form a box at the top right hand side of my computer screen displayed a $dollar value in AUD. I proceeded to the payment section and received confirmation of the payment. Payment of $650 was confirmed but this was almost double the $350 that was displayed throughout the form completion process.

title: A Fantastic & Trustworthy Group.
body:
This was my original Insurance Ploicy with "INS & GO"....& I was so thankful that we had organized our travel insurance with Them...as , almost at the last minute, just a couple of weeks before going for a longish flight & a much anticipated European River Cruise, I was suddenly deemed as being "unable to travel" caused by some unexpected impinged sciatic nerve problem, due to which my G.P. declared, that this trip was definitely impossible for me.
We...a group of 3 seniors, were forced to, regretfully cancel, but were so delighted with the help & understanding from this insurance company, as one reads so many problems encountered by travelers tryng to cancel & claim via insurance...that we were absolutely delighted with the help, consideration & attitude ...plus a complete refund...from Insure & Go .....
I can thoroughly recommend InsureandGo Australia to anyone requiring & honest & responsible Travel Insurance Group, along with their fantastic staff, who were definitely there to assist us in every possible way, during this extremely depressing PLUS financially "trying" situation.

title: Expectations more than exceeded
body:
Following some minor damage to a hire car in Norway, the hiring company was very reluctant to provide to me the necessary documentation required to validate the claim, but after much haggling provided the necessary materials. On the other hand, CoverMore could not have been easier to deal with and dealt with my claim without question.
Efficient and hassle free

title: good to have that security
body: Easy to set up, didn't have to claim but happy to have the policy "just in case". Wouldn't travel without it, especially when you hire a RV to travel around in!

title: It took time a full refund made
body:
My solo holiday to the USA was booked in September 2109, well before Covid19 struck.  In late February, I was told I needed urgent heart surgery and must cancel my holiday.  In early March I began claims procedure.  The airfare was refunded through my insurance agent quite quickly.  At the end of July Cover-More finally paid out all the other booking deposits I had made.  Not once has it been possible to speak to them on the phone.  Automatic email responses have eventually been followed by requests for additional information and additional information and yet further information.  Had I been less persistent and insistent, or had my June surgery not been effective, this claim would have "fallen through the cracks" and not paid out.  

However - in the end, they paid up and that is the final measure of any insurance company.

title: so far...

We bought an annual domestic policy and have had one claim so far which was covered; I claimed on-line and received the payment within 2 weeks of claiming. We added the ski coverage as well which was so reasonable, but thankfully have not had to claim anything. So far, it has been excellent value for money.

title: Will use again

body:
My flight home from Thailand was cancelled and I had to purchase additional flights as I am a Midwife and had to be in the country for a birth. Two months later still waiting for my claim. I am a gold
level Medibank health insurance customer but apparently the loyalty doesnt cross over to travel insurance. Really disappointed. Have sent follow emails going on two weeks now and havent heard anything.

title: Easy application at a great rate.
body: Great value, easy and no fuss. Would definitely use it again and recommend it to anyone I know who would be travelling in the near future. Travel insurance is a must.

title: Don't touch it!
body: My elderly mum became unwell and was hospitalised - that service was really good.  But after she was discharged from hospital there was delay after delay in getting clearance to fly home.  I was with her, which was good because I can speak some of the language and she can't, but the company's policies would not meet the costs of changing travel plans for my dad and me so that we could remain with her.  She was considered well enough to be on her own but not well enough to travel.  They wouldn't provide an interpreter for her either.  Lots of text messages, phone calls and emails were sent, most of which were never even acknowledged let alone answered.  End result - mum was expected to remain on her own in a foreign country without the ability to speak the language.  Cover-less/care-less would be more accurate.

title: Unhappy with Customer Service
body:
Due to my husbands pre existing condition we paid a higher premium for Gold insurance and were happy to do that. We purchased our insurance inDecember and like most had to cancel our trip due to COVID 19. We were told that we would be covered for cancellation. I had trouble filling out the online claim, so sent everything required by hard copy In early April. I got an email saying that they had received my documents and I would hear from a caseworker. I did hear back saying that more documentation was needed, so I once again sent through the paperwork (this time by email). Once again heard that my case was being reviewed, once again asked to send more documentation saying that they also required letters from the two airlines that I was using saying that they would not issue vouchers to us. This was confusing to me as we weren?t claiming airfares. I rang the office and was told that this was incorrect and that my paperwork had most probably been lost. Today I received another email saying that my paperwork had been received and once again told that a case worker would contact me. This has been going on since the beginning of April. I got off the phone today with a massive migraine. 
I am an ex airline employee, who in other times have recommended airlines, hotels, tour companies to friends and relatives. I now feel that I can offer no recommendation to Insure and Go
Regards,
Donna Johnston

title: Great insurance until you need to claim.
body:
I have insured with Covermore for many years.  We have never had any major claims, apart from some minor medical bills.  Those were done without any issue.  As such we have always been happy with it. 
However, we have booked a trip to Hong Kong at the beginning of the year.  I bought a premium insurance policy, specifically with cancellation cover.  In the mean time, there was a riot and protest in Hong Kong.  

I rang up to inquire if I can cancel my trip and be covered by the insurance.  They cannot answer this question and simply send me in circles! 

First, I spoke to the policy consultant.  She said she is only in charge of policy and cannot answer any question whether a claim can be made. She said I must make a claim in order to get an answer.  I said but I haven't cancelled yet?  She said "just make a claim and then the claim consultant can tell you if you can claim and the worse they can do is knock you back!"   I then made a claim and rang up again.  The claim consultant said I have to wait 10 days before they can even see my claim.   He cannot answer the question whether my policy allows me to claim.  He said I need to speak to the policy consultant.  I explained to him that I got sent by the policy consultant.  He said, just pretend you haven't made a claim and inquired about the policy.  When I got transferred to the policy consultant, she said, she has no idea about claim, and without surprise, she said, I must speak to the claim consultant!?  I hang up.

This seems a bit of a joke that an insurance company cannot even answer a question.   I thought I am doing the right thing by inquiring first before cancelling my trip.  

My trip is getting closer and I can only sit here for 10 days and wait to see if I can get covered before I cancel and make other alternate arrangements. 

I have a bad feeling after the 10 days, they will say something like, you havent cancelled your trip yet, so cannot claim.  You must cancel first, then make a claim and I can't claim at the end.  This is extremely frustrating and disappointing.

I will update this situation.  Until then, I will not recommend anyone buying from Covermore.

title: Great service
body:
Travelled using free credit card insurance last year. My phone was stolen. It took months and hoop after hoop to jump through all for $200.  I wasted twice that in time with red tape.
This year I went back to covermore. I hurt my ankle in remote northen Sumatra. Covermore were fantastic , organising flights , wheelchair with a helper at each airport and business class flights so I could elevate my leg.
To top that off, within 5 days of me issuing a further claim to cover loss of holiday etc. I received notification that my claim was to be paid in full. No hoops!
Unbelievably helpful for an insurance company.
Ill never use anyone else.
Thanks to all involved.
Cheers
Tim

body:

Our flights have been cancelled and we will receive a full refund from Emirates.  On contacting your call center to request a refund  (like other friends we were traveling who took out travel insurance with other companies) we too were referred to the 14 day cooling off period.  

Even though we are not able to claim on this policy or to travel due to travel bans, Insure and Go are not even offering a credit to be used later.

Will be using another company in the future.

title: Disappointing
body: I have used TID several times before but have never had to make a claim. This time had to make a claim for a cancelled international flight associated with my cruise being cancelled by the cruise company due to change of cruise schedules. TID were timely in their response to my initial claim (which was denied) and my request for reconsideration (which was also denied) based on the fine print which states that any associated travel cancellations associated with a change in scheduling by a travel service will not be covered. I find this inflexibility in implementing the fine print poor service to customers, particularly repeat customers. My mother who was also to travel with me and was with another insurance company had her claim for the flight paid out in spite of having the same fine print. Even though it was the cruise which was cancelled and I understood no direct costs associated with this company would be covered, and I was not claiming any costs directly associated with the cruise company involved (I had read the fine print when buying the policy and thought I would be covered for such things as flights provided by another separate company). Fortunately I only had to cancel one flight and not several otherwise I would have been significantly out of pocket in spite of trying to do the right thing by having travel insurance. title: A welcome surprise
body:
Two days before flying to France to watch the Tour de France I came off my bike, breaking a number of bones, so no tour for me! 
One I was recovered enough to think about lost money, I submitted  my claim to Covermore hoping to recoup airfares and rental paid in advance for a campervan. For the former I had good evidence to support my claim and was pretty sure Covermore would meet my claim, which it did. It was a different story, however, for the campervan as my son (who lives in Europe) had pre- paid the amount for me and in return I had paid some of his debts owing in Australia. I provided some evidence for this arrangement ( in the form of email exchanges and bank withdrawals) but clearly it wasn't in a form where I could argue that it was "straightforward". Luckily for me Covermore recognised that not everything goes to plan and sometimes a little latitude needs to be given. Thanks Covermore!

I have a six month old girl who got sick with a fever in an Eastern European capital city. Upon calling Allianz's so called "medical assistance", I was offered a telephone conversation with a nurse in Australia.

When I asked for them to arrange a doctor, I was told, "we don't do that, we rely on local knowledge to find doctors, but I can google some for you?" 

I was then given the address of the main public hospital that doesn't even take children, then proceeded to tell me that it was up to me to obtain a doctors report and estimate of costs if it cost more than 2000 dollars, which I should then send to Australia for them to assess. 

In the mean time I have a sick six month old baby? Go to hell Allianz.

I made my own arrangements, found a children's hospital and obtained treatment no thanks to Allianz. I will shortly be changing the car insurance I have with you when I return to Australia.

title: Amazing customer service turned a stolen camera into a great story!
body:
We were all the more confident taking our first overseas holiday as a couple with Covermore. When we had decided on our destination, I began to navigate the web of insurances, all with different requirements for a medical situation of mine and infuriatingly few details.  When I called Covermore, it was refreshing to speak with incredibly helpful, reassuring and comprehensively informed staff, and even more refreshing to hear that I didn't have to jump through any hoops to get cover. Off we set without another thought to insurance (as it should be)...until our camera was stolen in Vietnam.  We immediately called Covermore and received clear, easy to follow instructions as to what to do next, and even when we were unable to obtain a police report due to the language barrier, photos taken on our iPhones of the experience (including the kindly hotel concierge translating to the police for us, and our handwritten accounts of the incident!) were sufficient to prove that we had done all we could to follow the issue up with police. We were on our way again, and lodged the claim when we arrived home...and once again imagine our surprise when a claims officer went the extra mile and called us to clarify whether anything extra was stolen along with the camera (case, SD card etc) and the money was in our account a few days later.  I had never imagined the service would be so great - it turned that sinking feeling in the pit of my stomach into a great dinner table story!
Reliable, good coverage, excellent customer service, good value for money in my situation

title: The only travel insurance company I trust
body:
Unfortunately my children were hospitalized whilst travelling overseas on holiday, but TID were absolutely fantastic in supporting me and my family towards a speedy recovery every single step of the way.
My case was complex as essentially the whole family contracted the illness only 5 days before we were scheduled to go home. A summary of my experience is as follows:-

1. They provided a call back service for their assistance line knowing I didn't have a lot of credit on my pre-paid mobile, this was in the hospital at 2am when there was no place for me to recharge.
2. The support officer provided me guidance every step of the way including informing me what paperwork would be required by the hospital in advance
3. TID had a registered nurse that would call me every day to check up on my family to ensure we were well looked after and were recovering
4. We had to re-schedule our flights, again we were provided guidance on how to do this (we've never done it before)

Fast forward to our arrival in Australia, we had a massive medical bill and additional expenses which we needed to claim for. It took me about 45 minutes to fill out all the forms which was reasonable since we had a number of incidents, making sure I provided documents as requested. The quoted response times were 10 business days to have an officer assess my claim and being a bit cynical I thought TID would ask me for 100 extra documents and drag out the process. 5 business days in and the full claim was processed and the money in my bank account, and there was only one call by the claims officer to clarify two things. No additional paperwork apart from what I submitted through the form.

I can't thank TID enough for supporting me and my family throughout the ordeal. Highly recommended travel insurance company, and way better than the complimentary travel insurance offered through my various credit cards!

title: A less than 60% partial credit, when no service has been received, is not acceptable
body:
I purchased a gold international single policy on 10 February 2020 for $181.22 for a journey beginning 8 April 2020-10 May 2020. 

My airline, having indefinitely cancelled all flights, had given a full credit to rebook my flight, available until 31 August 2021. I telephoned Insureandgo on 6 April to request that my insurance policy be postponed accordingly. 

I was told no postponement or refund was possible and that I should contact the complaints department by email if I wasn't happy with that statement. I did so immediately, received a reply within the allocated time frame giving the same negative response. 

A further "internal review" resulted in a partial credit of $108 being offered on 21 May. This is not acceptable. I've paid for a service I haven't received. 

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has issued industry guidelines  as follows:

All policyholders, including consumers, eligible small businesses and larger businesses, who cancel travel plans will be able to get a credit or refund for any unused travel insurance premiums, again without administration or cancellation fees."  ACCC

I would like insureandgo, who I've used before for travel insurance, to do the moral thing, abide by the spirit of the ACCC guidelines and offer a FULL credit note. Not just to me but all customers in a similar position. 

Prior to publication of this review I accepted an option to mediate again with Insureandgo. I cannot fault "[name removed]" for the prompt and courteous customer service but despite numerous emails I did not receive any clarity as to why Insureandgo could only offer a partial (below 60%) credit. 

If  Insureandgo consider that "... the nature of travel insurance is different from flights and accommodation, as insurance is active as soon as you buy it", therefore "... pro-rata credit is the extent of the goodwill gesture" then why do many other of the large players in the travel insurance industry not think so? 

AIG, Suncorp, QBE and Allianz, are understood to be following the ACCC guidelines and offering full refunds or credits. Why can't Insureandgo be morally correct and do the same? 

I believe that there is an important ethical principle at issue here. I am not seeking financial compensation. I understand that these are difficult times for everyone. However, I paid for a service, the service was unable to be used at the specified time so I wish to postpone it.

With regret, I am rejecting the partial credit and will seek full redress via the industry Ombudsman. 

Extremely disappointing service from a large player in the industry who can well afford to recompense customers.

title: Very appalling staff conduct!
body:
My last trip to Malaysia in December 2012, was unfortunate enough to be robbed in a dodgy tourist area. I came back and made a claim with TID for the robbed items and went through the trouble of providing all the supporting documentations that was requested. These included receipts, pictures, police report, itunes history, and even sending my phone?s original box and other supporting items to TID. (I am told I won?t be reimbursed for the postage cost, this is not reasonable)
Then, today, on the fourth week of my claim being processed and also coincidentally the 10th day of my last correspondence, I received a call from TID informing me that a search through their insurance claim database has revealed. - That I recently made a similar claim with Commonwealth bank?s complimentary travel insurance! The details of which I?ve been told are for a claim made in early December 2012 for a similar attempted robbery!! I was shocked to hear this, but what is more shocking is that she then proceeds to question me (in a very sarcastic tone), what items have I submitted for this claim and received a payout for. This is insulting at best; an accusation implying that I?ve made similar claims with Commonwealth!
I know that there is no such claim being made and did not realise that Commonwealth bank provides complimentary travel insurance. She explains that I would have got it when I purchased the travel tickets through Commonwealth. I?m confused and so requested that she checks the recorded details with me. She confirms and spelled out my full name and date of birth recorded on this ?claim history?. (This is extremely appalling I later find) Many people would agree that, my full name is nowhere close to John Smith and is quite unconventional. The possibility of coming up with an incorrect record for similar name and DOB is just impossible.
The truly enraging part is that it occurred to me that the traveling ticket receipt, which I?ve provided, shows that the tickets is bought with a Commonwealth card. And, to top of the insult..! I went to the local Commonwealth Bank branch to clarify and was told that, only purchases made through their credit card (Gold and above) gets the complimentary travel insurance. Now I do not own a credit card with Commonwealth Bank!!
The bank can prove this, the only two cards I have ever owned with Commonwealth bank is a debit card linked to a savings account and a CommSec debit card which was never used. 
This is really a story to tell. I cannot believe that TID has gone to such lengths to support their own motives. 
I will be investigating my ?claim history? with Commonwealth Bank and keep you posted.

Appalling staff conduct..

Then I rang and a lovely young lady's voice said "of course we can help you..." & proceeded with the application over the phone! The second policy was the same, and now finally, when the security situation overseas seems to be easing, the one-year policy I secured just yesterday morning from one of your operators called [name removed], as I was with [name removed] driving to the airport for yet another trip with 1-day's notice to Angola & then Libya.I must have sounded apologetic about the short notice because she assured me that, yes, it was fine for me to take the policy out for my husband and no, it was not her intention to make him talk to her as he was driving and to tell him to have a safe trip!What could be easier than that!?

body: International call centre was terrible. No one called back. It took 3 days to get a flight back from Nha trang after my son broke his arm. title: Why even have travel insurance?
body:
After travelling to Europe and needing travel insurance, looked online and saw TID had some good reviews and i had used them before with no hassle. Had a hotel booking cancelled on us and had to rebook figured we would be ok since we have travel insurance. Get back to Aus and started a claim, downloaded the attached document, filled everything out, explained the situation and submitted all the relevant documents. Get an automated reply saying someone will get back to me, a week later someone emails and says they need further information which i had already provided in the original claim along with all the correct documents, so i tell them the situation again and attach all the same documents again! get another automated reply saying someone will get back to me, a week later no response. Send a follow up email asking for an update NOTHING but another automated response, a week later send another follow up email NOTHING but another automated response, a week later send another follow up email NOTHING but another automated response. Finally got a response after 5+ emails saying they solved my case and would like to inform me that my claim was REJECTED because the hotel booking site i used had become insolvent and they would NOT cover such event. Why the hell would I get travel insurance if this kind of thing isn't covered? 

If you travel and have no problems yeah why not use TID, but if you want service and decent communication then probably don't use TID, NEVER EVER in my life time will i EVER use TID again or recommend TID to anyone

title: Junk insurance
body: Allianz uses multiple loophole strategies to avoid paying claims.  They apply an excess to every part of a claim so they don't have to pay if each part is less than the excess. Even though they say they will replace lost or damaged personal belongings, they give themselves an out by saying they have the option to depreciate the item, to get below the excess and avoid paying the claim. title: Beyond expectations
body:
I know travel insurance is supposed to cover; accidents, illness and losses if you are overseas. I didn't anticipate the support Cover--More provided when I desperately needed help in a time of great duress.   It wasn't about me.  It was about my family at home.  I was just finishing my trip around Ireland and about to stay a few days in Dublin when I turned on my mobile and received a message from Australia.  Ring urgently.  It turned out that my daughter had been admitted to hospital and was about to undergo surgery for bowel cancer.  The shock was enormous and totally unexpected.  She's an athlete.  This couldn't be happening.  I could hardly breathe through the tears and the shock but managed to change all of my bookings.  I went straight to the ferry terminal to go across to Liverpool that night. The next day I was outside London ready to drop off the rental car and I flew out the next day.  I arrived just before she went into surgery.  I think there are times when people need their mums and this was definitely one.  The following weeks were a chaos of hospitals, cooking special meals, running children back and forth. Finally I phoned Cover-More.  Breakdown. Tears again.  The girl on the line was very patient while I tried to tell her my story.  I hadn't really had the time to speak to anyone about it until then.  But she listened kindly and sympathetically and took down notes. From then on Cover-More completed my claim by email.  There was the extra cost of changing my airfare, a river boat cruise I had to cancel and the almost two weeks of rental car costs I had paid before leaving the depot in London. The staff were excellent, caring and helpful and the company fair and honest.  Who could have asked for more?.
Caring and helpful staff

title: Unclear Cover
body:
I purchased coverage for Bali on the 20th of September (I have used TDI previously for other trips too).
I read the PDS very well and paid for additional coverage. Once overseas we decided to extend for 1 day, I called and spoke to a customer service agent who advised that we would have to call back to extend (which we couldn't do online as I checked out as a "guest" and it was a public holiday in Australia. I called back on the Monday to extend by one day and the agent said "either way, you aren't covered for anything to do with the volcano". I was shocked, apparently there was a "link" to something on the website with a non-coverage statement placed 4 hours earlier. I did not see that at all, nor was there any statement when booking for Bali coverage, nor was it in the PDS or any email/information during or after the booking process. Thankfully nothing happened but I found this quite misleading!!
There should be a checkbox or some form of notice during the checkout process if there is a current event that you are not covering!

body: I purchased an Allianz travel policy when I purchased Expedia plane tickets. Greater research showed this was expensive insurance and did not meet my needs. Allianz does not cover the cancellations costs of travel if a relative over 85 dies. title: Received Full Amount Claimed For Cancelled Africa Holiday
body:
We booked an extended holiday for May-June 2020, travelling through South Africa, Botswana and Zambia, along with another couple, who we had previously travelled with us overseas. We both took out coverage with Insure and Go, as we had paid for our holiday in full in advance which included return airfares with Qantas, hotel accommodation in Pretoria and Cape Town, a Rovos Rail Train tour, safari camps in the Okavango Delta and Chobe National Park, two nights in Victoria Falls plus two connecting flights.
With the mid March 2020 DO NOT TRAVEL direction from the Federal Government due to the Coranavirus Pandemic, we contacted Insure and Go by telephone and email, who advised us to cancel our holiday and claim back as much as we could from travel providers, before submitting our claim for any amounts not refunded. We did this as directed through our travel agent, but it took over two months to receive the funds from some suppliers due to lockdowns affecting travel providers within Africa.
Once these amounts were received in late May 2020, we submitted our final claim to Insure and Go, with a detailed explanatory letter from our Travel Agent, and copies of receipts and invoices for all expenditure and refunds.
It took another 6 weeks for our claim to be reviewed, assessed and finally confirmed. During this time, I made a number of telephone calls to Insure and Go, who confirmed that our case was being assessed, but there were significant delays due to the unprecedented number of claims due to the Coronavirus Pandemic, and the fact that staff were working from home, which was also affecting their ability to respond to queries, and process claims.
I finally received an email and a telephone call from the Insure and Go claims officer, who advised our claim had been approved in full, less the policy excess of $100 per person. She apologised sincerely for the delays, and again explained the cause was the unprecedented volume of claims received and being assessed.
I was most appreciative of the positive outcome, and the fact that the Insure and Go policy had coverage for the pandemic.
A few days later, the cash had been transferred to our bank account, while our friends had also received confirmation that their claim had been approved in full.
Thank you to Insure and Go, and to your very polite and no doubt extremely hard working staff, in circumstances that none of us hope to ever see again.

When I got back to Australia, I launched my claim. The response I received was most certainly inadequate. title: Disgraceful is putting it mildly when it comes to Cover-More
body:
(Slightly long read (5 min) for those in a hurry)

Booked (Nov '19) to go to Cook Islands in August this year (2020). Selected Covermore Insurance when booking flights with Virgin Australia as it was an optional on the ticket.

In March of this year Virgin Australia email me stating that from July 2020 they would no longer be servicing the Auckland-Rarotonga (Cook Islands) route. They named the specific date at the time when services would cease on this route.

I decide to wait a little while due to the mass influx I imagined insurance companies would be getting due to Covid-19 as I had time up my sleeve, and began the claim 'process' in May.

To begin with, their online portal would not accept any of the documentation I tried to upload to it, despite using various formats that were stated on the website that they would accept. I tried various web browsers (Google Chrome, Firefox, IE) and still had no luck. Not a big deal, but a decent time waster. 

(17/5/2020) - Submitted evidence via email of Virgin Cancelling route, along with bookings of said flight, other flights at Cook Islands and accommodation. (I was only seeking a refund of accommodation and inter-island flights in Cook Islands.)

(4/6/2020) - Get a short response over 2 AND A HALF WEEKS LATER asking for written confirmation from the 'transport provider' (i.e. VA) of the 'reason' for the cancellation. 

What, the email from Virgin Australia stating the cancellation isn't enough evidence? The mere fact that Cover More was 'recommended' when purchasing a VA ticket speaks volumes of the lengths this company will go to NOT to pay out a claim. They are tied in with VA, and they don't know??

As requested, I submit Bank statements showing a FULL REFUND from VA, and once again resubmit the email they originally sent as I spoke to VA about this.

(21/6/2020) Again, 2 and a half weeks later, I get a response, stating that my claim was denied because they had 'determined' that it was due to Covid-19 for the cancellation.

If an airline gives a date months in advance of when they are cancelling a route, that is NOT due to a pandemic. In all the emails from VA they never once mentioned that it was cancelled due to pandemic. That was an 'assumption' made by Covermore, and their reasoning was because the date I received the route cancellation email.

I then ring Virgin Australia and as they must have been inundated with requests for 'formal letters', they sent me a formal letter stating that the route had been cancelled and a full refund had been provided. 

(16/7/2020) I get the letter from VA and send it to Covermore (16/7/2020). It states a ROUTE CANCELLATION and that a full refund has been provided. Alas, I wait again...

(30/7/2020) Again, it is approaching 2 weeks since last correspondence, and with the actual date of the holiday itself fast approaching, and no response from Covermore, I sent them notice that due to not receiving any reply to my previous email, I have forwarded this issue onto the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA).... I received a reply 2 hours later from Covermore.

They have again denied my claim and are 'unable to overturn the decision made in previous correspondence', but not from the Pandemic. This time because the service provider cancelled the flight (their PDS states 'flight' but in actual fact VA cancelled the 'ROUTE')!. They stated the clause in their not-even-toilet-paper-worthy PDS that supposedly covers this, and then had the gall to apologise for the 'inconvenience caused' with this whole thing wasting my time...

Covermore's conduct here, and in many other cases of people here, represents a textbook case of insurance bureaucracy, where they make you go through so many hoops and roundabouts in hope that you will give up and not bother. I can only imagine how people who are actually stuck in a travel situation overseas must cope, with the fact that there are ridiculous waiting times to talk to someone, and when they finally do answer, are not very helpful. 

Whenever anyone talks to me about travel, no matter what the topic, the first sentence out of my mouth is going to be 'DO NOT USE COVERMORE INSURANCE FOR TRAVELLING'.

The company is worthy of a class-action law suit, and another reason why the insurance industry needs a Royal Commission.

Why offer insurance when there are so many clauses that it really does not cover ANYTHING, as well as Covermore 'interpreting' matters to suit their own ends.

You guys dare to 'apologise', but do nothing to make that apology have meaning. It's just another 'sorry for the inconvenience caused' when no one really gives a hoot about people's grievances or how to compensate them ethically.

On the off chance you are reading this Covermore, my policy is claim number is 1366500.

May the word spread about your conduct during this period faster than Covid-19.

body: the policy was easy to set up and in my opinion -- good value . the providers Customer Support was good but the failing was in the agents handling the claim before submitting to Covermore . We submitted the claim in good faith with Flight Centre  Golden Beach when arranging my wife and daughters tickets to return home early due to the death of her eldest son .The FC employee seemed to know what she was doing and the claim was submitted seemingly seemlessly  -- HOWEVER n hearing nothing from Covermore -  I went into FC Hervey Bay to enquire about the claim  -- the employee there contacted Covermore and after a long wait -- was advised the the claim was being held up waiting for documentation  ., all documents were supplied to the Flight Centre Golden Beach Offfice but it seems she failed to submit them with the claim  -- on wanting to talk to the person who submitted the claim -- it was advised she was on annual leave  -- after several heated conversations with FC employees -- I approached FC Hervey Bay  and spoke to a male employee there who was sympathetic to my problem and said it would be fixed ASAP . and he did -- BUT only part of the claim was paid -- the original documentation was again not found . He too was disappointed in the result and got on  the phone again to Covermore Support and made them aware the claim was incomplete . On checking records the documentation was located and the claim was finalised today  - Friday 25 August 2017  after the original submission on the 23 JUne 2017 . U can understand my frustration at the way the claim was handled but it was not the fault of Covermore Insurances . I suggest that if FC staff are going the be acting on your behalf -- that they are trained in basic compilation of claims as in the end -  it reflects as being a problem with that insurance company.

title: Good claims service... when you find it
body:
A genuine claim for emergency accommodation while in the UK was declined recently because the claims centre believed our situation didn't fit the tight parameters of the policy's PDS.
One call to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority put me in touch with 1Cover's decision makers, who overturned the original decision and refunded our $5k.
While the service from the top was excellent -- empathetic, consultative, collaborative -- I have nothing good to say about the claims system itself. It is antiquated, overly laborious in the amount of documentation required, and takes too long. The claims centre doesn't think outside the square of the PDS and if, like us, your claim falls outside of that square, you will almost always be declined.
Not sure if we would insure again with 1Cover... like most travel insurers, the proof of their service is when you need to claim and the process for us was simply too distressing.
If I could be assured that any future claims would be handled by the top level staff, I would insure again in a heartbeat. But that's not the reality so our jury is out for now.

title: Just avoid
body:
Avoid TID - very good at selling you a policy, but won't pay on genuine real-life claim.

We had to rearrange our trip before it started - the flight was cancelled on the day by the airline, which would have made us miss our cruise. This is covered under the policy, so we paid for another flight and claimed. TID came back to us simply listing the sections of the policy where additional costs are allowed and "regrettably" we were denied as we were not under any of those.

When we pointed the specific section under cancellation costs which allows the re-arranging of the trip, then we have been served the generic policy exclusion about carrier cancellations. 

To add insult to the injury, other people in our traveling party claimed via their credit card generic travel insurance and got their claim approved. For what it's worth, it is interesting that their policy definition of special event under which you claim additional costs was identical to TID's, apart one word at the end - "pre-paid tour", i.e. cruise - which TID dropped.

Later in the dispute process now, all this was regurgitated again. After comparing the policies with our friends, it is quite clear that TID policy is all about protecting them in case of travel disruptions - it has a blanket exclusion on carrier disruptions and special events definition is missing pre-paid or pre-arranged trips, including cruises, which other provider policy has.

So - don't bother. We felt the claim process was about finding the excuse not to pay, rather than assessing the claim on its merit.

title: Read the fine print, do not buy this insurance!
body:
My wife and I traveled to Egypt to visit her parents. It was a special occasion so I purchased first class tickets. Given the instability in the region, I thought it may be a good idea to purchase the insurance, "just in case". We landed in Egypt on time but our luggage was 3 days late. I submitted all the forms and receipts, but they still denied my claims, continually asking for the same forms and receipts I previously turned in. Even worse, the military removed Morsi from his Presidency in the middle of our vacation. The US Embassy was evacuated and they issued an alert for all Americans to evacuate Egypt. Being responsible US Citizens, we immediately evacuated. Since we left, there have been 100's killed (including 2 Americans), 1000's injured and countless reports of violence perpetrated by the Muslim Brotherhood and their known, terrorist allies (i.e. Al-Queda and Hamas). I submitted another claim with all of this information to Allianz hoping to get something for the loss of our return airfare (I didn't even ask for the cost of the evacuation...just the money we lost from the original 1st class seats we were not be able to use). Not only was my claim denied, here is the asinine explanation I was given. Although Terrorists Acts are covered in the policy (per the "when it applies" section), there is also a General Exclusion for Terrorists Acts. What??? The examiner read both sections and agreed it was contradictory in nature, but stood behind the company line, "You should have read this before purchasing the policy." At this point, I've wasted more time then it's worth so I'm dropping it. The only thing I can do is choose to spend my money elsewhere and tell everyone I can how horrible this company truly is.

Contradictory verbiage in their contract and impossible claims process.

title: First time to use my TI Policy for Overseas medical.
body:
I have a duo multi trip ski pack policy.
I arrived home yesterday with my right calf in a splint suffering form a Maisonneuve Fracture (Fractured Fibula, Very Bad Ankle Sprain) from Skiing Japan last week. It took Allianz 6 days to get me on a flight. I could have done myself in 2 days. Granted my incident happened Friday, and they got the call about 6pm AEST. I still could have done it in 2 days.

I was told on Friday arvo, it will take 2 days to approve my submitted documents and have my x-rays assessed, then another 3-4 days to arrange logisitics.

From the first call to the final call, I must have spoken to 5 different Case Managers, and 3 different registered nurses. You can expect when this occurs, there will be miscommunication, notes not read properly, not enough notes taken by one manager for the next etc... But lines got crossed only on one instance over an acronym, and generally their follow up was great!

Criticisms: 
They didn't outline a good plan for early return for me. Didn't get a good plan on getting proper treatment. 
I had to ask what the next step is. 
They initially didn't approve a taxi ride the next day to the layover destination.
I thought they would take more control over the process and guide me better. 
An acronym ER wasn't clearly outlined to me. I thought it meant Emergency Room, but it means Early Return. So I lost a day clarifying this detail...
Our premium flights with ANA were originally changed to JAL Domestic & Qantas Business (me) business economy (wife). I rejected the proposal and they found 2 Korean Air business flights flying through Seoul.
I asked them why they didn't use ANA as I found next day business flights. She said our travel agents don't have access to the same flights as customers. 
I didn't get a call at 9am when emailed the night before that I would receive one.

Pros: 
When they arranged something it all happened on time to a T. 
As long as I requested approval for something by phone it was granted.
The phone line was mostly quickly answered, hardly a delay in contacting them, maybe once or twice.

Wanted: 
Streamlined checklist what I need to do. 
Once they received my itinerary & medicals, tell me what to do under my cover.
Clarify to me what I need to arrange and what they will arrange. 
6 Days was too long IMHO.

While I can't compare this service to another, thankfully, I'm glad to be home and get further orthopaedic attention. 

My financial claim is just beginning, lodged today, and will review my process when it's complete. I would think costs incurred while waiting for Early Return would all be reimbursable. I'm a fish on sand, lying in a hotel room for 6 days doing nothing with a NWB-Non Weight Bearing leg and crutches and didn't need to be spending money on foods and phone calls...

I probably would have begrudgingly accepted this if they had not accepted my travelling companions claim for the exact same thing. When i asked the claims officer about this he shrugged his shoulders and said he doesn't know why that has happened.
I have sent 2 email's requesting clarification on my denied claim and have yet to receive a response on either of them. 
I see most of the 5 star reviews are from people who have not needed to claim, I wonder how many of these would change if they actually had to go through the claims process with Allianz.
I currently have my home and contents insurance and car insurance with Allianz but i will be rethinking this in the near future.

title: 1Cover - travel insurance you clearly CAN do without
body:
When deciding on which insurance to choose, don't bother reading the 1001 reviews on price point and how well the booklet folded in your travel pack.

Look for the reviews where a claim is made and how long it took the claims team to pick up the phone, and how polite they were when letting you know you were not covered.

For example: 1Cover, who took an age to answer our call to inform them we had found we had lost our keys after returning to our local airport, were very polite when informing us that they would absolutely cover the cost of replacing our lost keys ... but not the cost of a locksmith to work out what the keys should look like.

So we had to pay a locksmith $200 to drill out our lock. Luckily the new lock came with two free keys so not only do we avoid having to spend hours filling out reams of rain-forest, 1Cover get to avoid paying us the $5 to have our key cut. A win-win scenario I think you will all agree.

Don't even get me started on the car key and the other 5 or so keys on the same ring!

Suffice to say that 1Cover informed us that they "don't cover that kind of thing" and that's what house and car insurance is for.

title: Misleading, false advertising
body:
As of 30th Jan Covid19 was classified as a known event by most insurance agencies. 

In your PDS exclusions that means no travel insurance policy purchased after this date will be accepted if cancellation/claims arise due to Covid19. 
However as of 02 March you were still advertising on your website that people could take out comprehensive travel insurance and in the case of a government level 4 travel ban to that destination you will honour it and pay out cancellation costs. 

These two pieces of information completely contradict each other. 

Budget Direct website very specifically had a banner indicating COVID19 cancellation coverage offered only in the event of a travel ban. 
I called on March 2 to confirm, if I take out travel insurance TODAY for my trip to Bali, and then a level 4 travel ban is placed by the Australian government, will I be covered? Even though covid19 is a known event? 
I was told by consultant that yes, take out comprehensive coverage today and cancellation costs are covered but only if a travel ban is put in place. You won't be covered if you get sick with covid19 overseas so be aware of that. 
I confirmed again, ok, so no coverage if we get sick overseas, but in the event a level 4 do not travel warning is issued we are covered for our prepaid costs and will be reimbursed if I purchase this comprehensive insurance plan online?
Again I was told that is correct, purchase the plan and you're covered for cancellations in this one very specific circumstance, no worries. 
Only if Bali is listed as "Do not travel". She even said "but travel bans are rare so that probably won't happen". The consultant was very confident no travel ban would be put in place, I made a comment saying Budget was the only travel insurance agency still offering this coverage and I was surprised that I'm able to take out insurance still. She said it's because a travel ban would "probably never happen".

I bought the insurance that day, 02 March per the advice given over the phone, and per what you were advertising on your website. 
And now the claim is rejected as covid19 was a known event at the time the policy was taken out. 
Yes it was a known event, so why were you still offering insurance for Covid19 cancellations when I bought that policy?
Why were your consultants telling people they were covered only in the event of a travel ban due to the not yet declared pandemic? 

You're being dishonest by saying our policies are invalid due to Covid19 being a known event when you were encouraging people to still purchase policies via your website and also over the phone. 
You guys hedged your bets and were still advising people to take out policies which you are now rejecting. 

If covid19 becoming a known event is the overriding factor of rejection of claims, you should not have been advising people they can take out polices as late as 02 March (and there after). 
You were betting the government would not introduce such strict travel restrictions and you lost that bet, now pay up.

title: They do not pay claims, poor response!
body:
Do not trust this company! They make excuses to not pay genuine claims! They don't response to claims until months later! You will know if an Insurer is good during claims time and it is no point buying any insurance at low cost when they don't actually pay you when you need to make a claim. This is an extremely hard lesson I learnt googling for "best insurance companies in Australia or cheapest", cheap is bad and this is Budget Direct, their name itself is a reflection. They spent a lot of advertising money and mostly appears at the top of search engines and many Comparison sites like Canstar, Find, Comparethemarket, etc, to entice ignorant consumer like me to buy their policies but when it comes to claims time, they do not response at all until months later and make all sorts of excuses to not pay genuine claims! So please do not get scammed, read each and every fine print in their policy! They used this to argue themselves out of paying claims. I am taking my case to the AFCA, also read the reviews of other policy holders before you buy! I am a frequent business traveller, been buying travel insurance since 30yrs ago with different companies and last year, it was unfortunate I came across Budget Direct whilst googling. I bought a comprehensive multi-trip travel insurance in 2019 for my trip to Egypt and Jordan during Xmas holidays. Halfway through my trip, my Mum passed away overseas, and I had to break my trip and fly back for Mum's funeral. Hence, I had to rebook my Business Class Air Tickets and cancel half my trip, and rebook all hotels overseas attending mums funeral for a week. To rub salt into the wound, when I tried to make a claim, I received no response for almost 2 months, sent them multiple emails, they of course made excuses using COVID-19, asked for mum's death cert and all documents to proof my flights, travels, hotels cost etc. They then come back to inform that my claims have been rejected! Below is their response:-

"The claimant has lodged the above claim under Section A-Cancellation and Amendment fees. As the claimant has already departed Australia she will not be covered under this section. We further considered this claim under Section C1- Cutting Your Trip Short & Section C2-Additional expenses. However, as the incident did not occur in Australia the claim does not fall within the scope of the policy and is therefor denied at this time."

I wondered why the hell would anyone purchase travel insurance for overseas travel if not for unfortunate events like what happened to me! My mum passed away when I was travelling, and this is not a good enough reason for budget direct to pay my claims! So beware all of you, think 100x before you think of engaging this company's services as cheap/budget doesn't mean quality and this is often true each and every time. I am really keen to hear what the ombudsman AFRA had to say about this when I lodge a formal complaint about budget direct tricking ignorant, unbeknownst consumers hundreds of million of dollars purchasing their policies hoping no one makes a claim and if one does, budget direct goes "See, read our 10,000 lines of fine prints in our terms of policies document when you purchase, you are not covered!!!" so unless you are a lawyer, and you have read through each and every word in the terms of their policy document, you are in for the shock of your life, when most of us would have thought we are covered by travel insurance if a family member passed away during your travels!!!
