title: Paid hefty policy price but now getting the run around on a claim!
body:
We have been using InsureandGo Australia in recent years as we felt that the procedure to get pre-existing medical conditions covered online was easy and reasonably priced.

We have just returned from an overseas trip to Canada, Alaska and the USA for which we used InsureandGo for travel insurance.  Paid almost $1,200.00 for the policy.

During the trip my camera was badly damaged after a fellow tourist bowled my husband over whilst he was holding my camera standing on a glacier in Jasper National Park.  It has a clear crack through it and we could not use it for the rest of the trip.  It is very clear that is won't be repairable given the extent of the damage.  It is also only going to cost $397.00 to replace it with the latest model of the same camera.  We would have to pay an excess of $100.00 so it would only cost the insurance company $297.00 to replace it.  We are now being met by resistance like the requirement to show a police report which we did not obtain as it was not stolen, just damaged.  We did say we could provide them with the name and contact details of the fellow tourist on our tour who caused my husband to fall over whilst he was holding the camera.  They also want us to get a camera repairer to provide a letter saying it is irreparable and send the camera in to them which would end up costing us more money on top of the $100.00 excess cost.  Remember, we paid almost $1,200 for the policy and are only asking the insurance company to contribute $297.00 for replacement of the damaged camera.  We provided them with images of the damaged camera showing the large crack which clearly would not be able to be repaired.

We have never made a claim with InsureandGo Australia before even though we have taken up a number of travel insurance policies with them in the past.

Unfortunately for us we also have travel insurance with this company for another upcoming trip to Bali and I am unable to cancel it due to the 14 day cooling off period having come and gone.  It goes without saying that we have become very disillusioned with this company and travel insurance coverage in general.  I doubt whether we will take out travel insurance with this particular company again in the future!

The following updates are posted by me as a way to indicate to people exactly what processes are expected when making a claim through this company.  I hope that it provides you with the information required to help you make a decision as to whether or not this is the travel insurance company you want to go with for your travel insurance requirements.

Update : 23/5/18 - It would have been so nice to actually get a phone call from these people but I still hadn't heard from InsureandGo by this afternoon so I ended up posting this review on their Facebook page.  Within the space of five minutes I got a response post advising that they were looking into my claim, specifically their most recent email to me with unreasonable documentation requests.  What a shame it had to take a post on FB to get a response!  They also seem to think that I was upset that they had denied my claim which was never the case at all, at least not at this point in time.  You will note nowhere in my review have I said anything about having my claim denied.  I have now been informed that I will get a response to my claim within a time frame of 10 business days from the day it was first lodged.  They also apologised that a mistake had been made when I was requested to obtain a police report on what was a damaged camera, not a stolen one.  Go figure!  I await in earnest!

Update : 24/5/18 - Still no phone contact, only an email.  I have now been contacted by a claims supervisor at InsureandGo Australia basically advising me that I need to arrange to get a damage report saying that the camera cannot be repaired and mail it to InsureandGo Australia for salvage(?). These days most reputable camera repairers charge people to prepare quotes to repair a camera and/or damage reports. I contacted 2 reputable repairers here in Perth and they charge from $22-27 for a damage report for insurance purposes. Then there is the cost associated with boxing it up and sending it back to InsureandGo Australia. Will these associated costs be covered by them as part of this claim?  Stay tuned!

Update : 25/5/18 - Still no phone contact, email once again!  Claims supervisor has now advised that "If you do not wish to provide a damage report, you can send the camera to us to replace/settle the item. If you provide a receipt for the postage cost,  I will reimburse this to you on this occasion."  I am posting the camera to them today but at this point I am feeling as though I have really had to put in a lot of effort to get this far with the claim.  It will be interesting to see how things pan out from here.

title: Great Initial Review
body: I have never used Cover More previously.   Although I have not yet travelled, but have taken out cover more insurance to cover us doing our overseas holiday.   I really enjoyed the application process, it was extremely easy to complete, in comparison to the free Credit Card ones where you had to have a phone interview, and when I declared that I was diagnosed with an EMC of PTSD some ten or more years ago, although I am not on any medications for that or meds for anything else at 71 years of age, they made a really big deal of it, just as though being lectured about it.  It just made me uneasy about medical insurance in general.   So much so that I have taken out my policy with cover more, which was so so easy to complete.  With cover more when I declared my PTSD as an EMC with cover more, explained that I was not on any drugs for it etc etc as cover more asked etc etc, at the completion of my application even though I declared PTSD it came up on my completed cover more application form that I have no EMC,s, which was interesting.  Just a dream, to deal with a company which has streamlined the process and made it so user friendly.   I have seen some of the negative comments made on this site re cover more.   I took out our insurance to predominately cover us for major incidents happening, in our situations at our age.  I just could not afford to be hospitalised overseas for weeks or months on end, whereas if someone stole our bags, or an aircraft was cancelled and I lost my airfare as a result, they are not incidents, that concern us really, although probably covered that I could claim for, but would not.   Furthermore, I was just happy that cover more gave us insurance even though I was diagnosed with PTSD many years ago, and I positively know that I would never have to submit any claims relating ro my PTSD, I just wanted travel medical insurance to cover major events, such as accidents/hospitalisations, and transport back to Australia if medically unable to do so, as a result of those unforeseen accidents and hospitalisations.   Thank you so much cover more, keep up the good work.

title: Scam insurance .... avoid like the plague
body:
Beware the maximum payout for luggage stolen from an unattended motor vehicle is $500.

So if you go to the opera, take your car into the opera with you. If you go to the beach, take your car down on the sand beside you, and if you go for a swim, make sure you take your car into the water with you. Do not leave your car unattended at any time, else your luggage will not be covered for more than $500.

I learnt this the hard way. When taking out gold insurance the website clearly says you are covered for $15,000 for stolen luggage. But the fine print buried deep has all sorts of exceptions, including the condition luggage is only covered if stolen from an ATTENDED motor vehicle (it boggles the mind to wonder how often luggage is stolen from a vehicle while the owner is present!!!).

So while the locked vehicle was parked for just 30 minutes next to a beach in Italy, ALL the luggage was stolen from the vehicle. A police report was obtained. Yet the payout was just $400, being $500 less $100 excess.

Insurance from InsureAndGo is SCAM insurance. Be warned.

I believe you can only truly gauge how good an insurance company by its claim process and payment.   We were traveling in the US October 2009 when my wife got stomach pain while we were in San Francisco - she could bare walk! We sought treatment with a travel doc from the Traveler Medical Group because they were nearby - Dr [name removed] provide an excellent emergency service if you ever need travel medical treatments in San Francisco.  The doc provided copies of his diagnosis, treatment and medical prescriptions for submission for travel insurance claim.   As per instruction from Travel Insurance Direct my wife saw her GP when we got back and posted all required info.  With three days she received a MSM text confirming the receipt of the claim and the claim was paid in full on the tenth day - over $AU 560 for that single treatment.  We elected to the pay extra $25 for no excess.  Support Travel Insurance Direct and stop getting ripped off.
Easy application process, particularly in regards to pre-existing medical conditions as compared to HBF that requires a doctor to fill out forms for pre-existing conditions that does not and will not be covered!. When we came home I put the 3 claims in and had them approved within 4 days and having provided bank accounts, etc. I waited for the money---that's when it all fell apart.
First they tried to pay it into the account but the bank refused to take it, but I had left instructions to send a cheque if it did not work on the second bank account either--it did not happen. I called up and asked for the cheques (3) to be mailed as registered mail and they said OK, but that did not happen either. Next phone call I got the team leader and he explained that they never use registered mail, but no cheques had been sent anyway. He promised to take care of the matter but absolutely refused to let me speak to his supervisor about the matter. (I have since had the bank investigate and it turns out that Covermore gave them all the info except my account number, which I DID supply in the claim).

It is now almost mid July and I claimed it the 23'th of May.

The cheques has still not arrived, leaving me over $ 1500 out of pocket, no sight of getting it and wondering if I am actually covered for the rest of the 12 months I have paid for with them, -that is a very disappointing result from Covermore.

please read the above

title: Using for the past 10 years with no issues
body:
I have used TID for almost 10 years now and I have nothing but praise for them. We travel overseas at least 2 times a year and in this time we've had to make 2 claims. Both times it was handled professionally after the claims were lodged. 

In the first case, a phone was pick pocketed on NYE on a beach in Thailand, we submitted our police report and we got a fair chunk of the phone cost back minus depreciation very quickly. 

The second case was where my parents fell and injured themselves while in Hong Kong and required treatment while over there. I provided the practitioner reports and they asked for a detailed rundown of what happened. There was some back and forth with this one, asking for more details and clarification but nothing I deemed as unreasonable. We got the entire cost back of the treatment after a few weeks.

For those who've had positive experiences, please share with the community here! Alot of times, the ones who have negative experiences are most vocal and can often skew the reviews overall.

title: Please Explain!!
body: I recently travelled to Vietnam and took out comprehensive travel insurance with Allianz through southern cross credit union my partner also used Allianz comprehensive travel insurance through the commonwealth bank. Unfortunately Cyclone Debbie hit and on the day we were supposed to fly 31st March 2017 the major highway from Mullumbimby to Coolangatta was cut for 24 hours. After contacting Allianz and taking their advice we cancelled our airfare as there was no way to reach the airport and rebooked after being told with my cover i would be reimbursed for any added expenses... NOT THE CASE!! After 6 weeks of phone calls and submitting the same documents and going through the same information over and over (even though Cyclone Debbie made headlines for weeks and the whole of Australia knew about it!!) on the phone a settlement was made. Unfortunately it was on the original flight valued at $480 and not the new flight with added costs incurred valued at $775 stating that my comprehensive cover did not cover extra costs incurred??Not what I was told on the 31st March!!. BUT you paid my partner on the second flight within 3 weeks of his claim and less than a quarter of the documentation submitted??? We both used Alliianz and both had comprehensive travel insurance so I'm sorry if i don't understand!!  In all fairness the operators i spoke to were all very polite and believe me i spoke to a few. Would i ever use Allianz again NEVER!!! Would i recommend Allianz to anyone NEVER!!!

title: Read the fine print - if they give it to you before you pay!!
body: We did not have access to the full documentation around what was/was not included - just general info. - when we took this out. We are frequent travellers and have never previously made a claim - and never used this company previously. We had to cancel a trip for one of our family members prior to travelling. Our claim was for $400, the difference between the fare and what the airline gave us back. The illness was a mental health issue which was not pre-existing, as attested to by our family member's doctor. The issue which triggered the anxiety occurred well after the ticket was booked. Apparently anxiety or mental health issues are not covered, whether pre-existing or not.  I work with young people many of whom suffer from anxiety, social/emotional issues and these health issues are genuine health issues just as for any other health issue. So I feel this policy of 1Cover's is extremely discriminatory - and given the number of people in Australia now suffering some form of anxiety (or likely to in the future), most Australians should forget ever going to this company for travel insurance. Shame on 1Cover for not giving credence to a health issue which is as valid as any other health issue!!!

My wife had a case of bad food poisoning in Bali which led to an overnight stay in the best hospital on a drip-very worrying at the time,but 100% covered by travel insurance and immediately reimbursed with a very smooth process on our return to Perth.Every trip we go on, the first priority is Covermore insurance- its great peace of mind.
Great value and covers all necessary options.

title: What once was good.....
body:
I have used TID almost every year for 8 years and they were fantastic for all property, travel and health related issues - this was when they were associated with Mondial and Alliance... I have taken out another policy this year and I have spent more than 2 months on a claim, waiting for responses, not getting them in the promised "10 business days" or "15 business days"  - I am still fighting. I can only put this down to new management and/or new underwriters. I am so disappointed - I have previously recommended TID to everyone I know - I will now be doing the opposite. It's such a shame, as I always believed they were reliable, caring, well priced and had amazing customer service.
I liked that they used to care
I don't know what the cause of the problem is - I'm still shocked that they're not as good as they used to be.

title: Quick, efficient processing of claim.
body: 1st time user. Had planned a comprehensive overseas trip but had to cancel due to a medical situation. I submitted my claim and it was processed & paid out in full within a week of submission. Very pleased with the services.

title: Good Easy to Buy Travel Insurance
body: Very easy step by step process covering pre existing conditions - good value premium - if you can?t afford travel insurance you can?t afford to travel. I was recommended to this company and am well satisfied

title: New seriously impressed customer!
body: Whilst on holidays in the US my Dad suddenly passed away in the same week as I lost my passport. Cover More were fantastic and accepted all of my claims ranging from covering my new passport fee to covering additional nights accommodation in the city etc. Thank you to Cover-More for making such a difficult time a little less stressful. You have a loyal customer for life :)

title: Easy process and good value!
body: In comparison to other offers it was good value and policy was very easy to set up! Will definitely use again =)

title: Right Plan for me

title: Great Service

title: A customer for life!
body: My claim for extra accommodation costs was handled sympathetically, despite my inability to provide all documentary evidence I thought I needed. The cost of insuring with Oz Post compares very favourably with other companies - particularly for geriatric customers! :-)

title: Bought this mainly for the Hire Car Excess Cover
body: Was hiring a car for 5 days (travelling interstate).  The hire car company's excess (in case of accident) was a whopping $4000 and of course their insurance to waive this (Loss Damage Waiver) was also whoppingly large.  As I didn't want to shell out nearly the week's rental cost in LDW insurance, but at the same time didn't want to risk having to pay $4000 if I had an accident (even when it wasn't my fault!), I looked for alternatives.  I bought 1Cover travel insurance for $41, which covered me for the 5 days of my trip for the Rental Vehicle Excess PLUS much, much more.  Fortunately I didn't have to make a claim, but was happy to have the peace of mind having the insurance.  I will remember 1Cover for this in future.  So easy to purchase, I bought it using my mobile before I left home.  I checked out competitors and 1Cover won out hands down.

body: It was domestic and was reasonably priced. I thought $100 extra for 5 days because I have a knee replacement was excessive, but optional. The customer service person on the phone was excellent.

title: Great cover policy
body: Policy was Good value and very easy to set up. We didn't need to make a claim at all but from previous experience TID were very helpful in fixing any holiday 'hiccups'!

title: Excellent
body:
I have just returned from Thailand having spent 11 days in hospital in Pattaya with  a broken ankle, broken ribs and various cuts and grazes following a motorbike accident. I have never had to seek medical treatment overseas before, but I can honestly say that TID made the whole process easy. I was fortunate to be taken to the best hospital around with facilities & staff that would rival, if not better, any hospital in Australia (the Bangkok Pattaya Hospital) - but they were also expensive! However from the moment I contacted TDI they took control of my situation, within 24 hours they confirmed to the hospital that they would pay all my costs. They phoned me almost every day, either a case worker or nurse, to check that I was being well looked after and receiving the treatment I needed and they even flew a friend out from Australia to accompany me home and flew us Business Class.  What could have been a very nasty experience was  completely turned around by the care and support I received. I will definitely use TDI again and have no hesitation whatsoever in recommending them.
Cheap and easy to buy cover - very efficient and caring claims service. The best $110 I ever invested! Found them online and liked the reviews I read - I never thought I'd have to make a claim myself!!
I cannot fault the way my claim was handled

title: Slow reply times
body:
Whilst on holiday my iPhone sustained damaged that now renders it unusable. I called up and the woman I spoke to was fabulous with explaining to me what I needed to do. From there I went and obtained a report from a "reputable iPhone repairer" and submitted all the receipts and documents I need to on the online claim form, it was all very easy. I then received an email from a JB Hi-fi representative who said he had been authorised to provide me with a certain amount of money. This was without receiving any prior word from Covermore that this would occur, which left me feeling very "out of the loop" and unsure if the person was even genuine. There are some problems I found with this. 

a) I am still away without a working phone until December 2013, and am therefore unable to access a JB Hi-Fi store. 
b) JB Hi-fi doesn't sell iPhone 4 models, either new or used. Therefore leaving me with the only option of buying a new phone for a significantly higher amount of money. I only want to replace the phone I have, I'd be very happy with a second hand one.
c) Covermore haven't contacted me themselves (aside from automated "We have received your email..." messages) since I lodged the claim. The claim was lodged on the 14th May - 28 days ago.  
d) I sent an email outlining my concerns 12 days ago and haven't received anything back from them.

In summation, I feel the "We will settle or respond to your travel insurance claim within 10 working days from the time we receive it." quote on their website to have been very misleading. I'm not asking for much, simply a viable method to replace my phone. 

Claim REF: 704177
Polite and helpful on phone
Slow to reply, no personal contact since lodging claim, very unpersonal

title: Stress free claim

title: DO NOT use InsureandGo Australia!
body: This company is a con!!  We lost a mobile phone whilst in Europe - Like others who have posted reviews here, we found they delayed processing our claim by asking for more and more documents to support the claim, including the receipt for the replacement phone we had purchased - what has that got to do with them??!!  They call themselves InsureandGo AUSTRALIA, but they are NOT IN AUSTRALIA - they are in the Phillipines.  If you try to ring the call is diverted and you get a service person who has very poor English skills, making the whole process more difficult.  We posted some documents to the Sydney office by registered post and it took them 6 DAYS to collect it from the PO Box, emails typically took 5 days to receive a reply.   When the settlement was finally made they paid us ONE QUARTER of the original value of a 2 year old mobile phone!  NEVER AGAIN !! Make sure you go with an Australia company who you can at least communicate adequately with.

title: Excellent
body: Great value and helpful with all my claims and prompt assistance and reimbursements. Thank you and highly recommend for your future travels.

title: Get with these guys. For a medical emergency the help and advice was outstanding.
body:
I recently broke my ankle and damaged my ACL knee joint in a surfing accident in Sumatra. There was little medical help in the area I was in, so TID arranged to get me out of there, purely on my word, to Jakarta, where I could get professional help. From there they got me back to Australia (on one leg). The level of help available on the phone is so reassuring when in difficulty in a foreign country. I was able to speak with experienced and helpful people about my medical issues at any time I needed, day or night. Then when it was time to get back to Australia, their travel people were just amazing. They arranged everything perfectly including business class flights so that I could stretch out and rest my leg, down to having someone meet me at the airports to help with luggage and transfers as I was temporarily disabled. People I was with, and had met on this trip were all asking who this travel insurance company was as they could not believe the service I was getting and how cheap my insurance had been compared to theirs.  Anyway thanks TID you have my vote and appreciation.
Always able to be contacted when needed. (And I contacted them a lot). Price fantastic. Outstanding help on the phone.

title: Read the fine print regarding flight delays and cancellations.
body: Be aware that you may think you are covered for flight delays and cancellations but the fine print exempts cost recovery when the insurer believes the airline to be responsible. The airlines of course accept no such responsibility and won't reimburse prepaid costs when they cancel or change the timing of flights.  I lost $1,000 in prepaid travel arrangements, which had to be cancelled with less than 24 hour's notice. I would have lost over $10,000 in prepaid arrangements if another flight hadn't been available in time. The law in Australia needs to change, as compensation is available in many other countries.

title: Peace of mind and compassionate help for unexpected needs
body: We only recently started purchasing travel insurance. And for our recent trip, I'm so glad we did.  Our 8YO developed a spontaneous testicular torsion while we traveled in a country where we didn't speak the local language. Referred by doctor to the hospital and onward to surgery the day before our flight home, we contacted InsureandGo who were very compassionate and contacted the local hospital admin to resolve the billing questions so that we wouldn't have to deal with language troubles. It let us put our focus on our LOs health and our attention on getting back home. Once home the claims process was straight forwards and quickly done.  Excellent service. Highly recommend.

body:

I spent an extra 25 hours in KUL airport and paid $220 to change the ticket for the next day plus misc expenses due to my long stay (like meals, storage and acc). After three weeks they denied my claim because they have a clause that says they will not pay for claims caused by:

"Transport Provider caused cancellations, delays or rescheduling other than when caused by strikes."

This is precisely the sort of thing people take out claims for. Won't ever use them again, will dissuade my family and friends from ever using them.

title: Broken tooth while overseas
body:

They put a lot thought into it and created the best interface around. It is quick, transparent and very clear.
But the best insurance is tested when you make a claim...

I am very impressed with TDI and would highly recommend them for your insurance.
Very happy - Paul

title: Beware Allianz Travel Insurance
body:
I had to cancel 2 overseas trips in 2015 due to being diagnosed with breast cancer. I started the claims process in April 2015. This company will do anything to delay settlement. Then when they do settle because they have no choice they will not pay the full amount and you have to start the process off again. I am still waiting for the full payment. 
I will never use them again. 
Beware when you purchase travel insurance as they underwrite many other companies insurance, eg Webjet, NSW Teachers Federation, Virgin etc.  If I could give them a zero I would.
As others have stated,  "won't return emails. have to wait anywhere up to 55 minutes to answer phone". Imagine being stuck overseas waiting for their permission to be treated or evacuated (I read this in their terms and conditions after experiencing their appalling behaviour).

I highly recommend 1Cover Travel Insurance to anyone who is thinking about overseas or domestic travel.  I used it for domestic travel to cover my rental excess & it was cheaper buying through 1Cover than it was through the rental company.  Now I use 1Cover Travel Insurance for my overseas travels as well. The cover is one of the best & so it the price. I also found while browsing online for other quotes, 1Cover doesn't bombard you by asking for your personal details. It's great on the privacy score too.
Cheapest

title: Don't use Insure and Go
body:

So we flew out and government said not to travel on 18th March. We were at sea. Earliest we could disembark was 24th March. Home 27th. Rang and told yes covered. Everything was prepaid before we left home. Some will only give credit on  another cruise etc. Car and accom took 15 to 75% cancellation fee. Out of pocket $43k. Insurance knocked us back due to covid 19, yet nothing in policy about pandemic. Now disputing. Will never use again. Would give 0 stars if could.

body:

June 30th 2017 Update: So easy to fill out

title: Have travel insurance and feel comfortable safe.
body: I found 1 cover is a good value and so easy to buy it online before I went to holiday. I have pieces of mind that i don't have to worry about anything in overseas. If something happened to me. Lucky i didn't make any claimed at all.

title: Very comprehensive travel insurance - would recommend to anyone.
body: This was the first time I had used InsureandGo - I was looking for comprehensive travel insurance for a family cruise. title: Had to make a claim and Cover-More were outstanding.
body: I bought my policy online which was very easy.  Unfortunately, due to family illness, I ended up needing to cancel my trip and submit a claim. Then when we decided not to make a claim (thanks to Apples help) we where treated like we had lied about the original claim and where contacted several times by alliance several times to enquire as to why the claim was being ceased. We felt like criminals.

title: Last Minute
body: Totally forget about organising insurance earlier but remembered at the last minute and was able to organise quickly and without any fuss - best of all it was the very reasonable cost that didn't eat into our holidays spending.

title: Good comprehensive and Value for Money Policy
body: Easy to sign up, did it at the last minute and the cover seemed to be comprehensive and value for money. Quick communications from Allianz so was kept in the picture. Will use again when needed

title: Great travel insurers
body: Easy to follow terms and good value policy. The policy was easy to setup and I am very satisfied with the silver policy I have selected. Did not use customer support just did it all online.

title: Great
body: Great value, have been using 1Cover for all my travel insurance, also have recommended to family and friends , we did make a claim 2 years ago as my daughters phone was stolen, the claim was addressed very promptly with no problems at all, great service.

title: disappointment
body:
I am writing a review because I think I need to do this to put this whole lousy experience behind me. I placed my claim in October after having a fall then getting influenza. I was sent the required response of a reply will be given in 10 working days.
 Well I was requested to send doctors notes dating back to 2016 which was 2 years prior. I sent the paper work then was told it wasn't what you wanted as it was faxed through by me. It had the doctors information on it. If that wasn't acceptable how was the doctors certificate that I sent with the claim acceptable. 
 I needed more  information from the doctor. This time the dates were more recent. The request was sent to my doctor and an invoice was sent back the same day. We are talking January 30th. As I hadn't heard anything from medibank I rang 3 weeks later and yes they had gotten the invoice. I got the same person I had spoken to about the doctors notes. Steve said yes we have got the invoice and I will pay that now while you are on the line. He said it will take up to a week to be in their bank and then I would hear again. We have the info and it will be passed onto out claims department and you will hear from us in 10  working days. 
 On the 26th of march they said that my claim was approved for cover. Then they said the cruise department I booked with had to give a refund which had earlier been denied.Ok so  I got in touch with them and yes there is a refund. I send that information to you and am now told that I didn't send proof of it being paid into my account and that you don't pay until that is done.  On the 11th of April you get in touch for that information and on the 2nd of may the money is paid into my account. 27 weeks after the claim was made. I find this disgusting handling and would not recommend or use your company again. In Steve's own words that's my prerogative. I have never had such bad dealings with any company in my life and hope never  to again..
I realise this doesn't matter to you or to Steve in claims but I think  the whole process was dealt with badly and I should get the money that I missed out on in interest because you made it so damn hard for me. I do believe you were hoping I would get sick of it and drop it but I couldn't afford to do that.

title: Read the small print
body: This company is operating under false pretensions. It stated one is covered for cancellations But if you read the small print this is not true. My flight was cancelled due to a hurricane and I had to purchase another flight at a cost of $2,100 or I would have had to wait for another 10 days .They refuse to cover my cost for this flight even though I appealed. I suggest travellers buy elsewhere

title: TID Good Insurance
body: The policy is good value and can been done online or through customer support.  Customer support know what travel insurnce is needed based on expected risks.  Fortunatelly have not needed to use TID  and would not go overseas without travel insurance.

title: Medibank Travel Insurance
body:

body: I am disappointed in the way that InsureandGo have treated policy holders during Covid 19. A number of the other larger travel insurance companies are offering cash refunds for cancelled policies. InsureandGo won't give that option, they only offer a partial credit that is worthless to me. title: This great will use it again
body: I used this cover while travelling overseas it is simple to use and inexpensive  I would recommend this cover to family and friends and I will use this cover again.

title: Great insurance cover. Dont leave home without it
body: Easy to take out. Great price. Great value. Peace of mind for parents who have kids travelling through asia. 24 hour help hotline is essential. I have used this insurance a few times and wouldn't hesitate to recommend to anyone.

title: Easy application
body: Have used them several times before - very easy to apply and get cover. Extremely competitive rates compared to other insurers. Fortunately I have not had to make a claim yet.

title: Easy to apply for and prompt response

body: At least 4 times in the last 5 years that I can remember. I always use them. Easy to use online for quotes and payments.  Good customer service.

title: Won't be buying Travel insurance ever again from Allianz
body:
Paid $179 for insurance to Hawaii (Nov, 2018)
Mobile phone got water damaged whilst on a day trip. Went to Apple store (just the thing you want to do whilst on holidays) - said not repairable - valued $700US was written on document.
Paid the $200 excess & they wanted to give me  approx $130 due to depreciation!!  Refused & they then gave me approx $220 to buy a new Apple Iphone.    All I can get for $220 is two cans & a ball of string.  How do I replace what was a perfectly working iphone for $220.   
Also strikes were on whilst in Hawaii & therefore had no services (housekeeping etc) other insurance companies paid people $50 per day (was in their policies).  We got zero, not in our policy.
Will do my homework much better next time.
Will not use Allianz again.

title: Very prompt response
body: Our luggage was delayed by nearly 3 days and after having to purchase clothes and toiletries, we made a claim on-line with Cover-More, providing copies of receipts, itinerary and a letter from the airline. Within 3 days I had a response and confirmation of reimbursement of all extra costs to be paid within a few days. Thank you Flight Centre for making sure we had good travel insurance - definitely worth every penny!

body: After much research we chose InsureandGo and provided full medical details before travel to Mongolia. Unfortunately an accident occurred with myself and my wife being injured, resulting trip curtailment and early flights home. The staff at InsureandGo were extremely helpful in providing prompt assistance and return flights. Later claims were made and after providing all details claims were paid in full. We can't thank InsureandGo enough.

body:
I've purchsed 1Cover comprehensive travel insurance every time we went overseas and to date, no claims were ever made. All went well, no bad experience to date.

I found 1Cover to be price competitive and offered a comprehensive cover.

Policy was easy to set up. I normally organise it on the go,  using my phone. 

Recently I had to make changes to the travel dates which were readily arranged. Great & prompt service. Very happy with 1Cover.

body:

I started to cry. Not because of the pain but because my expensive, gorgeous, form fitting costume had to be cut- off me.

title: Never got the SIM, appalling customer service, absolutely no help offered
body: I never got the SIM.  I wrote to them explaining this, and they said they had no record of my email address.  Only problem is that I was replying to their email saying it would be dispatched with my address in their email.  Several emails later, still no attempt to resolve, and no suggestions from them how to get my SIM.  They just kept telling me they had no record of the request, even thought I forwarded them the confirmation email they sent me in the first place!  I asked for the issue to be escalated, and got no response.  They offered no resolution at all, and wanted me to ring them in Australia from Spain, Switzerland or Italy.  If I had the promised SIM, that might have been OK.  It has cost me a small fortune in SIMs since arriving in Europe, and their website says they offer no compensation, even for a SIM that never arrived.  I can only assume it is a scam.  Pathetic customer service that didn't even acknowledge my questions, or acknowledge that I was replying to their "order confirmation" email in the first place.  Don't be fooled by this company.  They do not care, and do not help.  Organise your own SIM in the countries you visit, and save yourself the stress of dealing with this terrible company.

The lovely tele-operator advised me what letters I'd need from the doctors and what receipts I'd need to lodge my claim. When I did, they paid out for everything. As a

Helpful, reliable
quite high premium

title: Great

title: A necessary expense.
body: Simple to set up, economical and accessible. However, all went well and fortunately I didn't have to make a claim, so I think you cannot say you are truly happy with an insurance company until you see how they respond and behave when you make a claim.

title: When Travel Insurance don't deliver
body: Policy was good value and very easy to take out. The problem came when we submitted a claim. We were booked for a Cruise to Bahamas during the time that Hurricane Matthew hit the US East Coast. We cancelled Cruise and followed instructions to evacuate Florida. We decided to change flights and return home early as the risk of severe storm damage and not being able to return on planned dates with Airport closures, etc. was high. Upon our return we claimed for cost of flight changes and one nights hotel accommodation due to lay over for connecting flight home. We were put through the mill by Travel Insurance Direct assessor requesting information that had been provided but apparently not to his satisfaction. In the end we received a notice that 90% of claim had been rejected as it did not fall within the specified reasons set by Travel Insurance Direct for the general category we had to use for the claim. Based on my personal experience with Travel Insurance Direct they are not an honorable company and will do anything not to settle your claim. They use false advertising to get you to purchase the product and then don't deliver when you are out of pocket due to events completely outside your control.

title: Easy and economical

I like that I can declare pre-existing illnesses for all travellers. I have never needed to make a claim but the peace of mind is worth the price.

title: Robbed
body: WOW! How can a company like this simply pocket your money and be so totally callous as to not even agree to a credit or a date change during a event like we are currently going through. This is a very narrow minded approach to business robbing people once but after 6 policies with them i will head straight to their opposition regardless if they are more expensive. I urge everyone considering Insure and Go to simply Go elsewhere. So much for we are all in this together.

title: Read your PDS. Your actual certificate is very misleading .
body:
So disappointed .I always have used Allianz for my travel insurance ( but never had to claim before ) 
Imagine my shock when claiming for a broken arm while skiing ( I had the snow pack for this reason ) that in the very fine print at the end of the document there was a clause of an etc $700 excess for having the snow pack ( which I  paid extra for ) making the excess $900 !!!!! 
No disclosure of this at all on my certificate anywhere . I thought I had complete cover with a $200 excess cause that?s what was in my certificate ..... NO I didn?t. 
I find this a breach of duty to disclose extremely underhanded from such a reputable company . 
READ THE FINE PRINT .. it was all there just about 15 pages down !!!

title: No refund when policy clearly covered us for a 'pandemic' situation.
body:
Flights to UK cancelled resulting from the pandemic, but we thought we were one of the lucky ones that wouldn't suffer loss because our travel insurance stated we were covered for a pandmic and we took it out in Dec 2019 - pre-COVID.

Unfortunately, because we have been offered a voucher by the travel agent, we are advised we are ineligible for a refund. This, despite that fact said travel voucher must be booked by end 2020, rendering it useless, in light of international travel restrictions 

Budget Direct are hiding behind 'travel credits' as grounds for refund avoidance. The travel credits offered will almost certainly be useless within the time frame we have to use them. 

We have been traveling for two decades, have taken out travel insurance dozens of times, and made a claim on two previous occasions, both of which was satisfactorily resolved. This was our first time insuring with Budget Direct. Take heed BD.  When this is all said and done, people will remember and you will get your just desserts.

title: Easy claim
body: The insurance was reasonably priced and when we returned and had to claim for dental the process was straight forward. I emailed the relevant documents and it was paid without any further questions. I?d use them again.

title: Claim processed within 24 hours - on a weekend!
body: Cover-More's policies are definitely dearer than most travel insurer's out there, however based on the feedback their customers provide and the overall coverage I have always gone with them. In 5 years of using them I have never had to make a claim until a trip I just returned from for items I lost. I filled out the insurance form Saturday morning and the claim was approved yesterday afternoon! Thanks Cover-More.

title: peace of mind

body: 12 Day tour of Vietnam ended up being 6 nights in one hotel and no tour. After 2 and half days were advised to prepare to go home ASAP as nothing was open for us due to the Virus. body:
We went on a recent trip to Italy - Rome, Amalfi Coast and Florence. Whilst shopping for a necklace for my wife in Florence, my wife's purse was stolen (credit cards, cash etc). I cancelled the credit cards and contacted Cover-More. After providing banking details, Cover-More accepted my claim without any fuss. This was my second satisfactory experience with Cover-More and I would use them again without hesitation.
Second claim in two overseas trips and overall experience with Cover-More was exceptional.

body: Difficult to obtain travel insurance once over 70 years particularly with any health problems. Allianz would accept the policy others would not. title: Poor Service Whilst Overseas And Back In Australia!
body:
Recently in Nepal and my husband became very ill with a severe infection, involving his liver, requiring a week in hospital. Despite numerous official hospital emails documenting my husband's illness, from the doctors there, we were continually told by The Assist team that they did not have a "diagnosis" and so could not pay the hospital. After several phone calls and emails to Assist over the week, it came down to the doctor happening by with his coffee, when I was on the phone and him telling the nurse from Assist the exact same information again, to be told  that apparently the diagnosis would now be Ok! As my son noted, it could have been him on the phone for all the nurse knew!  
This was in the hour before we were due to leave the hospital with my still very weak husband. I had rung 6 hours earlier to try to finalise the situation, told by the claims officer that he would sort it and get back to me in 2-3 hours. (Actually he initially told me perhaps I could pay the hospital myself and claim it back!) Six hours later turns out he had done nothing on our file and had gone home! Then nurse said she would get back to me about the hospital payment, as they "were busy." As we were due to walk out the door, I insisted on staying on the line (much to her displeasure) until she finally organised a guarantee to pay the hospital bill. Pure incompetence had led to an extremely stressful situation, that did not need to occur.
I knew how ridiculous the medical situation was, as I am a doctor in Australia myself. Others could easily have been fobbed off, and still be chasing thousands of dollars paid upfront!
Then after more pressure, the Assist nurse finally arranged their official medical authorisation, that we would have to fly home Business Class due to my husband's continuing poor medical condition, as continually ordered by his treating doctors via emails. I had to buy the tickets, as Cover-More could not sort it with Singapore Airlines and I could then claim it back. 
Well 21 days ago,I submitted the paperwork with receipts, totaling 9 pages, for the claim. Supposed to be "10 business days to be at least acknowledged" Business day 15 today, so thought I should check what was happening. Lucky I did! The "experienced" claims officer managing the case had in that time finally paid the hospital bill but "missed" seeing my 9 pages of paperwork for our business class flights and hotel costs. So if I had not followed up, never would have been attended to apparently. I can only assume my paperwork with very private information was not floating around the Cover-More office somewhere? But now I am lucky and they will attend to it right away! Today! Fabulous! 
Seems remarkable we have been unlucky enough to encounter incompetency and poor customer service, in all areas we have been dealing with! Other explanation is this incompetency and attitude is rife in the organisation.

title: Beware! They take your money then won't pay!
body: I am currently in Bali. I booked an accredited PADI Divemaster Course which required me to take 2 months off work.  Having waited and saved for so long and foregone previous holidays to do this course, I took out Gold Cover so if anything went wrong I would not be out of pocket and/or could do this course with no problems. I got a sinus infection which delayed my course by several days (because obviously one cannot dive with a sinus infection). This company has delayed the claim process at every opportunity. They requested documents from me which I sent them. They requested them again 3 days later. They also wanted a birth certificate, a copy of my original flight, passport and medicare card and on and on it went.  It seems they take your word for having an airline ticket and that you are an Australian citizen and/or have residency when you purchase the policy but if you need their assistance...different story.  Who carries their birth certificate and medicare card with them when travelling overseas? And do they realise how difficult it is to find an internet cafe in a third world country let alone one with a scanner. Given the fact that I was trying to study, attending classes and diving for most of the day on most days (sometimes up to 12 hours a day 6 days a week) it left me little time when I resumed the course, to source such an internet cafe and go to it to scan documents and check my emails. Sorry for the inconvenience Insureandgo, I DO NOT have a smart phone!  I  don't know if this company expected the dive company to alter the course curriculum just for me, (even though this company referred to my course as a "diving lesson")  However, regardless of what they may or may not have thought, they have succeeded, in my opinion, of blatantly disregarding their duty of care and have used every excuse and delay tactic to to weasel out of paying my return airfare. I do not intend to sit back and accept this kind of treatment! My friend in Australia has contacted the media and upon my return, I will be sitting down with all the emails and documents with the media with the view to take this matter public so others can be made aware of Insureandgo and the way in which they treat their trusting customers. I will also be writing and blogging on the PADI website to warn other divers.

title: They are happy to take your money but slow to payout.
body:
For starters, product review should only accept reviews from people who have made claims not from people who have just taken out a cover. All insurances are nice when they want your business until it's time to pay up then it's chalk and cheese.
I took out two policies with Insureandgo , one for 4 days and the other for a month. Took sick while on the 4days policy and I contacted the insurer only to be bomb barded with emails about what they required like a doctors report,fitness to fly which the Doctor doesn't issue only the unfit forms and the doctor stated I was fit to fly, mean while I was concerned this would add cost to the doctors bill which I didn't want. I didn't have access to my emails while away so didn't see these emails till I got back home.  I filled their online claim form and sent it in which takes them 10 to 14 days to even look at your claim and then get an email stating they won't approve claim till they get flight itinerary, passport and Medicare information and in this time I was away for a month and not sure if I was even covered or if I could even trust this mob because I hadn't received anything back from them only those continual emails. so I rang them when I got back to see why they wanted this stuff and it was because they wanted to see if I was an Australian and this is why they held my claim up. Well I was most annoyed as I felt this was crap as they should have checked this out before they took my money, they take 10 to 14 days to even look at the claim and this is ridiculous then I sent them the documents then they wouldn't pay as they wanted to known if the bank details were correct, they had that information, just another delaying tactic.  A couple of years ago I made a claim with a different insurer and all they wanted was the medical bill and no mucking about and they paid it within a couple of days but not this mob, they have you jump through hoops that are unnecessary and the amount was for only for $49. If insurandgo muck you around with a small claim I can only imaging what they would do with a claim for a few thousand dollars.  While I was away for that month I was very concerned that I may not be covered as they were playing around with a small claim and felt I couldn't trust them. . 
Would I use insureandgo again the answer is definitely no way I felt I couldn't trust them and if you feel you don't trust your insurer then go somewhere else.
I finally got the $49 about a month and half later.

title: Poor Customer Service
body:
We were recommended to use Covermore to apply for our son's pre-existing condition from HeartKids Australia.  After we had sent all of the required documentation we were told in an email it would take 2 business days to process, we were told on the phone it would take 3.  It took 6 business days to process and during this time, we made a number of phone calls to follow up and find out what was going on.  The people we spoke to were very unhelpful and basically told us there was nothing they could do.  On one particular day, my husband had to call back 3 times after being on hold, then 'cut off', and after this process (which took 30 mins) it was after 5pm and no one was no longer available to talk to. After the 6 days, our application was denied.  We called to speak to the nurse, out of curiosity, to find out why our application was denied.  We were unable to speak to the nurse, but were assured we'd get a call back, this never happened.  It saddens me that this company is recommended by Heartkids, and I will not recommend them to my fellow friends.  Their service was terrible and it was a complete waste of our time.

title: Sick child in Laos
body:
My 10 year old son recently got sick, vomiting and diarrhea, while we were travelling in northern Laos. One of the reasons I chose TID was that they had a 24 hour help & emergency line. I phoned the number (someone from UK) and the person I spoke to advised me to get back to Luang Prabang as soon as possible and find a doctor. When we returned to Luang Prabang the following day, we contacted TID again. They advised me they had a local contact and would get back to us with the number.
In the meantime (day 3, still vomiting) and sick with worry about dehydration, I managed to find a local English speaking doctor who did a blood test and diagnosed acute gastro (food poisoning) and provided medication, etc. We were very relieved.
I hate to think what might have happened had I been sitting waiting for the number that never came.
I have complained to TID, who advised that yes they did get the number, but for one reason or another, the information was never passed on to me.
I'm not sure if I perhaps expected too much here. They seem happy to cover our out-of-pocket expenses for medical care, but in terms of "Help & Emergency" I will not be using TID again.

title: Showed Absolutely No Compassion For a Pregnant Lady Who's Husband Required 5 Surgeries To Save His A
body:
I am extremely disappointed with this company and believe that existing and potential customers might want to hear my story before booking travel insurance through this company.  
My husband was in a terrible accident whilst travelling and spent 4 weeks in the hospital where he underwent 5 surgeries to save his arm. Whilst there were a few staff members which were friendly, compassionate and helpful, the majority of the staff I spoke with throughout this process showed absolutely no compassion and understanding for what my husband and I were going through and caused unnecessary and unreasonable delays making this process extremely stressful and more difficult than it had to be. This company should understand I should have been spending most of my time caring for my husband (and unborn baby) instead of on lengthy telephone conversations with the insurance company in order to obtain updates and requirements to process my husband's claim, telephone calls which one would expect would be made by the company to save time.  
As a company that made a 6.6 billion euro profit in 2014, I find it appalling that when rebooking flights from Canada to Australia for my injured husband, this company refused to upgrade me (six and a half (6 1/2) month pregnant) to sit with him in order to provide the assistance he required throughout this lengthy flight, as he only has one functional arm and hand, despite his treating doctors in Canada stating in the certificate which stated my injured husband's fitness to fly that he required a non-medical escort to assist him with various tasks. They refused to do this in order to save a couple thousand dollars.  
I understand that companies must be profitable to operate however I find it very difficult to believe a couple thousand dollars here and there to upgrade spouses, especially in circumstances like mine would make a dent into this company's yearly profit. Quite the opposite, one would think it would ensure existing customers are satisfied with the service they receive from this organization and likely to become return customers and to recommend this company to friends and colleagues.
During the process, I repeatedly asked to speak to managers or the dispute resolution team to make a complaint and was continually advised that no managers were available or that I could not speak to managers as they would only repeat what the call center staff advised and that I should email the same staff which show no compassion or assistance and that my email would be forwarded on to the dispute resolution team.    
The above are only some of the complaints and concerns I have in relation to the way this company has handled my husband's claim.  
As previously stated, I am six and a half (6 1/2) months pregnant and this company's handling of this claim has amplified the stress I've had to endure during this traumatic experience and I think that any existing and potential customers ought to know this is how Allianz treats customers. They showed absolutely no compassion for a pregnant lady who's husband spent 4 weeks in the hospital, underwent 5 surgeries to save his arm and had to stay in Canada for an extra 5 weeks.  Their customer service was horrendous.

Never did anyone tell us that this would happen otherwise we would never have submitted a claim - this is totally wrong and taking advantage of people that don't understand it when it was Consumer Affairs who advised us to claim.

Where is the empathy towards people that are losing a lot of money that like us can not afford to do so but have wasted our time and hard earned money on.  I would advise anyone that are considering using this company to carefully make sure you fully understand - mind you they never answer the phones to you and take days and days to reply.  where is the law that states you must refund for services that you are unable to provide - this is Australian Consumer Law - are 1Cover above the law in this country.

I had to cancel the trip due to closed borders, and put in a claim.  They told me it'd take a maximum of 10 days, but almost 3 weeks went by and no response, so I followed them up.  They just got back me, and have rejected the claim - apparently WHO announced COVID at the end of January (not then a pandemic) and I was supposed to have a magic crystal ball and know this would lead to worldwide shutting down of borders.  WHO didn't announce it as a pandemic until March.  It is pathetic that Budget Travel have grasped at a minor announcement as a way to rip off their customers.  I'll be taking this further, and will no longer use Budget Travel for any insurance.  Avoid this mob, they will rip you off.

title: Car rental excess cover what a joke no  I'm wrong, what a con, I would not recommend this coy to any
body:
We recently took out travel insurance for a short holiday to Tasmania. The main reason that we took it out was to cover the excess on our rental car in case we had an accident. After doing a little research I found it was cheaper to take out travel insurance rather than pay the extra through the car rental company. Our policy stated we were covered for $3000.00 car rental excess. As luck would have it, we awoke on the last day of our holiday to find there was a small crack in the windscreen, the rental company charged us around $200.00 for a new windscreen. We had a $100.00 excess on the travel policy so I thought we would get $100.00 back, and assumed it would be a simple claim.
No, we are are NOT COVERED at all because in their small print it says that you must take out the extra collision damage waiver and 3rd party insurance through the car rental company if you don't,   you have no cover. So yes I take responsibility for not reading  properly those 40 odd pages of small print.
 But for insure and go to state that they cover $3000.00 in excess  is rubbish  and misleading , the most they would ever pay out is the reduced excess that you would pay  around $300.00 to $ 500.00 , oh and they also won't cover you if you hire a car for longer than 15 days in a row.  
I'm about to take out a yearly policy as we have a few trips planned,so I have been doing more research on insurance policies and I am pleased to say there are other companies that do genuinely cover your car rental excess without having to pay the exorbitant costs that the car hire places charge, other travel insurance companies do not restrict you to 15 days of car hire. So Insure and Go your policy is rubbish and a con!

title: Runaround for nothing!!
body:
I purchased Covermore insurance 6 months before travelling to the US. A couple of weeks before I left I injured my ankle. I received treatment in Australia but required further treatment in the US. I called Covermore to explain my situation. I asked whether it would be possible to receive coverage for further physical therapy in the US. I was very clear that this was for ongoing therapy for an injury that occurred before leaving Australia. Three Covermore agents insisted that I visit a US physician for a referral to the physical therapist. So I did. After half a day and $300 US I had my report and referral. I sent all of the paperwork in. I've just heard that my claim has been declined because it is for ongoing treatment. Why wasn't I told that in the first place? Now I am a further $300 US out of pocket - and I only went to the Physician because Covermore told me to. I received so many phone calls from totally useless agents and spent extra time and money. And then the agent who gave me the 'bad news' told me that they were only trying to take care of me!!!! Just tell the client upfront. Don't give them the runaround and get them to spend even more money when there's little chance they will be covered. I am absolutely disgusted and I will be sharing this with my travel agent and anyone else who is considering Covermore travel insurance.
After leaving this review for possible mediation I received an email stating that my claim was denied because it was a pre existing condition - which it wasn?t!!
As stated before my dissatisfaction stems from the fact that I was unnecessarily sent to a physician in the US with no compensation from Covermore.

title: PAST OVER DUE UNPAID CLAIMS
body:
Over a year after lodging a claim to Cover More, we have received three notices from a debt collection agency here in Canada because the Health Care centre where my partner received his initial treatment (Dec 2017) has not been paid yet. 
I had sent these invoices multiple times and had received a confirmation in Sept 2018 from Cover More stating there was nothing outstanding at the Health Centre- I forwarded the email for the Health Centre Finance to the claims officer and asked them to contact them directly because I am so tired of running around for Cover More only to still receive unpaid invoices (all of which I forwarded months and months previously) from the Health Centre. 
I was really careful to keep a track of all the invoices I sent cover more and more often then not I had to follow up on unpaid invoices. At one point I asked for a collated list of all the invoices I had received payment for/and the invoices paid to health providers- Instead of receiving one; I was told to check back through my emails- surely it wouldn't be hard to collate a list of everything paid out to our claim?

I feel I have done everything correctly;  I have had so much patience and I really don't think it should take over a year to have this settled. 

I am so frustrated that we now have a debt collection agency sending us bills which should have been paid over a year ago. 

I would never use Cover More ever again nor would I recommend them to any one else.

title: Insurance Invalidated with no compensation or redress
body:

I took out a 12 month multi trip Gold insurance policy including medical excess premiums with InsureandGo starting in February 2020.  The total cost was $2700.  Due to the present coronavirus worldwide travel ban my overseas flights in April by were cancelled by Qantas.  I was able to gain refunds for most of the air travel, ground transport and hotels by various companies.

So I have paid for a service which they can no longer supply.  In the circumstances a refund, or at least an extension of the policy, is both a  moral and legal obligation of InsureandGo.

We have used 1Cover for travel insurance for a number of years without incident and like other users were impressed with the simplicity of the purchasing process and the level of cover provided. For the first time this year we had reason to make a claim - what an arduous and unpleasant task that proved to be. They claimed to have initiated necessary actions, which they had not. They did not provide timely payment which delayed the provision of information and progress of the claim. 

Despite the medical discharge stating my husband would need to be upgraded to Business Class for the flight home they told him that they would not pay the $600-$700 for the upgrade as he would be okay to fly economy in a day or so. When we asked if they would replace the tickets for myself and our two children and pay our accommodation until that time, they indicated they asked about the cost of the upgrade and indicated that they might accept it. 

1Cover did not provide any assistance to secure the upgraded tickets or obtain the additional support we required from the airline.

What really annoyed me was that I bought the insurance from Australia Post. But I had to do all the follow up with a redirected "Travel Insurance Partners" that could be an overseas company run by a 'Nigerian prince'.

I feel for the people who are not responsible for any of these but have to reply to these sort of complains. And to those people, don't care about me. I will never buy any policy from Australia Post ever again.

title: I wish I could give them MINUS 5 Stars!!
body:
Buying a policy was super easy. Paying them was even easier. Getting a claim approved is impossible.
I took out a comprehensive travel insurance policy online after reading CANSTAR reviews. When buying a policy online a night before the travel, I was presented with three options. I chose the most expensive option (Comprehensive). 

While coming back to Sydney my first flight got delayed, my subsequent flight was missed because of the delays from first flight and because of the stress, and time zone change, I lost my bag. Because of first flight delay and subsequent missed flight I was stuck in an airport over what my policy dates covered me. 

Budget direct will not cover lost bag because Budget direct expect customers are to call them from overseas when the flights are delayed so that they can renew the policy (maybe charge us more) as the policy is not auto renewed. Best is enable global roaming on your mobile when buying Budget Direct travel policy or try to find a public phone in China (as in my case to make a call to BD) or where ever you are stuck. Don't bother telling your family that you will be late, or your work that you will be late, but do call Budget Direct to renew the policy as its more important!!

While flights are delayed and something happens to you and you are outside the policy cover doesn't matter while you are in transit or not you are not covered unless you call them to renew the policy. 

I called budget direct call centre for claim form, they mentioned to me you are covered until you reach home. After making a claim, claim officer doesn't say the same thing. 

I asked the claim officer what's the way to buy an auto renewal policy as I didn't see an option when buying my comprehensive policy online. She mentioned, I have to call Budget Direct.

How budget direct is CANSTAR's best comprehensive travel insurance provider, is beyond me!!

title: Disappointed
body:
I purchased travel insurance to travel from Australia to the Netherlands in March 2020. While I was there the Australian government imposed the COVID-19 travel ban. I tried to get an earlier flight out but was unsuccesfull. Because of the travel ban I needed to apply for an exemption to travel. I could not board my original flight and not long after the airline cancelled all flights.  Once I received the exemption I had to purchase a new one way ticket ( considerably more expensive) and was able to fly home.
I contacted the Cover More emergency service number the day I supposed to fly back to australia and a day before my cover expired. I was told I would not receive any assistance. I asked if I could extend my cover as at that time I did not know how long I would be stuck in the Netherlands. I was told I needed to contact the Covermore customer service centre in Australia during Australian business hrs or email them. I emailed shortly after and until this day ( 12 days later) have not received a reply. 3 days later I rang the emergency assistance number again and again I was told Covermore would not provide me with any assistance and that I should get in touch with the customer service in Australia if I wanted to extend the travel insurance. I objected to this and the lady on the phone agreed to opening a case. As I was calling on an australian mobile number, I gave her my number and she would call me straight back. I waited for two hrs and never got a call back. 
Therefore I give the Cover more customer service 1 star

title: Allianz Travel Insurance do not honour claims.
body: Most of the reviews below are from people who contacted customer service and have not actually made a claim. Here is my story; I was standing as a party of 8 in a queue of people at a hotel reception desk in Athens when a thief ran in from the street and stole one of my bags containing laptop, mobile phone etc. It was all captured on security cameras, we gave chase down the street chasing the thief to no avail, and the police were called who came to the hotel and took my statement. My claim was refused for the following reason; I left my bag unattended even though it was right next to me within arm's length. I was holding my passports in one hand and my wallet in the other hand. Apparently we all need a third arm and hand to hold on to our luggage to stop thieves. Allianz claimed I was in a public place even when handing over my documents at a reception desk and my luggage was piled up at the reception desk. I was gobsmacked when I was refused a claim for such a black and white simple claim. 17 years as a NAB / Allianz customer and the only claim I have made has made me cancel all other NAB /  Allianz house, contents and car insurances. BYE BYE Nab / Allianz. Really what is point of taking out travel insurance. Will keep this review posted on my fair trading hearing regarding this matter.

body: We had a problem in Vietnam......Allianz had three fatal fails to manage our case satisfactorily.....one... they never asked us initially to provide essential travel documentation to process our claim as admitted by our case manager.......two they never contacted us within 72 hours as promised to discuss our case and when we contacted them after 72 hours they advised us the paperwork they needed... delay caused by them... meant they couldn't help us in time......three.. we rushed around and sent them this paperwork and they advised us my wife would be upgraded to business class to assist her severe coxit injury on the long trip from Danang to Singapore......Singapore to Perth.....four when we then lined up for business class Singapore airlines advised they knew nothing about it.. we then booked into our original economy class tics....nobody from Allianz had advised us of the flight mess up or change before we went to Danang airport.....we rang the case manager to complain about the mix up... he advised us that they had been unable to book an update for Barbara's fare and as we had now booked in economy class and she could not be upgraded for the rest of the trip.......I lodged an e-mail complaint a week ago and got an e-mail to say somebody would discuss with me in 24 hours.....eight days ago.......thanks Allianz......you succeeded in turning our holiday into a total nightmare and failed dismally in what was promised and not delivered.. this view of the company as a continued bad fail was supported by their lack of response to my e-mailed complaint still 7 days after their e-mail guaranteeing to discuss our complaint in 24 hours....shame on you Alliance.....I have asked for a premium refund and will not be claiming for any of our expenses

easy to organise.

title: Not very flexible!
body: I had a tooth that broke while I was in Milan. The back of my tooth was sharp and it was cutting into my tongue. I called TID up and they said that because the tooth was a root canal tooth, they would not pay for a dentist visit. I said that I understand that the root canal would not be fixed, I just wanted the back of the tooth filed down so that it wasn't cutting into my tongue. I told them I was more than happy to wait until I got back to Australia to have the tooth either repaired properly, or extracted. All I was asking for was one dentist visit to have the sharp edge of the tooth filed down. It was cutting into my tongue, and there was a red and sore spot developing. I could hardly eat, or talk, as it was getting more painful by the hour. Anyway, they refused. The funny thing is that the visit probably wouldn't have cost too much, and my excess was $200. TID might have been out of pocket maybe $100 or $200. Anyway, I've used them about 8 times already, and I was happy to continue to use them. Now I'll have to shop around for a more comprehensive insurance before my next trip. One that is more transparent and flexible! It was annoying too because after they said no, I was basically on my own. I was hoping they could help me find a dentist, as I was having trouble finding one. Anyway, I was just so surprised that they were not at all flexible. It really makes you wonder about all the fine print in these policies. Might start the reading now, so that I can complete the reading before my next holiday in 6 months time!

title: Read the Fine Print.
body:
We paid over $300 for travel insurance and when we made a claim for $141 for three medical consultations we were shocked to find that when our claim was approved TID deducted a $100 excess.

I can appreciate the excess being deducted when there are huge medical claims being made but to deduct $100 from a minor claim of $141 is ridiculous.

We have made three such trips in the past 5 years, the previous two times taking out travel insurance with CoverMore. We also made similar claims for similar amounts with CoverMore but were never slugged any excess.

I might add that TID made us visit our local GP to verify that our 6 year old child and I are not prone to viral infections as part of the claims process. How ridiculous! What young child is not prone to catching a viral infection when travelling to Asia for 5 weeks?

All in all I am disappointed with the claims process and feel that the insurance was not worth it in the first place. In future I will be looking for a credit card that offers free  travel insurance. At least then if there is an excess for 'minor' medical costs, I can at least accept this situation because there were no upfront insurance costs in the first place.

$100 Excess on minor medical expenses is grossly unfair.

I made a potential claim via email, but it took well over a week for a response, and when I had a response the process for me to get a refund for the damages was, in my opinion, too difficult.  It involved too much paper-trail work, and I was on holiday, traveling from place to place, and therefore could no longer obtain the police report and other information as requested by the insurance company.  While the price is low, and the cover seems good, I am not sure I will use them again as their response times were slow, and the claims process appears too cumbersome.
Fortunately, the damage to the window of the car only exceeded the excess which I would have had to pay, by $60.

title: Terrible insurance company
body: I had to cancel my trip due to the passing of a close family member (who was not travelling with me) a week before leaving for Fiji. After getting in touch with Allianz to start the claim process I was told I needed to supply over 2 years worth of their medical records and a full list of medications they were prescribed. After trying to satisfy the conditions Allianz require I have since found out that medical records cannot legally be supplied for the purpose of a travel insurance claim due to confidentiality laws. Allianz knows full well that they will not be able to receive medical records (not stated in their PDS) and therefore use this as a reason they will not pay. I can supply all travel receipts and a death certificate but this is not enough. Their lack of compassion and discretion in a sensitive time and misleading service means I will never insure with this company again. You can only measure the quality of an insurance company when you need to make a claim and in this case Allianz fell well short of the mark.
