title: Should change name to No Cover!
body: We have used Covermore for many years for travel insurance and have never had an issue with them.  In July, the underwriters changed to Zurich Insurance.  We made a claim in October for a lost item in an aircraft seat pocket.  Seven weeks later, the claim was denied.  The policy wording is ambiguous and not transparent.  The company will avoid making payouts for claims and the process of making a claim is not easy.  We might as well have had no insurance.  Don't waste your money with Covermore - they are not the company they used to be.

title: repeat customer - so far so good!
body: This is the 4th time I have purchased travel insurance from Insure and Go. It was easy to set up and easy to compare policies. So far I haven't had to make a claim but, if I do need to claim, I hope their claims process is as straightforward as their purchase process. The 4 stars reflect the fact that I haven't yet experienced the claim process

title: Never had a problem/Never had a claim!!!
body: Very easy to discuss with online operator, who explained all details. So will keep using them for future trips. Would be much easier if they could you your old records when you ring instead of going thru them all again. We have two more trips already booked so guess I will have to go thru all the details again!!!!

title: Extremely disappointing
body: It was the first time I used InsureandGo and it is also the last.  When I purchased the policy for my 10 week trip in 4 countries in 2018, I was asked if I would be on a cruise ship in Alaska.  I replied that I would be using the Alaska Marine Ferries but not a cruise ship.  I was then advised to cover myself with the cruise component of their insurance product, which of course incurred a further charge.  One of the 5 ferries we used in Alaska broke down which caused chaos in the ferry system and was well known up and down the Alaska coast.  We had to cut our stay in Skagway by a day, forfeit our trip on the White Pass Scenic train, and catch the next ferry a day earlier than planned and so move onto Haines a day earlier.  Otherwise we would have had no way out of Skagway for several more days (as a minimum) and that would have completely thrown out the rest of our schedule.  So that's what we did and when I returned home I claimed the 1 night's accommodation in Skagway which we had to forfeit, supported by evidence from my travel agent.  The travel agent received a refund for the White Pass Railway ticket and made it a contra entry against the extra night's accommodation they purchased in Haines, so all I was claiming was the 1 night's accommodation forfeited in Skagway.  InsureandGo refused to pay it and denied the claim.

title: Fantastic experience.
body:
I have used Cover-More twice twice over the last few years and have also had the unfortunate luck of claiming twice as well. One claim was due to theft and the other illness. Both claims were easy, hassle free and I received my refund in good time. Thank you Cover-More I will definitely use your services again.
No problems, even when having to claim twice!

title: Ignored overseas but broken neck and skull fracture
body: The policy was worthless. My son was left with fractured skull and other injuries and NO help was provided. Everything was difficult and I eventually paid for him to be flown out. Hopefully I will be reimbursed - I will repost if not. I?m disgusted how a young man could be treated so badly

title: Peace of mind
body: Have not had make a claim yet so I can?t make a judgment on customers support but I can say is the policy was easy to set up and was good value

title: The worst ever! Don't waste your money!
body: I have traveled extensively and I purchased my first one year travel insurance policy. I unfortunately took it out with insure and go. I traveled overseas 4 times during this time a a few interstate trips. I made 2 claims both declined. On my last trip I lost my camera whilst in Vietnam - they refused to cover it. Their claim process is just that, a process. They come up with every excuse in the book to not pay out on a claim. Each time you provide the information requested they come up with another hurdle. The final reason given to me for why they declined my claim was " I should look after my possessions as if they were not insured."  They would have no idea how I look after my possessions unless they were with me on my holiday. No one goes out of their way to lose things especially a camera with your holiday photos. they do not want to pay claims, don't waste your money!

title: Wouldn't travel without it!
body: On my recent trip to Bali I had travel insurance through Allianz but thankfully did not have to make a claim myself.  However I dealt with Allianz in providing a witness statement to a fatal injury that occurred to another Australian tourist who also had Comprehensive Travel Insurance with Allianz.  Allianz was in that instance very understanding, supportive, quick in responding and organising all communication between Bali Hospitals, Embassy and the immediate family back in Australia and bringing the young Australian home for burial.  I wouldn't use anyone else!

title: Safety Net
body: Policy was excellent value. Very easy to navigate setting up the policy. Unfortunately, I had to claim; support was very clear and kind throughout the process. It took longer to process than I thought; but turned out fine.

title: Thank you for all your help

I would certainly use 1cover Travel Insurance next time we go on a holiday.

title: Happy with coverage and service
body: Easy to purchase, good cover and good price.  Good web page and easy to understand coverage and exclusions. Liked email communication prior to and after trip. Will likely purchase again for next trip overseas.

title: Satisfactory experience. Thanks
body:

The claims team were professional & courteous, there was no quibbling over amounts or circumstances.

title: Beware Annual Policy
body:
I have held an annual policy for at least 5 years as I travel overseas at least 3 times pa. I recently was advised by TID that the annual policy only covers you for travel that you TAKE within the 12 month period of the policy.
In my case I held a policy from April 2017 to April 2018. I booked a trip in January 2018 for travel in May 2018 but had an accident in March 2018 and thought I might have to cancel the trip. Despite booking the trip in the insurance period and suffering an event within the insurance I was told by TID I could not claim because the planned travel was outside the insurance period. This means the window to plan, book and take the trip starts off at 12 months and reduces to one day by the end of the 12 months, even if you renew the policy. Not really practical I suggest.
Shop around because other insurers do cover you if you have to cancel a trip planned for outside the 12 months if the event occurs in the period of insurance.

title: Terrible - policy wording out-of-date and biased
body: While visiting my parents during the July school holidays, my father became very unwell and was hospitalised, and then  several days later died. I had to book new flights (new dates) for my daughter & I from NZ back home to Australia (including domestic flights), returning on the 2nd day after the funeral. Flight Centre were very supportive and suggested I make a claim with CoverMore as they assured me that I would be covered for the cost of the new flights. However, CoverMore rejected my claim as my father did not live in Australia and therefore I was not covered. How many people nowadays have parents and even husbands/wives & children living in other countries! I won't be using CoverMore again.

I was able to cancel our accommodation with No charge. Since we are now not able to travel I rang Insure & Go requesting a refund of the policy but was advised that it was out of the cooling Off policy. I then sent an email to complaints but No response. All I want is my money back. We are not going to be making any claims. 
I also went to their website and clicked on credit but they only offer $49 credit when the policy Cost $101.74.  So not even half.
  Insureand Go I will never use you again and also advise everyone who is looking for travel insurance NOT to use you.

body:

I would like to say, that I am rather pleased with the final outcome that I have received from Travel Insurance Direct. Since I wrote the initial review I emailed my details as requested to a customer service officer and I received a call this morning. 

I would like to say, that I am rather pleased with the final outcome that I have received from Travel Insurance Direct. Since I wrote the initial review I emailed my details as requested to a customer service officer and I received a call this morning.

title: Disgusted with the lack of follow up
body:
I took out Travel insurance with Covermore and prior to travel my father had a serious new medical condition. Long story short- had to canel my travel plans and lodged a claim with Covermore- still waiting 2 months later and the continual 10 working days keeps starting every time you speak to them. They requested details of the Treating doctor to contact them to send a medical questionairre- a month later the doctor advised me he hadnt even received the questionnaire- Covermore told me they were waiting for the doctors response. I contacted the claims officer and asked about a timeframe for a decision- guess what I was told- maybe 10 days! But it could be lomnger if they require more information. 
Covermore is a waste of hard earned money- Virgin should rething offering Covermore as travel insurance when you book Virgin flights. NEVER again.
No empathy regarding what my family is going through, just- that will take another 10 days for a response. Now Ive read all the other reviews- what is the management team doing to address the poor service customers are receiving???

body:
I had to make a medical claim when I returned from my trip to the USA.  While in the US I had an allergic reaction and had to visit a hospital to get a cortisone shot. I had all the documentation and receipts for the medical costs however I was annoyed that TID also required me to visit my family doctor when I returned to have him verify that this medical condition was not pre-existing. Other travel insurance companies I've used in the past have never asked for this so I thought the claim process with TID was a little cumbersome.  On a positive the refund was processed rather efficiently.
Cheap
Cumbersome claim process for medical claims

title: Bloody Hopeless
body:
We took out a policy with Cover-More insurance for travel.

On a recent trip we had a disruption caused by forces beyond our control. We made a claim only to receive a very legalistic letter quoting sections of the policy that invalidated our claim. There was very little care or concern for our circumstances and situation and absolutely no offer of any assistance. The complex policy structure and wording seems to be designed primarily to invalidate simple claims. 

The whole reason for taking a policy out is to have peace of mind and protection in the event of disruption.

My advice is to read very carefully the policy inclusions and exclusions as this lot seem to delight in denying claims.

I would avoid Cover-More at all costs. They have lost my business.

title: Stranded in Bali,fork out all this money & still waiting.
body: We were stranded in Bali for an extra 7 nights,sick daughter in Kuta bimc hospital,the holiday from hell,we were so lucky the  money we had in our account which we were using to SETTLE on our house when we arrived back home which we had to put back,day 15 still don't know when I'm getting $7k back from travel insurance,it's a joke.

title: Thank you Allianz
body: For the first time ever, we had to make a (rather big) claim on our travel insurance due to missing a connecting flight (extreme weather being the cause). The claim process was smooth and our communication with Allianz was very satisfactory. The claim was processed in full, 4 weeks after we lodged. I have purchased a new policy with them again and will continue to do so.

title: A necessity, wouldn't travel without it.
body: We have always used TID Travel Insurance Direct specially when travelling overseas. We have found it easy to set up online and very competitive with other travel insurance companies. We wouldn't hesitate to recommend to other travellers.

title: You get what you pay for...
body:
Yes they are cheap but that is exactly what you get, TID are happy to take your money but not so happy to pay out on a claim. My camera broke, it got wet and stopped working. I was told you can make a claim however you probably won't be reimbursed as you don't have sufficient evidence that you own the camera, you didn't get witness statements when it broke. Who am I going to tell? Did you speak with hotel staff or the police what??? Its a broken camera not stolen, the police and hotel don't care. I also need to provide proof I actually went on a holiday and a receipt for the replacement. Ah I haven't bought a replacement hence the insurance claim. 
I was then told if you do decide to submit a claim, complete a statutory declaration for proof of ownership and a statement of what occurred. I would then need to get a repair quote, however 'you will not be reimbursed for this'. Why not? I don't want the repair quote I already know the camera's not working. I then stated if they want evidence of ownership I am happy to send them the camera, 'oh no sir this doesn't prove you own it'..
Well you get the drift of the stupidity of this conversation. The customer service is terrible and the claims process has to be the worst I have ever dealt with. Pay the extra money and sign up with an insurance provider that will help you not make life difficult.
Cheap.
Customer service didn't want to assist in anyway, terrible claims process.

title: Claim no:974035 very quick response.
body: I felt the policy was good value, easily set up be travel agent, very satisfied with the result of my claim, it was dealt with professionally and quickly, I could not have asked for more, staff on the phone were very courteous and friendly, the claim was settled and funds transferred into my bank account, having dealt with Cover-More for over 20 years of travel, I can only strongly recommend them. Thanks again. W.B.

title: It was fantastic I found this product.
body: I have trouble finding a cover that will cover me due to a small health issue a "Cavernoma" that has caused me no trouble in over 9 yrs but many covers won't cover me these days. This Insurance did. I had to pay more but that was fine. We didn't have to use the Insurance so can't comment on that. I was impressed a few days before we were due to return they emailed me to check I wasn't staying longer and would still be covered if I did. I will be using again.

title: Great cover

body:

Needed to get stitches and go to emergency and had to pay a fair bit up front unfortunately. A few days later I submitted all paperwork from hospital and the claim was processed the next day! This was the online claiming system, not mail. The online claim is easy to use, simple, and no fuss.

Super fast, reliable, and I'll be using these guys in the future.
Reliable, Fast-processing

title: Covermore Useless
body:
We took out Covermore insurance for a trip to Fiji. 
After we booked I discovered I needed an operation neither I nor my doctor were expecting so we submitted a claim.
Covermore lost the paperwork a couple of times and then took 2 weeks to admit they had received anything.
Next they took several weeks to give an answer, they only looked at it and did anything on the days I rang up.
Then they rejected the claim with a vague reason so we appealed. Again they only did something when we rang up. Then they gave their reason that the claim was rejected because of a previous condition even though I and my doctor was not aware of this.
The whole idea of insurance is to cover you for the unknown and unexpected. 
Pretty useless.

body: I was a little confused when trying to buy insurance for a one way trip, but a prompt response to my query clarified things. I have used Insure and Go for several trips, and always had great service, including on the one occasion I made a claim.

body: This was our 6th ski trip and the first time I have used Allianz. My previous insurer required 7 days between the purchase of the policy and departure. Allianz was quick easy affordable and the person I spoke to on the telephone was friendly professional and efficient.

body: Really disappointed that no help was offered when our first airline cancelled our flights. While it is now clear that this is an exclusion clause in the pbs, it is a total cop out. It makes me wonder now if insurers, including yourselves, would actually be of any assistance if we really needed it! The only positive in this situation was the help And politeness of the customer service officers who are put in a really awful situation.

title: Painfully frustrating!
body:
Spending 11 months abroad with my girlfriend was an amazing exerience, but when faced with crippling pains, cancelled flights and stolen iPhones, covermore was a pain to deal with! Email after email, phone call after phone call, we were getting nowhere. Until I spoke to  a senior case manager, nothing was getting done about our situation. The lengthy process just to get a few sessions of physio covered was ridiculous and it felt as if the company only cared about having to fork out a few measly dollars. As for helping out with finding emergency accommodation..I was told "don't call us, we'll call you" and surprise surprise the phone never rang. Being polite to the staff members lead nowhere! I had to get quite verbal before anyone even took a second look at my case. 3 weeks later, I received minimal cover and after that it was back to square one. Frustrating to the stage where I cut my journey short and came home in order to seek medical advice.
Good work covermore!
Massive company. It's not going to disappear on you

title: Still waiting...
body:
I had to cut short a trip in December due to a death in the family. There was a bit of back and forth emailing, with TID wanting additional information. I gave them the last piece of requested information on February 14th, and still haven't been told their decision or reimbursed any of the money. 

After waiting over a month with no updates, I sent another email only to be told they're still waiting for my family member's doctor to give them the additional information. Another 4 weeks has gone by, still nothing. This is getting ridiculous... how long am I expected to wait?

I wish I could stop thinking about this (every time I do it reminds me of what happened in December and I get a pit in my stomach) but feel like if I do they'll never ever follow it up with me.

I'll update this review if they ever respond to me.

As an aside: I wish people wouldn't leave reviews unless they've actually had to make a claim. How can you review a service if you haven't tried to use it? I wonder how much the rating would drop if only people who have actually had to deal with TID wrote reviews.

title: Shocking service - well short of customer expectations
body: We purchased a 1 year comprehensive travel insurance plan from 1Cover for our son's overseas holiday.  Unfortunately six months into the trip he fell off his bike and broke his wrist and needs surgery.  We were advised that 1Cover would not pay for the surgery and our son would have to fly home, at his own expense, and present to a public hospital and go on the waiting list for surgery! I was advised by the 1Cover agent that surgery would be covered by the Accident Compensation Cooperation (ACC).  When I called ACC I was advised that this surgery would not be covered as our son had been out of the country for over six months.  When we called 1Cover to advised them of this and to discuss this decision 1Cover reluctantly agreed to cover the trip home.   As soon as you return to your country of origin you are on your own -1Cover end the policy and dump you onto the already overstretched public health system.   My son had a one year working visa, had trips booked to other countries in Europe, had accommodation booked with services that he had to pay for and a "dream job".  Surgery overseas was the quickest and preferred option but not the cheapest option for 1Cover.  Shocking customer service.  I would never recommend this company for any parent taking our insurance for their child traveling overseas.

title: An unjust scam
body: An absolute injustice! Just finishing high school, I decided to purchase airline tickets, approximately $1700, to travel to Europe. However due to a random panic attack that had me incapacitated indoors for 4 days hallucinating and paranoid, I decided to review my decision to go overseas (as nothing like this has ever happened before). So I decided it was best to identify why I had this panic attack and how to deal with something like this in the future. Thus I decide to get my ticket refunded. However I was denied sufficient compensation as it was claimed my anxiety was ?pre-existing condition.? The only money I received back from the flights was $200! Note: I had never experienced a panic attack like this, and my anxiety had never before stopped me from travelling. As an 18 year old who earns near to nothing, losing this money was absolutely heartbreaking. I was scammed due to a clause that was discriminate towards mental health and hidden in the special conditions. For example if someone had had a weak ankle from a previous condition, bought airline tickets, and then broke their foot due to randomly falling, they would be compensated immediately. I find it an absolute injustice towards mental health, and is something Covermore needs to re-evaluate in order to avoid exploiting young people. After cancelling those flights the airline company would have profited handsomely from reselling the tickets. I am utterly discouraged to ever buy another ticket, and honestly, as mental health problems are so increasingly relevant in today?s society, for it not to be regarded correctly as a sufficient excuse for compensation is terrible. Most of my peers my age also have many mental health problems, and to know their money would be taken out of their hands due to a freak attack has dissuaded them from buying a ticket. All in all I am disgusted at the way Covermore completely rejected my claim, and hope they learn to understand the significance of mental health, and treat it just as justly as if it were a physical condition.

body:
I was involved in a head on car vs scooter accident in Indonesia where I almost lost both my life and the life of my friend. I was the passenger of the scooter and my friend was the driver. We were both wearing helmets and travelling at a very safe speed (less than 50km/h). The driver of the other vehicle was at fault and the police report indicates he was driving on the wrong side of the road and speeding around a blind corner (not to mention I remember the whole thing myself). Long story short I spend months in recovery (physically and mentally).

From the start Allianz didn't want anything to do with the incident. I was hospitalised in a third world country and needing to get home for surgery. I ended up having to organise my own way home from a hospital bed with no help from these guys whatsoever. No compassion other than the clearly scripted "Oh we hope you are recovering well" crap. Yeah, as if you guys give a damn about your customers.

After a long, stressful and drawn out claims process once I had gotten home, I was declined my claim (for medical expenses, missed flights, rescheduled flights, destroyed property). Their reasoning was my friend didn't have an international drivers licence. This licence is not required to operate a scooter in Indonesia as stated by the RAC (the people that issue the licences). Not to mention I'm not operating the scooter. I better start asking every person I step into a car with if they have a licence or not, hey? Ridiculous.

There is no compassion in this business. No heart. They don't care about your well being or continued suffering. They just want your money. Don't give it to them.

Message from staff was basically only interested in insuring young  (under 40), low risk people to destinations with relatively low medical costs (rule out USA).  1Cover has every right to assess risk and decide on whether to insure but very disappointed that the customer interaction was dismissive and dishonest in terms of explaining the reasons for their risk assessment. There are a couple of problems with this, firstly Hertz are under no obligation to repair the vehicle, we have all rented cars that are damaged and have been for some time.  Secondly even if they have repaired my car Hertz will not  give me any more information than the invoice that they used to deduct one thousand pounds from my credit card so I can not comply with Allianz's unreasonable demand.
If you are like me and you believe that you were insured for the excess and you have been charged that excess and claimed for it you would think that you would be entitled to be paid the claim. Not so! Allianz are not prepared to do so.
I strongly urge potential Allianz customers to find an insurer who is more honest in its dealings with this issue of car rental excess.
I intend to take this matter to the Insurance Ombudsman, start a blog criticising Allianz and I will be writing to all travel magazines and columns in newspapers to bring this matter to people's attention.
You have ben warned be very careful on this matter.

title: BEWARE OF INSURE AND GO FINE PRINT -FLIGHT CANCELLATION DUE TO  "Operational Requirements, IS NOT CO
body:
My flight was cancelled on a major airline because of 'Operational Requirment' so we had an extra night and days worth of expenses. No problem my policy says it covers 'Flight Cancellation" NO THAT IS A PROBLEM AS IN TINY WRITING IT STATES 'If flight is cancelled because of Operational requirements (which is still cancelling the flight- YOU ARE NOT COVERED!!!!!! There are usually 3 reasons flights are cancelled, Bad weather, machanical problems or Operational Requirements which covers a multitude of problems. I have discovered many flights are often cancelled citing this reason rather than machanical or bad weather. So chances are 1in 3 that your cancelled flight is NOT COVERED. 
I only was out of pocket a few hundred dollars, I am sure many people have been burned for far more money than I did. Remember cheap insurance is cheap for a reason, because they don't pay out very often.
BUYER BEWARE.

title: Run Away
body:
In all my experience in dealing with travel insurance, I have never come across such incompetent claims handling and service. To start, my first claim they decided to correspond with me via postal letters to my Australian address knowing full well I am traveling overseas for a year. Stupid right? Keep reading.

After various complaints they managed to finalize my straight forward bronchitis claim, only for me to have to keep receiving further emails regarding my complaint from their IDR department. Again, shows how little due diligence they conduct contacting you. All the information for my claim was in my first email and in their system but obviously it's too much effort for their claims department to handle.

My second claim (straight forward dental) was not responded to within the 10 business day limit per the General Insurance Code of Practice. Again, I had to make a complaint via unorthodox channels (i.e their media department) to get a response. Even then there was no explanation why it was out of code, only stupid questions from the claims manager as to if my tooth was sound and natural. If my tooth wasn't sound I wouldn't of felt pain. If it wasn't natural then the claim wouldn't only AUD$42. It's hard to believe this would be coming from a claims manager. Of course her explanation as to why my claim was outside of code was even more dumbfounding, something along the lines of 'oh, we couldn't find any attachments." Common sense would suggest you email me to ask me to re-send. Again, lack of due diligence. To top it off, payment of the claim wasn't made. So I had to email again with no response from the claims manager after 10 days. Finally I get it resolved after having to provide a copy of my bank statement to show I never got the AUD$42 (even though this is the same account they paid into in my previous claim)! 

The final straw which prompted me to write this review (no I don't like writing bad reviews) is that during a chance encounter with an New Zealand couple whilst in Romania, I find out we were both insured by 1Cover. During this 4 hour train ride all they could talk about was how bad their experience with 1Cover was, how they were messed around after falling seriously ill in France. Seems like I am not the only one being handed terrible claims experiences.

1Cover don't even have their own claims department and this seems to be why it's so terrible. Claims are handled by their insurer Allianz and their claims department obviously needs an overhaul. Poor processes and procedures, clearly a lack of staff training and most alarmingly, unability to relate to the customer: the traveler. Along with all their mistakes, just a lot of impersonal corporate insurance resonance in all their dealings.

Whilst 1Cover sales teams do their job, until the day 1Cover has their own in-house claims department that they can control, Don't be insured by them. You know, you've worked hard for your money and whilst trying to enjoy then your travels, when you suffer an incident (big or small) you just don't need the unnecessary frustration and aggravation from 1Cover claims.

*If you look at their 'reviews', a lot of those 5 star reviews aren't even from claims. They're just reviews from people who returned from their trip but didn't make a claim i.e follow up email with link sent to all customers.

title: Deliberate Delay Tactics, Broken Promises and Unethical Review Process.
body:
We have heard of it happening in the broader insurance company community whereby the Insurer deliberately creates delays and generally makes it so hard for the consumers to pursue legitimate claims that the claimants eventually give up.  Going on our own personal experiences and by looking at so many other similar instances documented on this site, it is very apparent that Budget Direct are the masters of employing these tactics.  We lodged out claim for international flight refunds then followed up several times when nothing happened and were then asked to submit "additional" information (which we had already previously submitted) then chased up again and again.  After months of deliberate delays our claim was rejected as the airline, SAA, have offered a credit but as the trip for us was a one-off and we will never be flying long-haul again due to our age and health reasons (further complicated by the advent of Covid 19).  We then asked that the rejection be reviewed by a Manager/Team Leader in accordance with Stage One of the Budget Direct Dispute Resolution.  As a results we were promised written determination within ten business days and then fifteen business days but nothing ever happened.  No contact, no apologies just silence.  This is not good enough and we will not be one of those customers who just get so sick of the deliberate delays that they give up.

Update as at 17/07/2020.  Budget have now just written saying the claim is rejected even though we had comprehensive cover but we can further challenge the decision by going to Stage 2.  Obviously this is just more deliberate delay tactics so they can hang on to our money for even longer.

Our strongest recommendation to anyone considering using Budget Direct is Don't use them as they are totally unethical.

title: Looks good on the surface but watch out for the detail
body:
The CBA offers international travel insurance IF you pay for all your travel with your CBA gold (or higher) credit card. That seems nice. However, please note, unless you go into your netbank and ACTIVATE the cover - there is a push button on the insurance page -, or call, or call into a branch to activate it, you only get the absolute MINIMUM cover. If you do either of the latter, take a note and/or send a confirmatory email.
Fortunately, we picked this nuance up, what I will call "sleight of hand" a few months later when browsing the page and got a bit of a shock when I realised we did not have automatic full cover. The base cover is REALLY basic.
As luck would have it, things went pear shaped just before our journey and we had to delay our trip, which, had I not taken that necessary activation step, would not have been covered.
Not good eh? Well, in my view and experience it seems that there is another layer of avoidance of responsibility by CBA and/or their underwriter, Allianz. On two occasions I was given incorrect information about who to contact by CBA staff in the insurance section. Rather unprofessional what? Then, to add insult to injury, Allianz refused the claim because, after two pages of standard legalese, they claimed that I had not activated the cover. This despite me providing ALL the information in writing to their assessor including a copy of the activation page. I could not help but get a very strong impression that their first response is : dis-allow the claim and let the claimant fight it! My case was cut and dried in terms of what the cover provided for.
Overall it is a good deal, if you activate it and you keep a copy of everything. Best advice, read everything, keep copies of everything and take notes of every conversation. I have names and dates of all these stages to cover me. Just watch your back!!!

If you forget something they say we should be careful. Everybody does care about their stuff but if any incident happen then insurance should cover it that's why we buy insurance policy. I mean in any case they can say that incident happen because you didn't care, its unacceptable. Now I did put a dispute to Customer relations team and they are going to do review again. Still I am hoping for the best. We hadn't used a travel agent, so cancelling all our bookings was a lengthy process. We cancelled our trip from Brisbane to Paris that was booked with Expedia, but Expedia did not cancel the flight, so we were only able to claim the cost of flight and not the airport taxes because we didn't know that we had to make the claim for the taxes ourselves until we were told
 ?as per industry regulations, departure taxes for flights and cruises are a fully
refundable component of these bookings provided the booking was not utilized. Please contact the provider of your flight booking to request a refund of this component of your booking.)?
But in the end we were happy enough with the outcome. Of the $6636 we claimed we recovered $5,135. And to be honest - we are just happy that our daughters open heart surgery went well. I would use Australia Post Travel insurance again.....now that i have worked out the process for making claims.

1Cover should really consider to change their underwriter - because Allianz is the worst - and they are giving 1Cover a bad name.

title: Disappointed. Be Aware Of What Is Required In Case You Need To Make a Claim.
body: I have always traveled with 1Cover Travel Insurance and felt safe doing so. I had read the PDS and believed I had found the best product for my needs. I have never had to make a claim until this trip and was surprised and disappointed by what I learned the hard way. For EVERY (yes EVERY) item that you wish to claim as lost or damaged including your suitcase, clothing, toiletries you must have a valid receipt showing YOUR OWNERSHIP. I was not aware of this detail until now. I had read in the PDS that evidence of the value of any item being claimed would be required in the event of a claim but had wrongly assumed this was referring to replacement value and did not consider needing to prove ownership. I thought had done everything I would need to make a claim, reported the damage immediately to the airline, obtained a written report from them, taken photographs and retained the damaged suitcase. Not good enough to make a claim with 1Cover. 1Cover will pay me a maximum of $100 less my $100 excess (yes that's $0) if I complete an application, submit documents and wait for it to be processed. Of course I'm not going to bother. I've learned my lesson and will be keeping ALL my receipts in future, and looking for alternative travel insurance as well. They say the test of any insurance is when you make a claim, and sadly I no longer feel safe using 1Cover as I feel nervous of what other "details" might apply if I need to make a claim in future and would not wish to risk a huge medical or liability bill while believing I was covered.

title: Insufficient Record Keeping
body:
My son travelled to Paris early in the year and was robbed of his mobile phone on the Metro in Paris on his way to England. He phoned us immediately with his cousin's phone and explained what haapened. We immediately phoned Covermore Emergency number to seek their advice. 

The main issue as my son was in transit he could not report the incident immediately as he would miss his connection which would lead to additional costs. The Covermore representative said it would not be necessary to report the incident as he was in transit. 

I asked did I need an email from the representative to confirm this advice and it was very clearly stated that the calls were noted and I assumed would be available for future reference. My son also phoned Covermore and they gave him the same advice and said it would not be worthwhile reporting in England as this was not in the same jurisdiction.  

When we made the claim for the stolen phone Covermore said that we should have reported the theft and that could not find any calls made to them at the time of the incident. 

I then had to spend a substantial amount of time and effort finding the phone and skype records to confirm the calls had been made and provided this evidence to Covermore. Covermore customer service was extremely poor and did not apologise for their lack of record keeping and varying advice.

title: Zurich = diminished customer care
body:
My partner & I have been Cover-More clients for years and always opt for the annual multi trip policy. We also pay a premium for a pre-existing medical condition.  In all our years, we have only ever had one claim - for lost specs as I recall. It was paid promptly, no hassles. Then in September this year we embarked on a 6 week NZ/European holiday. On the flight over to NZ, my partner had a heart attack & ended up in Auckland Hospital where he was treated & released with a stent after 3 days. We flew home a week later not being able to continue our holiday. 

We promptly put in our claim and were very thorough in our documentation. We downloaded everything that was required & took the doctor's form to our GP to fill out - which he promptly did. He stated that my partner had no known previous problems whatsoever with his heart. We sent it all off. Then, the delaying tactics started. We were informed, after the 10 business day delay, that we needed to prove that things we had claimed for (i.e. train tickets etc) were non refundable. We had already documented everything that had been refunded such as accomodation. Anyway, we dutifully complied by photocopying the train information from their sites & sent it all off. We waited & then another 2 weeks later they informed us that their medical assessment team needed a report from the doctor before the claim could be considered. What the hell was the doctor's form that we initially sent in all about then?

We waited longer than the 10 business days this time & in the meantime saw the doctor again. We asked about this new report & he said that they had received a request from Cover-More for a history & that Cover-More needed to pay for that report. So we waited yet again while Cover-More came up with the money. The long & the short of it is that after nearly 3 months, they settled the claim. They didn't short change us anywhere but we felt their delaying tactics were uncalled for. They should have instigated the doctor's report immediately or at least when they asked for more info from us initially. They treat each request separately so that they can apply this 10 business day delay for each new review. Another reviewer has mentioned this. Filing a claim & waiting for settlement is frustrating especially after having suffered the distressing situation initially. They are there to try & minimise their payout. I do not believe that they care at all for the customer.

Anyway, once they agreed to pay, the money arrived one day later. I can't fault them that. I believe that since Zurich has taken over the underwriting, the product has diminished. Interestingly, Choice Magazine, in the Dec/Jan.  issue, reviewed travel insurance policies sold by travel agents. Choice deemed that if you buy comprehensive travel insurance through Flight Centre for instance, it's arranged by Cover-More & underwritten by Zurich, as are the NRMA & Virgin Australia policies. None of these brands scored high enough to be recommended. 

Cover-More used to be good but the bean counters have set out their priorities which, unfortunately, seem to be savings first and customers second. We've since done a check & compared apples with apples. There are less expensive plans out there and they are highly rated. Cover-More doesn't cut it anymore on cost or service. Since our annual policy will be up for renewal in January, we'll be taking our business elsewhere.

title: Allianz travel cover for CBA credit card holders is different to what existed previously
body: Allianz took over travel cover for CBA credit card holders in July 2015.  Allianz say that customers were notified of this change and its implications.  I travel frequently overseas, relying on insurance activated by using my CBA Platinum MasterCard to purchase at least $1,000 of the travel costs.  In December 2016 - 17 months after the Allianz/CBA deal went ahead - I received the first email from CBA saying that notification of travel to Allianz would be required to activate the travel insurance.  (CBA's MasterCard people had been aware of my earlier trips.)  The Allianz travel notification form can only be reached via CBA's Netbank.  This Allianz travel notification form is pre-filled in the name of the primary Netbank customer - even if the MasterCard card-holder is a different person.  The Allianz form SAYS that the name of the traveller can be changed - but this option seemed to have been left off the form!  Importantly, the Allianz form requires destinations and dates of travel  - which details of course may be subject to change for many travellers en route.  Most importantly, the Allianz form requires the traveller to list any pre-existing conditions - and specifies that a higher premium (or exclusion of insurance) may then be calculated.  The trouble with this is that the Platinum MasterCard holder has already PAID an annual premium (implied in their high annual card fee) to include insurance - and Allianz SHOULD have requested any pre-existing conditions then.  (Once the annual premium has been accepted, a new condition is NOT pre-existing, even if it occurs prior to a particular episode of travel during that year.)  When Allianz was complained to about this situation a) their call centres showed little interest - and would not give any contact details for Allianz's Australian HQ; b) Allianz HQ in Germany took their time to refer it back to Allianz HQ in Australia; and c) Allianz HQ in Australia pretended that all the changes to the insurance were above board (and that this traveller had actually filled in the Allianz forms and activated the insurance - when in fact filling in those forms in the traveller's name had proved impossible!).

Due to not having a set and paid itinerary we found that we had no grounds for a claim after many, many emails and phone calls with vague and condescending responses. Fair enough perhaps, but then we also informed our policy, which was paid for another seven months, was automatically cancelled due to a brief return to Australia before re-arranging our plans and continuing the trip in Europe. I understand that these decisions are all within the vast fine print of our policy, but the rudeness and vagueness of Covermore's responses to my enquiries has been monumentally frustrating. And, of course, I'm [censored word removed] about losing thousands of dollars!
You no longer have to work out what to do with your money, as you will no longer have any.

title: Don't Rely on Cover-More - Use another insurer
body: We submitted a claim to Cover-More for accidental damage to our waterproof camera (it was destroyed when water entered the camera, which the manufacturer determined was most likely due to accidental misclosure of the battery compartment). After receipt of our claim Cover-More requested that we obtain a quote for the cost of repairs and copies of purchase receipts. We submitted our camera to a qualified repairer for assessment and determination of the cause of the damage. They forwarded the camera to the manufacturer for review. Whilst awaiting the report from the repairer, Cover-More advised that they had declined the claim on the basis that they determined the cause of the damage to be mechanical and the responsibility of the manufacturer. They made this determination without waiting for the report from the repairer/manufacturer (who in fact advised the damage was most likely accidental and not a mechanical fault) or ever viewing the camera or obtaining their own assessment. So it seems Cover-More just make their own rules when it comes to determining payment of claims, even after consumers follow their directions in relation to pursuing information requested as part of the claim process. I am just thankful that we didn't need to rely on Cover-More for a more substantial claim. Who knows what reasoning they will give to deny expensive medical claims if our experience with a minor claim is anything to go by. We are frequent travelers and will NEVER entrust Cover-More with our travel insurance needs again. It is just not worth the risk.

body:

Under no circumstances take out travel insurance with Allianz. Our suitcases went missing in transit from Beijing to Munich. We waited the 12 hours specified in the PDS and contacted Allianz.
To cut a long story short Allianz were of no help at all, the lady on the other side of the phone sounded like she was on a holiday not us. We had to purchase new suitcases and clothes out of pocket, and still waiting for a refund on our claim, and by the way we are aleady back home in Melbourne.
To all prospective travel insurance clients, stay away from Allianz you are better off having no insurance at all, and you better check who underwrites the insurance from cheaper companies, you will find Allianz in a lot of fine prints.
We will be going overseas again in July, with extensive research I found Travel Insurance Direct to be the most reliabe, having said this they are just as frugal but at least easyer to deal with.
In conclusion travel insurance is a scare tactic, as most of the costs be it medical or personal items you have to cover up front and then hope to god your insurer re imburses you for it. It's Youre decision as to which choice you make, but rest assured you will never get what you pay for in regards to travel insurance.

title: Appalling Service
body:
I unfortunately took out an annual multi-trip policy for travel to the U.S. only days prior to the government advising that international travel for Australians was banned due to Covid-19.  I have since tried contacting Cover-More on multiple occasions by phoning, emailing various customer service contacts and via their Live-Chat, to see if I can adjust my policy to delay the start date or get a refund as I'm quite clearly unable to use it in any way currently.  I've endured ridiculous wait times on the phone and live-chat,only to be cut-off without ever getting through to anyone.  My emails  simply receive the same automated response saying someone will get back to me and yet my request remains ignored.  This has gone on since March. I'm incredibly frustrated and annoyed.  I think it's outrageous that this company can keep my money for a service they clearly are not able to provide while travel restrictions remain in place for Australians.  My advice is steer well clear of Cover-More.   I intend making a complaint with their regulatory body to try and get a reasonable resolution.   Ignoring customers is thoroughly unacceptable.

One week later: I accepted the offer of mediation through this website, as a reasonable way of contacting Cover More and resolving my issue.  Aside from a bot response within a couple of hours saying a team member would get back to me within 1-2 business days (I heard that before), I had absolutely no contact or response from them.   I will now contact the ACCC to see what can be done.   

I cannot express how angry I am with Cover More.   Their non-response during Covid-19 beggars belief and unlike other corporations who have responded to customers needs during this time, this company has obviously decided that totally ignoring their customer base is the appropriate way to hang on to their money.  It's disgraceful.

title: They initially declined a legitimate claim and put us through hell before apologising.
body:
These travel policies were not good value for money as they would not pay a legitimate claim until I wrote a scathing review and a company rep contacted me and I said my wife never said the stolen article was in her unmonitored travel bag that was in the ship's luggage section a few metres behind where we were sitting. She was rung and took the call on the side of a busy and noisy Melbourne street where she was asked about her bag and answered honestly that her bag was in the ship hold and thought nothing of the question and did not realise she was being asked about her handbag, where her phone disappeared from was which was on the seat next to her. I asked they relisten to the call, they used to reject the claim. After that, they conceded the question was ambiguous and the background noise made hearing anything very difficult. My wife was issued with an apology and the claim was paid.
I strongly recommend you read the policy terms and conditions very carefully before corresponding any claim information and insist all correspondence is in writing so that both parties have access to what is said. Recorded phone messages are very one-sided and make it difficult for the policyholder should a claim be rejected for questionable reasons.
As for the policy itself, and its issue, it should have been easy, but they missed spelt my wife's name so we had to have the policy re-issued.
As for the claim process, it was awful.  
The following is the original post from 2016:
"It (the claim process) was overly bureaucratic, the web site directed us to the wrong person who sent us the wrong claim forms and then once we had the correct claim forms and emailed them to the company the relevant claim number could not be found so we had to go through the process again. The people we dealt with were always polite, though and seemingly helpful as they strung us along.
We travelled overseas for 4 months and used Allianz Travel Insurance via Visa Gold for the first 3 months plus a private extension to make sure we were covered for the next month. We have travelled overseas before, but this is the first time we have needed to make a claim. The claim was for a phone taken from my wife's handbag on a boat in Vietnam. We spent many hours (well in excess of 20!), filling a police report in a foreign country, filling in Allianz claim forms and refilling in Allianz forms as the ones we were sent were the wrong ones or the right ones were conveniently lost. The requirements of finding receipts, proof of ownership, having the phone blocked etc were onerous but acceptable, but the time it took was ridiculous. We were then rung by a Claims Officer multiple times and asked questions, one of which was about her bag, location and distance from her, to this question she answered referring to her travel bag saying it was behind her and more than 1 m away; your backpack/suitcase often is when you are on a boat or a plane. If they wanted to know about the bag the phone was in they should have asked about the phone and its location. They used that to deny the claim, saying the phone was not adequately supervised, we have protested obviously, and can now wait for another two weeks for another ruling. By that time, we will be overseas again with travel insurance from a different company!!! They had been dealing with the claim for over a month before rejecting it, if they were not going to pay they should have said so at the start, I would have been annoyed then, but to put us through hour upon hour of useless work is plain mean and makes me furious enough to write this scathing review."

Long and short of it.. Covermore are not worth it. Pay a little more and get decent service. All insurance companies seem nice, but the real nice ones come out when you need to make a claim. Stay away from Covermore and any company underwritten by Vero. I have all the written documentation to back this up including the telephone transcripts, yet not even an apology for wasting my time on my honeymoon.

title: Rip off premiums
body:
My partner had the unfortunate situation recently where her mother passed away unexpectedly whilst visiting her over in Scotland. As a result my partner had to extend her Budget Direct travel insurance by approx 1 week ( ie from 1/6/2012 to 6/6/2012). We checked the Budget Direct web site to find out how much it costs for a policy for those exact additional dates, and the premium was approx $51.00, so we reasonably assumed that would be the same price just to extra our existing policy by those dates. But instead they charged us $83.00, because "thats the way the system works"!! So far, Budget Direct has refused to acknowledge their pricing system is wrong to charge more for an "extension of cover" as opposed to "new cover" when dates and extent of cover are exactly the same (but we will keep trying). So be careful you only get charged for the exact days of cover you really need.

Premiums are often calculated for periods of cover more than you actually need - thus they are overcharging some customer

title: You'd think travel insurance would cover flight delays and additional expenses, missed accommodation
body:
I have booked insurance with Covermore a lot over the past 4 years. 25 countries worth of insurance to be exact... When I was robbed in Cambodia in 2014, I filed a police report with Cambodian officers, uploaded the police report and covermore reimbursed me of my loses no questions asked. That was good. >> ...Fast forward to July 2018, and I'm off to Japan. My first flight was delayed by an hour (due to plane rotation), so my airline took the courtesy of re booking my connecting flight (causing me a 10 hour layover in Hong Kong, so I booked a Lounge pass to pass the time, expecting it to be covered in insurance). This delay caused me to miss my Airport Transfer from Narita airport to Tokyo, one night accommodation in Tokyo. 
I claimed all of the above, waited 4-5 weeks for a response and it's come back as a denied claim, they will pay me nothing, due to the delay being caused by the airline. I'm sorry covermore... but if i take out car insurance i expect all things "car" are covered. If I take out travel insurance and I am flying overseas, I expect all things "flight" to be covered. I can't believe you dont cover one of the most common and obvious travel issues that travellers would encounter. Ridiculous!   You have lost my service.
Oh.. and just now i sat on hold to covermore, trying to speak with someone about my denied claim... waited on hold for 25 mins and then got hung up on. Umm..?

title: They Take our Payment but dont give us cover!
body:
We were already overseas on a 10 day stay and realized we hadn't yet insured ourselves....we found 1-Cover and found these EXACT words on their home Page -  'Already Overseas? Forgotten to purchase travel insurance? Already overseas? Don't panic, Cover is available here'.    

So we clicked on and filled out the form and made a payment for $180.  I paused a minute over this clause that worried me stating - 'There is a waiting period of 7 days that applies from the Start Date on the Certificate of Insurance to all claims arising from, related to or associated with any injury or sickness.' 

I thought that cant be right and got a consultant on an instant message service, the consultant confirmed we would not be covered for anything over the first 7 days of our 10 day stay!   So I asked to immediately cancel.   The consultant said that would be no problem and just asked us to email requesting a cancellation and we will get a refund.  I sent two emails requesting cancellation and refund.  I then insured us with Travel Insurance Direct and we were covered immediately, and it only cost $120.

Now do you think 1Cover refunded out money?  Of course not!  I have a meeting with our bank to arrange a credit card refund because 1Cover wont respond, they just keep our money and deliver no insurance cover at all.   

So if you don't want to be covered for 70% of your holiday, or you could say you want to pay $180 for 3 days rather than $120 for 10 days then try 1Cover!
The instant messenger service was handy.
You pay for 10 days and get 3...plus it is $180 rather than $120.

title: Refused refund
body:
A negative rating if I could.

In March 2020 I took out travel insurance with INSUREANDGO for a domestic trip to Tasmania in June.  
Due to the Covid-19 travel restrictions as they relate to closed state borders I am unable to travel.
As such the policy is of no use to me due to circumstances beyond my control. 
Until recently, many Aussies who had to cancel holiday plans due to coronavirus have been unable to claim refunds for travel insurance. However, a recent announcement by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) suggests that might be about to change.
On 2 April, the ACCC confirmed it would be letting brokers and insurers work together, to implement a range of COVID-19 relief measures for small businesses and everyday Aussies.
One of the benefits included in the relief package is the ability for consumers to claim refunds on unused insurance policies, which includes travel insurance, as long as the trip was cancelled for reasons related to COVID-19.
"All policyholders, including consumers, eligible small businesses and larger businesses, who cancel travel plans will be able to get a credit or refund for any unused travel insurance premiums, again without administration or cancellation fees."  ACCC
So far, the authorisation applies to Suncorp, Allianz and QBE. But the ACCC has said any other insurance company or broker is welcome to participate, as long as it informs the ACCC.
I contacted INSUREANDGO asking for a refund but was refused as I was outside the normal 14-day cooling off period. I was told to lodge a complaint, which I did. I await their response.

To me it?s unethical for INSUREANDGO to keep my hard earned money for an insurance product I didn't get to use.

title: A Very Difficult Claim Process
body:
I would never ever recommend Cover More Insurance. Their delaying tactics on paying a simple, straight forward fully documented claim, which included  unreasonable demands for unnecessary and irrelevant information was appalling.  I made a claim for a serious ankle injury which occurred shortly before my fully arranged and paid for trip to Europe and which made it impossible for me to walk without pain and so travel.  My claim was fully supported by X-ray, CAT Scan and an MRI of the ankle plus letters from my GP and Podiatrist clearly stating the date of my injury. (Just prior to planned departure).  Cover More took nearly a year to settle the claim writing several times to my GP each time requesting more and more  detailed information on my medical history over several years.  None of this information had any relation to my simple, sudden but debilitating ankle injury. These totally unnecessary requests took my very busy GP many valuable hours to complete.
Eventually my Claim was declared legitimate but Cover More would not pay me for several more weeks yet until I personally claimed from the airline any taxes associated with my unused airfare. 
I have travelled extensively for many many  years and never before made an Insurance Claim. As I plan my next 2 overseas trips I am carefully researching other people's reviews of Travel Insurance Companies to make sure I don't insure with another company like Cover More.
Sue

title: Do not, I repeat do not use Budget Direct Travel Insurance!!!!!
body:
Bought Travel Insurance from these clowns for our NZ holiday. They failed us in every aspect of both the immediate situation,  claims process,  and final decision.  Absolute fools  from go to finish.

Jetstar (yeah fail) canceled our flight due to crew requirements (Pilot got sick and Jetstar HR does not keep spare pilots anywhere in the network if one does not show up), so they offered 3 flights in the next 3 days to get home. Those were a 7 hour milk run, a 10 hour milk run and a 12 hour super milk run. We tried to pick a flight and it could not get us booked in. We get to the airport an hour later and finally in service. No flights left, next flight Tuesday (was a Saturday). Just utter crap.

We call Budget direct while in NZ asking for advice.  Firstly they could not find our policy even when I had said all the reference numbers on the phone and my details, so I email them and they dont get them...so I try again on another email they provide. No reference exists to our booking. Told they can't help us. Thanks.  Then after another call (so 4th international mobile call costing money) ask again with a new person and still my policy does not exist.

Person on the phone says our claim though odd with a pilot getting sick would get a successful outcome under the claim.

Under that advice we book alternate carrier flights Air NZ and book a hotel for the night to fly out next morning. Cheapest flight and cheap hotel to not claim too much. 

Get home and submit the claim, get zero reply for 2 weeks. Call Budget Direct and they have no claim from me. I repeat the email and they confirm this is the correct one. Send again...another 2 weeks and still not received by them. So I email and they say it has not arrived but I should send again...so I send to the person I was emailing instead. They advise I will get  text on receipt in 48 hours with a claim number. 1 week later I ask again on email and finally with no email reply get a text saying my claim will be evaluated in 6 business days. Weeks later I get a letter in the mail saying they were only just looking now and 10 business days to process. 

Eventually get an email from BD saying it was not under their terms of flight delay or cancellation for a pilot getting sick so no claim. 

Thanks budget for showing zero customer service when in NZ, zero customer service when claiming and zero compassion for something that should be covered.

Thank you very much for the recent submission of your travel insurance claim. This is an automated email to confirm you that we have received your claim. Please note that our current turn around time is approximately 10 business days, after which we will contact you regarding your claim.
 
Kind regards,
 
Claims Department

 
Five days later I recieved another email........

Thank you very much for the submission of your travel insurance claim.
 
We have assessed your claim based on the information you provided us with, and take pleasure in advising you of payment on your insurance claim. Please be advised you will receive a cheque for the amount specified below within the next three to five working days.

Thank you Cover-More

body:

We had a major delay (over 36hrs) in San Francisco (plane breakdown), luggage was gone and connecting flights back in Australia missed and non-refundable. As pensioners, medically TPD disabled and with our young son, we were struggling to handle the delays medically and the stress. We contacted the insurance hotline in the hotel to find out what we needed to do and spoke to a case manager and explained what happened. He went over the policy in detail, explained various areas that we were covered for (Travel expense, re-booking flights, clothing etc) and that we were covered. They stated "go buy some clothes as the weather there is bad and atrocious, and you don't have any luggage. All transport is covered, meals and purchase connecting flights on your return to Australia" They sent a confirmation email on what we were covered for, explained what information evidence we needed from the Airline, keep receipts and started the claim for us. 

We are low income and needed to confirm what we could do.

On return to Australia ($2000 extra in flight cost and expenses), we submit the claim under the three categories they stated and it's TOTALLY DENIED. Told that the case manager made a mistake and we were not covered for anything. Told they apologise for the wrong information and written confirmation and that they manager would be counselled. 

We spent and purchased according to their advice and written confirmation. Gathered all required evidence they said we needed, but no offer of compensation for their mistakes.

Disgusting company.

title: TID- First and only experience with them
body:
Decided to take out a policy with TID during my 4 week trip in Asia.

Wasn't sure on how the insurance work, decided to add extra cover for my MacBook Pro and iPad Mini Retina Wifi + 4G. On my last leg of my trip, I had my backpack stolen from me whilst on the train. Attended the police station within the hour. Filed a report, got a copy of a police memo stamped with the items I lost and the officer that looked after me and my friend. I did mention I also had my friends iPad in my backpack due to his camera bag being full of body and lens. I did not lodge a claim for this but stated this in an email to TID. He lodged it with his insurance company and I lodge my own. 

On return, TID requested I provide proof of purchase, proof of travel and credit card statements showing the paid flights.

In return, I supplied them with my proof of purchase except for the backpack and jacket that I had due to this being purchase over 6months ago. Proof of travel, all flight tickets and boarding passes supplied. (17documents supplied in total at the very start of the claim).

4 Screenshots of my statement showing purchase of these flights.

After waiting for a reply for 9 days(I promptly followed up every second-third day), they requested original police report and original invoices for my purchases. Fair enough, sent them on the 17th of March via express post.
Even attached them by original bank statements showing the purchases for my items.(another 5 docs, 22 now).

Response received today, baring in mind I lodged this on the second day i arrived back in Australia(28th of Feb).
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear ******,

Thank you for your e-mail. Please be advised that the receipts & police report has been received. Please note that we have requested further information from the police station in Hong Kong. Once the additional information is received we will be able to assess your claim further.

If you are not satisfied with any aspect of the claims process you can escalate your concerns to the Customer Relations team who will perform an independent review of your case and advise an outcome of this review within 15 business days.

Please contact us via the details below if you would like to discuss your claim further.

Regards,

Senior Claims Officer 
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Are you kidding me? My friend had his claim assessed and paid out based on a receipt and report within days.. Yet I am still waiting for these guys to contact Hong Kong Police. Surely the Hong Kong Police force have a contact number, even on the report itself has a contact number for the police officer who looked after me.

These guys are a member of FOS, I will be lodging a complaint tomorrow. Just for anyone else that needs to lodge a complaint, TID fall under
Cheap, you get what you pay for.

body:
This is the first time I?ve used Covermore. I just spent about one hour filling in the form for a 3 month trip. I find it annoying hat you cannot put your phone number in a different way to the web field. Like 0431 123 456. Can?t do it, it changes it to 04 3112 3456. Just makes the checking process longer again..
I also think that you shouldn?t have to wait till the very end to be told you need to read the PDS...best to do the 1 hour worth of reading FIRST THEN start to fill in the details.
It is critical to read and understand the pds because they will use it as evidence against you when you make a claim, which is typical of every insurer, and always refer you back to the pds, (just check some of the claim testimonies) and it?s annoying to realise you needed an extra hour when you started, only to realise that you?d run out of time and had to abort. title: Horrible, I wish zero stars was an option.
body: I purchased travel insurance for a 4 week trip to Europe over May/June. AND Budget Direct refused to pay out, after our trip was cancelled due to COVID19. I was told that because I didn't book insurance in January (I booked in February) that I should have known. The video below shows pdf files currently on Budget Directs website, with one file showing the travel insurance policy conditions purchased after the 5th of march 2020, and the other showing the same policy purchased BEFORE the 5th of March. (I booked BEFORE the 5th of march 2020). on page 19 of the file it is clear that the word "EPIDEMIC" is missing from the file for purchases AFTER the 5th. So how can Budget Direct refuse to Cover my policy when I booked before the policy conditions changed????

title: Didnt have a problem
body: Havent used insurance yet. title: Not very helpful when asking for policy clarification
body:
Happy with everything to do with TID up to the point where I wanted to query whether orthodontic work was covered or excluded by 'existing medical condition'.  Operator just read the material from the website, which I had already read and which did not clearly state whether it was in or out.  Whilst I can understand that front line operators may not know all the subtleties of medical conditions and policy, I really don't think that a response of 'I don't know, ask a doctor' is very helpful.  

A call to a competitor company was handled quickly with a transfer to the medical claims team who stated that no, orthodontic work is not covered.  Simple, that's all I wanted to know.  One less policy for TID.

Great value and so easy to set up and understand.

title: Disgusting company to deal with
body: The whole claims process and customer service is disgusting!! The worst company I've ever dealt with and such a long and painful wait for the claim to go through! body:

title: Never again

g a few days of trip end was seen - this needs to be clarified at the beginning, when application for cover is made.

title: Terrible reflection on the Travel Insurance Industry
body:

title: Terrible
body:
Absolutely terrible service. Unreliable and rude. The folks who manage email enquiries behave like aggressive salespeople. I would recommend NOT purchasing a policy from 1Cover.
The policy was cheap. Nothing else.
I was charged for an insurance policy that I did not ask for. When I emailed 1Cover they refused to refund my money (they were quite rude about it). When I asked for the matter to be referred upline I did not receive a response for several months (even though I emailed several times). 1Cover only responded when I contacted the Ombudsman - they gave me a refund but did not provide the full details of the fees involved (their responses to these email enquries also took a long time).Responses to enquries about what the policy covered and the claims procedure were very brief and completely inadequate.Whenever I emailed them to ask about the costs and procedures involved in renewing policies I was provided with very little useful information or too much information ('here is the policy - find the information yourself'), and ALWAYS asked for my credit card number.

title: Unsure if I could have received a refund
body:
I traveled to Mexico and USA recently.  Unfortunately I suffer from chronic fatigue syndrome.  I booked the trip 10 months in advance, and during that time, my condition deteriorated significantly.  I wanted to cancel because I felt unable to travel.  I called 1cover to find if I would be eligible for a refund, but received an inconclusive answer.  They couldn't tell me for sure.  Basically I would have to stay home, submit a claim and hope for the best.  I ended up going on my trip, because I didn't want to risk not getting my money back. A good price, and I guess peace of mind in case of emergencies.  Not sure about terrorist acts though, I landed at LAX just prior to the shooting, and could easily have had my trip disrupted....

title: Delaying tactics for settling an overseas injury claim
body:
I badly injured my ankle in France and was told by French doctors and the Cover-More Emergency Contact Medical Team to come home to see a surgeon. Booked business class flights as instructed by the Cover-More Emergency Contact Medical Team and was told I could claim all the costs back when I got home. 

It has now been almost 11 weeks since initially speaking with Cover-More and every one-two weeks I get an email requesting more information. Emails state that the same requests have been sent to my travel agent who is acting on my behalf, yet she gets different requests. Sent documents 11 weeks ago to be translated which weren't done, sent them a second time which were apparently never received, and only after sending them for a third time were they translated, then sent to the medical team for another review! 

Cover-More appear to be using delaying tactics by dragging out their response times to my emails - their policy is to reply within 10 business days so I am left waiting until the ninth or tenth day to get a response asking for more information. 

I am so disappointed with this service. I understand that procedures need to be followed, but 11 weeks is too long to wait given the stress this situation has caused for myself and my family.

title: Travel insurance, lack of information
body: I am going to the UK next year. I am looking at travel insurance and I had a specific question that Covermore travel Insurance refused to discuss with me. It related to the Rental of a vehicle and the insurance thereof by the rental company. There is an exemption to the policy that it does not cover me if I am making a reversing manoeuvre and also does not cover me to damage to the vehicle that is 6 feet and above. My question to covermore was, does their insurance cover me in the case that a truck hits me and causes damage to the top of the motor, which is over 6 feet from the ground. All I get is generic rhetoric and I should read the PDS, which I have but they offer no direction what so ever. Their response was, make a claim and we will see. When someone is showing due diligence to obtain information from and insurance company and is met with such a lack of information, I consider the insurance cover is less that acceptable.

title: Excellent

title: Scam. They don't pay when you need them.
body:
My partner and I booked a holiday over Easter/ANZAC period to Bali on 20/04/2019. Unfortunately our flight from Melbourne to Bali was unfortunately delayed by 18 hours. It was scheduled to depart on 7AM, so we went to the airport at 4AM, and found out the flight is delayed. We stayed around until 8AM and was told to go home and the flight is rescheduled to 8 PM (which is 13 hours delay at that time). I called CoverMore to confirm whether my travel insurance would cover any additional costs due to this delay and the lady who answered the phone said because my flight is delayed more than 12 hours, I can claim up to $200. So I was under the impression that I had $200 to spend. So we took a taxi and went home to get some sleep, and the round-trip costed roughly $180. When we went back to the airport at 5Pm, we found out that the flight is further delayed until 1 Am next morning. So we waited at the airport for another 8 hours.

After we got to Bali, there was nobody to pick us up, even though we had prebooked  Airport transportation. So we had to take another taxi to our hotel, that cost roughly $30 AUD. Not to mention that we lost a day of prebooked hotels.

After we came back to Melbourne, I submitted all of the documents (including a letter from the airline, which is issued to everybody on the flight specifically for insurance claim purposes) and receipts for a claim of $200. However they simply rejected my claim. I just felt I was scammed, because I was under the impression that I am eligible for $200. Had the lady who answered the phone said No claim initially I would've probably seeked alternative transportation. 

In the future I would probably purchase from a better travel insurance company. I've talked to a few people on the same flight and they all got their claims.  I kindly explained to them my situation and they just simply wouldn't pay. To be honest I feel CoverMore is not worth my time and money to deal with after this experience.

title: Terrible Service
body:
This is the second policy I?ve bought with TID. Fortunately I never needed to claim on my first one, as it is very easy to sign up and give your money but from the multiple negative reviews on Facebook very difficult to claim or in fact even get any customer service. 

This second policy I purchased has needed to be cancelled due to COVID and promises of sent forms and return phone calls has not happened and I?ve been chasing them up for a month with no help.
